docs.text: 1 Reading and writing for English Majors (Sophomores) Course Syllabus - Spring 2026 Course Information • Instructor: Prof. Fan-pei Yang • Email: fpyang@faculty.hss.nthu.edu.tw • Course Code: 11420FL 201002 • Class Format: Hybrid literature study and film analysis • Lecture time & Classroom : Tuesday 10:10~12:00 at HSS 人社 C412 • Teaching Assistant: Chien-Chien (Gwyneth) Wang Course Description This course is designed to enhance reading comprehension and writing skills for sophomore English majors through the study of contemporary literature and film adaptations. Students will develop critical thinking, analytical writing, and creative expression through close reading, class discussions, and various writing assignments. Learning Objectives By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. Analyze literary themes, characters, and narrative techniques 2. Write clear, coherent, and well-structured essays 3. Engage in thoughtful literary discussions and debates 4. Compare and contrast different media interpretations of stories 5. Develop personal voice in creative and analytical writing 6. Apply various writing techniques and styles 2 Required Materials Books: • Yann Martel - Life of Pi • Zora Neale Hurston - Their Eyes Were Watching God • Markus Zusak - The Book Thief Films: • The Pursuit of Happiness (2006) • My Dog Skip (2000) • Life of Pi (2012) • Dead Poets Society (1989) Weekly Schedule 2/24 Week 1: Introduction to Literary Analysis Focus: Course overview and analytical reading strategies • In-class Activity: Reading comprehension techniques workshop. Ex., the importance of understading the key ideas, pay attention to unfamilar words, predicting what might happen next, questioning the significance of certain events, connecting to real life scenarios. • Discussion: What makes a story compelling? Ex., what’s more important, plot or characters? While reading the novel(s) for this course, were there instances where you need to reread some parts? Why? • Writing Technique: Thesis statement construction • Assignment: Reading journal setup 4 journals entries will be required for the semester, each entry would need to have at least 500 words. The main point of these journal entries is to keep track of your reading progress, the content could include: date, pages read, key events (and why it is important), any symbolic meaning, personal reading reflection (ex., responses, reactions, questions/confusions, connection to real life, etc.) 3 The due dates of each entry can be found in the following weeks 3/3 Week 2: Narrative Voice and Perspective Focus: Introduction to The Book Thief • In-class Activity: Analyzing Death as narrator - textual evidence gathering. Students may be put into groups to discuss the following: Personality of narrator, attitude toward humans, emotional tone, would there be changes in narration if the narrator was human, why was a non-human narrrator chosen, etc. • Discussion: Unusual narrators in literature • Writing Technique: Point of view in writing • Assignment (due 3/10): Character analysis essay (Liesel Meminger) (700 words) The essay could be about Liesel Meminger’s personality, strengths/weaknesses, key motivations, character development (changes over time, turning points), relationships with other characters, what Liesel represents, etc. Remember to provide evidence such as quotations or scenes（page number required） 3/10 Week 3: Symbolism and Metaphor Focus: Continuing The Book Thief • In-class Activity: Symbol hunting in selected chapters Students may be put into groups and assigned to discuss symbolism found in the Book Thief (ex., books, words, bread, colors, the accordion, etc.) • Discussion: The power of words as a central theme • Writing Technique: Using literary devices in writing • Assignment (due 3/17): Brief symbolism analysis assignment (300 words) Choose one major symbol from the book (ex., books, colors, words/language, objects, etc.) and analyze（ex., where it appears, how its meaning evolves, what it reveals about character or setting, connection to larger themes, etc.） 3/17 Week 4: MOVIE DAY - The Pursuit of Happiness 4 • Assignment (due 3/24): Reading Journal 1 3/24 Week 5: Social Commentary in Literature Focus: Introduction to Their Eyes Were Watching God • In-class Activity: Historical context research presentation groups Students may be assigned the following topics: 1930s American South, segregation laws, black communities, women’s roles during that time, economic conditions of that time period Then have in class research and discussions, afterwards, each group would have to share their findings • Discussion: Janie's journey and female empowerment in the 1930s • Writing Technique: Incorporating historical context in literary analysis • Assignment: social commentary essay (700 words) This essay could be about gender roles and marriage, racism and segregation, economic hardship, black female identity, etc. 3/31 Week 6: Dialogue and Dialect Focus: Continuing Their Eyes Were Watching God • In-class Activity: Dialect analysis and interpretation What instances of Southern Black vernacular can be found in the book? What other dialects or accents can you think of? • Discussion: Authenticity vs. accessibility in literature Does writing in dialect reinforce stereotypes? Who is the intended audience? • Writing Technique: Creating authentic character voices • Assignment (due 4/7): Creative writing - dialogue-heavy scene (300 words) The assignment should be about characters’ dialogue and what’s revealed, such as arguments, secrets revealed, cultural misunderstandings, etc. 4/7 Week 7: MOVIE DAY - My Dog Skip • Assignment: 無 5 4/14 Week 8: Midterm Week Focus: Review and assessment • In-class Activity: Peer review workshop for reading journal 1. Students would be grouped into groups of 2 and will be asked to read each other’s first reading journal entry and conduct peer review based on a rubric sheet. • Writing Technique: Essay revision strategies • Assignment: 無 4/21 Week 9: Magical Realism and Survival Focus: Introduction to Life of Pi (novel) • In-class Activity: Defining magical realism through textual examples • Discussion: Reality vs. storytelling - which version do you believe? • Writing Technique: Unreliable narrator techniques • Assignment (due 4/28): Reading Journal 2 4/28 Week 10: MOVIE DAY – Life of Pi • Assignment (due 5/5): Thematic analysis essay (faith/survival) - 700 words Choose faith or survival as your essay topic, the content can be the analysis of Pi’s actions/beliefs, interpretation of symbolism, broader meanings, etc. 5/5 Week 11: Exam Day 截⽌⾄ 11 週前的⼩說與電影內容考試（包含 5-10 題選擇題與⼀題 essay question） 5/12 Week 12: MOVIE DAY - Dead Poets Society • Assignment (due 5/19): Position paper on education philosophy (300 words) This assignment could be about the comparison of traditional and progressive education, creativity and discipline, what should be priortized, etc. 6 5/19 Week 13: Argumentative Essay and Educational Philosophy Focus: Education, conformity, and individual expression • In-class Activity: "Carpe Diem" philosophy discussion • Discussion: Traditional vs. progressive education methods • Writing Technique: Argumentative essay structure • Assignment (due 5/26): Reading Journal 3 5/26 Week 14: Synthesis and Integration Focus: Connecting all course materials • In-class Activity: Theme mapping across all books and films Themes that can be found in the novels and movies of this semester: Survival, identity, family, freedom, control, power of storytelling, education, etc. Students can create visual maps or just discuss the connecting themes across works and what kind of works moves them the most • Discussion: Universal themes in literature and cinema • Writing Technique: Synthesis essay writing • Assignment (due 6/2): Final synthesis essay (1200 words) - comparing themes across all works Week 15: Presentations and Course Wrap-up Focus: Student presentations and course reflection • In-class Activity: Student presentations of final projects Students will select their final presentation topics from one of the essays they have written during the semester. Each student will choose a previously completed essay and develop presentation slides that effectively visualizes and communicates the main ideas, key findings, and most compelling insights from their work. The presentation should conclude with a brief personal reflection in which students discuss what they have learned throughout the writing process and how they can apply the writing techniques covered in this course to other academic, professional, or personal 7 contexts. Each presentation should be approximately 8–10 minutes in length.• Writing Technique: Presentation skills and oral communication • Assignment (due 6/9): last reading journal Major Assignments and Grading Assignment Breakdown: • Participation and Discussion: 15% • Short Writings: 20% • Major Essays (1. Character analysis essay 2. Social commentary essay 3. Thematic analysis essay 4. Final synthesis essay): 40% • Reading journals: 25% Major Essays: 1. Character Analysis Essay (700 words) - The Book Thief 2. Social Commentary Essay (700 words) - Their Eyes Were Watching God 3. Thematic Analysis Essay (700 words) - Life of Pi 4. Final Synthesis Essay (1200 words) - Cross-textual analysis Writing Techniques Covered: • Thesis development and argumentation • Literary analysis and close reading • Comparative analysis • Creative writing and voice development • Research integration and citation • Revision and editing strategies • Film analysis techniques Discussion Topics Throughout the Course: • Power of storytelling and narrative truth 8 • Coming-of-age and loss of innocence • Social justice and inequality • Survival and human resilience • Faith, spirituality, and meaning-making • Education and intellectual freedom • Cultural identity and authenticity • Parent-child relationships • Death and mortality in literature Course Policies Attendance: Attendance will be taken on movie days scheduled in the syllabus., On days when attendance is taken, arriving more than 10 minutes late on the second period will be counted as an absence for that day. Late Work: 1. Late submissions will be graded as follows: o 1 day late: −5% o 2 days late: −10% o 3 days late: −20% o 4 days late: −30% o 5–7 days late: −40% o More than one week late: submission will not be accepted Academic Integrity: All work must be original. Proper citation is required for all sources. Participation: Active participation in discussions is expected and will be evaluated based on quality, not just quantity of contributions. 9 Office Hours: Available by appointment - please email to schedule. "The real question is not whether machines think but whether men do." - B.F. Skinner Let's make sure we do both - think critically and write passionately.

docs.text: Chang 1 Reading and Writing II Spring 2026 Instructor: Yu‐jung Chang Class Time: Tues 10‐12 Classroom: HSSC406 E‐mail: yjchang@mx.nthu.edu.tw COURSE DESCRIPTION This course is the second part of a year‐long sequence designed to strengthen your English reading and writing skills. You will develop your ability to critically engage with assigned texts, participate thoughtfully in class discussions, and produce clear, coherent essays of exposition and argumentation. Through a series of assignments, you will learn to explain ideas logically, organize information effectively, and support your points with relevant evidence. During this semester, you will:  Write multi‐paragraph expository and argumentative essays, including timed, on‐ demand essays written under exam‐like conditions.  Provide constructive and supportive feedback on your classmates’ writing.  Revise your own work based on feedback from your teacher, peers, and digital tools.  Use AI chatbots to support your writing process, while critically evaluating their feedback and making informed decisions about what to incorporate or reject.  Respond to multiple reading texts that model the types of essays studied in the course. docs.name: 初級日語二
docs.text: 授 課 大 綱 課程資訊 課程名稱：初級日語（二） Beginning Japanese II 任課教師：王瑋婷 (WANG,WEI-TING) 上課時間：T34n 學分數：3 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (15%) □ 創作與創新能力 ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (15%) 課程簡述 本課程接續上學期內容，隨課本進度授課，協助學生奠定良好的日語發音及文法概念基礎，建立簡 單會話溝通能力。本學期進度為指定教科書 6~12 課內容。 *教學目標： 1. 學會聽、說、讀、寫日語基礎語彙及句型。 2. 能於生活中聽、說應用所學句型，具基礎日語溝通能力。 3. 理解日本文化，提升國際視野。 4. 提升學生生活品質及未來發展潛力。 課程大綱 課程說明 本學期進度為指定教科書 6~12 課內容。將隨各課主題內容講解語彙，並逐項分析主題 句型，透過口說及書寫練習強化同學們對句型的掌握度，也將透過會話演練及課堂活 動等，讓同學們進一步活用句型內容。課程中亦將帶入日本文化介紹、推薦線上學習 資源等，以強化同學的學習興趣，培養主動自發的學習精神。 指定用書 《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 改訂版》，大新書局 參考書籍 1.《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 文法解說書》，大新書局 2.《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 聴解タスク》，大新書局 3.《大家的日本語 初級 讀本篇》，大新書局 4. PPT 文法說明、其他課程補充講義等 教學方式 1. 以「單字講解、文法導入及說明、口頭及書寫練習、造句及問答應用、會話活動(、 聽力練習：視時間狀況進行)」等方式授課，以讓同學充分掌握文法，培養聽說讀 寫能力。 2. 適時補充日本文化、歌曲、生活會話、實用語彙等內容，以增進同學對異文化的理 解，提升學習興趣。 教學進度 原則上以兩週教學一課為目標，但仍視同學學習狀況等進行調整。 W1 2/24 L6 (動詞句：表達「受格」及「動作進行場所」、「邀約」等句型) W2 3/3 L6 W3 3/10 L7 (動詞句：表達「方法/道具/語言」及「對象」、動作「已完成/ 尚未完成」等句型) W4 3/17 L7 W5 3/24 L8 (形容詞句：連體及句尾修飾用法、否定式等) W6 3/31 L8 W7 4/7 L9(助詞が相關：表好惡、理解、擁有等；表達原因、理由的句型） W8 4/14 期中考、L9 *前 90 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期中考 W9 4/21 L9、L10 (存在句：表達「存在、位置」的句型；助詞や的用法等） W10 4/28 L10 W11 5/5 L10、L11 (常用的「數量詞」及應用句型) W12 5/12 L11 W13 5/19 L11 W14 5/26 L12 (形容詞句：過去式、比較級、最高級句型) W15 6/2 L12 W16 6/9 期末考、L12 *前 90 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期末考 成績考核 小考及作業 30% *小考進行數次(原則上每課 1 次，測驗字彙及文法內容；課程內容較多時，有可能 視情況改為單字小考+作業)，期末將刪除其中成績最差的 1 次。 *小考週次如請公假/喪假/病假等，出示證明則可以免考不計分。 事假及無證明的病假、生理假可補考，必須於隔週第一節下課補考完成， 每課文法+詞彙小考 15 分鐘；單字小考 10 分鐘。 遲到同學當天下課 10 分鐘內補考完，以-5 計算成績；曠課不可補考，以零分計算。 課堂參與 15% (含出缺席及課堂參與度) *無故曠課一次扣 2 分；課堂參與度欠佳者，視其參與程度減扣 0.5-1.5 分。 *為維護課堂參與成績公平性，各類請假評分規則如下： 1. 公假/喪假/具醫療證明的病假：不扣分 (病假可接受請假日 3 日內的藥袋或掛號資訊、快篩、體溫計畫面為證明) 2. 生理假：不扣分，每月最多以 1 次為限 3. 事假/無證明的病假：1-2 次不扣分；第 3 次扣 0.5 分；第 4-5 次扣 1 分； 第 6 次起不再接受請假，會登記為曠課扣 2 分。 4. 不接受事假/無證明病假連續請假 2 週以上。自第 2 週起將登記為曠課。 5. 上課遲到 15 分鐘以上，自第 3 次起將會扣分，每次減扣 1 分。 *如有特殊身心狀況，請另來信提供醫療證明並討論課堂參與事宜。 期中考 25% / 期末考 30% 其他注意 事項 1. 請謹慎評估個人日語程度合適與否、以及作息/時間分配等因素，無法配合認真參 與課堂者，請勿選課。 2. 課程中常常進行小組(大部分是兩人一組)會話練習，不願參與練習者建議勿選課。 3. 生成 AI 使用原則：本課程無涉及 AI 使用

docs.text: 授 課 大 綱 課程資訊 課程名稱：初級日語（二） Beginning Japanese II 任課教師：王瑋婷 (WANG,WEI-TING) 上課時間：Ｗ34n 學分數：3 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (15%) □ 創作與創新能力 ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (15%) 課程簡述 本課程接續上學期內容，隨課本進度授課，協助學生奠定良好的日語發音及文法概念基礎，建立簡 單會話溝通能力。本學期進度為指定教科書 6~12 課內容。 *教學目標： 1. 學會聽、說、讀、寫日語基礎語彙及句型。 2. 能於生活中聽、說應用所學句型，具基礎日語溝通能力。 3. 理解日本文化，提升國際視野。 4. 提升學生生活品質及未來發展潛力。 課程大綱 課程說明 本學期進度為指定教科書 6~12 課內容。將隨各課主題內容講解語彙，並逐項分析主題 句型，透過口說及書寫練習強化同學們對句型的掌握度，也將透過會話演練及課堂活 動等，讓同學們進一步活用句型內容。課程中亦將帶入日本文化介紹、推薦線上學習 資源等，以強化同學的學習興趣，培養主動自發的學習精神。 指定用書 《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 改訂版》，大新書局 參考書籍 1.《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 文法解說書》，大新書局 2.《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 聴解タスク》，大新書局 3.《大家的日本語 初級 讀本篇》，大新書局 4. PPT 文法說明、其他課程補充講義等 教學方式 1. 以「單字講解、文法導入及說明、口頭及書寫練習、造句及問答應用、會話活動(、 聽力練習：視時間狀況進行)」等方式授課，以讓同學充分掌握文法，培養聽說讀 寫能力。 2. 適時補充日本文化、歌曲、生活會話、實用語彙等內容，以增進同學對異文化的理 解，提升學習興趣。 教學進度 原則上以兩週教學一課為目標，但仍視同學學習狀況等進行調整。 W1 2/25 L6 (動詞句：表達「受格」及「動作進行場所」、「邀約」等句型) W2 3/4 L6 W3 3/11 L7 (動詞句：表達「方法/道具/語言」及「對象」、動作「已完成/ 尚未完成」等句型) W4 3/18 L7 W5 3/25 L8 (形容詞句：連體及句尾修飾用法、否定式等) W6 4/1 L8 W7 4/8 L9(助詞が相關：表好惡、理解、擁有等；表達原因、理由的句型） W8 4/15 期中考、L9 *前 90 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期中考 W9 4/22 L9、L10 (存在句：表達「存在、位置」的句型；助詞や的用法等） W10 4/29 L10 W11 5/6 L10、L11 (常用的「數量詞」及應用句型) W12 5/13 L11 W13 5/20 L11 W14 5/27 L12 (形容詞句：過去式、比較級、最高級句型) W15 6/3 L12 W16 6/10 期末考、L12 *前 90 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期末考 成績考核 小考及作業 30% *小考進行數次(原則上每課 1 次，測驗字彙及文法內容；課程內容較多時，有可能 視情況改為單字小考+作業)，期末將刪除其中成績最差的 1 次。 *小考週次如請公假/喪假/病假等，出示證明則可以免考不計分。 事假及無證明的病假、生理假可補考，必須於隔週第一節下課補考完成， 每課文法+詞彙小考 15 分鐘；單字小考 10 分鐘。 遲到同學當天下課 10 分鐘內補考完，以-5 計算成績；曠課不可補考，以零分計算。 課堂參與 15% (含出缺席及課堂參與度) *無故曠課一次扣 2 分；課堂參與度欠佳者，視其參與程度減扣 0.5-1.5 分。 *為維護課堂參與成績公平性，各類請假評分規則如下： 1. 公假/喪假/具醫療證明的病假：不扣分 (病假可接受請假日 3 日內的藥袋或掛號資訊、快篩、體溫計畫面為證明) 2. 生理假：不扣分，每月最多以 1 次為限 3. 事假/無證明的病假：1-2 次不扣分；第 3 次扣 0.5 分；第 4-5 次扣 1 分； 第 6 次起不再接受請假，會登記為曠課扣 2 分。 4. 不接受事假/無證明病假連續請假 2 週以上。自第 2 週起將登記為曠課。 5. 上課遲到 15 分鐘以上，自第 3 次起將會扣分，每次減扣 1 分。 *如有特殊身心狀況，請另來信提供醫療證明並討論課堂參與事宜。 期中考 25% / 期末考 30% 其他注意 事項 1. 請謹慎評估個人日語程度合適與否、以及作息/時間分配等因素，無法配合認真參 與課堂者，請勿選課。 2. 課程中常常進行小組(大部分是兩人一組)會話練習，不願參與練習者建議勿選課。 3. 生成 AI 使用原則：本課程無涉及 AI 使用

docs.text: 教學大綱 初級二 擔任老師: 張嘉芬 教科書: 大家的日本語初級 I 114-2 (星期三 & 四課程) 若遠距教學代碼將公佈於公告欄或 line 週次 課程目標與內容 第一週 複習 L1～L5 助詞的應用 第六課 是否一起去呢? 助詞「を」與 N 和 V 之關係&使用 第二週 第六課 是否一起去呢? 動態助詞「で」的表現: 場所 + で 2 + V (で 1 L5) 邀約的表現: ○1 客觀邀約→いっしょに～V ませんか ○2 主觀邀約→～ましょう 第三週 第七課 歡迎光臨 表示方法/使用/手段-助詞で 1 (同 L5) 的表現: 工具 + で 1 工具包含有形與無形 物品/方法/語言… 第四週 第七課 歡迎光臨 受詞與授受動詞的表現: 人 に N をあげます/もらいます 動作完成的表現:副詞もう + V た 第五週 第八課 差不多該告辭了 形容詞的表現 ○1 : い/な adj. 肯定形 第六週 第八課 差不多該告辭了 形容詞-○2 い adj.-否定 / な adj.- 否定/ ③ adj.與 N 的連接 第七週 第九課 真可惜呀! 形容詞- 好惡與能力的表現：好き/嫌い/上手/下手 第八週 期中考 考試 第九課 真可惜呀! (第二、三節) 表示有/無(擁有)的表現: あります/ありません 第九週 第九課 真可惜呀! 助詞 ①から 2((接續助詞)表原因、轉折、條件 ②から 1 (格助詞)  場所/時間(L4) /人/事/物(L7)等的開始/起點/出所/ 經由點 第十週 第十課 請問有魚露嗎? (物/會移動之生物)所存在的位置表現:～にあります/います 第十一週 第十課 請問有魚露嗎? 場所周邊之人/事/物存在的表現:上、下、左、右… 十二週 第十一課 這個麻煩您了 數量詞與動詞的關聯:單位- 快速記憶法 第十三週 第十一課 這個麻煩您了 時間量詞的應用:○1 「期間中的次數」句型表現 ○2 「時間量詞與 V(其他)」的句型 表現③時間量詞與 V(花費)的句型表現 第十四週 第十二課 祇園祭玩得如何? (い/な)adj./ N -時態的表現 第十五週 第十二課 祇園祭玩得如何? 比較的表現: ○1E A 前者比後者 A ○2E A 二者比較擇其一 ③全體比較擇其一 第十六週 期末考筆試&分組話劇表演 課程說明 本課程以圖文並茂方式導入教學，並重複演練以助加深記憶。每課文法解說 完畢後，指導同學短文創作、會話、發音(配合指定教材 CD) 聽力、閱讀、習題 演練等練習並小考(包含不定期隨堂小考)、搶答競賽、桌遊 (視時間)、話劇表演 等,以培養基礎日語之聽、說、讀、寫能力並增加學習趣味性。課程中適度安排 歌曲欣賞、影片欣賞，日本國情與文化相關介紹等活動，以調和課程氣氛，提升 學習樂趣，以及導入商業與科技日文會話應用教學，擴展學習領域，連結未來職場 工作。 課程目標 本學期進度「大家的日本語初級I 改訂版」6～12課 一、實現表達及溝通能力。 二、認識與學習他國文化。 三、創作與創新能力 四、將本課程之所學適宜地應用於生活、職場，並透過日本語教育多元思考與 溝通合作之影響致力於終身學習。 指定用書 《大家的日本語 初級Ⅰ 改訂版》，大新書局 ISBN978-986-321-087-0 參考用書 日文會話辭典 大新書局 ISBN 978-986-321-132-7 N5 日檢閱讀 山田社事業有限公司 ISBN 978-986-246-478-6 全新開始學日語會話 國際學村出版社 ISBN 978-986-454-120-1 評 量 期中考筆試 20%、期末考分組話劇表演 5%&筆試 20%、其他 55%(課程參與、出缺 席、小考&不定期隨堂考皆無補考) 請假申請者請提前告假(病假證明隔週出示亦可)無證明文件者當日以曠課計之

docs.text: Introduction to Syntax Spring, 2026 Time: Tuesday 3:30-6:20pm Class TA: 涂彥允 Zachary Instructor: Chun-Chieh Hsu (許淳潔) TA Contact: zachary9110@gmail.com Contact: cchsu@mx.nthu.edu.tw TA Office hours: By Appointment (A525) Office hours: By Appt. (A531) TA Office hours: By Appointment ● Course Description This course aims to introduce students the fundamentals of syntax. We will start from the basic concepts such as linear order, selection, categories, and then advance to syntactic description of various complex structures. Students will be guided step by step to understand syntactic argumentation. By analyzing data from a variety of different languages, students will learn to appreciate the diversity and the intricate design of syntactic constructions in human language.  Highlights of this course:  You will get to read and examine data from more than 100 different languages!  You will get to further understand your mother tongues (Mandarin/Hakka/Taiwanese) as well as your second languages (English/German/French/Spanish/Japanese/Korean, etc.), and be able to analyze these languages in a systematic way!  You will get a chance to learn many special and interesting features about human languages. For example, why do some languages have “gender” system but not others? What is the function of “gender” system?  You may have a chance to learn the properties of some languages that you have been very curious about but do not have a chance to learn them, e.g. Finnish, Russian, Polish, Latin, Indonesian, Zulu, the language of indigenous groups in Taiwan, etc.!  You will get a chance to invent an artificial language of your own! ● Textbook & Course Website  Tallerman, Maggie. (2019). Understanding Syntax, 5th Edition, Hodder Education  Course Website: NTHU eeclass: https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/  Relevant handouts will be supplemented in class., and all announcements will be posted on the website. ● Course Requirements & Evaluation 10% Class attendance & participation Come to class prepared and get involved in contributing ideas and asking questions. Your active participation during the class are highly encouraged. Absence of classes should be informed beforehand with supportive documents, unreasonable absences will result in grade deduction. If you have more than THREE absences (regardless of the reason), you get ZERO for this category. 15% Preview and Learning Reflection There will be weekly assigned reading from the textbook and a learning sheet (available from course website) will be available for you to do the preview. You need to complete the learning sheet BEFORE the class and bring it to the class for discussion every week. In the learning sheet, you do two things: (1) summarize TWO key points that you learn from the assigned reading, and (2) raise TWO questions based on the reading. About the questions you proposed, you may briefly explain your thoughts, and we may discuss them in the class if time permits. The grading will depend on the quality and the content of what you write on the learning sheet. Note: No plagiarism. If you are found to copy and paste the textbook or other people’s words, you get “0” for this course. 15% Group PPT exercise & presentation The class will be divided into several small groups of 2-3 people. Every week, 3-5 exercise questions will be assigned, and each group will work on the exercise questions together and prepare the answers in a PPT file. The PPT file should be submitted and uploaded to the Course Website before the deadline. Each week, one group will be chosen to present their answer at the beginning of the class and discuss the exercises together with the class. If your group voluntarily makes extra presentations to share ideas, the group may receive bonus credits. 30% Final Exam One final exam will be given to test your comprehension and learning. It will cover all the important concepts and ideas discussed in the class. It is advised that you must do the preview and HW every week to prepare for the big final exam. 30% Group Project Term Paper – to apply what you learn in the class! [15% Task 1] You will be asked to create an artificial language to illustrate all the concepts that we have discussed in the class [15% Task 2] You will pick up 1-2 real language(s) that you are interested in but not familiar with, and do in-depth syntactic analyses and description by applying what you have learned in the class. More detailed instructions will be given later.  Other Class regulations: 1. If you are late or absent from the final exam, NO make-up exams will be provided. 2. docs.text: 1 Course Title: Graphic Literature Instructor: Shuyu Lee (shuyulee@mx.nthu.edu.tw) Course TA: Bella Chao (sj970624508@gmail.com) Credit Hours: 3 Classroom Language: English Course Platform: eLearn Course Description: In our world of increasingly multimedial cultural production, the graphic narrative, a mode of story-telling that combines images and texts, has obtained a new status as a serious genre in contemporary literature. This course aims to help students build their understanding of graphic story-telling and develop their ability to appreciate and analyze visual representations. We will begin by familiarizing ourselves with the language of comics and its close cousin, film, and then go on to explore graphic novel classics, with a focus on the ways in which graphic narratives help to express ideas about identity, memory, sexuality, spirituality, postmodernism, and the post-truth media landscape. The course is conducted through a combination of lectures and group discussions. Learning Outcomes: Students will become improve their visual literacy. Students will develop the ability to analyze and interpret contemporary multimedial literature. Students will be able to learn to engage in scholarly discussions with their peers. Core Capabilities (大學部學生核心能力): 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English (溝通表達與語文能力) 10% 2. The ability to analyze classic canons of literature (文學經典的分析與詮釋) 10% 3. The ability to look for problems and conduct research (問題發掘與研究能力) 20% 4. The ability to think creatively (創作與創新能力) 30% 5. Attendance 1-A: Regular attendance is expected. ▋☆▋▌▍▎▏Two unexcused absences are allowed. Meaning: you are free to miss two classes with no consequences. ╴▁▂▃▄▅▆▇ 1-B: How to apply for excused absences and leaves?  Email the course instructor: All applications should be emailed to the course instructor.  The email should contain relevant documentary evidence for the application of the excused absence.  Emails with valid evidence will receive responses.  Emails containing no evidence have no function and therefore will be ignored. 1-C: Excused Absences and Leaves: ○1 Physical illness: Verification for a sick day requires documentary evidence, such as a doctor’s note or a clinic’s medical bill receipt. ○2 Emergency or death in the immediate family: Documentary evidence is required to excuse the absence. ○3 Public duties: Documentary evidence is required to prove the legitimacy of the public duties leave. ○4 Indigenous community ceremonies: One absence per year is excused. (In compliance with NTHU mental health leave guidelines, the course instructor will refer the students who have taken three mental health days to the NTHU Counseling Center. docs.name: 文學翻譯二
docs.text: 114 學年度下學期 (2026) （內容之黃色標示，為修訂或新增之說明 2025/12/26 ） 上課時間：W 56 課程名稱：文學翻譯（二） Literary Translation II 課號：11320FL 214000 教室：人社 C 407 授課教師：李康莉（strawnana64@gmail.com） 教師時段：如果需要討論，每週三 課後 3:20-4:10PM 老師在外語系教師休息 室。歡迎預約，可以跟老師約「課後時段」。 助教：尚無 課程資料：每週上課內容及閱讀材料將上傳至數位學習平台 Elearn 系統，請同 學記得開啟追蹤訂閱呦！^_^（https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw） Introduction to Literary Translation II The main purpose of this course is to experience the joy and challenge of translating literary texts. ^)^ During this semester, we will engage in practical translation of James Joyce's "Araby" (E2C) and Haruki Murakami's "Norwegian Wood" (C2E), focusing on both fiction and prose translation. In addition, we will cover four topics related to the translation of poetic texts (E2C), one workshop on lyrical translation, and one C2E translation of Chinese classical poetry. I aim for this course to be more workshop-oriented rather than traditional lectures. We will emphasize group discussions and foster an environment that encourages input and creativity from group work and every student. Although the course will prioritize practical training over theoretical approaches, it will still encourage creativity, imagination, subtle interpretation, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Students will enhance their proficiency in both languages while developing intermediate-to-advanced translation skills and strategies to navigate challenges that arise during the translation process. By the end of this course, I hope my students will be able to: 1. Enjoy the translation process, experiencing both the excitement and challenges involved. 2. Grasp the fundamental concepts of poetry translation. 3. Develop skills ranging from elementary to advanced levels when translating prose and fiction. 4. Compare, comment on, and provide feedback regarding translated versions. 5. Improve their writing skills in both English and Chinese. 6. Demonstrate confidence and creativity in problem-solving. 7. Accumulate vocabulary relevant to creative writing and writing in general. 8. Cultivate a keen attention to word choice, sentence structure, and the emotional resonance of a text. 9. Enhance their sensitivity to the nuances between the two languages. 10. Articulate their concepts and methods of translation fluently in their final projects. 11. Utilize tools, including AI, to inspire and facilitate the translation process, while making decisions based on specific translation principles. 課程說明 文學翻譯課程，講述內容以實務技巧為主，理論為輔。 依「難度」與「文類」，區分為上下學期課程—— 文學翻譯(1) — 文學翻譯基礎理論與練習、小說（一）、散文（一） 文學翻譯(2)— 文學翻譯進階理論與練習、小說（二）、散文（二）、詩歌 本課程包含「英譯中」與「中譯英」文學翻譯。從文學作品閱讀、以及翻譯實作練習 中，培養同學對中英兩種語感差異的辨析與轉換能力。並透過各種作業練習、分組討 論實作等，掌握基礎到進階不等的文學翻譯技巧。 初階課程：希望修習完本課程的同學，都能從實作中切實感受、體驗文學翻譯的「過 程」，無論挑戰或樂趣。主要著重於翻譯技巧，原文句法轉換拆解，思索詞彙在上下 文脈絡中的細微語意，並開放討論最佳譯法。 進階課程：大致與初階課程雷同，以實作為主。進階課程有更多中譯英的探討。文類 則多包含了詩歌翻譯。相較於初階課程，本課程希望也能多講述一些文學翻譯理論、 並邀請講者進行實務工作面向，與職場生態的介紹。 本課程主要目的在於希望同學能初步了解文學翻譯，能體驗並享受文學翻譯的過程與 成果。：） 三、指定用書： 1. 上課指定教材 2. 教師提供的補充資料 四、參考書目 1. Bassnett, Susan, Translation Studies, Methuen & Co. Ltd, 1980. 《翻譯研究：理論、簡 史、實務》林為正譯。五南。 2. Bassnett, Susan, “From Comparative Literature to Translation Studies”, Comparative Literature: A Critical Introduction, Blackwell, 1993. 3. Catford, J. C., A Linguistic Theory of Translation, OUP, 1965. 4. Venuti, Lawrence, Rethinking translation: discourse, subjectivity, ideology, 1992 5. Venuti, Lawrence, Translation changes everything: theory and practice, 2007 6 Venuti, Lawrence, The Translation Studies Reader, Routledge, 2000 7. Rose, Marilyn Gaddis, 《翻譯與文學批評：翻譯作為分析手段》（2007）。 8.《探索翻譯理論》（第二版），Anthony Pym 著，賴慈芸譯。台北：書林，2016。 9.《英中筆譯 1》《英中筆譯 2》，廖伯森等著。台北：眾文圖書。 10.《英譯中基礎練習》，廖伯森 審訂。台北：眾文圖書。 11.《翻譯進修講堂》，廖伯森 等著。台北：眾文圖書。 五、教學方式： 1 本課程鼓勵課堂上的公開討論。文學翻譯沒有標準答案。還是希望同學多能 將自己主觀的創意思考，對詞彙的理解或聯想，或對文本的詮釋，帶入課堂 發言。 2 本學期希望能更多採「小組討論」或「工作坊」方式進行。 3 授課方式：「教師講述」、「文學作品細讀」、「課堂討論」「實作練習與教師回 饋」、「分組討論」、「同學譯文觀摩」、「中譯本比較討論」「講師集體講評」 等方式進行。 4 本課程以中文授課為主。 六、 作業內容（本學期 作業形式可能包括）—— 1. 翻譯習作 2 次：小說 ＆ 散文段落 翻譯 2. 翻譯習作 1 次：詩歌 翻譯 3. 一次中譯本比對、糾錯＋分析練習 （optional）視開學後情況而定 4. 一次業師演講心得，或文學翻譯探索心得報告（optional）視開學情況而 定。 ＊本學期之「翻譯習作」，需針對教師之回饋建議，繳交「後續修訂」一份。 每學期 總文字量 約莫 7000-8000 字 七、期中考—— 是非題，選擇題，簡答或申論題 八、期末報告—— * 形式：採口頭與書面報告兩種形式。 * 內容：同學挑選適合自己程度或喜好的文學文本進行翻譯。英譯中，中譯英 皆可。 原文+譯文總字數 須達 2000 字。期末報告總字數約 4000 字。 選擇詩歌翻譯不在此限（須至少挑選 2 首）。期末報告總頁數 4-5P。 * 報告方式：本學期期末報告，同學至少須於「擇定口頭報告日」 4 天前 繳 交「翻譯初稿」一份，教師會先閱讀，必要時會給予初步意見回饋。同學進行 口頭報告後，可依當天教師意見或同學回饋，進行後續之修訂，調整。於學期 結束前（本學期最後一週）繳交「完整期末報告檔案」一份。 本學期『期末報告繳交日期』為： 2026/ 6/12。 九、評分方式 Assessment 1. 出席 Attendance 10% 2. 平時成績 In-class participation+ Occasional take-tome exercise 10 % 3. 翻譯作業 Translation assignments 30% 4. 期中考 Mid-term Exam 20% - might include multiple choices, short-answer, or essay questions 5. 期末作業發表 Final Translation Project (Oral Presentation + Final Paper) 30% - 除提供文字檔案，同學須進行口頭報告說明。報告內容除了個人的翻譯 作品，也鼓勵同學講述自己的翻譯概念、翻譯策略與方法。 十、課程主題（16 週課程） Course Syllabus (16 weeks) Week Date Theme 1 2/25 Introduction to Literary Translation II Prose & Fiction -1: Translating Araby by James Joyce (E2C) or text of equivalent level of challenge Plot- Periodic text reading sample: A Rose for Emily by William Faulkner 2 3/4 Prose & Fiction-2: Translating Araby by James Joyce (E2C) Suspense- Reading sample: Edgar Poe’s A Telltale Heart 3 3/11 Prose & Fiction -3: Translating Araby by James Joyce (E2C) Narration & Depiction Reading sample: Johnny Bear by John Steinbeck 4 3/18 Prose & Fiction -4 Feedback to students’ assignment 1 5 3/25 Prose & Fiction - 5 C2E translation Translating The Norwegian Wood by Haruki Murakami or text of equivalent level of challenge C2E reading sample: Eileen Chang’s Love in Fallen City 張愛玲 《傾城之戀》 6 4/1 Prose & Fiction - 6 C2E translation - Translating The Norwegian Wood by Haruki Murakami C2E reading sample: Eileen Chang’s Love in Fallen City 張愛玲 《傾城之戀》 7 4/8 Prose & Fiction - 7 C2E translation - Translating The Norwegian Wood by Haruki Murakami C2E reading sample: Eileen Chang’s Love in Fallen City 張愛玲 《傾城之戀》 Feedback to students’ assignment 2 8 4/15 Mid-term Exam 9 4/22 Ａ[業師演講週] (the week after Mid-Term Exam, or before Final Presentation, TBD) - 可能安排本週（期中考後一 週），或期末報告前一週，視邀請情況而定。 Lecture from Editor/ Translator/ Freelancer- first-hand experience sharing 邀請繪本翻譯、文學書編輯、其他自由翻譯者來分享職涯 經驗 ………………………. B 如無業師演講，則安排以下課堂內容—— A E2C Translation- Character & Dialogue Periodic text: Wuthering Heights by Emily Bronte 《咆哮山莊》不同譯本賞析、討論 Or B E2C Translation- Style A Farewell to Arms by Ernest Hemmingway 《戰地鐘聲》不同譯本賞析、討論 10 4/29 Poetry translation -1 E2C Translation Fixed poetic form Periodic text: translating William Shakespeare’s Sonnets 11 5/6 Poetry translation -2 C2E Translation Fixed poetic form Translating classical Chinese poems into English modern lyric [In-class workshop] Poetry Translation Assignment: Christina Rosetti or others 12 5/13 Poetry translation -3 E2C Translation Sound & Meter Translating “metered” poems- John Keat’s To the Nile (students’ sample: Malfalda; Lackadaisy) 13 5/20 Poetry translation -4 E2C translation Symbol & Metaphor Modern poetry translation: translating Robert Frost’s several poems Feedback on translation assignment 3 14 5/27 Poetry translation -5 E2C/ C2E translation Tortured-Poets Workshop Lyric translation: translating Bob Dylan, Taylor Swift and others Student’s sample: translating Chinese popular lyrics into English [ In-class translation workshop] Explication of Final Presentation 15 6/3 Final Presentation 1 期末作品成果發表 1 16 6/10 Final Presentation 2 期末作品成果發表 2 Final Paper Due Date 本學期期末報告——最後繳交日期: June 12, 2026 The End l The topic and date of lecture and the invited speaker will be decided (TBA). l The syllabus and selected text for reading and translation are subject to change according to the actual condition in class. 十一、教室與請假規則（Class Rules） 1. 比照學校請假規則無特別。 2. 不預設標準答案。鼓勵同學針對某一詞彙的聯想、文意可能解讀，提出個人 的思考與想法。鼓勵發言、提問、參與討論或表達不同的觀點。發言時使用 中英雙語均可。 3. 如遇請假或缺課，可以主動向同學或教師詢問或索取課堂作業與繳交時間， 以免延誤或影響到個人成績或權益呦。^_^ 4. 如有引用文獻、比如中譯本等參考資料、網路資料、來自同學的創意、AI 或其他翻譯工具軟體的靈感，於作業或報告中標註說明，或口頭說明之。 5. 涉及抄襲或剽竊之作業則不予計分。 十二、AI 使用準則——有條件開放使用 基於透明與負責任的原則，可以利用 AI 或其他軟體工具提供協助。並將體驗 AI 對目前文學翻譯的幫助或不足之處，納入教學體驗。 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採 取有條件開放，詳細說明如下：「本文學翻譯課程，旨在鼓勵學生獨立思考，發 揮人文感性創意，AI 能協助糾正語意錯誤，提供中文修改與潤稿協助，激發語 彙創意與靈感，也提供多樣翻譯選擇及分析回饋。針對較難理解的原文語意， 則可利用 AI 等工具協助解釋、說明，以對照判斷原文之理解。唯，針對 AI 各 項建議，同學須自行主觀判斷、仍須多方查證或檢核。 學生可於課堂翻譯作業或報告中的「註腳」、「註解說明」、「引用文獻」「資源工 具」等單元，簡要說明如何使用生成式 AI，其他資源與工具軟體，彼此分享使 用心得。 本門課授課教材或學習資料，若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭 標注。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.text: 1/3 【初級韓語二】課程教學大綱 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 初級韓語二 英文名稱 Course English Title Elementary Korean II 任課教師 Instructor 李伶美 (Lee Yeongmi) 上課時間 Time M789 上課教室 Room 先修課程 Prerequisites 「初級韓語一」 建議有修過「初級韓語一」或者具備韓文課時數達「48 小時」左右。 此科目對應之 系所課程規畫 所欲培養之核 心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) The ability to communicate and express oneself in the English/a foreign language. (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 The ability to analyze classic canons of literature. ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (10%) The ability to look for problems and conduct research (including conducting linguistic analysis through scientific methods) (10%) □ 創作與創新能力 The ability to think creatively ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (20%) The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives (20%) 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 本課程指導學生熟悉韓語發音及單字、句子之基本構造等，同時由淺入深地介紹文法關係，以及 透過基本句型的學習，期望學生能具有基本之讀、寫及翻譯的能力。同時亦將配以口語練習的互 動方式，讓學生熟悉一般日常生活及各種場合之對話用語。 課程大綱 (Syllabus) 一、課程目標 (Course Outcomes) 1. 能夠讓學生熟悉正確的韓語發音以及書寫方式，建立韓語學習的基礎。 2. 培養自我介紹、購物等基本的日常會話能力。 3. 理解並表現介紹自己、家人、日常活動等日常生活中的基礎內容。 4. 藉由熟悉基本語彙、表現、發音等，以便在日常生活中能夠提問及回答。 2/3 5. 理解並且熟悉以個人主題所構成的對話。 6. 瞭解韓語及其基礎構造，並能以文章表現自己的想法 ; 讀完簡單的文章內容後，能夠充 分理解。 二、教材 1. 指定書目 (Text Books)：《延世大學 韓國語1 (課本及 Workbook)》台北：聯經出版公司。 2. 參考書目 (References)：《我的第一本韓語文法》新北市：國際學村。 3. 韓文學習網站 (web page) (1) https://dict.naver.com/ (Naver 詞典) (2) https://dic.daum.net/index.do (Daum 詞典) 三、教學方式 (Teaching Method) 1. 由教師引導發音、單字練習。 2. 講解韓文之基礎知識及句型。 3. 練習實用日常會話。 4. 不定時小考及作業、上課參與。 四、成績考核 (Evaluation) 1. 期中考試：35% 2. 期末考試：35% 3. 平時成績(包含小考及作業，上課參與情形，出席率及上課態度等)：30% 小考不開放補考（公假不在此限，但須於次週補考完成），上課參與不開放補參與!! docs.text: Department of Foreign Languages and Literature Reading & Writing II (2) National Tsing Hua University Huang 1 Course Description This course is the second part of a one-year course that is designed to improve students’ English academic writing ability. Emphasis will be placed on writing research papers. Students in this course will explore the textual, rhetorical, and discursive conventions common in academic writing, have hands-on practice of conducting a field research, learn to critically evaluate reading sources, and write source-based research papers. Through process writing, students will be guided to do pre-writing activities, topic development, text analysis, critical thinking, library research, peer review, and revision. Although grammar will be addressed when needed, the focus of this course will be based on developing the content (ideas, structure, and logic) of writing rather than mechanics. Course Texts and Materials  Required Text • Spack, R.. Guidelines: A cross-cultural reading/writing text. (3rd ed.). New York: Cambridge University Press.  Required Material • An e-mail account. It is essential that you check this e-mail account regularly. This is because I send out reminders and notes about the class regularly through email. If you change your e-mail address, please inform me immediately. • A working account at the eLearn website. You will need to upload assignments to this e-learning platform (https://elearn.nthu.edu.tw/). Requirements and Major Course Projects  Attendance and class Participation • Participation by each student in all aspects of the class is a primary requirement for receiving a passing grade. Evaluation is based on: (a) participation in peer response, classroom discussions, and collaborative writing; (b) your diligence and the amount of effort you put into this course, into learning about the topics raised, and into your assignments; and (c) the degree to which you work toward making this course your own. Policy for absence and late attendance: **Students are required to notify the instructor in advance about missing a class. Please email at least one day before class time. You will fail this class if you have more than three absences even with prior notice. If absent, you are responsible for all notes and assignments. **Class will begin promptly. Late attendance will directly affect your grade. If you are more than 10 minutes late for class, you will be considered absent. 閱讀與寫作二(下)—學術 Reading & Writing II (2)—Academic Writing Instructor: Hung-Tzu Huang 黃虹慈 Time:T3T4 (Tuesday 10:10-12:00) Location: 人社 C521 Contact information: hthuang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: 人社 B507, Phone: 574-2710 Office hours: by appointment Department of Foreign Languages and Literature Reading & Writing II (2) National Tsing Hua University Huang 2  Main Papers You will write two main papers in addition to other classroom and/or homework assignments. Each paper will have three drafts (first, second, and final). Paper 1: Writing from Field Research (6-7 pages for each draft) Paper 2: Writing from Library and Web-based Research (10-15 pages for each draft) *All papers should be uploaded to eLearn. Please submit assignments in Microsoft Word files, using 12-point Times New Roman font, double-spaced, and with 1 inch margins.  Homework & preparation In addition to main papers, you will have reading and writing assignments. You will also be required to do library, Internet, and/or field research. See course schedule for details.  Writing conferences Writing multiple drafts of written assignments is an integral part of process writing. Also, getting feedback from others about works in progress can enrich the writing process and add the valuable perspective of a reader. Throughout the semester, you will meet individually with me—either during my office hours or during class time—and with other members of the class to share your work and to reflect on your writing process. Policy for plagiarism and late assignments: *** Plagiarism is a type of academic dishonesty which may result in failing of the class or suspension from the university. Always cite the sources you use in all assignments. If you have any questions regarding plagiarism, please consult the instructor. *** If you utilize generative AI in any part of your assignment writing process, it is imperative to include a thorough disclosure statement. Ensure that your assignment paper encompasses both the prompts and the generated outputs, along with any additional records of the text generation and editing procedures. Failing to adhere to the ethical practice of full disclosure will result in not passing the class. *** Late assignments will NOT be accepted and graded. If you are absent on the day of peer review sessions without prior notice, you will lose all points. Grading Attendance and participation 5% Homework & preparation 5% Paper 1: Writing from Field Research 45% Paper 2: Writing from Library and Web-based Research 45%

docs.text: 1 Course Title: Reading and Writing II (2): Media Writing Instructor: Shuyu Lee (shuyulee@mx.nthu.edu.tw) TA: Bella Chao (sj970624508@gmail.com) Credit Hours: 3 Classroom Language: English Course Platform: eLearn Course Description: Media writing refers to communication-oriented writing used mainly in the professional fields of journalism, public relations, and marketing. Designed for FLL students, this course focuses on news writing for journalistic and public relations purposes. This year-long course maintains a balance between reading and writing. Using the latest real- life news reports from around the world as our reading materials, we will learn how to find news, understand news, and analyze news. Then, as informed news readers, we will learn to write our own news stories. The first step toward this goal lies in adopting the language of news, a fast-paced, efficiency-minded style that makes news writing unique. We will also look at ethical issues in news writing and how well-written news contributes to social equality and justice. Learning Outcomes: Students will become skillful in communications in different media. Students will develop an awareness of audience and increase their intercultural communicative competence. Students will be able to write clear and concise documents for communicational purposes. Students will be able to critique their peers’ works and offer constructive feedback. Core Capabilities (大學部學生核心能力): 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English (溝通表達與語文能力) 30% 2. The ability to analyze classic canons of literature (文學經典的分析與詮釋) 0% 3. The ability to look for problems and conduct research (問題發掘與研究能力) 20% 4. The ability to think creatively (創作與創新能力) 25% 5. The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives (全球化與國 際視野及多元文化認知能力) 25% Required Texts: All handouts are to be accessed on the course’s eLearn platform 2 Supplementary Readings: Smith, Ronald D. Becoming a Public Relations Writer: Strategic Writing for Emerging and Established Media. 5th ed., Routledge, 2017. Bender, John R., Lucinda D. Davenport, Michael W. Drager, and Fred Fedler. Writing and Reporting for the Media. 13th edition. New York: Oxford University Press, 2023. Harrower, Tim. Inside Reporting: a Practical Guide to the Craft of Journalism. Third edition. New York: McGraw-Hill, 2013. Whitaker, W. Richard, Janet E. Ramsey, and Ronald D. Smith. Mediawriting: Print, Broadcast and Public Relations. Fifth edition. London: Routledge, 2019. Roberts, Jasmine. Writing for Strategic Communication Industries. Ohio State UP, 2016. https://ohiostate.pressbooks.pub/stratcommwriting/ Assessment: Attendance 5% Active Participation: ⚫ Volunteering to raise and answer questions ⚫ Volunteering to read texts ⚫ Other behaviors that demonstrate attention and engagement in class NOTE: Disruptive behaviors (examples: talking, making noises) that affect lectures and other students will lead to very low grades. 20% Assignments 75% Class Policies: 1. Attendance and absences 1-A: Regular attendance is expected. ▋☆▋▌▍▎▏Two unexcused absences are allowed. Meaning: you are free to miss two classes with no consequence. ╴▁▂▃▄▅▆▇ 1-B: How to apply for excused absences and leaves?  Email the course instructor: All applications should be emailed to the course instructor.  The email should contain relevant documentary evidence for the application of the excused absence.  Emails with valid evidence will receive responses.  Emails containing no evidence have no function and therefore will be ignored. 1-C: Excused Absences and Leaves: ○1 Physical illness: Verification for a sick day requires documentary evidence, such as a doctor’s note or a clinic’s medical bill receipt. 3 ○2 Emergency or death in the immediate family: Documentary evidence is required to excuse the absence. ○3 Public duties: Documentary evidence is required to prove the legitimacy of the public duties leave. ○4 Indigenous community ceremonies: One absence per year is excused. Documentary evidence is required to prove the indigenous identity and the date of the ceremony. ○5 Maternity leave: Documentary evidence is required. ○6 Menstruation leave (for biologically female persons only): One absence every four weeks is excused. No evidence is required. ○7 Mental health leave: Five absences per semester are excused. No evidence is required. (In compliance with NTHU mental health leave guidelines, the course instructor will refer the students who have taken three mental health days to the NTHU Counseling Center. In other words, the course instructor will notify the NTHU Counseling Center about the students who have accumulated three mental health absences.) References: 4 1-D: Attendance may be taken anytime during the class meeting. Students found absent at roll call will be marked absent for the day. 1-E: Three unexcused absences will incur a half letter grade reduction in semester grade. That means your semester grade will go, for example, from an original A to A-. Four unexcused absences will lead to a full letter grade reduction for the entire semester, which means your semester grade will turn, for example, from an original B into C. 5 2. In-Class Assignment Writing Sessions (All assignments are written in class) 2-A: Failure to be present for an in-class assignment writing session will result in receiving zero points for the assignment. 2-B: Make-up writing sessions are given only in the following cases:  Emergency hospitalization  Death of an immediate family member  Labor and delivery (i.e. giving birth)  Other force majeure events. ◆DEFINITION of a force majeure event: the event must be unforeseeable, external, and irresistible. ◆EXAMPLES of force majeure events: earthquake disasters, traffic accidents, armed conflicts (war), and civil unrest (riots). 2-C: An assignment paper submitted in the incorrect file format would result in one full letter grade reduction. This means, for example, a paper originally getting an A will now be recorded as a B. 2-D: Because of the introductory nature of this course, the use of generative AI for assignments is forbidden. If you are found using generative AI during an in-class assignment writing session, you will receive zero points for the assignment. 6 3. Other Policies ⚫ Course materials (including the syllabus, handouts, and remote class images, audios, and videos) should not be sold to or shared with anyone outside of the class. ⚫ Warning: The textbooks, or textbook pages, used for this course were originally created for journalism students in the United States, not foreign languages and literature students in Taiwan. Due to the differences in educational contexts, the in-class lectures will sometimes deviate from these textbook pages. The ultimate guidelines on writings in this course lies in the “living” in-class lectures rather than the “dead” textbook pages. What does this mean? People who read the textbook pages but miss the in-class lectures may end up following the wrong guidance and thus making mistakes in their assignments. docs.text: 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number 11420FL 300601 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 30 中文名稱 Course Title 中級日語二 英文名稱 Course English Title Intermediate Japanese II 任課教師 Instructor 真武薰(KAORU MATAKE) 上課時間 Time R5R6R7 上課教 室 Room HSS人社B303 提醒您：請遵守智慧財產權，勿使用非法影印教科書 Please respect the intellectual property rights, do not use illegal copies of textbooks. 課程簡述 (Brief course description) 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 Core capability to be cultivated by this course ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (55%) The ability to communicate and express oneself in the English/a foreig language. (60%) ■ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 (5%) The ability to analyze classic canons of literature. (0%) ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (15%) The ability to look for problems and conduct research (including conducting linguistic analysis through scientific methods) (5%) ■ 創作與創新能力 (5%) The ability to think creatively (5%) ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (20%) The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives (20%) 課程大綱 (Syllabus) 一、課程說明(Course Description) 該科目原則上實體教學，不過，有特別的需求時，用視訊方式上課。 加強詞彙及句型。重視 自己積極學習的態 度，鼓勵學生積極參與學習語。增加培養自學日語之基礎（聽說讀寫）。 另外學日語歌，看 DVD 等，順便接觸日本 文化。 Course keywords: 單字解說，重音，句型導入，文法解說，口頭練習，自然對話（natural speed），聽力練習 二、指定用書(Text Books) 『大家的日本語初級Ⅱ』 改訂版 大新書局 2015.09 自備講義 三、參考書籍(References) スリーエーネットワーク編『大家的日本語 初級I・II 標準 問題集』改訂版(大新書局、2016 年) スリーエーネットワーク編『大家的日本語 聴力解説タスク25』(大新書局、2000 年) スリーエーネットワーク編『大家的日本語 初級Ⅱ文法解説・參考詞彙・課本中譯』改訂版(大新書局、2016 年) スリーエーネットワーク編『大家的日本語 初級Ⅱ 練習ABC，問題解答（附中譯） 』改訂版(大新書局、2016 年) スリーエーネットワーク編『大家的日本語 初級I・II 句型練習冊』改訂版(大新書局、2016年) スリーエーネットワーク編『大家的日本語 初級I・II 讀本篇』改訂版(大新書局、2016年) 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) 講師授課方式。 每一課先上單字（包括日式漢字寫法和大寫的差異） ，再套入新的句型 及課文，然後以句型再練習實用之短句及對 話。最後再以短句做應用練 習。每一課都有單詞小考及作業（詞彙，句型，作短句，綜合等）每一課作業，錯誤分 析之後，回饋大家。 五、教學進度(Syllabus) 大概的目標是每6小時念完1課。這學期念第19課〜第25課。但看學生的吸收狀態，可能調整進度。 第一週(2/26)：課程說明，複習上學期學過的內容，文法，動詞變化複習。 第19課 單字，句型 （た形、V-Taことがある、V-TaりVTaりする、表變化的A-kuなる、AN/Nになる），會話 第二週(3/05)：第19課 練習及問題 第三週(3/12)：第20課 單字，句型 （普通形），會話 第四週(3/19)：第20課 練習及問題，聽力 第五週(3/26)：第21課 單字，句型（普通形＋と思います、普通形＋と 言いました、普通形＋ でしょう？），會話，練習及問題，聽力 第六週(4/02)：校際活動週停課一日 第七週(4/09)：第22課 單字，句型（連體修飾），會話 第八週(4/16)：第22課 練習及問題，聽力 第九週(4/23)：期中考 第十週(4/30)：還考卷 檢討內容 第23課單字，句型（普通形＋と き、V-(r)uと、…【條件文一】），會話 第十一週(5/07)：第23課，會話，練習及問題 ，聽力 第十二週(5/14)：第24課 單字，句型（くれる、V-Teくれる、V-Teもら う、V-Teあげる【授受表現】），會話 第十三週(5/21)：第24課練習及問題，聽力 第十四週(5/28)：第25課 單字，句型（V-Taら、〜。V-Teも、〜。【條 件文二】），會話 第十五週(6/04)：第25課 練習及問題，聽力 第十六週(6/11)：期末考 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 期中考 30％ 期末考 30％ 平時表現 40％ （包含出席率，作業以及上課參與情形等。請假 時一定寫請假單。無故曠課達4次者，則不給予學 分。不准沒核對過《解答》修改的作業。會扣分。請準時交作業等東西，假單及作業遲交3週之後無法接受） 七、可連結之網頁位址 web版「エリンが挑戦！にほんごできます」 https://www.erin.ne.jp 清大圖書館電子圖書 「大家學日語」 國立清華大學數位學習系統（iLMS） eeclass 數位學習平台：https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw

docs.name: 中級日語二
docs.text: 授 課 大 綱 課程資訊 課程名稱：中級日語（二） Intermediate Japanese II 任課教師：王瑋婷 (WANG,WEI-TING) 上課時間：R34n 學分數：3 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (15%) □ 創作與創新能力 ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (15%) 課程簡述 接續上學期所學內容，隨課本進度，協助同學熟悉初級程度的主題句型，進一步奠定日語溝通能力。 本學期進度為教科書 L.19 後半 ~L.25 內容。 *教學目標： 1. 學會聽、說、讀、寫日語初級語彙及句型。 2. 能於生活中聽、說應用所學句型，具初級日語溝通能力。 3. 理解日本文化，提升國際視野。 4. 提升學生生活品質及未來發展潛力。 課程大綱 課程說明 本課程授課對象為修畢中級日語(一)的同學。 隨課本進度授課，完成整冊進度後，可熟悉相當於日檢 N5 程度的日文應用，進而向 N4 程度挑戰。 課程中將隨各課主題內容講解語彙，並逐項分析主題句型，透過口說及書寫練習強化 同學們對句型的掌握度，也將透過會話演練及課堂活動、聽力練習等，讓同學們進一 步活用句型內容，提升日語流暢度及溝通能力。 課程中亦將穿插補充生活會話練習、日本文化介紹、分享線上學習資源等，以強化同 學的學習興趣，培養主動自發的學習精神。 指定用書 《大家的日本語 初級 II 改訂版》，大新書局 參考書籍 1.《大家的日本語 初級 II 文法解說書》，大新書局 2.《大家的日本語 初級 II 聴解タスク》，大新書局 3.《大家的日本語 初級 讀本篇》，大新書局 4. PPT 文法說明、其他課程補充講義等 教學方式 1. 將以「單字講解、文法導入及說明、口頭及書寫練習、造句及問答應用、會話活動」 等方式授課，以讓同學充分掌握文法，培養聽說讀寫能力。 2. 適時補充日本文化、時事等內容，以增進同學對異文化的理解，提升學習興趣。 教學進度 原則上以兩週教學一課為目標，但仍視同學學習狀況等進行調整。 W1 2/26 L19 (動詞た形應用：表達經驗〔Ｖたことがあります〕、列舉動作〔Ｖ たり、Ｖたりします〕；表達狀態變化的句型 〔～なります〕) W2 3/5 L19、L20 W3 3/12 L20 (日語「普通體」及其會話應用) W4 3/19 L20 W5 3/26 L21 (陳述/推測句：陳述個人意見及推測、引述他人發言、向他人做 確認等的句型) W6 4/2 校際活動週停課 W7 4/9 L21 W8 4/16 L22 (連體修飾句型) W9 4/23 期中考、L22 *前 90 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期中考 W10 4/30 L22、L23(事態時間點說明〔～とき〕、條件句〔～と〕) W11 5/7 L23 W12 5/14 L23、L24(授受動詞概念、動作的授受表現) W13 5/21 L24 W14 5/28 L24、L25 (條件句〔～たら〕〔～ても〕的應用) W15 6/4 L25 W16 6/11 期末考、L25 *前 90 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期末考 成績考核 小考及作業 30% *小考進行數次(原則上每課 1 次，測驗字彙及文法內容；課程內容較多時，有可能 視情況改為單字小考或作業)。期末將刪除其中成績最差的 1 次。 *小考週次如請公假/喪假/病假等，出示證明則可以免考不計分。 事假及無證明的病假、生理假可補考，必須於隔週第一節下課(15 分鐘)補考完成； 遲到同學當天下課 10 分鐘內補考完，以-5 計算成績；曠課不可補考，以零分計算。 課堂參與 15% (含出缺席及課堂參與度) *無故曠課一次扣 2 分；課堂參與度欠佳者，視其參與程度減扣 0.5-1.5 分。 *為維護課堂參與成績公平性，各類請假評分規則如下： 1. 公假/喪假/具醫療證明的病假：不扣分 (病假可接受請假日 3 日內的藥袋或掛號資訊、快篩、體溫計畫面為證明) 2. 生理假：不扣分，每月最多以 1 次為限 3. 事假/無證明的病假：1-2 次不扣分；第 3 次扣 0.5 分；第 4-5 次扣 1 分； 第 6 次起不再接受請假，會登記為曠課扣 2 分。 4. 不接受事假/無證明病假連續請假 2 週以上。自第 2 週起將登記為曠課。 5. 上課遲到 15 分鐘以上，自第 3 次起將會扣分，每次減扣 1 分。 *如有特殊身心狀況，請另來信提供醫療證明並討論課堂參與事宜。 期中考 25% 期末考 30% 其他注意 事項 1. 請謹慎評估個人日語程度合適與否、專注力、以及作息/時間分配等因素，無法配 合認真參與課堂者，請勿選課。 2. 課程中常常進行小組(大部分是兩人一組)會話練習，不願參與練習者建議勿選課。 3. 生成 AI 使用原則：本課程無涉及 AI 使用

docs.name: 中級日語二
docs.text: 114 學年度 下學期「中級日語二」課程大綱 任課教師 廖紋淑 科目名稱 中級日語二 Intermediate Japanese II 課程時段 F2 F3 F4 擬開設年級 大學部 年級 研究所 學分數 3 學生人數限制 □無 有（ 42 人） 科號 1120FL 300606 修課限制 限外語系：□是 否 教室 人社 C412 課程綱要 課程說明 學習目標 認知 ⚫ 習得日文基礎句型 ⚫ 藉由日語學習同時理解日本文化 技能 ⚫ 奠定基礎日語會話技巧 ⚫ 培養基礎日文讀寫能力 情意 ⚫ 以日語與他人溝通，獲得成就感、增添學習興趣。 ⚫ 觀察日語表達的習慣與特色，體察日文文化 核心能力： 溝通發表與語文能力：60% 問題發掘發掘與研究能力：20% 全球視野與多元文化認知能力：20% 指定用書 『大家的日本語 初級Ⅱ 改訂版』 大新書局 參考資料 『大家的日本語』初級Ⅰ 『大家的日本語』初級讀本篇 教學方式 1. 各課採用「單字解說，句型導入，文法解說，口頭演練，聽力 練習」等方式進行，培養學習者閱讀能力以及口語表達能力。 2. 以板書與補充教材等幫助學習者理解文法使用基礎概念，並搭 配日常生活常用語彙練習，增加記憶力外，並達到能夠簡單運 用日語會話溝通的能力。 3. 適時以日語歌曲，以及日語電影影片等輔助教學，藉由觀察日 語表達的習慣與影片中使用的場景來體察日本文化，提升學習 意願。 4. 每堂課都有隨堂小考（不接受補課或提前考試）及作業 教學進度 上課的目標是每 6 小時上完 1 課為原則。依學生的吸收狀況，隨時 調整上課的進度。 第 1 週：課程說明、第 20 課普通形 第 2 週：第 20 課普通形、普通体運用不同語調表達發話意圖 第 3 週：第 21 課課文及練習。第 21 課「〜と思います」敘述推測、想法、 意見、「〜と言いました」引用 第 4 週：第 21 課「でしょう」確認事實，期待對方同意自身發話。 第 5 週：第 21 課課文及練習。第 22 課「連體修飾」 第 6 週：第 22 課「連體修飾」詳盡地說明，描寫人事物 第 7 週：第 22 課課文及練習 第 8 週：複習 F 第 9 週：期中考 第 20 課－第 22 課 第 10 週：檢討期中考卷 第 11 週：第 23 課「～時」適當地表達執行動作的場合、情況、「〜と〜」 條件句、詢問以及回應機械用法、路線 第 12 週：第 23 課詢問以及回應機械用法、路線。課文及練習。 第 24 課：第 24 課「をくれる」物品的授受表現 「て／あげる／くれる／もらう」行為的授受表現 第 13 週：第 24 課課文及練習。 第 14 週：第 25 課「〜たら、〜」條件句 確定條件、「〜ても〜」某條件發生後卻未發生期待的結果 第 15 週：第 25 課文以及練習、複習 G、總複習 第 16 週：期末考 第 23 課－第 25 課 成績考核 1. 課堂參與：15% 2. 課堂中的隨堂測試：20% 3. 期中考：25% 4. 期末考：30% 5. 作業：10% 注意 1. 本課程不接受同學停修申請。 2. 所有測驗考試，不接受補考，提前考試。 3. 為維護上課品質，不接受旁聽。 4. 請假（病假、公家、喪假、事假…等）請務必提出相關證明， 同時請假期限需在請假日之前後 1 週完成，否則不予准假。 請同學斟酌自身修課狀況，規劃安排課程，並尊重選課結果 可連結之網頁位址 「國立清華大學數位學習系統 eeclass https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw」

docs.text: 授 課 大 綱 課程資訊 課程名稱：中級日語（二） Intermediate Japanese II 任課教師：王瑋婷 (WANG,WEI-TING) 上課時間：R678 學分數：3 此科目對應之系所課程規畫所欲培養之核心能力 ■ 溝通表達與語文能力 (70%) □ 文學經典的分析與詮釋 ■ 問題發掘與研究能力 (15%) □ 創作與創新能力 ■ 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 (15%) 課程簡述 接續上學期所學內容，隨課本進度，協助同學熟悉初級程度的主題句型，進一步奠定日語溝通能力。 本學期進度為教科書 L.19 後半 ~L.25 內容。 *教學目標： 1. 學會聽、說、讀、寫日語初級語彙及句型。 2. 能於生活中聽、說應用所學句型，具初級日語溝通能力。 3. 理解日本文化，提升國際視野。 4. 提升學生生活品質及未來發展潛力。 課程大綱 課程說明 本課程授課對象為修畢中級日語(一)的同學。 隨課本進度授課，完成整冊進度後，可熟悉相當於日檢 N5 程度的日文應用，進而向 N4 程度挑戰。 課程中將隨各課主題內容講解語彙，並逐項分析主題句型，透過口說及書寫練習強化 同學們對句型的掌握度，也將透過會話演練及課堂活動、聽力練習等，讓同學們進一 步活用句型內容，提升日語流暢度及溝通能力。 課程中亦將穿插補充生活會話練習、日本文化介紹、分享線上學習資源等，以強化同 學的學習興趣，培養主動自發的學習精神。 指定用書 《大家的日本語 初級 II 改訂版》，大新書局 參考書籍 1.《大家的日本語 初級 II 文法解說書》，大新書局 2.《大家的日本語 初級 II 聴解タスク》，大新書局 3.《大家的日本語 初級 讀本篇》，大新書局 4. PPT 文法說明、其他課程補充講義等 教學方式 1. 將以「單字講解、文法導入及說明、口頭及書寫練習、造句及問答應用、會話活動」 等方式授課，以讓同學充分掌握文法，培養聽說讀寫能力。 2. 適時補充日本文化、時事等內容，以增進同學對異文化的理解，提升學習興趣。 教學進度 原則上以兩週教學一課為目標，但仍視同學學習狀況等進行調整。 W1 2/26 L19 (動詞た形應用：表達經驗〔Ｖたことがあります〕、列舉動作〔Ｖ たり、Ｖたりします〕；表達狀態變化的句型 〔～なります〕) W2 3/5 L19、L20 W3 3/12 L20 (日語「普通體」及其會話應用) W4 3/19 L20 W5 3/26 L21 (陳述/推測句：陳述個人意見及推測、引述他人發言、向他人做 確認等的句型) W6 4/2 校際活動週停課 W7 4/9 L21 W8 4/16 L22 (連體修飾句型) W9 4/23 期中考、L22 *前 90 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期中考 W10 4/30 L22、L23(事態時間點說明〔～とき〕、條件句〔～と〕) W11 5/7 L23 W12 5/14 L23、L24(授受動詞概念、動作的授受表現) W13 5/21 L24 W14 5/28 L24、L25 (條件句〔～たら〕〔～ても〕的應用) W15 6/4 L25 W16 6/11 期末考、L25 *前 90 分鐘正常上課，後半進行期末考 成績考核 小考及作業 30% *小考進行數次(原則上每課 1 次，測驗字彙及文法內容；課程內容較多時，有可能 視情況改為單字小考或作業)。期末將刪除其中成績最差的 1 次。 *小考週次如請公假/喪假/病假等，出示證明則可以免考不計分。 事假及無證明的病假、生理假可補考，必須於隔週第一節下課(15 分鐘)補考完成； 遲到同學當天下課 10 分鐘內補考完，以-5 計算成績；曠課不可補考，以零分計算。 課堂參與 15% (含出缺席及課堂參與度) *無故曠課一次扣 2 分；課堂參與度欠佳者，視其參與程度減扣 0.5-1.5 分。 *為維護課堂參與成績公平性，各類請假評分規則如下： 1. 公假/喪假/具醫療證明的病假：不扣分 (病假可接受請假日 3 日內的藥袋或掛號資訊、快篩、體溫計畫面為證明) 2. 生理假：不扣分，每月最多以 1 次為限 3. 事假/無證明的病假：1-2 次不扣分；第 3 次扣 0.5 分；第 4-5 次扣 1 分； 第 6 次起不再接受請假，會登記為曠課扣 2 分。 4. 不接受事假/無證明病假連續請假 2 週以上。自第 2 週起將登記為曠課。 5. 上課遲到 15 分鐘以上，自第 3 次起將會扣分，每次減扣 1 分。 *如有特殊身心狀況，請另來信提供醫療證明並討論課堂參與事宜。 期中考 25% 期末考 30% 其他注意 事項 1. 請謹慎評估個人日語程度合適與否、專注力、以及作息/時間分配等因素，無法配 合認真參與課堂者，請勿選課。 2. 課程中常常進行小組(大部分是兩人一組)會話練習，不願參與練習者建議勿選課。 3. 生成 AI 使用原則：本課程無涉及 AI 使用

docs.text: Course Name: Victorian Literature Instructor: Yi-Chuang E. Lin Credit 3 Scheduled course hours: Mon 10:10-13:00 Course Description: In this course we will examine and discuss British society, culture and also scientific advancement under the reign of Queen Victoria (1837- 1901) through its Literature. Through the fictional works of Charles Dickens, Emily Brontë, Lewis Carroll, George Eliot, and the essays of John Stuart Mill, Karl Marx, Thomas Huxley and Matthew Arnold, we probe deeper into this triumphant age of British History, and explore its social concerns, economic discourses, scientific advancement and the unsettling brave new world with the introduction such as “imaginative numbers,” electromagnetism, etc. Course requirement: One individual in-class presentation in English (15%) Four scheduled in-class and possibly additional pop Quizzes (50%) Class attendance, participation and contribution (15%) Final Paper (20%) Course Schedule: 2/23 Introduction Matthew Arnold, Dover Beach Charles Dickens, Bleak House 3/2 Charles Dickens, Bleak House: The parallel narrative points of view 3/9 John Henry Cardinal Newman, The Idea of a University Charles Dickens, Bleak House Tom-All-Alone’s, Jo, and the poor of the Victorian age 3/16 Charles Dickens, Bleak House A too far-sighted mother nation 3/23 Charles Dickens, Bleak House Krook’s Spontaneous Combustion 3/30 John Stuart Mill, The Subjection of Women Lewis Carroll, Alice in the Wonderland Falling into the Rabbit Hole and Journey into the Underworld 4/13 Lewis Carroll, Alice in the Wonderland The alter dimension Mad Hatter’s tea party (t-party) and Algebra 4/20 Lewis Carroll, Alice in the Wonderland 4/27 Thomas Henry Huxley, Science and Culture (Two Cultures Debate) Matthew Arnold, Literature and Science; Culture and Anarchy 5/4 Alfred, Lord Tennyson, The Lady of Shalott and Ulysses 5/11 Emily Brontë, Wuthering Heights Class and Race 5/18 Charles Darwin and Evolution Emily Brontë, Wuthering Heights 5/25 Emily Brontë, Wuthering Heights Byronic Hero, Nietzschean superman, Freudian id and alter-ego 6/1 Movie Section 6/8 Final Paper Due

docs.name: 雙語網頁設計
docs.text: 課程名稱 (中文) 雙語網頁設計 (英文) Bilingual Web Design Spring 2026 Time: Fri 09:00-12:00 Location: HSS C521 Instructor: 陳宗穎 chen.ty@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: HSS-B506 Office Hours: Wed 12:00 – 13:00 or by appointment Last Updated on Dec 2, 2025 課程大綱內容 一、課程概述 This course focuses on the full training of front-end Web programming skills for fluently bilingual or multilingual students majoring in foreign languages and literature, so they, without the assistance from computer experts, are able to design multilingual webpages independently. This training will be combined with the students’ training in multilingual reading and writing skills in the department to practice the concept of digital humanity and to have more choices of their career paths. Experience in Web design or computer programming is NOT required. 二、課程目標 The students in this course will be focusing on learning HTML5, CSS, and JavaScript (jQuery in particular) to complete in-class assignments and a bilingual (Chinese and English) course project. For the in-class assignments, the students will have to complete mini Web programming tasks on-site, without the help of generative AI. The tasks will be scored based on their completeness within the time limit. In the course project, students will build a bilingual personal website to present their CV or portfolio to academia or the industry. On the same website, they will also need to introduce a theme they are interested in and present a bilingual article on a properly designed webpage. With their experience in completing tasks and projects, the students are expected to be capable of understanding more advanced Web design knowledge and presenting insightful ideas in diverse and multilingual contexts. 三、課程進度表 週次 主題 閱讀範圍 2/27 Peace Memorial Day (No Class) 3/6 Introduction & HTML Basics Course Website (HTML Basics) 3/13 HTML5 & CSS3 Couse Website (HTML Basics & CSS Basics) 3/20 3/27 JavaScript & jQuery Couse Website (JS Basics & jQuery) 4/3 Tomb Sweeping Day (No Class) 4/10 JavaScript & jQuery (cont’) Couse Website (JS Basics & jQuery) 4/17 4/24 Responsive Web Design Course Website (Mobile First) 5/1 5/8 5/15 5/22 CSS3 & jQuery Animation Course Website (Web Animation) 5/29 6/5 6/12 四、指定閱讀： Course Website: https://nthutychen.github.io 五、參考書籍 Murphy et al. (2012). Beginning HTML5 and CSS3: The Web Evolved. New York: Springer. Fielding, Jonathan. (2014). Beginning Responsive Web Design with HTML5 and CSS3. New York: Springer. 六、評量方式 In class assignments (60%) After each lecture lasting 2-2.5 hours every Friday, the students will spend the rest of the time in class completing assigned Web design mini tasks. The tasks will be scored at the end of the lecture. There will be no make-up assignments, so if you miss a lecture, you will also miss an in-class assignment. Bilingual website projects (40%) The students will have to complete two bilingual website projects at the end of the course on Jun 13, 2026 before midnight. The first project is a personal website at https://xxxxxxx.github.io/personal/ (xxxxxxx is the student’s GitHub account) and the second project is a thematic website at https//xxxxxxx.github.io/writing/ introducing general English reading and writing guidelines with an English article. Both projects must be in both Mandarin Chinese and English, and other languages are optional. The website must include only Web programming introduced in this course, and the students are not allowed to use any templates or plagiarize any content in their projects. If these guidelines are violated, the projects will receive a ZERO score. The personal website should include a self-introduction of at least 500 words (in English) and a curriculum vitae. The website must be designed with abundant visual features with Web programming rather than text- only. The thematic website should be designed to introduce English reading and writing guidelines (i.e., thesis statement, coherent writing, cohesive writing, and takeaways) with an analysis of a selected article from The New York Times. There is no specific Web design guideline for the two projects, so the students can build functional websites in the ways that work best for themselves, as long as the content is presented following the above instructions. However, A+ will only be given to projects that can be presented properly in both desktop and mobile devices with a responsive Web design. AI Policy For assignments to be completed on-site, the students will NOT be allowed to use any generative AI. Those who use generative AI to complete the assignments will score a zero. For the two website projects, I remain open-minded to the involvement of generative AI, although I STRONGLY ADVISE AGAINST USING IT, especially before the students are highly familiar with Web programming. Students should be learning ‘how to design a bilingual website’ in this course, rather than ‘how to use AI to design a bilingual website’. If you do not believe that learning makes you better than AI, you can just go with ‘vibe coding’ and do not have to take this course. Even if you use AI to ‘support’ your learning, your bilingual projects will still have to follow the project guidelines. In particular, your websites MUST NOT include anything that is not explained in this course. The students will learn enough skills to design a very professional website in this course.

docs.text: COURSE SYLLABUS National Tsing Hua University English for the Workplace Spring 2026 Instructor: I-Tsen Huang Email: itsen1213@gmail.com Course Description Integrating the four skills of the English language with professional language development and covering both spoken and written communication, the course is aimed at advancing students’ verbal and soft skills for workplace success and expanding their lexical repertoire in business jargon, idioms, metaphors, and workplace English. To help students cultivate self-development and personal growth at work, the course taps into advice from industry leaders, career coaches, self-help authors, management gurus, scholars, and psychologists. Harnessing expert insights from popular podcasts and the “Bartleby” column of The Economist, the course offers practical training in functional business skills, key business topics, and real-life business stories to help students navigate uncertainty and change in the workplace. Office hours by appointment only Tuesday 13:00 - 15:15 Required course materials The course materials are available in each of the weekly folder on the eLearn learning platform. Students are required to access the files and print them out. Grading policies I. Attendance – 10% a. Each late arrival will result in a 2-point deduction of the semester grade. b. Missing 15 minutes of class—arriving late, departing early, or leaving during class— counts as half an absence. II. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University, Department of Foreign Languages and Literature 11420 FL 310100 第二語言習得 Second Language Acquisition Spring Semester 2026 Tuesday 12:10 AM – 15:10 PM Instructor: Viphavee Vongpumivitch (viphavee@gapp.nthu.edu.tw) Course objectives: This course aims to provide college students who major in Foreign Languages and Literature (FLL) a broad overview of theories and research issues in the field of Second Language Acquisition (SLA). Topics covered include issues in first and second language learning, evidence of second language development, the impact of individual differences on learning, different theoretical perspectives on SLA, bilingualism, and second-language learning in the classrooms. The course is important for students who want to become language teachers, as the knowledge gained from this course can help guide how to teach languages. The course is also important for students learn foreign languages, as the knowledge gained from this course can enable them to improve their own language-learning capabilities. Thanks to a special funding from the Taiwanese Ministry of Education, the students in Spring 2026 will be able to use AI- assisted language-learning tools to explore further issues in SLA and see a connection between SLA theories and their own language-learning experience. 核心能力 Core capability 20% 溝通表達與語文能力 The ability to communicate and express oneself in the English/a foreign language. 50% 問題發掘與研究能力 The ability to look for problems and conduct research (including conducting linguistic analysis through scientific methods) 10% 創作與創新能力 The ability to think creatively 20% 全球化與國際視野及多元文化認知能力 The ability to examine issues through global and multicultural perspectives Textbook: Lightbown, P.M. & Spada, N. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Humanities and Social Sciences Syllabus 11320FL 326600 English-Chinese News Translation Spring 2026 Instructor: Chen, Kuo-Hua Thursday, 1:20 PM - 3:10 PM chenkuohua@mx.nthu.edu.tw Course Description With the aim of developing students' translation skills in a journalistic context, this course will be taught bilingually in English and Chinese, which includes translating English language news articles into Chinese ones. This course is also designed to be an application-oriented course and heavily utilizes real-world news material from various media. It not only helps students understand the process of journalistic translation, but also familiarizes them with writing news stories across different media. Based on a general belief that translation is a skill developed through regular practice, students are required to complete a large number of exercises/assignments and participate in group discussions to improve their translation abilities. Course Objectives Students are expected to enhance skills of news translation through the course, to become news translators in the future. Upon successful completion of the course, the students will be able to: 1) Become familiar with the issues and challenges in translating English news stories. 2) Apply their translation skills to develop the concept of trans-editing. 3) Understand the process of journalistic translation in various news media. 4) Discover errors and problems found in the journalistic English translation. 5) Develop ability to collect and search information from diverse resources. Textbook & References There will be no textbook required for this course, but the following books are recommended should you feel a text would be helpful. 新聞英文閱讀與翻譯技巧 (廖柏森，眾文) 英中新聞筆譯 (廖柏森，眾文) Translation Strategies in Global news (Claire Scammell; Palgrave Pivot) A Discourse Analysis of News Translation in China (Liang Xia; Routledge) Grading Policy Exercises 20% Participation 30% Midterm 25% Final Exam 25% Participation It is vital to participate in classroom activities, such as answering teacher’s oral questions promptly and acquire extra points counted to your final grade. Students are requested to focus properly on course content and classroom interaction. However, laptops, smartphones, tablet computers are permitted and encouraged in class to do note-taking or search for specific information. Students are even required to use an APP to submit their in-class translation exercises. docs.text: 課程名稱 (中文) 音韻學 (英文) Phonology Spring 2026 Time: Wed 09:00 – 12:00 Location: HSS C412 Instructor: 陳宗穎 Office: B506 Office Hours: 12:00 – 13:00 Wed or by appointment Teaching Assistant: 王泓懿 hyw976@gmail.com Last Updated on Jan 21, 2026 課程大綱內容 一、課程概述 Phonology is a subfield in linguistics which studies the mental knowledge of how sounds of a language are organized. This course begins by introducing and reviewing main evidence for mental phonological knowledge to explain the fundamental aspects in phonology. Students are then presented with diverse sound patterns in a wide variety of languages around the world and trained to complete a number of phonological analyses, which are believed to simulate what real language learners do. In addition to these traditional trainings, students will explore modern phonological theories and research methods and link these aspects to their real-life experience of language use, which could help set up themselves for advanced studies in phonology in the future. While phonetics is not a prerequisite of this course, students are highly recommended to have the background knowledge of phonetics before taking this course. 二、課程目標 This course seeks to (i) explain the core aspects of phonology to students so they can understand the importance of this subject and link abstract concepts to real-life examples, (ii) convince the students that phonological knowledge does exist and that phonology is one of the scientific studies of a mental language system, (iii) train students to discover evidence of phonology from their real-life linguistic interactions (iv) introduce patterns at different levels of phonology across less-known languages (i.e. languages other than Chinese and English) and train the students to analyze these patterns using a traditional approach, and finally (v) provide opportunities for the students to applied the acquired knowledge to test and solve real-life problems. 三、課程進度表 日期 主題 閱讀範圍 2/25 Course Overview Odden Ch. 1 3/4 Basic Phonological Units and Phonological Acquisition Odden Ch. 8 (Optional) 3/11 Consonant and Vowels, Phoneme and Allophone Odden Ch. 2 3/18 3/25 Abstract Knowledge (I) – Phonological Features & Rewrite Rules Odden Ch. 34/1 4/8 4/15 Abstract Knowledge (II) – Underlying Representation Odden Ch. 4 4/22 4/29 Midterm 5/6 Complicated Phonological Process: Rule Ordering Odden Ch. 5-65/13 5/20 5/27 Phonological Typology and Phonological Naturalness Odden Ch. 7 6/3 Autosegmental Phonology Odden Ch. 9 6/10 Sign Language Phonology Guest Lecturer 四、指定閱讀： Odden, D. (2013). Introducing Phonology. Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press. 五、評量方式 Assignments (35%) Each student will have to complete four to six assignments in this term, which are composed of phonological analyses as well as essay questions. Students are encouraged to discuss the assignments together, but they have to write and submit their own assignments. Students submitting assignments with very similar content will have to share the credit for the assignments. Also, any assignments that are judged as ‘unacceptable’ (usually those that do not follow the instructions) will get no credit. Midterm (30%) On Apr 29, 2026, students will be tested with regard to fundamental aspects lectured in previous weeks. They will be required to define phonological terminologies, solve phonological puzzles, and possibly answer open questions. Since this test is the baseline of whether students have learned knowledge that allows them to complete the course project, if students score less than 50 points on this exam and got one C+ (or lower) for any assignment completed before the exam, they automatically fail this course. Personal Term Project (35%) In their term project, students will have to extend their knowledge acquired in this course to complete an independent phonological study. In a task that will be specified in the second half of the semester, students will be asked to observe/elicit and analyze phonological patterns from other speakers’ linguistic output in order to explain the linguistic behavior of human beings. The paper will be assessed based on its clarity and whether the students thoroughly understand and apply the fundamental concepts of phonology. The paper is due 23:59, Jun 12, 2026. LATE papers are NOT ACCEPTED, and papers that are ‘unacceptable’ or contain PLAGIARISM will not be graded (i.e., you will get a zero!). AI Policy This course is completely open to the use of generative AI in the assignments and personal term project papers, and the use of generative AI should be fully disclosed in the students’ works. However, students are still solely responsible for the issues caused by generative AI, and it is extremely important to note that over- reliance on generative AI could easily lead to unacceptable assignments and papers that WILL NOT be graded.

Designed for students without extensive biology backgrounds, we will examine how the brain processes language, forms memories, and generates thoughts. Through films, discussions, and student presentations, we will bridge neuroscience with humanities and social sciences to understand the neural basis of human communication and cognition. Lecture Time & Classroom Thursday 10:10~13:00 at HSS 人社 C511 Prerequisites None. This course is designed for students from all academic backgrounds as part of general education requirements. docs.text: Studies in U. S. Proletarian Literature 1. 課程說明 In the United States, proletarian literature flourished in the years surrounding the Great Depression. Having witnessed various social injustices inflicted upon workers in farms and factories alike, writers diversely gendered and racialized committed themselves to exposing capitalist exploitation and envisioning a just society. This course will study selective works of proletarian literature produced in this period, paying special attention to Richard Wright’s novel Native Son. By studing their representations of the struggle of the working-class people, along with visual adaptations of some of these works and films addressing similar concerns, we will explore the problems of capitalist society and examine the achievements and limitations of the literary project for social critique. 2. 指定用書 Literary Texts used: Carlos Bulosan, “If You Want to Know What We Are,” “The Story of a Letter” Stephen Crane, “The Man in the Storm” Mike Gold, “Jews and Christians” and “The Soul of a Landlord,” from Jews Without Money ; “Go Left, Young Writers!” Meridel Le Sueur, “The Fetish of Being Outside”; Excerpts from The Girl Richard Wright, “I Have Seen Black Hands” Richard Wright, Native Son (restored text established by the Library of America, Harper Perennial 2005) Visual Texts used Charlie Chaplin, Modern Times(1936) John Ford’s film adaptation of John Steinbeck, The Grapes of Wrath 3. 教學方式：a mix of lectures, class discussion, and student presentations 4. 教學進度 Week 1 2/24 General Introduction; Charlie Chaplin’s Modern Times Week 2 3/3 Discussion of Modern Times. Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour Yuan-yang Wang 王遠洋 yy.wang@mx.nthu.edu.tw N/A By appointment Course Goals / Description Examining the Indo-European root of the word “queer,” Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick points out that the word derives from the German “quer” (transverse) and Latin “torquere” (to twist). According to the OED, “Queer” emerged in the early 1990s and was adopted by LGBT activists. Scholars of literature have challenged the Eurocentric perspective on the formation of canonical literature with their comrades, including advocates of social movements, literary publishers, commentators, influencers, public figures, and translators. Also, they have devoted themselves to building “queer literature,” an emergent field since the late twentieth century. To trace a queer literary history, many canonical authors were rediscovered, relocated, and reimagined in the light of multiculturalism and gender criticism. In this course, students will investigate the works of the canonical authors with the potential of “being queer.” How these authors became queer is also a microcosm for students to seek the boundary between literary canon and emergent literature. Topics will include postcolonialism and gay/lesbian identity, gay/lesbian writers as an iconography of gay and lesbian community, gay/lesbian identity and global diaspora, and gay/lesbian award-winning writers and their influence on the literary circle.
