docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11420IPMT100300 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 30 中文名稱 Course Title 商務英文與多元文化視角 英文名稱 Course English Title Business English for Empathic Leadership and Cross-Cultural Perspectives 任課教師 Instructor 徐正和 Erik. H. Kaga 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information solitarygam@gmail.com; ehsu@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time F5F6 上課教室 Room 台積 223 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) N/A 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives Can-do statement #1 CORRESPONDING CEFR CAN-DO STATEMENTS [LISTENING] can with some effort catch much of what is said around me, but may find it difficult to understand a discussion between several speakers who do not modify their language in any way. Can-do statement #2 [READING] can understand articles, reports and reviews in which the writers express specific points of view. Can-do statement #3 [SPEAKING INTERACTION] can take an active part in conversation, expressing clearly my points of view, ideas or feelings naturally with effective turn-taking. Can-do statement #4 [SPEAKING PRODUCTION] can present a topical issue in a critical manner and weigh up the advantages and disadvantages of various options. Can-do statement #5 [WRITTEN PRODUCTION] can write at length about topical issues, even though complex concepts may be oversimplified, and can correct many of my mistakes in the process. Can-do statement #6 [STRATEGIES] can generally correct slips and errors if I become aware of them or if they have led to misunderstandings. Can-do statement #7 [QUALITY OF LANGUAGE] can link what I say or write into clear, well- organized text, though I may not always do this smoothly so there may be some “jumps.” National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 課程目標 Course Objectives By completing this course, students will be able to: 1. Communicate effectively and appropriately in global and multicultural business environments. 2. Apply cross-cultural frameworks (e.g., Hofstede, Hall) to interpret differences in communication styles. 3. Use business-related vocabulary and expressions to participate in meetings, discussions, and negotiations. 4. Produce clear, audience-appropriate written communication such as emails, proposals, and reports. 5. Collaborate in task-based projects that integrate language, culture, and problem-solving skills. 課程說明 Course Description This course is designed to strengthen students’ communicative competence and intercultural awareness in business contexts. Through an integrated, task-based framework, students will engage in authentic communicative activities that simulate real-world business interactions across cultures. Building on a cross-disciplinary perspective, the course draws from the instructor’s professional experiences in international enterprises, media, and education to help students understand how language, culture, and identity shape global communication. Weekly thematic topics—such as leadership, branding, teamwork, and negotiation—provide students with structured opportunities to discuss, analyze, and present ideas in small task forces. By the end of the semester, students will be able to conduct professional conversations, deliver short presentations, and craft business messages that demonstrate both linguistic accuracy and intercultural sensitivity. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) ESP in business communication, intercultural competence, global English, collaborative learning, presentation skills, literature circle 指定用書 Textbooks No fixed textbook. Selected readings, case studies, and authentic materials will be provided weekly. Suggested readings may include excerpts from: Intercultural Business Communication (Chaney & Martin) The Culture Map (Meyer) Harvard Business Review articles on global leadership and communication 參考書籍 References N/A National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 教學方式 Teaching Approach This course adopts a task-based and intercultural learning approach combining theoretical insight and practical communication. Each week introduces a core topic linked to real-world business situations and global cultural dynamics. Students will work in small task forces to complete interactive assignments such as simulations, case discussions, role-plays, and mini-presentations. Authentic materials—video interviews, short case studies, advertisements, and cross-cultural incidents—are used to foster reflection and strategic language use. AI tools may be conditionally employed under instructor supervision for brainstorming, language polishing, and presentation rehearsal, with transparent acknowledgment of usage. Literature Circle is used to conduct class activities. Literature circles for English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners are small, student-led discussion groups that integrate theory from reader-response theory (emphasizing personal meaning-making) and sociocultural theory (focusing on social and collaborative learning). This approach enhances English-speaking skills, critical thinking, and literary analysis by providing a practical and communicative context for students to discuss texts in English. Key aspects include structured roles, collaborative learning, and the use of accessible reading materials, while teachers guide and support the process. Weekly Tasks & Reflections 25% Written or oral responses integrating business vocabulary and intercultural insights. AI-assisted reports and assignments are allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare for reports and assignments by brainstorming and tentative revision, but students must show how AI helps them reach the result. 僅限使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告之準備（如腦力激盪與初步修訂 等），學生須註明 AI 如何用於協作其作業或報告。 6. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number IPMT200100 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 50 中文名稱 Course Title 人力資源管理與應用心理學 英文名稱 Course English Title Applied Psychology in Human Resource Management 任課教師 Instructor Ari Chen 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information caoiaoi@gmail.com 上課時間 Time T5T6T7 上課教室 Room 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) - This course explores the integration of positive psychology principles into human resource management and addressing contemporary workplace challenges. Students will learn to implement evidence-based practices that create positive workplace climates, enhance employee engagement, and develop resilience. Topics include gratitude practices, mindfulness experiences, growth mindset cultivation, and effective communication. Blending theory with practical applications, the course equips future HR professionals with innovative strategies to foster workplace cultures where employees and organizations thrive, leading to enhanced productivity and long-term success. 課程目標 Course Objectives Incorporating applied positive psychology into human resource management courses represents an innovative practice that prepares students for the evolving demands of the business world. It equips them with the knowledge and tools to create thriving workplaces that contribute to long-term organizational success. By understanding and applying these principles, students can drive meaningful changes in their future careers, making them valuable assets to any organization. The course emphasizes creating a positive workplace climate, enhancing employee engagement, developing resilience, cultivating a growth mindset, improving communication, and establishing meaningful goals. By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. Integrate applied positive psychology principles to address key HR management. 2. Design and implement strategies to enhance employee engagement and well-being 3. Develop initiatives that build resilience and foster a growth mindset among employees. 4. Cultivate positive workplace relationships through effective communication. 5. Utilize strengths-based approaches in HR functions such as recruitment, development, and National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus performance management. 6. Evaluate the impact of applied positive psychology on organizational outcomes and effectiveness. 課程說明 Course Description In today's dynamic work environment, human resource management faces unprecedented challenges, including remote work, employee burnout, and disengagement. This course explores the integration of positive psychology principles into human resource management as a strategic imperative for organizations seeking to thrive in the 21st century. Students will gain knowledge and tools to implement evidence-based practices, positioning them at the forefront of a revolution in workplace culture and organizational effectiveness. The course emphasizes creating a positive workplace climate, expanding creative thinking through gratitude practices, enhancing employee engagement via flow experiences and mindfulness, developing resilience in the face of setbacks, cultivating a growth mindset for achievement, improving communication and conflict resolution to strengthen relationships, and establishing meaningful goals to promote thriving at work. This course equips students with the insights needed to lead employees and organizations toward greater well-being and productivity, aligning with modern HR practices that emphasize strengths-based approaches and positive organizational behavior. Through a blend of theoretical foundations and practical applications, students will gain the knowledge and tools to lead a revolution in workplace culture and organizational effectiveness. This course equips future HR professionals with innovative strategies to create environments where employees thrive, leading to enhanced productivity, creativity, and long- term organizational success. Key words: Human resource management, applied positive psychology, positive psychology, flourishing workplace, work performance, employee, gratitude, mindfulness, positive relationship, positive communication, growth mindset, resilience, meaningful, well-being. 指定用書 Textbooks Raymond A. Noe, John R. Hollenbeck, Barry Gerhart & Patrick M Wright (2022). Fundamentals of Human Resource Management (9th ed). McGraw Hill 參考書籍 References Sims, Ronald R. Sage Publications. Snyder, C. R., & Lopez, S. J. (Eds.). (2021). The Oxford handbook of positive psychology (3rd ed.). Oxford University Press. This handbook offers an extensive exploration of positive psychology concepts and applications, featuring contributions from leading experts in the field. Seligman, M. E. P. (2011). Flourish: A visionary new understanding of happiness and well-being. Free Press. In this book, Seligman expands on the principles of positive psychology and introduces the PERMA model for achieving well-being. Hefferon, K., & Boniwell, I. (2011). Positive psychology: Theory, research and applications. McGraw-Hill National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus Education. Joseph, S. (Ed.). (2015). Lectures and small & large discussion groups on key concepts 2. Case study analyses of organizations implementing positive psychology 3. Group projects designing positive psychology interventions for HR scenarios 4. Individual reflections on personal strengths and their application in HR roles 5. Guest speakers from organizations successfully implementing positive psychology 6. Role-playing exercises for positive coaching and communication 7. Practical assignments for implementing concepts in daily life 評分標準 Grading Individual Assessment ● Peer and Lecturer Review 10% ● Class Participation 10% ● Discussion 10% ● Anecdotal record 10% ● Midterm Individual Assignment 25% Group Assessments ● Case discussion 15% ● Final group project 20% 教學進度 Course Schedule Week 1: Course Orientation Week 2 Introduction to Human Resource Management and Workplace Flourishing Week 3: Cultivating a Positive Workplace Climate Week 4: Enhancing Employee Engagement and Performance Week 5: Promoting Sustainable Employee Growth Week 6: Positive Coaching for Performance Improvement Week 7: Building Resilience in the Workplace Week 8: Mid-term Assessment Week 9: Effective Communication and Conflict Resolution Week 10: Delivering Constructive Feedback Week 11: Building Strong Workplace Relationships Week 12: Recognizing Employee Contributions and Achievements Week 13: Retaining Employees Through Meaningful and Purpose Week 14: Guest Speaker: Practical Applications of Positive Psychology in HR Week 15: Recruitment and Selection through Strengths-Based Approaches Week 16: Final Project Presentation Classroom Conduct & Device Policy 1. Cell Phone & Laptop Policy • To maintain a focused and respectful learning environment, all mobile phones must be turned off or set to silent mode and stored out of sight during class. • Laptops or tablets may only be used for course-related purposes (e.g., note-taking, required online activities). • Using devices to scroll social media, watch videos, chat, or complete unrelated work is strictly prohibited. • If a student is observed repeatedly using devices for non-class purposes, it may result in a deduction from the Final Grade. 2. Respectful Learning Attitude • This course emphasizes professional attitude and mutual respect. Behaviors that disrupt your own learning or the learning of others will affect your final grade. These include: • Not paying attention during class (e.g., scrolling on your phone/laptop, chatting) National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus • Arriving more than 10 minutes late without valid reason • Leaving class early without notifying the instructor in advance • Displaying inappropriate, dismissive, or disrespectful attitudes • Such behaviors will result in a deduction from your Final Grade, proportional to the frequency and severity of the conduct. 3. Participation & Presence • Active engagement is essential to your learning and to the success of this course. Students are expected to: • Be present mentally and physically • Participate actively in discussions and activities • Treat peers and the instructor with courtesy and respect • Contribute positively to the classroom atmosphere Attendance policy: Students are allowed to have three absences (including sick leave, funeral leave, business leave, or any kind). Students will fail the course if more than THREE absences are recorded. Students should also come to class on time. Frequent late appearances will result in the deduction of points. Submission Guidelines: • All assignments must be submitted by the specified deadline. • Late submissions will incur penalties affecting the entire term paper segment of your grade. • The penalty structure is as follows: Up to 24 hours late: 10% deduction 24-48 hours late: 25% deduction Over 48 hours late: Not accepted, zero grade Exam and Assignment Policies: • Overdue assignments will not be accepted without a valid medical certificate. • The same policy applies to missed exams. • No make-up exams will be offered under any circumstances. Grade Appeals: • Students may appeal grades within 5 business days of receiving the graded work. • Appeals must be submitted in writing, clearly stating the reasons for the appeal. Remember, consistent attendance and timely submission of work are crucial for success in this course. If you anticipate any issues meeting these requirements, please communicate with the instructor as early as possible. Permitted Uses: • Brainstorming and idea generation • Proofreading and grammar checks National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus • Formatting assistance • Code debugging (for programming assignments) Restricted Uses: • Direct content generation for essays, reports, or presentations • Solving complex problems without showing your work • Generating entire code blocks for programming assignments Disclosure Requirements: • Students must disclose any use of generative AI tools in their assignments. • Include a brief statement at the end of each submission detailing: 1. The quality of human input and prompts 2. Critical analysis and refinement of AI-generated content 3. Integration of AI-generated ideas with original thought Academic Integrity: • Undisclosed use of generative AI will be treated as academic dishonesty. • Students are responsible for verifying the accuracy of AI-generated information.

The course uses clear, accessible language and avoids unnecessary jargon, and all students will be fully supported in engaging with the materials and discussions. 對英文不夠自信？請放心選課。課程使用清楚、易理解的語言，避免過度專業術語。提供課堂講義，小組討論亦可使用中文！ Course Description Artificial intelligence is reshaping workplaces while organizations face mounting pressure to demonstrate social responsibility and sustainable practices. This course equips you with critical skills to become a responsible manager who can navigate complex ethical dilemmas in modern organizations. You'll explore how organizational behavior principles intersect with responsible management, examining challenges in ESG implementation, stakeholder management, AI governance, and sustainable development goals (SDGs)—from ensuring algorithmic fairness to building inclusive cultures that balance profit with purpose. Through dynamic mini-lectures, case studies, field investigations, and hands-on projects— including producing your own podcast—you'll engage with pressing topics such as business ethics, corporate responsibility, responsible AI implementation, and sustainable organizational design. The course combines theoretical foundations with real-world applications, analyzing ethical failures and successful responsible management practices. You'll learn to recognize moral blind spots, manage stakeholder conflicts, and develop interventions that promote both organizational effectiveness and social good. Perfect for students aspiring to become responsible leaders in management, technology, or social impact roles, this course prepares you to champion ethical decision-making and sustainable practices in any organization. Through team projects, reflection reports, and interactions with industry speakers, you'll build a portfolio demonstrating your ability to integrate responsibility into core business operations—making you stand out to employers seeking leaders who can create value while contributing to a more equitable and sustainable future. Course Objectives: By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. Explain key concepts in organizational behavior across individual, group, and organizational levels. 2. Evaluate real-world organizational challenges through ESG (S＋G) and AI governance lenses. 3. Design and implement micro-actions that improve workplace fairness, well-being, communication, and team functioning. 4. Develop responsible leadership and decision-making strategies for organizations adopting AI. 5. Propose governance mechanisms that address transparency, accountability, and ethical issues in modern organizations. [Please respect intellectual property rights. (30%) 課程目標 Course Objectives ▪ 培養數據驅動的系統設計能力：引導同學以企業可取得的資料（含公開與模擬 資料）分析問題、拆解業務情境，並完成領域/情境拆解、Use Case、系統架 構、資訊架構與使用者流程等核心設計。 ▪ 完成解決方案原型：透過每週 Studio 練習和 Figma、Sketch、Miro 等工具，於 期末時整合成 Prototype 或 Mockup，完成具體的系統解決方案與操作邏輯。 課程說明 Course Description National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus ▪ 本課程聚焦「企業系統設計」與「數據驅動思考」，同學將學習如何將企業的資 料、流程與需求，轉化為具有商業價值的系統解決方案。 ▪ 學期將以小組為單位進行專案實作，每組選定一個企業或品牌，搜尋其可得之 資料（如行為資料、訂單資料、產品屬性、內容資料或營運流程，若難以找到 企業公開資料，可用 Kaggle 模擬資料或 Shopify/Google 等的 Sample Data），並 依據資料分析其業務問題和優化機會。在各週的 Studio 練習，同學會依序完成 領域/情境拆解、Use Case、系統架構、資訊架構與使用者流程等設計，期末時 將所有成果整合成 Prototype 或 Mockup，於期末報告呈現解決方案的核心功能 與操作邏輯。 ▪ 期末報告不要求繳交程式碼，而是強調系統思考、數據應用和推理，以及介面 呈現邏輯，並鼓勵使用 Figma/Adobe XD/Sketch/Miro/Mockplus 等工具進行資料 流、架構圖、流程圖、Prototype 和 Mockup 的製作。 ▪ 課程結束後，同學將具備將資料與流程轉化為具體系統解決方案的能力，並可 將成果作為未來作品集的一部份。 課程關鍵字 Course Keywords 商業系統設計, 敏捷開發實踐, 資料流, 系統流程設計, 數據驅動應用 指定用書 Textbooks 參考書籍 References ▪ Torres, T. Kogan Page. ▪ Huyen, C. (2022). Designing Machine Learning Systems: An Iterative Process for Production-Ready Applications. O’Reilly Media. ▪ Knapp, J., Zeratsky, J., & Kowitz, B. (2016). Sprint: How to Solve Big Problems and Test New Ideas in Just Five Days. Bantam Press. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 教學方式 Teaching Approach ▪ 本課程結合授課、Studio 練習，以及專案實作。學生將以小組為單位，逐步完成 企業級系統解決方案並於期末發表。 ▪ 每週約 1.5 小時授課，介紹系統設計的核心概念與方法，包括數據驅動推理、領 域/情境拆解（Domain Mapping）、Use Case 設計、系統架構、資訊架構、使用者 流程、原型設計等。授課內容會與後面 1 小時的操作練習內容相關。 ▪ 每週最後１小時（第 3–14 週）安排分組 Studio 練習。學生將依照當週主題進行 系統設計任務，例如：資料流設計和繪圖、拆解企業的各領域（例如會員管理、 產品管理、訂單管理、庫存管理、物流…）與情境、撰寫 Use Case、規劃系統流 程、使用者流程、繪製 Storyboard、最後製作 Prototype 或 Mockup 等。Studio 目 的在於授課後即時練習，並將練習結果進行分享、確認方向。 ▪ 各組將在期末週進行成果發表，報告形式請參考課程說明。 評分標準 Grading ▪ 課程參與: 30% ▪ Studio 練習與簡報: 30% docs.name: 巨量資料分析與機器學習
docs.nameEn: Big Data Analytics and Machine Learning
docs.text: 1 IPMT301000 巨量資料分析與機器學習 國立清華大學科技管理學院學士班 Big Data Analytics and Machine Learning (Spring 2026) Interdisciplinary Program of Management and Technology (IPMT) College of Management and Technology National Tsing Hua University 教師：郭孟倫 (Tonny Menglun Kuo) 助理教授 Email：tonny@gapp.nthu.edu.tw 助教：羅筱淳(la112070009@gapp.nthu.edu.tw) 教室：台積 203（人限 40 人） 課程時間：Thursday, 14:20-17:20 R6R7R8 課程網站：eeclass Office hour： By Email 學分數：3 學分 先修建議：建議先修統計學一或機率與統計。即便不具備程式或資料分析背景也可修讀，但需願意學習寫程式。我們會 在課堂上逐步教授初階資料分析程式撰寫技巧。本課程並非設計讓學生掌握機器學習的方法論，而是強調學生如何在小 組實作中能夠掌握資料分析專案的特點，學會實用且帶得走的經驗。 課程簡介 領會過統計的魅力，卻不知如何應用在職場、研究與生活中？資料如何以視覺化方法呈現，有哪些操作秘 訣？機器學習(資料探勘)有哪些不同種類，該如何評估預測的結果呢？掌握資料驅動/知會決策(data- driven/informed decision)對於管理領域的相關實務(如：人力資源、營運與行銷)有哪些幫助？本課程旨在讓學生 運用統計及機器學習來解決複雜多變的研究及實務問題，同學能夠在課堂當中實務操作並依照分析目標及利害 關係人選用正確的機器學習方法與評估模式。本課程強調解構問題、資料間的關係以及動手實作，學生會學到 兩套統計軟體基本功能（R 語言與 Tableau），將數據科學應用在人力資源、營運、行銷與組織管理上。 本門課程共三部分：(一)資料分析基礎：逐步講授與實作練習來學習 R 語言的基礎與特性、資料特性與資 料轉換、基礎畫圖與視覺化。幫同學打下資料分析的基礎，有助於同學運用進階方法在課程當中；(二)機器學習 基本方法與應用，包含機器學習歷程、維度縮減、多元線性迴歸、評估預測效果、KNN、分類與迴歸樹、神經 網絡等方法。同學需了解這些基本方法背後的邏輯，嘗試在動手實作當中找出問題並討論；(三)期末專題：由同 學組成小組來針對一套或多套資料以專題導向學習方式分析，同學需運用本課程學會的方法，並依照不同利害 關係人來做出相關的分析結果與行動策略。 本課程主要透過微型講授、練習、小組討論、分組報告、個別作業等多種方式進行。本課程將會使用兩套 資料探勘/機器學習軟體：R 語言與 Tableau。學生將可熟悉相關機器學習分析技術的基礎套件（package），分 析、操作並解讀資料探勘的結果。需特別注意的是：學生不僅需要報告資料探勘的結果，且需在本課程的要求 與規範下學會將機器學習分析的報告轉化為業界及公部門容易理解的語言（實務摘要與行動方案）。學完這門課 程後，同學將能夠分析研究問題所需要的統計模型、運用統計軟體呈現量化資料結果，有助於未來在畢業專題 （Senior Project）、產業實習、或實際工作場中以有效率的方式分析統計資料。 課程目標 1. 選用正確的統計模型來描述、解釋或預測資料並回答研究問題。 2. 應用 R 語言進行巨量資料探勘，掌握統計資料的分佈與特性。 3. 解讀不同利害關係人的立場跟預期，將資料探勘的結果轉譯為可供參照的簡報、實務 摘要與行動方案。 4. 運用生成式 AI 工具（如 Julius.ai、ChatGPT）輔助資料分析，理解 AI 輔助決策的能力與限制。 5. 辨識 AI 系統中的偏見、公平性與隱私議題，以負責任的態度設計與評估 AI 應用方案。 6. 理解企業 AI 策略的基本框架，評估組織導入 AI 的成熟度與實施路徑。 7. 與不同背景的同儕合作，在專案中學習如何與跨領域成員溝通。 本課程為管理(第一專長)選修並支援人力資源管理學程 修過這堂課後，管理專長與人管學程學生可發展資料驅動決策的人才管理概念，了解 People analytics 與 HR analytics 中強調的流程優化與預測性人才分析。以下是未來可以運用到人力資源相關工作的實際應用案例： 2 1. 人力規劃分析 (Workforce Planning Analytics) ² 預測性分析：運用多元迴歸、時間序列預測未來人力需求 ² 維度縮減（PCA）：分析影響人力配置的關鍵因素 ² 資料視覺化（Tableau）：建立人力結構儀表板，追蹤編制變化 ² 實務案例：如 NASA 運用知識圖譜（knowledge graphs）追蹤員工技能、專案與訓練的關聯 2. 績效管理分析 (Performance Management Analytics) ² 多元迴歸分析：找出影響績效的關鍵變數 ² 分群分析：識別高績效者與低績效者的特徵模式 ² 支持向量機（SVM）：建立績效分類模型 ² 實務案例：Google 的 People Innovation Lab 運用跨功能數據分析，找出優秀管理者與高效團隊的特質 3. 留任與離職分析 (Retention & Attrition Analytics) ² 預測性分析：運用機器學習（隨機森林、神經網絡）預測離職風險 ² 早期離職分析：分析新進員工第一年內離職率 ² 離職成本計算：量化人員流動對組織的財務影響 ² 實務案例：IBM 運用 AI 和 People Analytics，能以 95%準確率預測哪些員工即將離職 課程進度表（課表為預排參考，授課教師有權依進度及學生程度滾動調整內容） 日期 週次 主題 作業 /備註 1 課程概述與 AI 時代的資料科學 基本概念、術語、R 語言的歷史、R 操作環境介紹與 Python 差異 AI Today：目前生成式 AI 前景、LLM 運作原理概覽 課堂示範：用 ChatGPT/Julius.ai 輔助資料分析初體驗 作業 1：R 環境建置 2 R 語言基礎(I) 操作介面、變量、資料型態(data type, levels, vector), date, and time, factor, table, string 作業 2：大數據分組報告 3 R 語言基礎(II) matrix, list, array, data frame, read.csv, read_delim, fread, fromJSON, apply function, merging, cbind, rbind 用 GenAI 輔助 Debug：示範如何用 AI 工具解決 R 程式錯誤 作業 3：Swirl R programing 課程 1-5 4 資料轉換、畫圖與相關分析 dplyr (e.g., selecting, appending, sorting, sampling, filtering, pivoting) types of plots, cor, cor.test Basic plots: scatterplot, histograms, boxplot, density plot ggplot2, cor v.s. cov Julius.ai 實作：自然語言指令產生視覺化圖表 作業 4：Swirl R programing 單元 7, 10-11 5 資料視覺化與因果推論簡介 資料類型/描述性分析 Tableau 軟體簡介與操作 因果推論(Causal Inference)概念：相關≠因果 觀察研究 vs.實驗設計、A/B Testing 概念 作業 5：Swirl R programing 單元 15 6 基礎機器學習方法 分類、預測、關聯與推薦、維度縮減、資料探索與視覺化 資料分割：檢視、分割、抽樣 作業 6：Tableau 資料視 覺化 7 機器學習歷程 研究目標與機器學習目標 處理極端值、過度擬和（overfitting） 資料不平衡處理（Class Imbalance: oversampling / undersampling） 8 多元線性迴歸 解釋性 v.s. 預測性迴歸 適配度、多元共線性、非常態資料 AI 輔助迴歸分析：執行迴歸分析並解讀結果 作業 7 9 維度縮減、模型偏誤與 Responsible AI Dimensionality, aggregation, pivot table, correlation analysis, PCA for classification and prediction) 作業 8 3 日期 週次 主題 作業 /備註 主成分分析（PCA） 案例：Amazon 的 AI Recruiter 偏好男性候選人 Responsible AI 框架：Bias, Fairness, Privacy and Data Governance 案例討論：Moderna 的 AI 部署與倫理考量 10 書報討論與業界應用：AI 工廠與企業 AI 策略 書報討論：Human + Machine / Competing in the Age of AI AI Factory 概念：企業如何建構、擴展與管理 AI 系統 行銷應用（顧客分群、churn prediction） 營運應用（需求預測、排程） 人資應用（招募、績效預測） 企業 AI 成熟度評估框架 11 期中報告 小組概念發想提案、期末評量尺規 資料來源、機器學習目的、潛在效果 期末專題選項 B 說明：AI Agent 專題 作業 9 12 K-Nearest-Neighbor (KNN)與特徵工程 Euclidean distance, Choosing k, Using K-NN for Prediction Feature Engineering (Scaling: Normalization vs Standardization; Handling Missing Data; Feature Importance) 小組個別討論(I) 13 分類與迴歸樹 切割方法 測量不純度（Impurity）：Gini Index、Entropy Regression Trees Random Forests and Boosted Trees 小組個別討論(II) 14 支持向量機 (SVMs) 與 GenAI 應用工作坊 Support Vector Machines Maximum Margin Hyperplane, Kernel Trick GenAI 工作坊：Prompt Engineering for Data Analysis 用 LLM 自動化資料前處理與特徵工程 作業 10 小組個別討論(III) 15 神經網絡與大型語言模型 Input, hidden, and output layers Weights, Specify Network Architecture, Overfitting Neural Nets vs Deep Learning 從 Neural Nets 到 LLM：Transformer 架構概念 LLM 在商業分析中的前瞻應用 16 期末分組口頭報告 建議與修正, 利害關係人行動策略, 繳交期末報告 選項 A：運用 R 語言對一套或多套資料進行機器學習分析，產出 利害關係人行動策略報告 選項 B：AI Agent Demo 展示 docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 60 中文名稱 Course Title 企業倫理與永續 英文名稱 Course English Title Business Ethics and Sustanability 任課教師 Instructor 洪華薇 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information hwhung@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time 上課教室 Room 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives With the setting of SDGs (sustainable development goals) by the United Nations General Assembly in 2015, corporations have been motivated to change the way they operate their businesses, and have started to emphasize their contributions towards a better society and the environment. Along with the global announcement of the ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) trend, hybrid business organizations are an emerging phenomenon that adopts market strategies to solve social and environmental issues. Social innovation has increasingly attracted academic and practical attention for its contribution to global sustainability. Various innovative collaboration and business models have been constructed to deliver social and business value. One of the key trends in the fast development of social innovation worldwide has been the rise of the third sector and hybrid organizations such as social enterprises. 課程目標 Course Objectives This course is designed for undergraduates who find interest in ESG and social innovation issues and, would like to extend their understanding with in-depth study of related concepts (ESG, CSR, social innovation, social enterprise, Benefit corporation, net zero carbon emission). Also, this course is expected to provide basic guidance for those who consider a sustainability-related job position as their potential future career. This course aims to introduce students to the concepts, theories, tools, and insights necessary for sustainability construction, social innovation, and social entrepreneurship. By the end of this course, students should be able to: 1) Elaborate on the nature of ESG-related concepts and topics 2) Understand the international standard and legitimacy of global ESG construction 3) Provide examples of the international/local management practices of ESG 4) Explain how globalization/localization features (dis) empower ESG 5) Illustrate how social innovation is being constructed through social entrepreneurship 6) Outline the relationship between social innovation and ESG 7) Present basic ideas of social innovation practice through fieldworks 課程說明 Course Description National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus In the wake of the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the global rise of ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) frameworks, corporations and hybrid organizations are rethinking their roles in society. This course explores how businesses can serve as catalysts for social and environmental innovation while maintaining economic value. Designed for undergraduate students with an interest in sustainability, social innovation, and responsible business, this course introduces the theoretical foundations and practical applications of ESG, CSR, social enterprises, and benefit corporations. Through case discussions, lectures, fieldwork, and project-based learning, students will gain insight into sustainable business models and the growing intersection between private enterprise and public good. By the end of the course, students will be able to critically analyze ESG strategies, evaluate social innovation practices, understand global standards, and propose actionable solutions for sustainable transformation in various industries. This course also serves as a foundational experience for those considering careers in ESG, corporate responsibility, or social entrepreneurship. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗 點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) ESG, Corporate social responsibility, social innovation, sustainability, social entrepreneurship 指定用書 Textbooks N/A 參考書籍 References 01) Elkington, J. (2020) Green Swans: The Coming Boom In Regenerative Capitalism. Greenleaf Book Group. 02) Berners-Lee, M. (2021). There Is No Planet B: A Handbook for the Make Or Break Years-Updated Edition. Cambridge University Press. 03) Figueres, C., & Rivett-Carnac, T. (2020). The Future We Choose: Surviving the Climate Crisis. Knopf Doubleday Publishing Group. 04) Edmans, A. (2021). Grow the pie: How great companies deliver both purpose and profit– updated and revised. Cambridge University Press. 05) Eagan, G. (2014). Wear no evil: How to change the world with your wardrobe. Running Press Adult. 06) Berners-Lee, M. (2020). How bad are bananas?: the carbon footprint of everything. Profile Books. 07) McDonough, W., & Braungart, M. (2010). Cradle to cradle: Remaking the way we make things. North point press. 08) McDonough, W., & Braungart, M. (2013). The upcycle: Beyond sustainability--designing for abundance. Macmillan. 09) Banerjee, S., Carney, S., & Hulgard, L. (Eds.). (2019). People-Centered Social Innovation: Global Perspectives on an Emerging Paradigm. Routledge. 10) Andersen, L. L., Gawell, M., & Spear, R. (2016). Social entrepreneurship and social enterprises in the Nordics. Routledge. 教學方式 Teaching Approach National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus Class sessions may include lectures, and small and large discussion groups. We will strive to clarify, supplement, and analyze text materials. You are responsible for all assigned readings and all materials presented in class. You are also responsible for all information disseminated in class and all course requirements, including deadlines. Lectures: Each lecture is 1.5 hours. Please note that all lectures will be taught in English. • The lecture will be delivered in a highly interactive way, speak-up and idea- sharing/discussion is always welcoming through lecturing, which is also counted as class participation. Case Discussion (60 minutes): • Case presentation (40 minutes): One group will be assigned a case to present in class, which should include the content and solution of a specific managerial situation in sustainability development. Each group will need to introduce the topic and address the discussion issue accordingly. • Case discussion (20 minutes): The discussion is open to the audience, adding up valuable comments, insight, debate, and discussion that help deepen the understanding of the case. Midterm Essay: • 5-10 pages of English essay including (1) social issue, (2) social enterprise ideas, (3) product/services, (4) sustainable business model, (5) resources required (6) potential social benefit (7) reference list (APA form) • 12 font Times New Roman, 1/-1.5 leading, PDF file • No plagiarism; shall also attach with the Turnitin report (acceptable similarity percentage: below 15%) (please register in advance through NTHU Library: https://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412- 1319-7120.php?Lang=en) • Conditional accept AI only when AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading Final Project: • Choose one industry, and select one representative company to present (in a group base): ■ Fashion Industry (Clothing, Cosmetics) ■ Entertainment Industry (Gaming, theme park, film, music) ■ Steel and Iron Industry ■ Semiconductor Industry ■ Agriculture & Food Industry ■ Digital Technology Industry ■ Retailing Industry (E-commerce) ■ Education Industry National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus ■ Others (e.g. Architecture) Final project initiation: 15-minute to 20 min presentation to introduce stages 1 & 2 (as below) Final project presentation: 20-minute well-organized presentation introducing stages 3 & 4 (as below) • Could be better to propose 1-2 existing interdisciplinary high-tech examples that is possible to be adopted for sustainable transformation in the selected company Project When to present Study Target Insights and Discussion Stage 1 Project initiation Identify Risk & Responsibility • Identify stakeholders • Identify the company’s main products/services, and how it earns money (business model) • Determine potential harm to the environment, society, and economy • Develop Materiality Matrix Stage 2 Project initiation Develop sustainable strategy • Align with international standards • Set up short-term goals & long-term goals • What could be improved in current business operations? (products/services) Stage 3 Final presentation Breakdown strategy into doable items • How is each department supporting /involved in the change of business operation? • Explain how each department (R&D, manufacturing, marketing, human resources, finance) could be improved Stage 4 Final presentation Adapt from existing solution • How the interdisciplinary high tech could help products/ services improve? • Reference existing cases and introduce it • Clarify the potential risk and contribution to sustainability. 評分標準 Grading Class Participation 15% Case Discussion 15% Midterm Individual Essay 25% Project Initiation 20% Final Project Presentation 25% 教學進度 Course Schedule Week Case Discussion Lecture 1 Course Briefing (Kick-off, Self-intro Card) 2 Globalization and Sustainability Trend (SDGs, Mega forces) 3 Team-up & Case Guidance Social Enterprise and Social National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus Entrepreneurship 4 Midterm Guidance Social Enterprise and Sustainability Business Model 5 Case 1 Local Social Innovation Practice (CSSP) 6 Guest Speech (No-class, roll call) 7 Midterm Individual Essay 8 Case 2 Business ethics, Corporate Social Responsibility, and CSR Reporting 9 Case 3 ESG and Sustainable supply chain (Carbon Trading) 10 Final Project Initiation Week 11 Case 4 Sustainability Practice in Business (Beverage Industry) & Final Guidance 12 Social Entrepreneurs Award High-Tech in Sustainability 13 Final project initiation 1 & 2 Circular Economy Practice 14 Final project initiation 3 & 4 Benefit Corporation, Future Career Training for Sustainability (Entrepreneur Support, Job Position, Certification, Practical skill) 15 Activity: How to make Christmas Sustainable? (self-contribution, plan, department/ E-commerce shop) 16 Final Project Presentation (Discussion, Future for ESG, Wrap-up) 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) (1)完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required R(2)有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (3)禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4)本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 課程相關連接 Course Related Links

docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number IPMT301500 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 50 中文名稱 Course Title 策略管理導論 英文名稱 Course English Title Introduction to Strategic Management 任課教師 Instructor 洪華薇 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information hwhung@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time R5R6R7 上課教室 Room 台積館 121 教室 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives This course is designed to cultivate students’ ability to think critically and strategically about how firms create, capture, and sustain competitive advantage. The overarching learning goal is to equip students with a solid foundation in strategic management theories and frameworks while also developing the analytical and problem-solving skills necessary for real-world business contexts. By the end of the semester, students will be able to identify and analyze the external and internal factors that influence organizational strategy. They will learn to apply key frameworks such as Porter’s Five Forces to evaluate industries and firms. Students will also be able to assess the merits of different business-level and corporate-level strategies, ranging from cost leadership and differentiation to diversification and international expansion. In addition to developing conceptual understanding, students will practice applying theory to practice through case discussions, group presentations, and the final project. These assignments are designed to strengthen their ability to conduct evidence-based analysis, craft strategic recommendations, and communicate ideas effectively. Furthermore, the course emphasizes ethical and responsible management by integrating topics such as corporate social responsibility, sustainability, and crisis management. 課程目標 Course Objectives By the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Understand core theories and frameworks of strategic management. 2. Analyze firms’ external and internal environments. 3. Formulate and evaluate competitive strategies. 4. Understand corporate-level decisions such as diversification, alliances, and international expansion. 5. Apply strategic thinking through case studies, group projects, and presentations. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 課程說明 Course Description Lectures: Each lecture is 1.5 hour. Please note, all lectures will be taught in English. • The lecture will be delivered in a highly-interactive way, speak-up and idea- sharing/discussion is always welcoming through lecturing, which is also counted as class participation. Case Review (40 minutes): • Case review sharing (35 minutes): Each group will be assigned to review one Case in the beginning of the course, and share their review with the class during the discussion session in turn. Each group will finished reading the Case and will present feedback upon to the class, consisting summaries, key indications, managerial inspiration and/or any other issues that you want to share with the class. • Q&A (5 minutes): Other groups need to prepare at least three questions to discuss with the presenting group. Final Group Presentation (30 minutes): • For the final project, each group will select a company or organization of their choice and conduct a comprehensive strategic analysis. Students are expected to identify and examine the key strategic challenges that the chosen company is currently facing. To support their analysis, groups should draw on multiple sources of evidence, including secondary data (such as company reports, news articles, or industry analyses), interviews with relevant stakeholders, or direct field observations where feasible. • The objective of this project is to give students the opportunity to apply the theories, concepts, and analytical tools learned throughout the course to a real-world context. Each group will synthesize their findings into a coherent and insightful strategic assessment, demonstrating both critical thinking and practical application. The project will culminate in a group presentation of approximately 30 minutes during the final weeks of the semester, where students will present their analysis and proposed recommendations to the class. Final Group Essay: • In addition to an oral presentation, a printed paper report must also be submitted. This report will put your presentation into words, and should be between 8-14 pages. • If AI is utilized, screenshots of conversations with the AI must be included. • APA format: 12 font Times New Roman, 1/1.5 leading, PDF file. • No plagiarism; shall also attach with the Turnitin report (acceptable similarity percentage: below 15%) (please register in advance through NTHU Library: https://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1319-7120.php?Lang=en) • Conditional accept: AI only when AI screenshot report is attached, which will also affect the grading. 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗 點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Strategic management, positioning, entrepreneurship, red ocean/blue ocean, sustainability 指定用書 TextCases None 參考書籍 References Case, J. docs.text: National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 科號 Course Number 11420IPMT3016 00 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Size of Limit 50 中文名稱 Course Title 專案管理：引導智慧與數位轉型 英文名稱 Course English Title Project Management: Leading Smart and Digital Transformation 任課教師 Instructor 賴怡君 教師聯絡方式 Contact Information Email: lai-ic@mx.nthu.edu.tw 上課時間 Time T5T6T7 上課教室 Room TBC 先修科目 Prerequisite(s) 無 本課程對應之學習目標與核心能力 Aligned Learning Goals and Learning Objectives ▪ 運用專業管理與科技知識的能力。(35%) Our students will master the knowledge of technology and professional management. (35%) ▪ 整合與活用第一專長及第二專長的專業知識能力，並具備跨領域規劃、領導與 執行團隊合作的能力。 (35%) Our students will be able to integrate expertise from their double specialty and thus plan, execute and lead in an interdisciplinary team setting. (35%) ▪ 具備中文及英文閱讀寫作商業報告與商業口頭簡報能力。 (30%) Our students will be able to read and produce professional business documents as well as deliver a professional oral presentation in English and in Chinese. (30%) 課程目標 Course Objectives ▪ Equip students with the capability to plan and lead smart and digital transformation projects, integrating technical architecture, process redesign, organizational alignment, and governance into a coherent project roadmap. ▪ Strengthen students’ ability to collaborate in cross-functional project teams, applying agile and DevOps principles to structure complex projects and ensure effective delivery. ▪ Enable students to complete a full smart or digital transformation project as a team and include the final project in their professional portfolio to enrich their project experience and demonstrate their development in digital transformation planning. 課程說明 Course Description ▪ Students will work in teams to select a real-world company, brand, or organization and assess its digital or operational pain points, identifying opportunities for smart or digital transformation. ▪ Each team will develop a complete transformation roadmap that includes current- state analysis, proposed system architecture, redesigned processes, a phased transformation roadmap, plans for governance, risk, and stakeholder management, as well as an evaluation of the expected benefits after the transformation. ▪ The final project output could be compiled into students’ professional portfolio piece, National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus demonstrating students’ ability to design structured, actionable, and organization- aware digital transformation strategies. 課程關鍵字 Course Keywords Digital Transformation Projects, Agile Practices, Project Roadmap, Cross-Functional Collaboration, Organizational Change & Governance 指定用書 Textbooks 參考書籍 References ▪ Greenway, A., Terrett, B. (2018). Digital transformation at scale: Why the strategy is delivery. London Publishing Partnership. ▪ Iansiti, M., & Lakhani, K. R. (2020). Competing in the age of AI: Strategy and leadership when algorithms and networks run the world. Harvard Business Review Press. ▪ Peters, L. J. (2024). Software project management: Methods and techniques. Prentice Hall. ▪ Müller, R., & Turner, J. R. (2010). Project-oriented leadership. Gower Publishing. ▪ Tidd, J., & Bessant, J. (2020). Managing innovation: Integrating technological, market and organizational change (7th ed.). Wiley. ▪ Tucker, D., Cirella, S., & Kelly, P. (2024). Organizational change management: Inclusion, collaboration and digital change in practice. SAGE Publications. ▪ Forsgren, N., Humble, J., & Kim, G. (2018). Accelerate: The science of lean software and DevOps: Building and Scaling High Performing Technology Organizations. IT Revolution Press. ▪ Kim, G., Humble, J., Debois, P., & Willis, J. (2016). The DevOps handbook: How to create world-class agility, reliability, & security in technology organizations. IT Revolution. National Tsing Hua University College of Technology Management Course Syllabus 教學方式 Teaching Approach ▪ The course combines lectures, case discussions, and project work, in which students will plan a smart or digital transformation project and present their work at the end of the semester. ▪ Lectures: Each week includes approximately 1.5 hours of lectures covering the core concepts, frameworks, and practices of smart and digital transformation. The lectures build foundational knowledge in system integration, process redesign, organizational alignment, and project management methods relevant to transformation initiatives. ▪ Case Discussions: The final hour of each weekly session (Weeks 3–14) will be used for group-based case discussions. One group will serve as the leading group each week. Case materials will be distributed one week in advance, and the leading group is responsible for guiding the class through the case context, facilitating discussion, and synthesizing key insights. docs.text: Prof. Yen-Chieh Huang ext. 62340 Institute of Photonics Tech./Dept of Electrical Engineering office: HOPE Lab 301/Delta 856 National Tsing-Hua University email: ychuang@ee.nthu.edu.tw Hsinchu, Taiwan 300 IPT5110 Spring, 2026 __________________________________________________________________________________ 1 Last update Feb. 23rd, 2026 IPT5110 Nonlinear Optics Spring, 2026 國立清華大學 光電光程研究所/電機工程學系 Prof. 黃衍介 class schedule: M7M8W6 Class location: Delta 212 TA: TBD, email: TBS 一、課程說明 The scope of this course covers most nonlinear optical phenomena associated with the 2nd and 3rd order optical nonlinearities, including electro-optic modulation, harmonic generation, parametric generation, Brillouin scattering, Raman scattering, optical Kerr effects etc. Near the end of the semester, high harmonic generation and plasma nonlinearity in the relativistic regime will also be introduced. To assist learning, this course begins with a review on the linear electromagnetic theory and then gradually moves into the nonlinear regime. This approach is to accommodate more and more undergraduate students taking this course. Student’s participation plays a key role in this course. All students are required to give a few presentations to earn their grades during the whole semester. 二 指定用書 1. (1) My slides are available on the course website for preparing your homework. (2) Each week, each student in a study group is required to expand my slides in synch with the course progress below. Write your name on the slide pages (3) Email the slide file by 10 am each Monday to Prof. Huang at ychuang@ee.nthu.edu.tw before the class. The file size can’t exceed 1 Mb. (4) Each student has to bring a memory stick to the class and get ready for a presentation. Presentation In each class, I will draw students, each giving a presentation and hosting a Q&A session for the scheduled course materials. Exams There will be quiz, two mid-term exams, and a final exam. All exams are open-book/notes. Details of the exams will be announced later. 五、教學進度 1. Electromagnetic waves in the linear regime (D. docs.text: IPT 514300 Digital Optics Laboratory Objectives: This Course will introduce classical optics in a graduate level. The theories of geometry optics, diffraction, liquid-crystal optics and Fourier Optics will be systematically present. With these basic understandings, students then will get hand-on experience on operating the spatial light modulators (SLM) and developing diverse digital optical systems. Instructor: Chang-Hua Liu Prerequisites: Optics, Electromagnetic theory or Graduate standing Office hours: by appointment (send me an email: chliu@ee.nthu.edu.tw) Textbook: None required. I will post the lecture notes. Supplementary References: E. Hecht, Optics (Addison Wesley) A. Yariv, P. Yeh, Optical waves in Crystals (Wiley) Grades: Homework: 15% Mid-term exam: 25% Labs: 40% Final exam: 20% Course Outline: Lectures will cover the following topics: - Lenses and image formation - ABCD matrices of optical elements and imaging systems - Aberrations - Optical waves in anisotropic dielectric medium (vector nature of waves, representations of a polarization state, Birefringence, Jones calculus and its applications) - Fraunhofer diffraction (Rectangular & circular apertures, Arrays of apertures & diffraction gratings, Fresnel lens, Fourier transformation by a lens) Laboratories (using SLM to realize the following experiments): - Amplitude and phase modulation - Wavefront modulation and control - Diffraction and interference - Fourier optics (dispersion and optical signal processing) - Fourier optics (talbot image and phase shift digital holography) - Field programmable lens

docs.name: 半導體光電量子特性
docs.text: 111 10IPT 692000 課程綱要表 課程名稱 (中文) 半導體光電量子特性 (英文) Quantum Properties of Semiconductor Optoelectronics 開課單位 電機系 授課教師 李依珊 課程代碼 IPT 6920 選課性質 ⎕必修■選修 學分數 3 開課年級 碩博 先修科目或先備能力 固態物理、量子力學導論 課程概述 本課程以微觀與介觀物理解釋半導體光電元件的量子特性。在充分習得了量子力 學後，可用單粒子狀態計算出半導體能帶結構以及光物質作用。課程亦提供數個 專題以啟發學生學以致用，包含低維結構基本理論與其應用、共振腔量子電動力 學以及光偵測技術。 The course provides the essential knowledge to understand the quantum properties of semiconductor optoelectronics at microscopic and mesoscopic levels. After a comprehensive review of quantum mechanics, formulations of electronic band structures and light-matter interactions will be derived in the framework of single-particle state. Some special topics shall be selected for inspiring discussions at the end of this class, including the theory and practice of low-dimensional structures, cavity quantum electrodynamics and light detection. 課程目標 學生習得低維奈米結構的物理，清楚在奈米結構中因量子效應可徹底改變半導體 材料性質，進一步結合各式新穎奈米元件的操作概念，期能啟發學生之創新應用 能力。 Students shall learn the theoretical and practical aspects of low-dimensional structures and gain the knowledge of quantized effects. After establishing the knowledge of novel optoelectronic devices, students can get inspired and are creative in thinking. 教科書 自編教材 參考書 1. Quantum Mechanics for Scientists and Engineers, D. A. B. Miller (2008) 2. Physics of Photonic Devices, S. L. Chuang (2009) 3. Quantum Theory of the Optical and Electronic Properties of Semiconductors, H. Haug and S. W. Koch (2009) 4. Quantum Optics, Y. Yamamoto (APPPHYS 387, Stanford University) 5. Mesoscopic Physics, Y. Yamamoto (APPPHYS 388, Stanford University) 6. Semiconductor quantum dots: physics, spectroscopy, and applications, Springer Y. Masumoto, T. Takagahara (2002) 教學要點概述 講義編選 自己編寫 教學方法 ☑講授 ☑學生上台報告 ☑討論互動 評量方式 期中與期末報告 Reading assignment and report 70% 出席與小考 Attendance and Quiz 30% 課程綱要 單元主題 單元綱要 Basic Quantum Mechanics Schrodinger Equation The square well The harmonic oscillator Perturbation theory Hydrogen atom and exciton in 2D and 3D Electronic Band Structures Bloch theorem and 𝑘∙𝑝 method Kane’s model for band structure Luttinger-Kohn Hamiltonian –degenerate valence bands Effective mass theory Pikus-Bur Hamiltonian –strain effect Band structures of confined system Light-Matter Interactions Interband transition via Fermi's golden rule Einstein's A and B coefficients Absorption, gain, and spontaneous emission spectrum General absorption due to electron-hole pair & exciton effect Fully-quantized theory of absorption and emission Coherent regime: optical Stark shift & optical Bloch equations Special Topic I: Low Dimensional System Electronic, optical and magnetic properties of quantum dots Single quantum dot Special Topic II: Semiconductor Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian Weak coupling regime and Purcell effect Strong coupling regime and Rabi splitting/oscillation Thresholdless photon laser Quantum dot in microcavity Special Topic III: Light Detection Photodetector Avalanche photodiodes Quantum dot infrared detector 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明：禁止使用 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當 中。因本課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，以下為相關的監管機制 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個人心 得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 25 (手動加簽 15 人) 中文名稱 Course Title 以證據為基礎的設計思考 英文名稱 Course English Title Evidence-Based Design Thinking 任課教師 Instructor 常善媚 上課時間 Time 每週二，第 7, 8, 9 堂 上課教室 Room 教育館 101 教室 Course Description(課程簡述) The course is a part of creativity exploration courses for freshman and aims to take students to start from local social issues and finish exploration activities design thinking requires and proposal training. We will choose items from Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), Child Welfare and Rural Education, and lead students with different expertise to apply design thinking and practice finding evidence in academic research, field observation and personal experiences. Also, this course will train students to find needs and make a proposal with creativity while cultivating student groups with leadership and innovation. 本課程為大一創意探索課程。目標帶領學生從在地社會議題出發，完成設計思考之需 求探索活動與計劃書提案訓練。本學期課程將選定永續發展目標(SDGs)中的「兒童健 康福祉(SDG3)」、「偏鄉教育(SDG4)」為主題，引導不同專長之學生團隊以設計思考為 工具，並練習於學術研究、田野觀察、與自我經驗之間尋找證據，進行需求洞察與創 2 意發想提案，培育具領導力與創新力的學生團隊。 Course Objectives (課程目標) By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. Understand the historical origin and main concepts of design thinking 2. Apply design thinking to explore and empathize with the interested target objects 3. Learn to track the origins of different evidence and distinguish between them 4. Use triangulation and speculation based on evidence with different origins 5. Conduct design thinking and problem solution based on existing evidence 6. Collect evidence and come up creatively with solutions based on it 1. 了解設計思考的歷史緣由與主要概念 2. 運用設計思考進行有興趣的目標對象的探索與同理 3. 了解不同證據的區別與來源 4. 能正確運用不同來源的證據進行三角檢證與思辯 5. 能倚賴現有證據進行設計思考與問題解決 6. 能蒐集並運用證據進行創意發想待解決的問題 Core capability to be cultivated by this course (欲培養之核心能力) 1. 創新與領導能力（To innovate and lead） 2. 跨領域能力（To cross disciplinary boundaries） 3. 生活實踐能力（To practice） 4. 社會變遷因應能力（To adapt to social change） 5. 慎思明辨能力（To think critically） Course Content(課程內容) ● Course keywords (關鍵字) 3 Design Thinking, Evidence-Based, Innovation, Problem Solving, Good Health and Wellbeing, Quality Education 設計思考、證據為基礎、創意、問題解決、健康福祉、優質教育 ● Detailed Course Syllabus (課程大綱) Topic Homework (Preview reading) Weekly quiz 1 甚麼是設計思考？ Introduction to design thinking (heterogeneous grouping) 2 docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 25 (手動加簽 15 人) 中文名稱 Course Title 網路使用與健康促進 英文名稱 Course English Title Internet Use and Health Promotion 任課教師 Instructor 常善媚 上課時間 Time 每週四，第 7, 8, 9 堂 上課教室 Room 教育館 101 教室 Course Description(課程簡述) 健康促進是目全世界共同追求的一個趨勢，主要透過健康與衛生的教育、疾病的預防以及健康保護 這三個層面來進行，以增強健康與延緩或預防亞健康或疾病的產生。本課程擬運用網路科技來促進 健康，並進行個人健康促進行為的體驗與實踐。 Health promotion is a global vision nowadays. Through taking efforts in health education, prevention and health protection, positive health is expected to enhanced and negative health is expected to stop. This course aims to promote ideas of health, and practice, experiencing personal health by means of Internet and technology. Course Objectives (課程目標) 1. 了解健康促進的概念與重要議題 2. 了解健康風險評估的概念與評估方式 3. 能正確運用網路進行個人健保資料查詢、用藥查詢、出國傳染病查詢、並辨別正確健康資訊 4. 能使用校內健康資訊系統並建立個人健康資料 2 5. 了解網路科技的進步對健康的負面影響 6. 了解如何運用網路科技促進健康行為 7. 了解網路成癮與線上遊戲成癮之評估與治療 8. 實踐日常生活中飲食、體重、壓力或網路成癮等的控制，規劃並落實個人健康促進計畫 By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. Capture the ideas and important issues of health promotion 2. Understand the concept and practice of health risk assessments 3. Check personal health insurance information, medication, global pandemics and tell correct health information 4. Use Campus Health Information System and build personal health status 5. Understand the negative impacts of Internet with its progress on health 6. Learn how to promote health behavior through Internet 7. Have the ideas of Internet Addiction, and diagnoses and treatments of online gaming addiction 8. Control diet, weight, pressure or Internet addiction, and plan practicing personal health promotion Core capability to be cultivated by this course (欲培養之核心能力) 1. 社會變遷因應能力（To adapt to social change） 2. 生活實踐能力（To practice） 3. 慎思明辨能力（To think critically） 4. 跨領域能力（To cross disciplinary boundaries） Course Content(課程內容) ● Course keywords (關鍵字) 健康促進、網路使用 Health promotion, Internet use ● Detailed Course Syllabus (課程大綱) Topic Homework Weekly quiz 3 (Preview reading) 1 健康促進的生活方式與學習品質 Life style and learning quality of health promotion 2 如何運用網路科技促進健康生活型態 目標設定三選一: 1.增進個人健康促進行為； 2.改善個人問題網路使用的行為； 3.運用數位工具幫助改善學習所遇到的阻 礙。 Promoting healthy life style through Internet and technology: There are three possible goals a. docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 25 (手動加簽 15 人) 中文名稱 Course Title 健康心理學 英文名稱 Course English Title Health Psychology 任課教師 Instructor 常善媚 上課時間 Time 每週二，第 5, 6 堂 上課教室 Room 教育館 101 教室 Course Description(課程簡述) Health psychology is an interdisciplinary field that applies theories and concepts from psychology to the study of human well-being, illness, and healthcare. This course is designed to help students explore how psychology can be used to promote health while gaining insight into themselves, others, and their environment. By learning how psychology can improve health, students can better understand how to support their own well-being and that of others. 健康心理學被定義為一個跨領域的學門，它應用心理學的理論和概念於人類的幸福、疾病和醫療保 健相關研究。本課程幫學生了解如何應用心理學促進健康，同時深入了解自己、他人、與環境。經 學習從心理學的概念來改善健康的方式，學生可以更好地理解如何幫助自己和他人。 Course Objectives (課程目標) By the end of this course, students will be able to: 1. Explore how psychology influences and is applied to health care. 2. Understand the major psychosocial factors that contribute to health behaviors and the development of 2 disease. 3. Learn to apply their knowledge of psychology in the development, implementation, and evaluation of health programs. 4. Students will be able to assess their own health status and formulate their own health goals and health plans. 1. 探討心理學如何影響並應用於醫療保健。 2. 理解影響健康行為及疾病發展的主要心理社會因素。 3. 學習如何將心理學知識應用於健康計畫的制定、實施與評估。 4. 學生將能夠評估自身的健康狀況，並制定個人的健康目標與健康計畫。 Core capability to be cultivated by this course (欲培養之核心能力) 1. International journal of environmental research and public health, 16(13), 2415. ● Teaching Method (教學方式) Lecture, Group Discussion, and Role-Playing 講述法、小組討論、情境演練 ● Course Requirements and Performance Assessment (課程要求與表現評估) 1. Attendance: 10% 2. Group discussion and participation: 30% 3. Midterm assignment: 25% 4. Final presentation and report: 35% 1. 出席率：10% 2. 小組討論與課堂參與：30% 3. 期中作業：25% 4. 期末報告與展示：35% ● Explanation of assignments (作業內容說明) 1. Attendance ➢ Pre-test: At the beginning of each week of the course, participants must answer five multiple- choice questions related to the content of the weekly preview. ➢ Worksheets: During the two-hour weekly class, participants will complete a worksheet. This worksheet must be turned in before the end of the course. 出席率 ➢ 課前測驗：每週課程開始時，學員需回答五道與當週預習內容相關的選擇題。 ➢ 學習單：在每週兩小時的課程中，學員需完成一份學習單，並於課程結束前提交。 6 1. Group discussion and participation Your attendance and participation are expected and will be documented. Much of the work in class involves collaboration and discussion, as human knowledge is socially constructed. You should contribute to the group work, raise your hands to share ideas and ask questions, and avoid using digital devices (e.g., cellphones, laptops, iPad, etc.) for reasons irrelevant to the class activities. You should make every effort to attend class and be on time, and you must be in the classroom for the entire time to receive full credit for the attendance. 小組討論與課堂參與 你的出席與參與是必要的，並將被記錄下來。課堂中的許多活動都涉及合作與討論，因為人類 的知識是透過社會互動建構而成的。你應積極參與小組討論，舉手發表意見並提出問題，並避 免使用與課程無關的數位設備（如手機、筆記型電腦、iPad 等）。你應盡力準時到課，並全程 參與課堂活動，才能獲得完整的出席與參與分數。 2. Midterm assignment ➢ Choose a topic from the second through eighth week topics and record a two-minute video. This video must contain two parts: The first part is to introduce your topic and share the main concepts from the course content, i.e., Like a YouTuber; the second part is for you to share your own experiences on the topic, your advice, or your goals and plans. In the video you can choose to show your face or not, but in addition to the sound, the video also contains video/pictures. ➢ You will upload the video to your "YouTube" and set public to share with other participants. (Please #HealthPsyNTHU) ➢ There are three important dates for the Midterm Report: - On Week 7 in class, you must turn in your midterm report topic. - You must upload your video before Week 8 and shard your video address. - Before Week 9 you must view everyone's videos and feedback. 期中作業 ➢ 選擇一個主題（從第二週至第八週的課程主題中選擇），並錄製一段 兩分鐘的影片。影 片需包含兩個部分： 第一部分：介紹你的主題，並分享與課程內容相關的核心概念，就像 YouTuber 一樣。 7 第二部分：分享你個人的相關經驗、建議，或你的目標與計畫。在影片中，你可以選擇是否 露臉，但除了聲音之外，影片還需包含影像或圖片。 ➢ 影片上傳： 請將影片上傳至 YouTube，並設定為公開，以便與其他同學分享。（請標記 #HealthPsyNTHU） ➢ 期中報告的三個重要日期： 第七周（課堂上）：需提交你的期中報告主題。 第八周前：需上傳影片並分享影片連結。 第九周前：需觀看所有同學的影片並提供回饋。 3. Final presentation and report ➢ The final presentation and report is a group report. The teacher divides the students into groups and lets each group choose the topic on which they want to make a report. The group members are determined by the teacher. Group assignments are determined after all students in the class have been identified. ➢ Each group is free to choose which topics related to health psychology they would like to explore. ➢ The oral presentation will be 20 minutes per group. After the oral report, a PPT file must be submitted. ➢ The content of the report must cite at least two research reports on the topic. ➢ Points will be calculated for the content of the report, detailed understanding of the research findings, and the contribution of each individual in the group. 期末報告與展示 ➢ 期末報告與展示為小組報告，由老師分組，並讓各組選擇報告主題。小組成員將由老師分 配，分組作業會在全班名單確定後進行。 ➢ 各組可自由選擇 與 健康心理學 相關的主題進行探討。 ➢ 口頭報告時間：每組報告時間為 20 分鐘。口頭報告結束後，需提交 PPT 檔案。 ➢ 報告內容要求：需引用至少兩篇 與主題相關的研究報告。 8 ➢ 評分標準：報告內容的完整性、對研究結果的深入理解，以及每位組員的貢獻，都將列入 評分標準。 ● Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI (AI 使用規則) This course allows the conditional use of AI. When submitting assignments, students must specify how they used generative AI in their coursework and provide a record or link to their interactions with AI. AI Usage Guidelines for Students: AI use is permitted under certain conditions. Students must clearly state how they utilized generative AI in their coursework. For more details, please refer to the Guidelines for AI Collaboration, Co-Learning, and Literacy Development in Higher Education. Website: https://ctld.nthu.edu.tw/var/file/217/1217/img/4991/712376723.pdf 本課程允許有條件使用 AI。學生在提交作業時，必須明確說明如何在課程產出中使用生成式 AI， 並提供與 AI 互動的記錄或連結。 學生使用 AI 的規範： AI 的使用需符合特定條件。學生必須清楚說明如何在課程產出中使用生成式 AI。更多詳情請參閱 《大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引》。 網站：https://ctld.nthu.edu.tw/var/file/217/1217/img/4991/712376723.pdf

docs.name: 體育產業解析
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number IPTH102200 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 15 中文名稱 Course Title 體育產業解析 英文名稱 Course English Title Sports Industry Analysis 任課教師 Instructor 許仁豪 上課時間 Time F3、F4 上課教室 Room 教育館 103 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本課程以運動行銷為核心主軸，結合選手形象、賽事運營與經紀實務三大面向，帶領學生從觀察 運動現場、理解選手特質，到實際規劃賽會與品牌策略，建構全方位的運動行銷素養。課程前半 段（第 1 至第 8 週）將聚焦於運動員本身，探討技戰術、個人形象、粉絲經濟與社群經營等主 題，協助學生理解選手如何成為行銷資產，並學習如何分析與運用選手特質建立品牌價值。 中段課程（第 9 至第 12 週）轉向賽事層面，介紹運動賽會的品牌操作、贊助策略與觀眾體驗設 計，並以國內外實例進行小組提案演練，強化學生在行銷活動規劃與提案表達的實務能力。最後 階段（第 13 至第 16 週）則深入運動經紀領域，探討經紀人角色、商業合約、形象維護與危機 處理等議題，讓學生了解運動產業背後的專業管理與長期經營策略。 課程設計注重理論與實務並重，透過案例討論、小組報告與創意提案，鼓勵學生主動思考、實 際應用，培養面對運動行銷產業多元挑戰的能力。適合對運動、媒體、行銷、公關、品牌經營 有興趣的學生選修。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 體育產業、運動科學、賽事經濟效益、運動行銷、運動經紀、運動媒體、場館設施 Event Analysis、Sports Science、Economic Impact of Events、Industry Policy、Sports Marketing、Sports Management、Sports Media、Facility Management 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程旨在培育學生對於運動產業的全面理解，期使學生透過跨領域知識，洞察並解決體育產 業面臨的真實問題。課程歡迎所有領域學生修習，教師將透過實際案例及影片講解，以生活化 的形式認識體育產業的各面向。(以棒球、籃球、羽球為主要分析)。 ● 參考書籍(References) 1. 曾荃鈺、歐嘉竣（2023）。 隱形賽局：揭開運動產業議題的真相。健行。 2. Greenwell, T. C., Danzey-Bussell, L. A., & Shonk, D. J.（2017）。 運動賽會管理（鄭志 富、鄭惠萍、陳美燕、蕭嘉惠、陳天賜、陳鴻雁、黃妍榛、呂宛蓁 譯）。禾楓書局。 （2013） 3. 黃偉揚、陳顯宗、何茂松、林國瑞、房振坤、劉家增（2012）。 國際綜合運動賽會管理： 理論與實務。洪葉文化。 4. 王順正、林玉瓊（2020）。做個有智慧的跑者。旗標。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 課程前半段將以教師講述課程為主，透過實例講解與賽會影片分析，學生將理解不同賽會類型 涵蓋的體育產業及其經濟效益；課程後半段將以專題討論的形式進行，學生將於課程前半進行 小組報告與討論，加強學生對運動賽事與產業的深入探索，再由教師進行補充與實例分享。 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 出席 40％(因故未出席一次扣 7 分，3 次無故缺席出席率為 0 分) 小組報告 40％(期中期末各 20％) 課堂報告及作業 20％ ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 進度說明 第 1 週 課程介紹與體育產業概述 第 2 週 認識運動員：特質、運動員的成長歷程、形象，如何作為行銷素材 第 3 週 技術與戰術的基礎認識 第 4 週 數據與運動表現 第 5 週 運動故事與品牌塑造 第６週 粉絲經濟與運動偶像 第７週 體育產業解析—世界青年羽球錦標賽 第 8 週 期中報告 第９週 運動賽會行銷—梅竹賽 第 10 週 體育產業解析—梅竹賽 第 11 週 賽事品牌與贊助策略 第 12 週 運動經紀人制度與角色 第 13 週 合約與肖像權、代言管理 第 14 週 危機公關與形象修復 第 15 週 期末報告 第 16 週 補考 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程為有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出。 本課程鼓勵學生在透明與負責的原則下，適度使用 AI 工具進行課業協作。學生應在作業或報告 的標題頁註腳或引用文獻部分簡要說明 AI 工具的使用情況，並遵循學校的相關指引。如未明確 標註，教師有權重新評分或不予計分。

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11420IPTH201100 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 專題研究 A1 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topics A1 任課教師 Instructor 指導教授 上課時間 Time 由教授指定 上課教室 Room 由教授指定 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程旨在學生於指導教授的指導下，針對各自選定之專題進行系統化的深入研究。透過專題 的進行，學生將有機會在所選領域內獲取實質的知識與技術成果，培養獨立研究能力，並具備 解決問題的實務經驗，進而提升對該領域的專業理解與應用能力。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 系統化專題研究的深入探索與應用,培養獨立研究與解決問題的能力,學術理論與實務技術的綜合 運用,強化學生在特定領域的專業能力,提升學生創新與應用能力 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程讓學生在指導下進行專題研究，培養獨立研究與問題解決能力，並提升專業應用。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 由教授指定。 ● 參考書籍(References) 由教授指定。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 透過專題學習研究技巧，並培養解決問題之能力。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 由教授指定。 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 由指導教授與課程共同評審，成績將依據專題成果的素質與研究態度進行評定。但若本學期 專題成果報告未按時(依公告)繳交，將由委員進行審查，並依相關規定酌情扣減成績。 *以上項目需於加簽提交專題課程大綱時，依規定敘明清楚。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (1) 完全開放使用且無須註明 Unrestricted use with no disclosure required (2) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output (3) 禁止使用，請註明相關的監管機制 Prohibited use; please specify relevant oversight (4) 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 Not applicable 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) 本課程之 AI 使用規則依授課指導教授訂定，需於加簽提交專題課程大綱時，依規定敘明清楚。

docs.name: 洞悉行銷與我的日常生活
docs.text: 1 ISS4095 Marketing in Daily Life 9.10 – 12.00 Wednesdays Course Description Our lives are surrounded by many forms of marketing activities. Some are designed to improve firm performance, while others aim to contribute to a better world. To enhance firm performance, companies often rely on the four fundamental strategies (i.e., 4Ps: product, place, price, and promotion). These strategies are intended to deliver value to customers and, in turn, generate value for the firms. This course will guide you through these strategies, help you understand how they influence your consumption decisions, and encourage you to consider whether and how these strategies enable companies to achieve their marketing objectives. Below are some examples of marketing activities aimed at improving firm performance. • Have you noticed that luxury brands offer products with both big logos and small (or even no) logos? Why would they provide products with small (or no) logos while the logo is often a major reason customers buy luxury products? (Products) • Have you ever ordered food through Foodpanda or Uber Eats? You may notice the overwhelming number of restaurants on these platforms. Should a restaurant join these delivery platforms as an additional sales channel, even when competition is so intense? (Multichannel management/ Places) • What is more effective in encouraging customers to repurchase from the same brand – lower prices or better quality? (Prices/ Values) • Taipei’s Zhongxiao-Fuxing MRT station was once covered with Foodpanda advertisements, a campaign that required a significant investment. Was this a smart move for Foodpanda? (Mass media advertising/ Promotion) • You constantly receive ads on social media, and they often seem to “know” who you are and what you intend to buy. Does targeted social media advertising actually benefit companies? (Targeted advertising/ Promotion) • Influencers are everywhere. Is collaborating with influencers a strategically sound choice for companies? (Promotion) 2 To create a better word, companies have begun exploring ways – often referred to as “nudges” – to enhance consumer and societal well-being. These efforts include encouraging healthier eating, promoting better lifestyle choices, and motivating charitable giving. This course will guide you in evaluating whether such nudges actually work and how they contribute to consumer and social welfare. We will also brainstorm new nudges together and imagine how they can help build a better word. Some examples of nudges for a better world: • When purchasing or consuming food, do you look at front-of-package nutrition labels? If so, does this help you make healthier choices? • Would you believe that a store’s or restaurant’s lighting or music could influence your preference for healthy vs. unhealthy food? • To encourage healthier choices, many products now come in reduced-sugar versions or smaller portion sizes. But do these products changes actually help consumers choose healthier options? And do they improve a company’s brand performance? • Did you know that your caffeine intake may influence your spending behavior? • Do you enjoy group exercise? What keeps you motivated to continue? Would you prefer exercising with people who are more fit than you or less fit? Course Goals The goal of the course is to develop a holistic understanding of how marketing activities – particularly the 4Ps and nudges – shape our daily lives. Students will learn key marketing theories by connecting them to real-life experiences. In addition to the textbook, selected journal articles will encourage students to think critically about why companies adopt these marketing strategies and how they can be effectively implemented to enhance firm performance as well as consumer and societal well-being. Pearson Education Limited. o Note: You may also use the later editions (18th [2020] or 19th [2023]). The reason we use the 17th edition is that it is available to you for free online. The conceptual content is largely consistent across editions, so using a different edition will not affect your learning. 3 Course evaluation • Class attendance 10% • Class engagement in class discussions: 20% • Midterm individual exam (open book): 40% • Final-term group report (3000 [min.] – 3500 [max.] words about applying nudges in consumer & social wellbeing): 30%. docs.text: Institute of Service Science National Tsing Hua University IT Service Security Spring 2026 Time: Friday: 9:00am – 12:00pm Instructor: Soumya Ray soumya.ray@iss.nthu.edu.tw TA: 何捷睿 Jerry Ho (only contact on MS Teams) Companies, government, and educational institutions are rushing to deliver online services and incorporate AI. Security is a major concern in these initiatives because bad actors are quickly exploiting weaknesses. Secure IT services protect the privacy of users and can even be a competitive advantage when offered as a core feature. This course will teach how to develop highly secure online services and lead organizations to adopt a security-conscious culture. This class focuses on the use of cryptographic technologies and software architecture patterns to create innovative online services for e- commerce, fintech, IoT, and other hi-tech initiatives. Prerequisites: This course is intended for students who are already be comfortable with programming: - Coding in an object-oriented language (Java, Javascript, C#, C++, Python, PHP, Ruby, etc.) - Basic web page design (HTML, CSS) - Basic database design (relational design, ERD/SQL) - Unix based systems (Linux, MacOS, etc.) Objectives: This course will enable students to design better security practices, develop secure software, interact with security practitioners, and digest the latest technical developments about security. You will also be able to help your future organizations to manage and implement secure solutions. Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence: In accordance with the published Guidelines for Collaboration, Co-learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, this course adopts the following policy: unrestricted use Grading: Grades are based mainly on individual performance: class/online participation; individual assignments; and contributions to the team project. Students will work as a team on a semester project to develop an innovative online security system. However, students on a team do not receive the same grade for the team project: each student is evaluated on their individual coding contribution to the project. docs.text: 1 Institute of Service Science, National Tsing Hua University Computational Statistics for Data Science (CSDS) Spring 2026 Instructor Soumya Ray soumya.ray@iss.nthu.edu.tw Office: 850 TSMC Building Teaching Assistants (contact on MS Teams only) TBA Prerequisite knowledge: You must have completed at least one statistics class before taking this course. This class focuses on the computational approaches to statistics, and only lightly reviews fundamental statistics topics. No prior programming knowledge is required but students with basic coding experience will have an advantage. Beginners must be willing to learn basic programming through homework tutorials. We will teach intermediate programming techniques in class that build on the homework tutorials. Course Description: This class covers computational methods for statistics. You will learn to develop tools that support decision-making, and produce reproducible analyses and reports. Computational focus: We will use computational methods of programming and algorithms to overcome limitations of traditional statistical methods. We will learn to reshape data, run simulations, discover dimensions in data, utilize machine learning, and create complex models. Methodological focus: We will use statistics to understand, explain, and predict scientific and business phenomena to inform decision making and conduct research. We will describe and visualize data, create statistical models from domain knowledge, test our ideas against data; predict new outcomes; and guard against fallacious use of statistics. Skill focus: We will learn to write data analytics code in R on par with industry standards. Students will implement their own algorithms, write code that is highly readable and reusable, produce highly performant code, create custom visualizations, and apply different styles of analytic programming. Software Tools: Students will use the RStudio or Visual Studio Code to write code in the R programming language. Our tools are all free and open-source. Using R requires learning basic concepts in programming and maintaining code, which we will teach in class. If you wish to familiarize yourself with these tools before class begins, please start with the tutorials at http://swirlstats.com Ethics Statement on Generative Artificial Intelligence and other Programming Resources: In accordance with the published Guidelines for Collaboration, Co-learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, this course adopts the following policy: Conditionally open. Grounded in the principles of transparency and responsibility, this course encourages students to leverage Generative AI (GenAI), like ChatGPT and Github CoPilot, and other coding resources, like StackOverflow and Github, to enhance their learning and improve the quality of their course outputs. This means that students may use GenAI or other resources but: 1. Must briefly explain how these tools were used in each homework assignment they submit. 2. Code copied from outside tools or resources must be properly cited and credited. 3. Must not submit code from GAI or outside sources that they do not fully understand. We expect students to carefully study, verify, and suitably alter their GAI assisted solutions to match homework requirements and reflect their genuine learning. If code is discovered that was not properly understood and adapted, or if the use of GenAI or other resources was not disclosed, instructors have the right to reevaluate the assignment or withhold scores. Students enrolled in this course agree to the above ethics statement. 2 Grading Policy Assignments: You will receive grades every week that count towards your total final grade ● Individual homework assignments (50%): weekly homework reports will be anonymously peer- reviewed by two other students chosen at random; TAs will assign scores based on peer- reviewers’ suggestions. You may offer a rebuttal if you feel that you deserved a better grade, and our teaching team will arbitrate. ● Peer review (24%): you thoughtfully review two students’ assignments each week after class. ● Tutorials and quizzes (13%): occasional interactive tutorials and quizzes on readings. ● Engagement (13%): your attendance will be recorded and graded from Week 3 onwards. Meaningful online discussion can be credited towards class absences. Extra Credit: You can earn extra points throughout the semester: ● Outstanding Homework: your peers may grant you an extra point for noteworthy reports ● Assistance Credit: if your peers mention your help on submitted assignments. ● Online discussion: if you ask or answer questions in-class, or in online discussions on MS Teams. Reference Material: Lecture slides will be provided before every class and made available online at our class website. Students will be given extra material from videos, research papers, practitioners’ blogs, and more.
