docs.text: 1 數位創新與電子商務 Syllabus Digital Innovation and E-Commerce Instructor: Prof. 王俊程 e-mail: jcwang@mx.nthu.edu.tw Office: TSMC Building 846 TA: Ying-Jia Hong, Santoso Halim Budi 說明： 數位創新是網路時代企業必備的能力，藉由善用科技的力量，讓企業能直接與世界的使用者對話， 提供合乎使用者需求的服務。數位科技與電子商務在經過十多年的發展，已經出現嶄新的服務型 態，例如直播服務，智慧型廣告系統等結合科技與服務的新樣態。本課程讓學生在理論與實務深入 研討，從理解科技的本質開始，藉由網路產業的生態，介紹網路商業模式的發展，網路多邊平台的 經營策略，長尾模式，社群網路經營，到消費者與生產者的共創價值模式。期末並以實際專案的形 式，讓學生可以從實作的經驗，運用所學的知識，感受科技創新對產業生態的衝擊。 Digital Innovation is a capability that every company needed in order to navigate the connected world. Through technology, companies can make direct contact with the world and understand the customers’ needs thus bypassing the traditional channels. After more than 20 years of development, we only see the emerging technologies become more widespread and have deeper impact on our society. This course will equip the students with theoretical perspectives and develop their ability to analyze digital initiatives, and evaluate AI-enabled and e-commerce businesses strategies and models. Topics range from Internet business models development, multi-sided platform, social media and social network, crowd sourcing and co-creation business models, and AI and other technologies. At the end of the semester, students will be required to complete a team project to apply their knowledge and demonstrate their integrated learning outcomes. Textbook: 1. E-Commerce 2021-2022: Business, Technology, Society. 17th ed. By Kenneth C. Laudon, Carol G. Traver. Pearson. (International Edition) 2. Information Rules, by Hal R. docs.text: https://bit.ly/nthu-baft Business Analytics Using Forecasting (BAFT) Term: Spring 2026 Instructor: Galit Shmueli (galit.shmueli@iss.nthu.edu.tw) TA: Matthew Bobea (matt.bobea@iss.nthu.edu.tw) Website: https://canvas.instructure.com/courses/13690093 Class Time: Wednesdays, 14:20-17:20 Classroom: Room 406, TSMC Building Course Description Business analytics is the use of data-driven decision making. Companies, governments and other organizations now collect and analyze large amounts of data about suppliers, clients, employees, citizens, transactions, etc. Forecasting is the arm of predictive analytics that provides a powerful toolkit for analyzing time series data. This course focuses on forecasting time series, where past and present values are used to forecast future values of a series of interest. The course covers issues relating to different steps of the forecasting process, from goal definition, through data visualization, modeling, and performance evaluation to model deployment. Quantitative forecasting uses statistical and machine learning methods to generate numerical forecasts, an important component of decision making across many business functions, including economic forecasting, workload projections, sales forecasts, and transportation demand. Forecasting is now applied to Big Data with many series, often measured at high frequency. Examples include IoT devices and sensor recordings, demand for thousands of products at retail chains, wind turbines, web traffic, etc. Forecasting can be combined with statistical monitoring methods for purposes of anomaly detection – for example, public health organizations collect and monitor clinical and other data for detecting disease outbreaks. Forecasting is also often combined with simulation for purposes of scenario building. The focus of this course is on using forecasting for improving service, with a special emphasis on human-oriented and socially-responsible forecasting. In the course we’ll work with real business problems and real data. We will examine types of applications where forecasting is potentially useful, and learn how to deploy the forecasting process. The emphasis is on understanding the concepts and logic behind a wide set of forecasting techniques and their relation to specific business analytics situations. The course is not about mastering the theoretical underpinnings of the techniques. The course will be driven by a business forecasting project that will encapsulate the different steps of practical forecasting. Software An important feature of this course is hands-on learning using forecasting and data visualization software. We will use the open-source R software . For data visualization we will use Tableau. To take this course, students are required to have basic familiarity with R. Course Objectives Upon successful completion of the course, you should possess valuable practical analytical skills that will equip you with a competitive skill in almost any contemporary workplace. More formally, the course will provide participants with the following skills and knowledge: ● Be familiar of business analytics potential and dangers in today’s data rich-environment ● Gain experience using forecasting methods ● Know how to decide when to use which technique ● Be able to implement major forecasting techniques using software ● Become a smart and critical user and consumer of forecasting techniques ● Gain the intellectual capital required to provide responsible business analytics services ● Be conscious of humanistic and societal implications of deploying data mining in organizations 2 Learning Goals In addition to the course objectives, students should expect to develop the following by the end of the course: 1. Effective Oral Communication - Each student will be able to communicate verbally in an organized, clear, and persuasive manner, and be a responsive listener. (Assessment: Project presentations) 2. Critical and Integrative Thinking - Each student will be able to identify key issues in a business setting, develop a perspective that is supported with relevant information and integrative thinking, to draw and assess conclusions. (Assessment: Individual Assignments, project proposal, team project report and presentations) 3. Interpersonal Awareness and Working in Teams - Each student will demonstrate an ability to work effectively in a team, exhibiting behavior that reflects an understanding of the importance of individual roles and tasks, and the ability to manage conflict and compromise, so that team goals are achieved. (Assessment: Team project report and team presentations, team meetings with instructor) Flipped Classroom The course is designed as a “flipped classroom”: students are expected to watch videos, read the textbook, take short quizzes, post on an online forum, and work on an assignment prior to each on-ground session. Face-to-face class time will be devoted to discussions, developing the team projects, gaining hands-on experience, invited lectures, and other forms of interactive learning. We will use Canvas for all the online materials. Required Textbook Practical Time Series Forecasting with R, 3rd edition (2024), by Shmueli & Polak ● Kindle eBook available on Amazon.com ● Data and code for book: https://github.com/gshmueli/ptsf-R-3e ● Recommended: free online book Forecasting: Principles and Practice Grading Deliverable Weight Individual assignments (8) 40% Online forum posts and quizzes (on Canvas) 10% In-class team activities (3) 10% Midterm team proposal presentation & report 10% Final team project report 15% Final team presentation 15% Final letter grades are determined based on curving the numerical grades (not based on fixed grade intervals). Each student is required to fill a peer evaluation report. If multiple team members indicate insufficient contribution of a member, a deduction of 30% of the presentation/report grade will be applied to that member. Guidelines for Deliverables Individual Assignments ● Assignments should be completed independently, without discussing with other students. ● Upload your file(s) to the course Canvas site by 14:00. ● Late assignments accepted, subject to a penalty of 25% on assignment grade for each late day. On-Ground Attendance Full attendance is mandatory in all sessions. You can miss a maximum of one class due to an emergency (e.g., illness). 3 Online Component Canvas: Before each class, watch videos, read the book chapters, post online, and take the online short quiz. Complete the individual assignment and submit a hardcopy in class. Use of Generative AI: Conditionally Open Grounded in the principles of transparency and responsibility, this course encourages students to leverage AI for collaboration and mutual learning to enhance the quality of learning and output. In accordance with the published Guidelines for Collaboration, Co-learning, and Cultivation of Artificial Intelligence Competencies in University Education, this course adopts the following policy: Conditionally open. You must briefly explain how you used generative AI for text summarization, topic ideation, writing improvement, translation, coding, image creation, quiz answering, or any other purpose. Mention this in the footnote of the title/cover page of your assignments, reports, and presentations. If usage is discovered without proper disclosure, the instructor has the right to reevaluate the deliverable and adjust scores. In turn, the instructor will indicate if course materials or learning resources were derived from generative AI. Midterm Team Proposal Each team should find a real dataset (at least 4 series to analyze) and a business/social idea that can be approached using forecasting with the collected data. Written Proposal Format: 2-pages, 11-point font, 1-inch margins, 1.15 line space, PDF format. In class Presentation: 10 min, maximum 6 slides. The proposal report and slides should include the following components: 1. Suitable Title - Should reflect the business goal and forecasting goal 2. Business Problem: ○ Who is the stakeholder or client? Choose the one who will make decisions using the forecasts. ○ Describe the business problem/goal. What are the business benefits of implementing this idea? What shortcoming does it address? How can forecasts improve their decisions? ○ What would be considered a success? 3. Forecasting Goal: ○ A description of the forecasting objective (what are you forecasting? Forecasting horizon, etc.). ○ Is the goal retrospective or forward-looking? ○ How will the forecasts be used? For what purpose? (Examples: building scenarios/anomaly detection/optimizing planning/etc.) 4. Data: ○ Brief description of available data (source, what they measure, time period, amount of data). ○ Some guidance on the data subset that will be used and the re-processing or preparation that might be needed based on your past experience. ○ Time plot of each relevant series (at least 4 series). 5. Methods: ○ What are some forecasting methods to consider? (optional: show initial results with smoothing) ○ Which performance measures are appropriate? How do they map to the business goal? 6. Implementation/Production: ○ Operational requirements or constraints (for example, will the forecasting system be run in real-time? will it require collecting new data? will it be a one-time analysis or ongoing?) Final Project Presentation (15 minutes) Each team presents their project to the class on session #16. The project is based on the ideation submission, where the idea is then developed into a forecasting solution with final recommendations. Create the following 7 slides (no more than 10 slides): 1. Cover: Informative title, team number and member names 2. Business problem (stakeholder, challenge/opportunity, humanistic implications) 3. Forecasting goal (forecast/time series analysis, retrospective/prospective, how to be used?) 4 4. Data description (source, what is measured, how much, how often) 5. Methods (forecasting methods, relevant outputs) 6. Evaluation (metrics of interest, benchmark, comparison, error magnitude/cost of selected model) 7. Recommendations Final Project Report (5 pages) Written report of the project details, from the business problem through the forecasting problem and solution, to recommendations. Format: 5 pages, 11-point font, 1-inch margins, 1.15 line space, PDF format. The report should be written clearly and professionally and include the following sections: 1. Cover page with informative title, team number, course name, and member names (no student ID) 2. One-page executive summary: summarizes the entire report for a non-technical manager (the business problem, data, a relevant chart, the forecasting solution’s methods and performance, and recommendations) 3. Detailed report: a. Problem description (business goal and forecasting goal) b. Data description (data source, what is measured, how much, how often, sample of 10 rows per series, time plots) c. Brief data preparation details (how your data were created from the raw data) d. Forecasting solution: methods used (with sufficient detail and screenshots; use Appendix if needed) and appropriate performance evaluation (proper choice of measures, benchmarking, error magnitude/cost of selected model). Charts with training and validation periods e. Time plot of series with future forecasts, for each of the key series f. Conclusions (advantages and limitations) and operational recommendations 4. Appendix (not counted in 5-page limit): Your R code (link to github) Session-Wise Schedule Week Topics Online Preparation prior to class: watch, read, discuss In-Class Deliverable #1 Feb 25 1. Introduction to business analytics 2. Forecasting applications 3. Responsible forecasting 4. Forecasting process, language & notation 5. Goal definition #2 Mar 4 1. Goal definition 2. Data collection and characteristics 3. Matching data with goal Cab bookings in India (group activity) Canvas Session 1 Read: Chap 1, Sec 2.1 Watch: video (8 min) Discuss #1: Forecasting goal (Install/update R, RStudio, R packages) Assignment 1 (Goal): Ch 1 Problems #1-5 #3 Mar 11 1. Data visualization 2. Data Preprocessing Transportation demand (group activity) Cab bookings in India (group activity) Canvas Session 2 Read: Chap 2 Watch: 2 videos (18 min) Install Tableau Assignment 2 (Visualization): Ch 2 Prob #1 + Tableau dashboard #4 Mar 18 Performance Evaluation 1. Data partitioning 2. Naïve forecasts 3. Predictive charts & measures Case 11.1: transportation demand Canvas Session 3 Read: Chap 3 Watch: 4 videos (21 min) Discuss #2: forecasting harms Quick quiz #1 Assignment 3 (Performance): Ch 3 Prob #1 and #2 5 Week Topics Online Preparation prior to class: watch, read, discuss In-Class Deliverable #5 Mar 25 Smoothing-based methods 1. Moving Average (centered/trailing) 2. Differencing, seasonal indexes 3. Simple Exponential Smoothing Canvas Session 4 Read: Chap 5, until Sec 5.4 Watch: 4 videos (23 min) Discuss #3: MA and differencing #6 Apr 1 [Company visits/meeting] Canvas Session 5 #7 Apr 8 Smoothing - cont. 4. Advanced Exponential Smoothing 5. Automated ETS 6. ETS for many series (Forecasting Australian wines) In-Class: Team Project Proposal Presentations Canvas Session 6 Read: Chap 5, from Sec 5.5 to end Watch: 3 videos (24 min) Quick quiz #2 Assignment 4 (Smoothing): Ch 5 Prob #8 Project Proposal 2-page Report #8 Apr 15 Regression-based forecasting 1. Including external information [meetings with teams] Canvas Session 10 Read: Chap 7, Sec 7.4 Watch: 2 videos (22 min) Discuss #5: Sept 11 travel #12 May 13 Neural networks Canvas Session 11 Read: Chap 8 Watch: 3 videos (30 min) #13 May 20 Ensembles Team projects: updates [meetings with teams] Canvas Session 12 Read: Chap 4 Assignment 7 (NN): Ch 8 Prob #1-3 (bonus: #4) #14 May 27 Forecasting binary events Logistic regression Case 11.3: forecasting stock price movements Canvas Session 13 Read: Chap 9 Watch: 4 videos (29 min) Quick quiz #4 #15 Jun 3 Communication and maintenance Canvas Session 14 Discuss #6: mango outbreak Read: Chap 10 Watch: video (13 min) Assignment 8 (binary Logistic Regression): Ch 9 Prob #4-10 #16 Jun 10 Team Project Presentations Canvas Session 15 Upload to Google Slides before class Submit Team Project Report by 23:59 on Jun 12, 2026 Upload report to Canvas (PDF)

docs.text: 1 ISS5096: Experiments and Causal Inference Jaewon Yoo Assistant Professor Institute of Service Science National Tsing Hua University Spring 2026 Course Duration: Feb 23 – Jun 15, 2026 Classroom: TSMC Bldg. R406 Class Time: Thursday, 14:20 pm- 17:20 pm TA: TBA COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course introduces experimental and quasi-experimental methods for causal inference that are widely used in a broad array of domains such as marketing and information systems. The focus of the course is on delivering a breadth of substantive topics and methodological considerations that emerge in utilizing the identification-oriented methods. Throughout the course, we will discuss topics that are related to methods such as randomized controlled trials (RCT), difference-in-differences (DiD), matching methods such as propensity score matching (PSM) and coarsened exact matching (CEM), and more advanced topics such as regression discontinuity designs (RDD), double-debiased machine learning (DML), synthetic control methods (SCM), and its extensions such as synthetic difference-in-differences (synth. DiD). To foster learning experiences, students will review relevant research papers on each topic and be asked to actively engage in presentations and discussions about the nature of causation and alternative means of inferring causal relationships. Students will also carry out a collaborative group project for which they will design an experiment and associated plan of analysis in an attempt to draw business insights. Leading tech companies such as Netflix, Microsoft, and Amazon are growingly paying attention to the importance of business experimentation and causal inference to enhance their decision making, and are hiring employees that are equipped with such analytical tools/mindsets (e.g., watch a recent video highlighting this by causal inference science team at Netflix). In line with this growing trend, this course also caters to those that are interested in joining the industry after graduation with one condition: a willingness to work hard on possibly unfamiliar materials. COURSE GOALS: o Learn how to determine which methods and results best support empirical inference questions. o Be familiar with causal inference methods that are widely used for business analytics. o Understand the trade-offs in the design, analysis, and reporting of field/quasi/natural experiment methods. PREREQUISITES: o Math: undergraduate-level probability and statistics; some experiences with regression analysis/econometrics will be helpful. o Programming: Knowledge of statistical programming (e.g., R and Python) o Recommended prior coursework: - ISS5077 Computational Statistics for Data Science (CSDS) covers hypothesis testing, regression, and applied statistical modeling; ideal preparation for this course. 2 - ECON3033 Econometrics I and ECON3034 Econometrics II — regression methodology and empirical research designs. - ISS5066 Programming for Business Analytics (PBA) covers regression, statistical inference, and R programming, but students entering with PBA alone should expect a steeper learning curve. - ISS5090 Business Analytics with Machine Learning (BAML) relevant background for the causal ML topics covered in Weeks 14–15. Students may also be interested in ECON5099 Causal Inference in Econometrics, which covers related topics. TEXTBOOK: Students can choose to purchase either the hard copy or the e-book for both textbooks 1 and 2, but please be prepared to have the textbooks ready before the beginning of the semester. If you choose to order online, be aware that it might take time for the textbooks to be delivered. So, if you plan to take the course, please make sure to place your order early enough so the books arrive in time. 1. Mostly Harmless Econometrics: an empiricist's companion by J. D. Angrist and Jorn- Steffen Pischke, Princeton University Press, 2008. 2. Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences by G. Imbens and D. Rubin, Cambridge University Press, 2015. 3. The Effect: An Introduction to Research Design and Causality by N. Huntington-Klein, CRC Press, 2021. (Opensource PDF version provided by the author here.) The following books are optional but may prove useful for additional coverage of some of the course topics. • J. D. Angrist, and Jorn-Steffen Pischke. 2015. Mastering 'metrics: The path from cause to effect. Princeton University Press. • Cunningham, Scott. Causal Inference: The Mixtape. 2021. Yale University Press. • Hernán, Miguel A., and James M. Robins. 2020. Causal inference: What If. CRC Press. Taylor and Francis Group. (Opensource PDF version provided by the authors here.) • Morgan, Stephen L., and Christopher Winship. 2015. Counterfactuals and Causal Inference, Second Edition. Cambridge University Press. • Pearl, Judea. 2000. Causality: Models, Reasoning, and Inference. New York: Cambridge University Press. • Blackwell, M., A User’s Guide to Statistical Inference and Regression. (Opensource PDF version provided by the authors here.) • Rosenbaum, Paul R. 2002. Observational Studies, 2nd edition. Springer-Verlag. • Rosenbaum, Paul R. 2009. Design of Observational Studies. Springer Series in Statistics. • Wooldridge, Jeffrey M. 2010. Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data, Second Edition. MIT Press. • Rubin, Donald. 2006. Matched Sampling for Causal Effects. Cambridge University Press. • Manski, Charles F. 1995. Identification Problems in the Social Sciences. Cambridge: Harvard University Press. • Chernozhukov, Victor, Christian Hansen, Nathan Kallus, Martin Spindler, and Vasilis Syrgkanis. 2025. Applied Causal Inference Powered by ML and AI. (Unpublished. Opensource PDF version provided the authors here.) 3 SOFTWARE: We use R (with RStudio) as the primary computing environment. Key packages include: tidyverse, fixest, did, rdrobust, MatchIt, WeightIt, grf, dagitty, ggdag, modelsummary. Students comfortable with Stata or Python may use those for their research projects, but in-class demonstrations and code examples will be in R. COURSE EVALUATION: Grading Policy Research Project 50% Problem Sets 15% The Effect Assignments 15% Participation (incl. presentations) 10% One-Page Summaries 5% Attendance 5% Total 100% Course Requirements 1. AI Use Policy*: Students are permitted to utilize AI tools or Large Language Models (LLMs; e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) responsibly as aids for brainstorming and generating initial drafts for assignments. However, it is imperative that the final submission predominantly reflects the student's understanding and personal input. To maintain academic integrity, students who choose to use AI tools must adhere to the following guidelines: a. Thorough Explanation: Students must provide a detailed explanation of how the AI tool was used in the completion of the assignment. b. Original AI Responses: Alongside their submission, students are required to submit the original responses generated by the AI tool. c. Critical Evaluation and Personal Input: Students should critically evaluate the AI- generated content and clearly indicate the portions of the work that have been modified or expanded upon with their own insights and understanding. d. Proper Attribution: Proper attribution should be given to the AI-generated content used, clearly indicating the sections that are AI-generated. ** Remember, attempting to cheat the system by heavily relying on AI-generated content without substantial personal input is ultimately the student's loss, as it undermines the learning process and personal growth. 2. Academic Honesty and Plagiarism*: All work submitted for academic evaluation must be the student’s own. The penalty for violation of academic integrity will result in a zero for that 4 assignment for the first time. Subsequent violation(s) will result in a failing grade for the course. Plagiarism will also not be tolerated. Academic dishonesty comprises of, but is not limited to, the following: • Cheating: Copying from other students’ quizzes and assignments or allowing others to copy from one’s own. • Plagiarism: Using other people’s original work without giving appropriate credit or acknowledgment to the authors or sources. • Self-plagiarism: Submitting a piece of work in more than one course without the explicit permission of the instructors involved. • Misrepresentation of authorship: Submitting work as one’s own, which has been prepared by or purchased from others. Students will be asked to upload their submission materials to Turnitin.com, an online plagiarism checker, to ensure academic integrity. Read more about online submission on http://learning.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1319-7120.php?Lang=en. 3. Attendance: All students are expected to attend every class. Please bring your own hard copy of the course materials, which will be distributed by the instructor before class. If you have any urgent reason to miss a class, you are still responsible for the materials covered during the class and are expected to complete the required work. Attendance will be taken on a regular basis and will count towards your participation score (5%). Class missing will cause about 1% loss of final grade. Students who miss a class should inform me or the TA prior to the class via email or phone call. 4. Attitude/Participation: In class, the most important thing for the students is to stay active and engaged about the topic being discussed. Positive contributions to class discussions will increase your score towards attitude. When we discuss a topic in class, effective discussions are only possible if everyone is well prepared. Please, be prepared to open and engage in discussions with your opinions and thoughts. 5. Problem Sets and ‘The Effect’ Assignments: Methods are tools, and it isn’t very instructive to read a lot about hammers or watch someone else wield a hammer -- you need to get your hands on a hammer or two. In this course, you will have 1) problem sets, which will be a mix of conceptual questions, analytic problems, computer simulations, and data analysis that closely resemble what we discuss in lectures, and 2) assignments from our third textbook, The Effect. I encourage you to work in groups on the homework, but you always need to write your own solutions including your computer code. Also, it is hugely beneficial to attempt the problems sets on your own before working in groups. Assignments are to be submitted on the due date. Late submissions will be penalized 1 percentage point of the assignment’s weight per day (e.g., for an assignment worth 7 % of the course grade, turning it in 3 days late caps the attainable score at 4%). 6. Journal Article Review a. One-Page Summaries: Before class starts, every student should submit 1-page summary of the assigned papers which will be discussed in class. A guideline will be distributed for students to use when summarizing the papers. b. One-Page Summary Guideline: i. Choose 5 papers from the assigned reading list and write a one-page summary addressing the following: 1. Main Question: What is the main question of the paper? Why do we care? 5 2. Parameters of Interest: What model aspects or facts are being estimated? 3. Data: What is the unit of observation? Where are the data from? How were they collected? 4. Answers: What does the paper find? What are the main weaknesses? How could it be improved? 5. Extensions: After the current paper, what could be done next in this general area? ii. You may also discuss: one-sentence conclusion, institutional background, conceptual framework, or relevant literature. Submit as PDF via Teams. c. Paper Introduction Presentations (Peer-Reviewed): Throughout the semester, students will be reading academic publications/papers that utilize different causal inference methods. Students will be asked to present the papers they reviewed each week (reading list will be distributed) by taking turns. The contents to be necessarily included are the value of the topic and motivational story. Other audience should also read the paper prior to the class for discussion. The presentations will be peer-reviewed. 7. Research Project: In lieu of a final exam, this course requires students to write a short paper applying or extending the causal inference methods we learn in this class. It should be no longer than 20 double-spaced pages and focus on the research design, data, methodology, results, and analysis. a. Progress Report & Project Presentation (Peer-Reviewed): Students will generate a potential research idea based on what we will discuss and suggest how to collect data and what causal inference methods/models can be used to carry out the research. The final project presentation will be peer-reviewed. b. Structured Peer Feedback: Final presentations are accompanied by structured peer feedback. After each presentation, every student completes a feedback form covering four areas: Research Question, Identification Strategy, Threats & Limitations, and a Constructive Suggestion. Feedback forms are shared with presenters to support their final revisions. The quality and thoughtfulness of your feedback contributes to your Participation grade. Here is a brief timetable for the projects: c. By Week 2: Find a collaborator or obtain permission from the instructor to work on an individual project. d. By Week 5: Submit a short (half-page) description of your proposed project and a feasible plan for carrying out the research. e. By Week 10: Submit a brief (no longer than 5 page) page memo of your main results, including tables, figures, and brief analysis. For methodological projects, this should include a description of the method and any analytical/simulation results. You will be required to give feedback on another group’s project, which will be counted toward the overall grade based on attentiveness and usefulness of the feedback provided. f. By Week 15: Submit your final version of the project. 6 COURSE SCHEDULE: Week Topics Reading 1 Introduction and Potential Outcomes: - Neyman-Rubin causal model - Fundamental problem of causal inference (FPOCI) - Causal estimands - Post-treatment bias under the truncation by death problem Group forming & Ice breaking activities. - Imbens & Rubin, Ch. 1 - Angrist & Pischke, Ch.1 - Holland, P. W. 1986. “Statistics and Causal Inference”. Journal of the American Statistical Association, Vol. 81, No. 396: 945- 960. 2 Randomization Inference: - Randomized experiments - Fisher’s approach to inference, permutation tests - Sharp null, randomization distribution Due: The Effect CH. 2 Research Questions Find a collaborator for the group project. - Imbens & Rubin, Ch. 5 (Skim Ch. 4 for some definitions.) - Rosenbaum, Paul R. 2002. Observational Studies. Springer- Verlag. 2nd edition. Ch. 2 3 Inference for the Average Treatment Effect: - Neyman’s approach to inference for the ATE - Finite-sample vs superpopulation inference Due: Problem Set 1 (Potential Outcomes); The Effect CH. 3 Describing Variables - Imbens & Rubin, Ch. 6, 9 (Skip 9.6–9.7), and 10 (Skip 10.6–10.7) - Angrist & Pischke: Ch. 2 4 Linear Regression and Randomized Experiments: - Simple linear regression in experiments - Covariate adjustment in experiments with regression Students’ Paper Introduction Presentations: 1.1. and 1.2. Due: Problem Set 2 (Randomization Inference); The Effect CH. 4 Describing Relationships - Imbens & Rubin, Ch. 7, 9 (9.6–9.7), and 10 (10.6–10.7) - Winston Lin. “Agnostic notes on regression adjustments to experimental data: Reexamining Freedman’s critique.” Ann. Appl. Stat. 7 (1) 295 - 318, March 2013. - Freedman, David. 2008. “On regression adjustments to experimental data.” 5 Observational Studies I: - Selection on observables - Regression for observational data Students’ Paper Introduction Presentations: 1.3. and 1.4. Due: Problem Set 3 (Inference for the ATE); The Effect CH. 13 Regression; Project Proposal - Angrist & Pischke, Ch. 3 7 6 Observational Studies II: - DAGs and the back-door criterion - Sensitivity analysis - Partial identification Construct a DAG for your own research project! - Imbens & Rubin, Ch. 21 and 22 - Morgan & Winship, Ch. 4 7 In-Class Group Project Meetings (30 minutes per group): The purpose of the meetings is to help each group materialize their ideas/topics for the group project. Due: The Effect CH. 6 Causal Diagrams, CH. 7 Drawing Causal Diagrams 8 Instrumental Variables I: - Noncompliance in randomized experiments - Instrumental variables in observational studies Students’ Paper Introduction Presentations: 2.1. and 2.2. Due: Problem Set 4 (Observational Studies); The Effect CH. 8 Causal Paths and Closing Back Doors - Imbens & Rubin, Ch. 23 and 24 - Angrist & Pischke, Ch. 4 9 Instrumental Variables II: - Two-stage least squares - Review of IV applications Students’ Paper Introduction Presentations: 2.3. and 2.4. 10 Panel Data, Fixed Effects, and Difference-in- Differences: - Fixed effects and first differences - Difference-in-differences Students’ Paper Introduction Presentations: 3.1. and 3.2. docs.text: Updated 2025/12/7 研究方法 Research Methods Instructor:許裴舫 Hsu, Pei-Fang Time: 1:20 PM - 4:20 PM, Friday Email:pfhsu@iss.nthu.edu.tw Classroom: TSMC Room 406 TA: Email: Course Overview The goal of this course is to provide students with an introduction to research processes. We will introduce fundamental elements of scientific research to help students execute their theses. Using good journal papers as examples, we will illustrate research methods such as survey, experiment, and qualitative analysis that are frequently used in management area. In the end of the semester, students will be able to 1. Acquire skills to locate researchable questions in business; 2. Conduct research to solve the identified questions; 3. Get conversant with the use of statistical analysis; 4. Develop skills to discriminate “good” from “bad” research. It is hoped that students will find research to be interesting and of practical use. Textbook Required: Roger Bougie & Uma Sekaran, Research Methods for Business: A Skill Building Approach, 8th edition, John Wiley & Sons Inc. (滄海書局代理) Course materials and assignment: online folder https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1sSwKLolfJFZWtqrOp7JyDBekHgmnEFKb 固定線上上課網址： https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87554972600?pwd=RkVmJnvXx1Mfnhpm1oubnbEGU0MjX7.1 Grading (Individual) Class Participation 25% Final Exam 25% (Group) Final Project (research paper) 25% Weekly Presentations 25% **(Peer evaluation will be used in the end of the semester.) ** (Do not miss class more than 2 times during the semester. Email professor before class if you need to be absent.) Rule for students use of the AI: Conditionally open. Additional credits are given for students who clearly report how they use AI in a helpful way for course assignments. Final Project (Research Paper) Please form a group of 5 members. Four groups in total.  Two groups will co-work with two companies respectively to analyze real business problems. docs.text: 1 Title: ISS 581100-3 Organizational Behavior Chinese Class Title: 組織行為 Time: Friday, 1:20 – 4:20 PM Course Conditions: (1) The course is offered in English. (2) Priority is given to IMBA and ISS students. o Brief course description: Organizations are rapidly evolving from human-centric hierarchies to hybrid systems where algorithms, AI, and people collaborate. This course offers an advanced exploration of Organizational Behavior (OB) through a dual lens: foundational behavioral science and emerging digital reality. We will structure our inquiry around two critical questions: (1) How do we navigate the individual? We examine the psychology of performance, motivation, and decision-making to resolve the friction between human needs and algorithmic efficiency. (2) How do we architect the environment? We explore how to design cultures, teams, and leadership structures that foster innovation and psychological safety in a hybrid world. By integrating evidence-based management theories with critical analyses of generative AI and automation, this course equips IMBA students to move beyond traditional management and become adept architects of the human-AI organization. Keywords: Organizational Behavior, Human-AI Collaboration, AI Leadership Strategies, Algorithmic Management, Future of Work o Course Learning Objectives: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: 1. Diagnose organizational dynamics: Apply evidence-based OB frameworks (e.g., Justice Theory, Job Characteristics Model) to diagnose root causes of performance and commitment issues in complex, cross-cultural environments. 2. Lead in the hybrid age: Formulate leadership strategies that balance human empathy with data-driven insights, navigating the tensions of algorithmic management, surveillance, and remote work. 3. Make evidence-based decisions: Mitigate cognitive biases in human decision-making and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs to solve unstructured business problems effectively. 4. Architect high-performance teams: Design team structures and processes that leverage 2 diversity (surface and deep-level) and human-machine collaboration to minimize process loss and maximize innovation. 5. Navigating ethical ambiguity: Critically assess the ethical implications of emerging technologies, such as privacy, bias, and autonomy, and advocate for responsible management practices that protect employee well-being. 6. Develop self-awareness: Synthesize feedback from peers, self-assessments, and reflection to construct a personal “Leadership Profile” that identifies unique strengths and growth areas for a career in a globalized market. Course Delivery Mode: Each class will follow a seminar format. Students are expected to complete all required readings beforehand and come prepared to actively engage in discussions. o Weekly Schedule WK Dates Topics 1 2/27 ⚫ National Holiday (no class); ⚫ a recorded video will be available on the course website: o Introduction to the course & What’s OB (Chapter 1) 2 3/6 ⚫ Job performance (Chapter 2) ⚫ Augmentation vs. Automation 3 3/13 ⚫ Organizational Commitment (Chapter 3) & Job satisfaction (Chapter 4) ⚫ Algorithmic management 4 3/20 • Motivation (Chapter 5) & Stress (Chapter 6) • AI for wellbeing 5 3/27 • Learning and decision-making (Chapter 8) • Collective intelligence: Human and AI 6 4/3 National Holiday (no class) 7 4/10 • Leadership: Power, Politics, and Influences (Chapter 13) • Algorithmic authority 8 4/17 • Leadership Styles and Behaviors (Chapter 14) • The human-in-the-loop 9 4/24 • Trust, Justice, and Ethics (Chapter 7) • Fair & responsible AI 10 5/1 National Holiday (no class) 11 5/8 • Personality (Chapter 9) & Ability (Chapter 10) • Reskilling: Cognitive/Emotional vs. Artificial Intelligence 12 5/15 • Team: Characteristics & Diversity (Chapter 11) • Human-machine teaming 13 5/22 • Team: Processes &Communication (Chapter 12) • AI-mediated communication 14 5/29 • Organizational Structure & culture (Chapter 15&16) • Algorithmic culture management 15 6/5 Presentation (Session A) 16 6/12 Presentation (Session B) Course Wrap-Up & Integration 3 * The course schedule provided is tentative and may be subject to changes. o Learning Resources • Mandatory readings: (1) Colquitt, J. A., LePine, J. A., & Wesson, M. J. (2025). Organizational behavior: Improving performance and commitment in the workplace (9th ed.). McGraw- Hill Education. a. The textbook can be purchased from https://eshop.hwatai.com.tw/SalePage/Index/10721244 b. The library offers access to an electronic copy (8th edition), allowing for a maximum of three concurrent users at any given time https://nthu.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/permalink/886UST_NTHU/13efpo 6/alma9957482017406774 • There will be additional readings for weekly topics. The detailed information will be available on the course website (Canvas) later. o Assessment Requirement Due Date Weight Professionalism and Engagement 1. “Hot Seat” (once) (10%) 2. Peer feedback (once) (5 %) 3. Overall contribution (10%) 1&2: Varied by individual team’s schedule 3: Continuous 25% Leadership profile development: Analysis and Reflections Week 10 15% Seminar Facilitation (50 minutes) Varied by individual team’s schedule 15% Team research project Proposal (Week 6) 10% Presentation (Week 15 & 16) 15% Group submission (Week 16 ) 20% Notes: (1) Specific due dates and detailed assignment briefs, along with grading guidelines, will be provided on the course website; the due dates are tentative and will be confirmed by Week 2. (2) Assignments should be submitted according to the procedures specified in the assignment briefs that are posted on the course website; (3) Professionalism and Engagement: Class discussions are central to the learning experience in this course, as they allow you to learn collaboratively by engaging with the assigned readings and each other's insights. Active participation goes beyond simply sharing your thoughts; it involves thoughtful engagement with the material, your peers, and the overarching themes of the course. To foster this dynamic, we will implement a “Hotseat” participation model. While everyone is encouraged to contribute to discussions, each week, 4-5 students will take on a leadership role. These students will be expected to share their perspectives, explain key concepts, respond to questions, and facilitate small- group breakout discussions. If you are scheduled for the Hot Seat and are absent or unprepared without prior notice, you forfeit the 10% grade. Further details about the “Hotseat” model will be provided in our first class session. 4 (4) Session facilitation: Each of you will be assigned to a 4-5 person team and will assume the role of facilitator for one session (approximately 50 minutes) during the course. The topic and specific instruction will be discussed in the first class. o Extension: For individual assignments, students have four slip days across the course that will be granted automatically. Any further extensions will only be granted in exceptional personal circumstances and should be negotiated with the course coordinator before the deadline whenever possible. Documentation (e.g., medical certificate) may be requested. o Penalties: Late submissions will incur an automatic penalty of 10% of the final mark per day. o Generative AI Policy: Augmentation, Not Automation In this course, we treat Generative AI (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Notebook LLM) as a collaborative teammate, not a ghostwriter. You are not just permitted to use these tools; you are encouraged to use them to elevate your thinking. However, you must adhere to the Human-in-the-Loop principle: AI may generate the raw material, but you must be the architect, editor, and final decision-maker. ✓ Green Light (Encouraged) o Brainstorming: e.g., “Act as a devil's advocate and critique my argument.” o Simulations: e.g., “Roleplay an angry employee reacting to this new policy.” o Editing: e.g., “Suggest ways to make this paragraph more concise.” o Synthesis: e.g., “Summarize the key differences between these two academic papers.” ✓ Red Light (Prohibited) o Copy-Pasting Analysis: You cannot submit AI text as your own critical thought. o Fact-Blindness: You are 100% responsible for the accuracy of your submission. If the AI hallucinates a fact or citation and you submit it, it is treated as an academic integrity violation. o Replacing Reflection: AI cannot write your Personal Leadership Reflection. Those insights must be yours. ✓ Mandatory Documentation (Transparency): If you use AI for any assignment, you must append an AI Disclosure Statement at the end of your document. Failure to disclose AI use is considered academic dishonesty. Format: o Tool Used: (e.g., ChatGPT-4o) o Purpose: (e.g., “I asked ChatGPT to identify three logical weaknesses in my argument. I then rewrote Section 3 to address those gaps using evidence from the Colquitt textbook.”) o The Prompts: (Briefly summarize 1-2 key prompts you used). o The Human Value-Add: (e.g., I accepted the AI’s structure but rewrote the analysis to include specific class concepts.) ✓ The Oral Defense Consequence: To ensure authenticity, the instructor reserves the right to conduct a random or targeted Oral Examination. If you cannot explain the logic, theory, or vocabulary used in your written submission without referencing the document, you may receive a score of zero, regardless of AI disclosure.

docs.text: Well-Being & Wise Decisions, Spring 2026 (11420ISS 581701) Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) Offered by Andrew Yeh, Qualified MBSR Teacher & Profs. G Shmueli (ISS) and L Fung (Econ) This evidence-based course provides participants with mindfulness training to enhance awareness, focus, manage stress, and improve decision-making in high-pressure environments. Cultivating mindfulness supports thriving in dynamic study and work environments while maintaining balance and clarity in one’s personal and professional life. The mindfulness-based stress reduction program (MBSR) originated from the stress reduction clinic at the University of Massachusetts Medical School and later transformed into the Center for Mindfulness at UMass. Thousands of scientific studies have confirmed the MBSR program helps with: ● Increasing focus and work efficiency ● Reducing stress ● Enhancing emotional awareness and regulation ● Improving sleep quality ● Alleviating symptoms of anxiety, depression, panic, etc. ● Easing chronic pain and enhancing quality of life ● Boosting immunity Cultivating mindfulness brings healing and profound transformation, allowing us to reclaim our lives rather than just existing in an ivory tower or self-imposed cage. Mindfulness practice enables us to draw from and enjoy the source of our own lives with our own strength. It helps us regain the ability to choose and self-affirm, nurturing a sense of groundedness and joy from within. For over 40 years, MBSR training has continued to expand into various fields such as medicine, psychology, education, business, sports, and even politics. This MBSR course is the most important and critical prototype of contemporary mindfulness training. Mindfulness training programs have been adopted by many international and Taiwan corporations including: *This course uses a pass/fail grading system per Article 27.1.5 of the academic regulations. It only counts for credit hours and is not included in the calculation of the GPA. Course format: 1 credit pass/fail* Requirements: Full attendance: 11 weekly sessions (2/25-5/20), Day of Mindfulness (4/11), (max 2 missed sessions after add/drop period); Weekly practice journal & class surveys. Resources: Will be distributed in class Optional reading: Full Catastrophe Living by Jon Kabat-Zinn Suitable Participants (priority given to international students) ● Those seeking to enhance emotional awareness and management skills ● Wanting to improve focus and work efficiency ● In high-pressure work or living environments ● Wishing to improve interpersonal relationships ● Experiencing sleep problems ● Easily prone to tension, anxiety, worry, and panic ● Prone to depression, low mood, and negative thinking ● Facing chronic fatigue or chronic pain issues ● Desiring self-care and tranquility of body and mind ● Eager for self-growth and deeper self-understanding Course Features | In-person ● Small class teaching, catering to each student ● In-person teaching for authentic interaction ● Group dynamics for shared exchange and growth ● Exclusive group for ongoing inquiries and discussions ● Weekly classes for steady progress ● Practice resources: free, abundant, uninterrupted ● Exclusive certification, shared learning, and continued practice Course Outline 2/25 Preparatory Class: Embarking on the treasure hunt Understanding what mindfulness and mindfulness-based stress reduction are Understanding the path of mindfulness learning Mindfulness acquaintance 3/4 Class #1: Are you kind to yourself? docs.text: 1 Well-Being & Wise Decisions, Spring 2026 (11420ISS 581702) 正念減壓課程 (MBSR) Andrew Yeh 葉懷佩, 合格正念老師, 以及 服科所 邱議德 和 科法所 林勤富 教授 這門以科學實證為基礎的課程將教導參與者運用正念技巧，以增強內在覺察、提升專注力、有 效管理壓力，並改善在高壓環境下的決策能力。修習正念，將有助於您在快速變動的學習與工 作場域中發展與成長，同時在個人與專業生活之間，保有平衡與澄明。 【課程介紹】 正念減壓課程 Mindfulness-based stress reduction program (MBSR)，始於美國麻州大學 醫學院的減壓門診，後轉型為麻大正念中心。至今，數千項的科學實證研究證實正念減壓課程 有助於： • 提升睡眠品質 • 緩解焦慮、憂鬱、恐慌等症狀 • 紓解壓力 • 緩和慢性疼痛提升生活品質 • 提升情緒覺察與調節能力 • 促進免疫力 • 提升專注力與工作效能 【 正念培育，帶來療癒與深層的轉化】 培養正念，能帶來療癒與深層的轉化。它讓我們得以重拾生命的主導權，而非僅是侷限於象牙 塔或自我設下的牢籠中。透過正念練習，我們能運用自身的覺察力，找到並培養內在的穩定力 量以及體驗內在的生命泉源；它幫助我們重拾選擇的能力與自我肯定的價值，培育由內而外的 踏實與喜悅。 課程形式：1 學分，通過/不通過制 「本課程採通過制評分方式，依學則第 27 條 第 1 項第五款採通過、不通過之方式評定者，僅列計學分數，不列入平均成績計算。」 要求: 1. 全程參與：11 次每週課程（2/25-5/20）、正念日（4/12）、(加 退選截止後，最多允許缺席 2 次)； 2. 每週練習日誌與課堂問卷。 資源：將於課堂中分發 選讀書籍：《正念療癒力》（Jon Kabat-Zinn 著；胡君梅翻譯） 2 四十多年來，因著正念本身所蘊含的豐沛療育力量，正念減壓訓練的應用已擴展至諸多領域， 例如：醫療界、心理界、教育界、商業界、運動界，甚至是政治界。本正念減壓課程，正是當 代正念訓練最重要與關鍵的原型。 目前，許多國際知名企業與台灣本地公司皆已導入正念訓練計畫，例如： 【適合對象】 • 有睡眠困擾 • 容易感到緊張、焦慮、擔憂或恐慌 • 容易陷入憂鬱、低落情緒或負面思考 • 身處高壓工作或生活環境 • 有慢性疲勞、慢性疼痛問題 • 希望增進情緒覺察與管理能力 • 希望提升專注力與工作/學習效能 • 想要改善人際相處及關係 • 想要學習照顧和善待自己，尋求身心安穩 • 期待自我成長，想更深入認識自己 【課程特色｜實體】 • 小班教學，兼顧每位學員 • 實體教學，真實的互動 • 運用團體動力，促進學員交流與共同成長 • 提供課後線上群組，協助提問與討論 • 每週上課，按部就班、穩紮穩打 • 免費且不間斷的練習資源 • 結業證書，鼓勵共好學習與持續練習 3 上課大綱 2/25 【預備課程】: • 開啟挖寶之旅 • 認識正念與正念減壓是什麼。認識正念 學習的路徑 • 正念會友 3/4 【第一堂課】: • 你對自己友善嗎 • 學習對自己產生溫柔的連結。發現慣性 與新的可能 • 身體掃描，飲食靜觀 3/11 【第二堂課】: • 溫柔，從對自己開始 • 靜態身體覺察。如何看待壓力，決定壓 力如何發展 • 身體掃描，呼吸覺察 3/18 【第三堂課】: • 開心，未必需要外求 • 靜態身體覺察。累積情緒存款。看到理 所當然 • 正念瑜珈，行走靜觀 3/25【第四堂課】: • 溫柔趨近，更多看見 • 動態與靜態的身心覺察。溫柔安全地拆 解壓力 • 正念瑜珈，靜坐 4/1【第五堂課】: • 由裡而外的安穩力量 • 動態與靜態的身心覺察。許自己一個廣闊 的天空 • 五層次靜坐 4/8 【第六堂課】: • 你真的會溝通嗎 • 拆解溝通要素，學習簡單有效能的溝通方 式 • 正念溝通 【一日靜觀】: 4/12 (Sunday) • 增強正念覺察的功力 • 學習不間斷的覺察。發展成為自己的好朋 友 • 各項練習 4/15 【第七堂課】: • 來些學理與科研吧 • 從慣性反應，到有覺察的回應。拆解壓力 的發展歷程 • 正念瑜珈，靜坐 5/6-5/20 【第八-十堂課】: • 收好智慧與覺察的寶藏 • 回顧與展望。後續學習資源分享與討論 • 身體掃描，靜坐

docs.name: 色彩學
docs.text: 課程資訊 (Course Information) 科號 Course Number JAD1131 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Size of Limit 50 中文名稱 Course Title 色彩學 英文名稱 Course English Title Chromatology 任課教師 Instructor 謝翠如 上課時間 Time 上課教 室 Room 課程大綱 (Syllabus) 一、 課程說明(Course Description) 色彩學是視覺藝術及各類型視覺設計的造型元素，本課程將透過觀察色彩現象、原理講授、設 計實作，介紹色彩學的基本知識，以及色彩學在設計、創藝術以及產業的應用。Chromatology is a fundamental element of visual arts and various types of visual design. This course will introduce basic knowledge of chromatology through observing color phenomena, principles, and design implementation, as well as its applications in design, creative arts, and industries. 二、 Keywords: color science, color vision, colorimetry, color planning 關鍵字: 色彩視覺、混色原理、色彩體系、色彩計畫 color science, color vision, colorimetry, color planning, color planning) 三、 指定用書(Text Books) 色彩新論：從心理設計到科學應用(五南) (New Theory: From Psychological Design to Scientific Application) 四、 參考書籍(References) Best, J. (Ed.). (2017). Colour design: theories and applications. Sherin, A. (2012). Design elements, Color fundamentals: A graphic style manual for understanding how color affects design. Rockport Publishers. Holtzschue, L. (2012). Understanding color: an introduction for designers. John Wiley & Sons. Bleicher, S. (2023). Contemporary color: Theory and use. Routledge. Becker, D. docs.name: 素描二
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11420JAD 120500 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 素描二 英文名稱 Course English Title Drawing II 任課教師 Instructor 紀宇芳 上課時間 Time W7W8 上課教室 Room Nanda 南大 8601 ／容量 55 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程將延續基礎素描表現能力之訓練，進一步延展至對於周遭物體、植物與空間的認識、捕捉 與表達。下學期課程裡將透過練習、鑑賞與實作等方式，探討素描的開放性與可能性。 透過形體觀察與描繪、光影明暗的比較與捕捉、肌理材質的構造、空間透視的層次與準確度，以 及概念的延展與呈現…，引導學生領略不同材質形態及空間觀察的表現手法，逐步發展、建立 美感思維，提升學生獨立思考與創作意識。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 素描、繪畫、光影、正負空間、透視圖法 Drawing, sketch, light and shadow, positive space, negative space, perspective. 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 延續上學期對於素描基礎特性與材料、技法的認識，本課將進一步培養學生敏銳的觀察力與描繪 能力，透過自然植物、肌理質感、建築空間、風景寫生等主題，開展對於素描本質的探索與表 現。除了引導學生們更加熟悉造形原理與光影明暗關係，同時也更深入領略不同材質形態的變化 以及空間、風景的深度與表現方式，融合獨立思考與概念發展，逐步奠定未來創作的基礎。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 本課程採自編教材。 ● 參考書籍(References) ．東京武藏野美術學院，鍾江村譯（2016）。《鉛筆素描：圖解基礎技法・掌握素描訣竅。鉛 筆デッサン》，台北：笛藤出版。 ．基特 懷特 著，林容年 譯（2019）。《藝術的法則：101 張圖瞭解繪畫、探究創作，學習大 師的好作品》。台北：木馬。 ．陳秋瑾（1999）。《素描與創作》。臺北：國立編譯館。 ．雷‧史密斯 著，劉婷婷 譯（2020）。《藝術家手冊：工具×材料×步驟×技法，從零開始，全 面剖析藝術創作者的專業領域》。臺北：漢湘文化。 ．游二川（2011）。《绘画材料与技法研究》。四川：重慶大學出版社。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 教師講授指導、案例賞析、學生實務練習創作、課堂討論及相互觀摩…等。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 課程由數個實踐單元進行素描技巧與概念延展，每二~三週為一個小單元，每一單元長度依照班 級學生作品完整度調整課程進度，如遇國定假日與校際活動週將進行彈性調動。 第 1 週：課程說明 第 2-4 週：植物的觀察與捕捉/私人空間、室內空間的表現。 第 5-7 週：自然景物、戶外環境寫生。 第 8-10 週：建築體與人造空間的觀察與描繪。 第 11-13 週：集合創作計畫。 第 14-15 週：概念傳達與創作表現。 第 16 週：期末作品分享發表。Final Project Presentation *課程安排依實際授課情形作調整，戶外寫生將依天候情況進行調動。 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 期中作品 30%；期末作品 30%；日常速寫 10% 作業進度、出缺席、課堂討論與學習態度 30% (服學夥伴額外加分練習) *缺課超過三次以上者(包含事假、病假等)，上課出缺席成績將以 0 分計。 *請假須提前依校方規則進行線上申請，請自行參閱<國立清華大學學生請假辦法>。 *課堂遲到、作品遲交、缺交，將嚴重影響學期成績。 *手機使用原則，課堂中請務必關閉手機鈴聲，如非必要勿使用。 ● 敘明學生使用 AI 的規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當中。 因本課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使用， 以下為相關的監管機制： ◼ 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個 人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予 計分。 ◼ 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website)

docs.name: 媒材與應用二
docs.text: 國立清華大學 課程大綱 媒材與應用 二 藝設創作組一年級 學分數：2 時間：週一 5、6 節 教室：8213 (平面一) 授課教師：梁莉苓 /E-mail: liling_liang@mx.nthu.edu.tw 一、課程概述 本課程規劃「異質媒材的應用練習」單元，藉藝術作品案例的選擇與解析中，引 導學生能尋找創作學習資源，自現當代作品的認識中，累積媒材與應用創作知能；且 能審視創作實驗優缺點，發想創作計畫及思考問題解決辦法，培養自主學習的創作實 踐能力。 二、教學進度 週次 課程內容 備註 1 2/23 課程介紹 ▸選小老師、分組 2 3/2 藝術作品案例的擇選與解析 1. 學習方法探討 2. 創作學習經驗的分享 3. 學生簡報與討論 ▸邀請藝術家演講 ▸一或二人一組製作簡報報告（第 4-6 週） 3 3/9 4 3/16 5 3/23 6 3/30 7 4/6 民族掃墓節補假 8 4/13 異質媒材的媒合技巧初探 9 4/20 異質媒材的創作實驗 1.實驗成果的自我檢討 2.創作計畫確認與討論 ▸自作品案例的選取與解析中衍生創作計 畫。創作實驗與作品製作可選擇採一或二 人一組進行。 10 4/27 11 5/4 作品製作與進度討論 12 5/11 13 5/18 14 5/25 15 6/1 期末作品評分與檢討 ▸期末創作共審於第十六週週四進行。 16 6/8 註 1：以上進度會依課程推進與學生學習的狀況調整。 註 2：創作討論與評分，需課後輔導如補看或加強討論同學，於課前 12:50~13:10 進行，不宜佔 用當週討論上課時間。 註 3：期末作品評分，需布展呈現作品同學，須在助教 TA 安排時段內，課前提早布展。 三、成績評量 （一）實驗製作、作品與報告。(60%) （二）校外參訪心得，自行參訪。(10%） （三）上課參與和其他隨堂表現 (30%) （四） 其它： a. 缺課或遲到將被扣分，無論假別達（含）五次未到課，學期成績不及 格；請依照學校請假規定線上申請，相關規定自行參閱參閱〈國立清 華大學學生請假辦法〉。（分組討論當週未到課需下週補課，否則算兩 次未到課。） b. 評量僅接受經上課討論的作品。 c. 本課程作業原則上不接受使用生成式人工智慧，除與作業主題相關， 且須在作業中註明運用的部分與方式。若非以上特例，若經查核發 現，教師有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。修讀本課程 之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 四、參考書籍 賴瑛瑛著，《台灣前衛：六○年代複合藝術》，台北市：遠流，2003。 賴瑛瑛著，《台灣現代美術大系──複合媒體藝術》，台北市：文建會， 2004。 Celine Delavaux、Christian Demilly 著，陳羚芝譯，《當代藝術這麼說》，台北 市：典藏藝術家庭，2015。 Eddie Wolfram 著，傅嘉琿譯，《拼貼藝術之歷史》，台北市：遠流，1991。 WillyRotzler 著，吳瑪悧譯，《物體藝術》，台北市：遠流，1991。 Michael Bird 著，吳莉君譯，《改變藝術的 100 個觀念》，台北市：臉譜， 2014。 教師自編寫簡報、講義或教材。 其它與個人創作或本課程單元相關之書籍、文章與網站等。

docs.name: 油畫二
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number JAD 120700 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 50 中文名稱 Course Title 油畫二 英文名稱 Course English Title Oil Painting II 任課教師 Instructor 吳宇棠 Wu, Yu-Tang 上課時間 Time W3W4 上課教室 Room 南大 8601 課程簡述： 本課程以風景寫生與人物習作為主，並規劃相關題材創作進度。 風景寫生教學重點在於戶外自 然光與空氣感的掌握； 人物習作重點為造形正確性、相關筆法操作與膚色調控。 課程關鍵字：油畫，肖像，風景，材料技法，光學色 課程大綱 課程說明： 本課程以風景寫生與人物習作為主，並規劃相關題材創作進度。 風景寫生教學重點在於戶外自 然光與空氣感的掌握； 人物習作重點為造形正確性、相關筆法操作與膚色調控。 教學進度： 第一週 課程說明；人物畫法示範 第二~四週 人物習作甲 第五~六週 校園寫生 A 第七~九週 人物習作乙 第九週 期中作業評分 第十~十一週 校園寫生 B 第十二~十四週 敘事人物習作 第十五週 期末評分與檢討 第十六週 PPT 教學 成績考核： 期中與期末作品評分各佔 30%；課堂參與、作業進度與學習態度合佔 40% 修讀本門課程之學生應準時到課；缺課或遲到將被扣分。缺課（不論任何假別）達五次，學期成 績將不及格。 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的圖像、作業、報告或個 人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 參考書籍： 王勝。《西方傳統油畫三大技法》。臺北市：國立歷史博物館，2000。 胡國強。《藝用人體結構繪畫教學》。臺北市：新一代圖書，2010。 郭書瑄。《圖解藝術》。臺北市：易博士文化，2005。 陳淑華。《油畫材料學》。臺北市：洪葉文化，2000。 陳景容。《油畫的材料研究與實際應用-修定版》。臺北：大陸書店，2002。 貝蒂．愛德華。《像藝術家一樣活用色彩》。駱香潔譯。台北：木馬文化，2022。(Edwards, Betty. Color： A Course in Mastering the Art of Mixing Colors. New York: Jeremy P. Tarcher/Penguin, 2004.) 凱文．D.麥克弗森。《油畫的光與色：暢銷版》。趙春園、張曉怡譯。上海：上海人民美術， 2017。 (Macpherson, Kevin D.. Fill Your Oil Paintings with Light & Color. Cincinnati: North Light Books, 2000.) Brain Gorst。《油畫技法全集: 各種油畫表現技法的步驟解析》。顧何忠譯。臺北市：視傳文 化，2004。 Brief Course Description： The course focuses on landscape and portrait painting, and plans the creative progress of related themes. The teaching of landscape sketching focuses on the mastery of open-air light and aerial perspective; the focus of portrait study is the correctness of shape, the operation of related brushwork and the regulation of skin tone. Course keywords: oil painting, portrait, landscape, materials and techniques, optical color Detailed Course Syllabus Course Description： The course focuses on landscape and portrait painting, and plans the creative progress of related themes. The teaching of landscape sketching focuses on the mastery of open-air light and aerial perspective; the focus of portrait study is the correctness of shape, the operation of related brushwork and the regulation of skin tone. Syllabus： Week 1 Course introduction; Portrait painting demonstration Weeks 2-4 Portrait painting practice A Weeks 5-6 Open-air campus painting practice A Weeks 7-9 Portrait Painting Practice B Week 9 Mid-term assignments review Weeks 10-11 Open-air campus painting practice B Weeks 12-14 Narrative Figure Painting Practice Week 15 End-of-term assignments review ang scoring Week 16 The concept of oil painting study (PPT) Evaluation： Mid-term grading 30%; Final grading 30%; In-class participation 40% Students should come to class on time. Absences or late appearances will result in the deduction of points. Students will fail the course if more than five absences are recorded. References： Edwards, Betty. Color by Betty Edwards： A Course in Mastering the Art of Mixing Colors. New York: Jeremy P. Tarcher/Penguin, 2004. Macpherson, Kevin D.. Fill Your Oil Paintings with Light & Color. Cincinnati: North Light Books, 2000.

docs.name: 台灣美術史
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學藝術與設計學系 114 學年第 2 學期 台灣美術史 授課教師：張晴文 （創作組必修/一年級/2 小時 2 學分） ●課程說明 本課程以台灣美術發展史為講述內容，引導學生認識並思考台灣美術自史 前時代至今的發展歷程。授課方式採教師講授並配合展覽參訪，以社會學為核 心，注重各時期代表藝術家及藝術運動、藝術表現和時代社會背景的關聯性。 主要教材使用台灣美術史學者蕭瓊瑞等教授合著之《台灣美術史綱》，配合自編 教材於課堂教學，成績評量以課堂參與及出席狀況、小組報告、期中與期末考 成績為依據。教師配合課程訂定報告的主題，由修課學生組成小組共同討論、 準備，於課堂上發表。 這門課的目的不在於強迫大家記誦多少藝術家的姓名、作品名稱，甚至也 不是死背那些對於歷史事件的「刻板認知」。希望透過這門史學的美術專業課 程，讓各位學習如何以歷史思維來創造自我和過去的連結感，並且對過去、對 自己有更好的理解能力。以下是在面對這學期課程時，我希望學生能有的基本 認知： 1. 藝術不是真空存在世界上的，它牽涉時間和空間條件。 2. 請在台灣史的基礎上理解、思考台灣美術史。 3. 台灣做為移民社會，是一波又一波不同事物相會、移動、嘗試尋找共存 共處可能的地方，也就是充滿各式各樣「交會」的地點。 4. 歷史不是「已完結的結果」，而是「動態的互動過程」。 5. 比起斷定一件事意味著什麼，首先應該思考「它為何發生」。 ●課程大綱 週次 日期 課程內容 報告主題 1 2/18 課程說明： 2 2/25 最初的抵岸：史前時代文明與藝術 海權帝國、陸權帝國之下：明鄭時期、清帝 國時期的藝術 3 3/4 「我是台灣人，故想要表現出台灣的特色」 ──黃土水與藝術體制 (1) 石川欽一郎 4 3/11 寫生，細描，以及新女性的身影 (2) 陳進 2 5 3/18 台灣是台灣人的台灣：日治時期美術中的台 灣民族認同 6 3/25 日治時期基礎建設與畫家筆下的鄉土 (3) 李澤藩 7 4/1 法國經驗與台灣美術 (4) 楊三郎 8 4/8 民俗台灣，生活美學的提倡 (5) 立石鐵臣 9 4/15 期中考 10 4/22 生命的尊嚴，純粹的美學探索：在野力量的 伏流 (6) 張萬傳 11 4/29 二戰陰影下的台灣，以及「光復」的歡欣與 迅速惡化 (7) 郭柏川 12 5/6 反共復國基地與中華文化大旗下的美術建制 (8) 黃君璧 13 5/13 新藝術運動，以及五月畫會、東方畫會 (9) 劉國松 14 5/20 經濟奇蹟的幕後，國際孤兒與鄉土運動 (10) 洪通 15 5/27 民主化之後的藝術眾聲 16 6/3 期末考 ●指定教材 劉益昌、高業榮、傅朝卿、蕭瓊瑞（2009）。台灣美術史綱。台北：藝術家 出版社。 ●參考用書 1. 蕭瓊瑞（2013）。戰後台灣美術史。台北：藝術家出版社。 2. 莊瑞琳 總編（2022）。臺灣美術兩百年（上）：摩登時代。台北：春山出 版。 3. 莊瑞琳 總編（2022）。臺灣美術兩百年（下）：島嶼呼喚。台北：春山出 版。 4. 賴瑛瑛（2003）。台灣前衛：六○年代複合藝術。台北：遠流出版事業。 5. 陳翠蓮、吳乃德、胡慧玲（2013）。百年追求：台灣民主運動的故事。台 北：衛城出版。 6. 林偉盛（2019）。大航海時代。台北：玉山社。 7. 何義麟、蔡錦堂（2019）。台灣人的日本時代。台北：玉山社。 8. 李筱峰、薛化元（2019）。戰後台灣史。台北：玉山社。 ●評量方式 1. 出席、上課表現：20%。請假請依照本校請假辦法辦理。6 次以上缺席（含 3 各種請假）者，本項成績不及格。本課程期末考之出席規定依照前揭法規 辦理：學生於期中、期末考試不得請假。但因公、急病、分娩、近親喪 亡、臨時發生不可抗力或不可歸責於當事人之因素，應檢附相關證明文件 經任課教師同意。請準時出席課堂，經常遲到將導致扣分。上課時不應使 用手機，請將手機收妥。 2. 小組報告：30%。依照規範於指定週次報告，惟報告可能配合課程內容順 延週次。在報告週次未如期準備，將導致扣分。小組報告評分項目包括： 報告整體內容、簡報設計、口語表達、報告流暢度、台風、紙本綱要。 3. 期中考、期末考：各佔 25%。採現場筆試，考試日期如課綱所示，若有調 動教師將提前於課堂及 eeclass 公告。 ●小組報告 分組進行。依照教師指定之主題，須準備 A4 一頁之紙本題綱（須印製給 班上同學），並配合簡報軟體呈現。紙本格式與口頭報告形式不拘，鼓勵創新之 呈現方式。每一主題之報告時間為 20 分鐘。 嚴禁口頭報告照稿念誦。報告內容如違反學術倫理，該次以零分計算。請 注意：在報告時直接使用網路既有文章或拼貼網路文獻做為口頭講稿，亦屬不 當研究行為。 ●生成式人工智慧倫理聲明 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工 智慧於課堂學習當中。因本課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影 響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課 程採取禁止使用，以下為相關的監管機制。修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課 不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個人心得。若經查核發 現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.name: 基礎設計二
docs.text: 課程代碼：JAD130101 科目代碼： 課程名稱 中文：基本設計一(B) 必/選修 必修 Required 英文：Basic Design I (B) 課程類別 設計組 Design Group 開課單位 藝術與設計學系 Department of Arts and Design 學分數 credit 3 課程概述 本課程引導設計組學生習得認識基本視覺元素、圖形設計實作，並由基本設計專案培養對視覺形式與 美感原則的理解。本課程使用業界主流設計軟體做為教學示範，學生自備電腦、軟體、簡易手工具與 耗材。本課程以專案導向學習(Project-Based Learning)進行，本學期有三個專案(1)海報設計(2)個人 視覺識別設計(3)作品集排版設計，專案教學的流程：(1)介紹專案所需要認識的設計原理、設計元素 (2)作品觀摩、說明設計目標 (3)軟體技術示範 (4)學生實作練習 (5)個別討論與建議。學生期末應將習 作和專案製作成果進行排版設計、印刷、裝訂為實體作品集於本系共評展示。期末最後一周將作品 pdf 檔上傳至 eeclass 作業區(50%)，課堂筆記、作品發想、手繪草圖、嘗試與練習等整理為學習歷程報 告，於期末繳交 pdf 至 eeclass 作業區(50%)。 This course aims to equip design students with fundamental skills in design elements composition and production techniques. Students are required to bring their own computer and use leading industry design software. Each session includes understanding key design principles, reviewing and applying these principles through hands-on tasks, and revisions. Students' work will culminate in a portfolio (contributing 50% to the final grade), showcasing their progress. Additionally, a comprehensive learning journal (accounting for the remaining 50% of the grade), including class notes, idea development, sketches, and design insights, is to be submitted at the end of the term. 教學方式 設計原理說明、示範與案例觀摩、設計實作、作品討論 Explanation of design principles, demonstrations and case study reviews, hands-on design practice, and work discussions. 教學進度 第 01 週：課程介紹-授課方式、設計工具、學習目標 Week 01: Introduction - Teaching Methods, Materials and Tools, Learning Goals 第 02 週：設計元素-點的練習 Week 02: Design Elements - Practice on Points 第 03 週：設計元素-線的練習 Week 03: Design Elements - Practice on Lines 第 04 週：設計元素-幾何形狀的練習 Week 04: Design Elements - Practice on Geometric Shapes 第 05 週：設計元素-有機形狀的練習 Week 05: Design Elements - Practice on Organic Forms 第 06 週：作品 1-運用點、線、形狀的海報設計(城市或地方主題) Week 06: Design Work 1 - Modernist Style Poster Design (City or Region Theme) 第 07 週：設計元素-認識字體與字型 Week 07: Design Elements - Introducing Font and Typeface 第 08 週：設計元素-運用字體的圖案構成 Week 08: Design Elements - Practice on Font and Composition 第 09 週：設計元素-應用文字作為構成元素 Week 09: Design Elements- Using Text in composition 第 10 週：設計元素-認識圖像符號、圖示、標誌 Week 10: Design Elements- Introducing pictogram, icon, logo 第 11 週：設計元素-圖像符號、圖示、標誌 Week 11: Design Elements- Practice on pictogram, icon, logo 第 12 週：作品 2-個人視覺識別符號(logo design) Week 12: Design Work 2-Logo Design 第 13 週：設計元素-認識色彩與圖樣 Week 13: Design Elements- color and patterns 第 14 週：設計元素-練習階調與漸層網格設計 Week 14: Design Elements- practice on coloring and mesh grradient 第 15 週：現代平面設計風格與排版設計 Week 15: Modern Graphic Design Styles and Layout Design 第 16 週：認識平面設計的輸出方法：印刷、雷刻與雷雕 Week 16: Introducing Printing and Lasor Cutting 第 17 週：作品 3-成果作品集排版設計 Week 17: Design Work 3 - Portfolio Layout Design 第 18 週：作品集展示與討論 Week 18: Portfolio Exhibition, Discussion 成績考核 一、期末共評及作品集 50% Portfolio: 50% 二、學習歷程報告 50% Learning Progress Report: 50%

docs.name: 基礎設計二
docs.text: 國立清華⼤學課程⼤綱 科號 Course Number 學分 Credit 3 ⼈數限制 Class Size 中⽂名稱 Course Title 基礎設計⼆ 英⽂名稱 Course English Title Basic Design II 任課教師 Instructor 陳如薇 上課時間 Time 週四 15:30-18:20 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中⽂字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程為設計的基礎開端，學⽣將學習如何從平⾯設計圖中轉換成立體模型，透過基本造形的演變、材質運⽤、 ⾊彩規劃、空間建構與設計情境等設計學習與實作練習，使同學具備未來進⾏設計之基礎能⼒。 本課程強調啟發性、實踐性和實驗性，讓學⽣養成於設計性向的啟發與美學認知的養成，課程以"基礎立體構成"的 課程將為學⽣提供⼀個全⾯的立體設計基礎，幫助他們從立體的⾓度來理解和設計產品，設計教學上著重於材 料、尺⼨、⼒學、結構、表⾯處理等內容，透過單⼀材質運⽤建構立體構成，運⽤綜合練習並透過不斷實踐和創 新來不斷提升⾃⼰的設計能⼒，並建立對產品設計的基本認知。 Three-Dimensional Form Making This course serves as an essential introduction to design, guiding students in transforming two- dimensional drawings into three-dimensional models. Through exercises in basic form development, material application, color planning, spatial construction, and contextual design, students will develop foundational skills necessary for future design work. The course emphasizes inspiration, practice, and experimentation. It aims to foster students’ design sensibility and aesthetic awareness. Centered on the theme of “Fundamental Three-Dimensional Composition,” the curriculum provides a comprehensive foundation in spatial and product-oriented thinking. Instruction focuses on material characteristics, dimensions, mechanics, structure, and surface treatment. Students will construct three-dimensional forms using single materials, complete integrated exercises, and continuously improve their design capabilities through hands-on practice and creative exploration. By the end of the course, students will have established essential competencies and fundamental understanding required for product design. 課程內容「中⽂暨英⽂關鍵字」(必填) ⾄少 5 個,每個關鍵字⾄多 20 個中⽂,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 基礎立體構成、形體認識、立體構成、材料特性、實踐性和實驗性 Basic three-dimensional composition, Shape recognition, Three-dimensional construction techniques, Material properties, Practicality and experimentation 課程⼤綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus l 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程為設計的基礎開端，學⽣將學習如何從平⾯設計圖中轉換成立體模型，透過基本造形的演變、材質運⽤、 ⾊彩規劃、空間建構與設計情境等設計學習與實作練習，使同學具備未來進⾏設計之基礎能⼒。 l 指定⽤書(Text Books) 無 l 參考書籍(References) 1. 設計基礎構成，孫媛媛、呂太鋒、席麗莎 2. 設計基礎原理：立體造形與構成，林崇宏 3. 基本設計概論 (Focus on designing)，張建成編譯，六合出版社 4. 基礎設計 (The Basic Principles of Visual Communication for Artists, Architects, and Designers) ，張建 成編譯，六合出版社 l 教學⽅式(Teaching Method) 個案教學 Case study、實作⽰範 Demonstration or Practice、作業發表 Presentation、作品整理 Portfolio l 繪圖⼯具 (Sketch Tools) 平⾯與立體材料 l 教學進度(Syllabus) Week 1-2 l 課程⽬標和內容簡介/理論剖析案例分享 l 立體構成概念造型原理 l 基本幾何形狀和曲⾯形體的認識和應⽤ Week 3-5 立體造型 l 立體構成美學原理 l 基本設計立體化⽅法和技巧 l 平⾯與立體構成的基礎技巧練習 Week 6-7 材料特性和使⽤⽅法 l 常⽤材料的特性和使⽤⽅法，如塑料、紙材等 l 材料選擇對設計影響的分析和應⽤、材料選擇 Week 8-11 造型實驗性與實踐性(作品⼆) l 設計⼀概念發展 l 立體構成實作 l 作品發表 Week 12-16 造型實驗性與實踐性 (作品三) l 設計⼆概念發展 l ⼩組討論 l 立體構成實作 l 作品發表 l 成績考核(Evaluation) 設計表現能⼒ - 總成績 40% （ 作業、課堂練習 ） 設計整合表現能⼒ - 總成績 40% ( 期中、期末報告設計項⽬ ) 設計熱誠 - 總成績 20% ( 課程參與出席率 10%、學習態度與學習回饋 10% ) l 課程其他要求 (Other Requirements) 1. 請勿遲到與早退。 2. 發表嚴禁缺席，如有特殊事件，需請假。 3. 輕鬆學習但嚴謹之態度。 4. 課堂上保持⽣活素養與基本禮儀。 l 採⽤下列何項 AI 使⽤規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 本課程無涉及 AI 使⽤ Not applicable 可參考下列網⾴範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw l 可連結之網⾴位址 相關網⾴(Personal Website)

docs.name: 圖文創作
docs.text: 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程將以故事創作為起點，引導學生設計出屬於自己的角色，並進一步學習以下內容： 1. 繪本故事創作的原則：從情節構建到角色塑造，探索故事的核心與結構。 2. 插畫角色設計的理論與繪圖技巧：學習如何設計出具有吸引力與獨特性的角色形象。 3. 插畫美術場景的構圖：掌握場景構圖的方法，營造氛圍與故事性。 4. 插畫創作中的光影與色彩研究：深入了解光影與色彩理論，並將其應用於插畫製作中。 5. 插畫與圖文市場的介紹：分析插畫市場趨勢，學習如何讓作品適應市場需求。 課程最終目標是讓學生完成自己的第一個插畫圖文創作，並學習進入社群媒體行銷的基本技巧， 為未來以圖文創作進軍插畫市場打下基礎。 ●參考書籍(References) 一、色彩與光線，詹姆士‧葛爾尼，如何出版。 二、創意插畫聖經，安德魯‧路米斯，讀書共和國 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 一、理論講述與討論(30%) 二、個案分析與作品賞析(20%) 三、行動實作與報告(50%) ●教學進度(Syllabus) 週次 日期 課程內容 備註 1 2026/02/24 學期課程大綱介紹。 簡單課程與學習重點介紹 2 2026/03/03 基本繪本故事創作原則與方式 理論講解、學生課堂實做 3 2026/03/10 繪本故事中的圖文配合 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 4 2026/03/17 插畫角色設計概念介紹 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 5 2026/03/24 角色設計線稿要點介紹、角色設計的 表情與動態姿勢設計 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 6 2026/03/31 角色設計五視圖設計 作業講評討論、課堂示範、 學生課堂實做 7 2026/04/07 角色設計上色要點介紹 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 8 2026/04/14 插畫構圖原則分析與討論。 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 9 2026/04/21 基礎透視原則與案例介紹討論 作業講評討論、課堂示範、 學生課堂實做 10 2026/04/28 各種打光原則與案例介紹討論。 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 11 2026/05/05 色彩理論介紹與案例分享討論。 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 12 2026/05/12 插畫完稿方式介紹 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 13 2026/05/19 小說封面插畫介紹與插畫家作品分享 與討論。 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 14 2026/05/26 插畫市場經營介紹與討論：插畫職場 經驗於實務分享 作業講評討論、理論講解、 學生課堂實做 15 2026/06/02 期末作品集報告與講評 學生口頭報告與討論 16 2026/06/09 期末作品集報告與講評 學生口頭報告與討論 ●成績考核(Evaluation) 一、作業表現評量(60%) 二、期末報告(30%) 三、上課參與(10%) ●生成式人工智慧倫理聲明：禁止使用 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學 習當中。因本課程的內容於生成式 AI 中，在版權中尚有許多疑慮尚未離清，且容易影響 學生對基礎核心知識之判讀與學習。 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁 止使用，以下為相關的監管機制 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或 個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或 不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) 教師個人作品網站: shihfen.myportfolio.com Detailed Course Syllabus ● Course Description This course begins with story creation as its foundation, guiding students to design their own characters while exploring the following topics: 1. docs.text: 中⽂名稱 設計概論 科號 Course Number 11310JAD 170100 學分 Credit 2 ⼈數限制 Class Size 40 Course English Title Introduction to Design 任課教師 Instructor 董芳武 上課時間 Time R3R4 上課教室 Room Nanda 南⼤ 8201 課程說明 (Course description) 本課程介紹設計的核⼼概念、原則和⽅法。透過理論講授、案例分析和討論，學⽣將深 ⼊了解設計專業發展歷程，以⼈為本的設計概念，產品設計的原則，以及接軌當今設計 的概念。透過本課程研習，學⽣將建⽴扎實的設計知識基礎，並培養與時俱進的思維， 奠定未來在設計領域學習的基礎。 This course introduces the core concepts, principles, and methods of design. Through theoretical lectures, case studies, and discussions, students will gain in- depth understanding of the professional development of design, human-centered design concepts, principles of product design, and the integration of contemporary design concepts. Jacqui Atkin 著 劉鎮州 校審、林妙芳 翻譯，《陶藝徒手成型技法》，視傳文化， 2012 2. 李亮一，《陶藝技法 1、2、3》，亞太圖書，民 80。 3. 梁家嘉編著，《基礎陶藝》， 臺北市/雷鼓，民 80。 4. 吳讓農七十回顧陶藝展(民 86)：臺灣省立美術館編輯委員會編輯。 5. 台灣現代美術大系/陶藝類現代造形陶藝(民 93) 藝術家出版社編輯。 6. 陶藝.臺灣.當代 溫淑姿撰稿(民 94) 臺灣美術館。 7. 造形發想法之理論與實際 蕭銘芚(民 88)。雄獅圖書。 8. 中華民國全國現代陶藝邀請展 (民 95) 臺北市/史博館。 9. 臺灣國際陶藝雙年展 陳妙鳳主編(民 97) 臺北縣鶯歌陶瓷博物館。 10. 美學的經濟: 詹雄偉(民 94) 風格者出版社。 11. 藝器.造藝/臺灣當代陶藝展 莊秀玲策展主編（民 97）北縣鶯歌陶瓷博物館。 ◎學期作業總覽及評量比例 ＊單元 1：陶鈴設計與製作（捏塑、造型技巧）(30%) (3 件一組) ＊單元 2：時間計時器（陶板、捏塑、造型技巧）(30%) (1 件) ＊單元 3：花器器物（土條、陶板、綜合造型技巧）、A3 裱板(35%) (1 件) ＊報告筆記：A4 草圖(單元一~三 )x 3、菊花練技巧測驗 (5%) ＊期末共評 (3 大單元作品、A3 裱板與各單元的 A4 作品設計草圖)：未出席者學期成績 以原所得分數之 50%計算。 ◎課後固定實習時段：(1)週一至週四（四選一）19:00-21:00 。(2)假日申請 依工坊規定辦理。 (3)專案申請：請洽管理廠長。

docs.text: 1 書法(Chinese Calligraphy) 課程大綱 課號：11420JAD 210000 時間：M5M6 教室：南大 8203 課程介紹 本課程以中國書法史、書作創作實技為主要授課內容。 透過課堂講授中國商周時期至明清時期的歷代書法字體、文字演變與藝術風格，為學習者建立系 統性的書法知識。除了中國書法史以外，也將介紹日本古典書法與現代書道的發展與特色，拓展 學習者對於視覺文化、地域差異之視野，並期許能應用於自身的創作之中。在技法方面，以歷代 的經典碑帖作為課堂實作與臨摹的學習對象。並鼓勵同學參加國內外之書法競賽。 ※本課程將使用清華大學 EE-CLASS 平台輔助教學，請修課者務必留意公告資訊。 ※鼓勵同學參與國內外書法之各項競賽、美展活動 教學方式 課堂簡報講解、實務操作示範 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則： 本課程為實務課程，無涉及 AI 使用 指定參考書 《中國法書選》，東京：二玄社，2013 年，冊 1-60。 評分規則 平時作業：40%，期中作業：30%，期末書寫考試：30% 週次 主題 備註 1 課程綱要、授課方式、評分方式說明 材料登記 2 1.中國書道史：先秦篆書 2.篆書基本筆畫 作業： 西周《大盂鼎》 3 1.中國書道史：清人篆書 2.篆書臨摹示範：吳昌碩《石鼓文》、楊 沂孫，《周廟金人銘》 作業： 楊沂孫，《周廟金人銘》 4 1.中國篆刻史：明清流派印的形成 2.落款與鈐印 作業： 落款常用格式書寫 5 1.中國書道史：漢代隸書 2.隸書基本筆畫 作業： 東漢《乙瑛碑》-1 6 1.隸書臨摹示範：《乙瑛碑》 作業： 東漢《乙瑛碑》-2 7 1.中國書道史：簡帛書 2.隸書臨摹示範：戰國《郭店楚簡 老 子》、西漢《馬王堆帛書 周易》 作業： 西漢《馬王堆帛書 周易》 2 8 1.日本書道史：近現代大字書與前衛書 2.墨色的濃淡與運動 期中作業： 以日本近現代大字書的概念，創作 篆書或是隸書作品。紙張尺寸： 75x75(CM) 9 1.中國書道史：魏碑與唐楷 2.楷書基本筆畫 作業： 北魏《孫秋生造像記》 10 1.魏碑臨摹示範：《張猛龍碑》 2.魏碑臨摹示範：《鄭文公碑》 作業： 北魏《張猛龍碑》或《鄭文公碑》 擇一臨寫 11 1.唐楷臨摹示範：顏真卿《麻姑仙壇記》 2.唐楷臨摹示範：歐陽詢《皇甫誕碑》 作業： 顏真卿《麻姑仙壇記》或歐陽詢 《皇甫誕碑》擇一臨寫 12 1.中國書道史：王羲之與王獻之 2.行草書基本筆畫 作業： 懷仁《集王字聖教序》 13 1.日本書道史：平安三筆 2.行書臨摹示範：空海《風信帖》 3.行書臨摹示範：懷仁《集王字聖教序》 作業： 空海《風信帖》 14 1.中國書道史：米芾 2.行書臨摹示範：米芾《紫金研帖》 作業： 米芾《紫金研帖》 15 期末書寫考試：臨帖、創作擇一 期末考試： 臨摹、創作均可、字體不限，作品 須落款鈐印。 16 期末成果發表：作品評比與鑑賞

docs.name: 人文與藝術創作
docs.text: 國立清華大學 課程大綱 人文與藝術創作 藝設創作組二年級 學分數：2 時間：週四 5、6 節 教室：8201 授課教師：梁莉苓 /E-mail: liling_liang@mx.nthu.edu.tw 一、課程概述 本課程關注學生能擁有「人文素養」，引導學生思考藝術與所處時代的關 係，及能將創作思維由「自我」擴及關乎「他者」的公共議題層面探討。此 外，著重認識在地人文藝術，參訪位處新竹市的李澤藩美術館等藝術空間。 二、教學進度 週次 課程內容 備 註 1 2/26 課程介紹 •選小老師 2 3/5 探討藝術與時代的關聯性 •報告分組 3 3/12 4 3/19 由「自我」出發的創作(一)： 狹義自畫像 5 3/26 6 4/2 在地人文藝術校外參訪： 加沃文行、李澤藩美術館、 絕 色影像館 •4/2 校際活動週停課，補課改為 校外參訪，預計兩次上課時間，調 課至4/18 (六) 13:10~17:10。 4/9 8 4/16 由「自我」出發的創作(二)： 廣義自畫像 13:30～14:30 9 4/23 10 4/30 期中報告繳交與討論 11 5/7 由「他者」出發的創作(一)： 政治與社會 12 5/14 13 5/21 由「他者」出發的創作(二)： 社區與環境 14 5/28 15 6/4 期末創作報告 16 6/11 註：課程進度會依課程推進狀況調整。 三、成績評量 （一）作業評量(70)% 1. 期中報告：題目「反思當前時代趨勢，探索藝術創作可能發展？」分 組進行。 2. 期末個人創作與報告：從期中報告發想創作計畫，創作類型不拘，需 融入期中報告內容。 （二）上課參與和其他隨堂表現 (30%) （三）其它： a. 缺課或遲到將被扣分，無論假別達（含）五次未到課，學期成績不及 格；請依照學校請假規定線上申請，相關規定自行參閱參閱〈國立清 華大學學生請假辦法〉。 b. 評量僅接受經上課討論的作品。 c. 本課程作業原則上不接受使用生成式人工智慧，除與作業主題相關， 且須在作業中註明運用的部分與方式。若非以上特例，若經查核發 現，教師有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。修讀本課程 之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 四、參考書籍 王墨林等著，鄭慧華編。《藝術與社會:當代藝術家專文和訪談》。臺北市：臺 北市美館，2009。 施叔青著。《兩個芙烈達‧卡蘿》。臺北市：時報，2001。 劉君著。〈從手藝人到天才：文藝復興時期藝術家身分和形象的建構〉，《從手藝人 到神聖藝術家：文藝復興時期義大利藝術家階層的興起》。北京市：商務印書 館，2018，頁247-314。。 劉瑞琪著。《陰性顯影》。臺北市：遠流，2004。 黃光男著。《台灣美術全集13．李澤藩》。臺北市：藝術家出版社， 1993。 黃晨淳著。《大師自畫像》。臺中市：好讀出版社，2004。 顧錚著。《自我的迷宮：藝術家的「我」》。山東市：山東畫報， 2004。 Catherine Grout著，姚孟吟譯。《藝術介入空間：都會裡的藝術創作》，臺 北市：遠流出版社，2002。 Sarah Bakewell著，吳瑪悧等譯。《人文主義的追尋：人文主義七百年來的 自由思考、探究和希望》，臺北市：遠流，2004。 Suzanne Lacy 編，陳衍秀譯。《量繪形貌：新類型公共藝術》，臺北 市：商周出版，2023。 李澤藩美術館 官方網站 https://tzefanlee.org/ 臉書 https://www.facebook.com/leetzefan 絕版影像館 官方網站 https://uniquephoto.com.tw/ 加沃文行 臉書 https://www.facebook.com/wowoart.link I G https://www.instagram.com/wo_culturalpractice/ 所有課程相關的書目、文章、電影、影像與網站等。

docs.name: 藝術專題工作坊
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11420JAD 225600 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 15 中文名稱 Course Title 藝術專題工作坊 英文名稱 Course English Title Workshop of Arts 任課教師 Instructor 紀宇芳 上課時間 Time T5T6 上課教室 Room Nanda 南大 8203 ／容量 40 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程將綜合觀念的開展與實務專案，探討藝術表現過程中創作者們如何透過觀念、藝術材料與 媒體運用進行實踐。課程中強調獨立實踐與思考，深入媒材運用與觀念思維的延伸發展，引導學 生於進階實踐中對當代視覺藝術創作進行思考、分析與探究。內容包含邀請外聘講者分享其創作 經驗，透過聆聽、理解、分析當代藝術作品與各項藝術專題，引導學生們藉由觀察各類別創作手 法與造形語彙，進行比較、深究各個創作者的變化與差異，以及他們如湖透過對議題的長期深 究、對材料特徵的反覆實驗，逐步開展對於主題的掌握能力，進而反思自我該如何累積並思考個 人創作特色與脈絡，以期檢視、發展自我的綜合造形技巧、組織創作觀念與多方整合能力。 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 當代藝術, 綜合媒材, 激浪派, 觀念藝術, 裝置藝術 Contemporary art, Ｍixed media, Fluxus, Conceptual art, Installation art 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程內容將經由觀念思考、造型實驗、漸進至獨立創作實踐與開放式討論…等過程。教學過程 中訓練學生邏輯思考以及回應當代藝術創作的知能。藉由藝術專題逐步培養學員獨立思考創作的 執行能力，如何透過研究、資料蒐集、分析、討論與修正，拓展原有的想法並深化觀念。工作坊 實作內容包含個人創作之概念發想引導，以及當代藝術內容與形式應用等諸多案例討論，配合學 習進度調整課程安排，適時引入當期重要展覽與藝術專案，並視情況安排各式演講、座談，以及 校外展覽之現地教學討論。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 無。本課程採自編教材。 ● 參考書籍(References) An, K. & Cerasi J.著，金振寧 譯。《誰怕當代藝術》，台北：典藏家庭， 2018。 Gilda Williams 著，金振寧 譯。《如何書寫當代藝術 How to Write About Contemporary Art》，台北：典藏家庭，2017。 John Berger 著，吳莉君譯，《觀看的方式》，臺北：麥田，2005。 暮澤剛巳著，蔡青雯譯，《當代藝術關鍵詞 100 》，台北：麥田出版社，2011。 Michael Bird 著，吳莉君譯，《改變藝術的 100 個觀念》，台北市：臉譜，2014。 陳永賢著，《英國當代藝術》，台北：藝術家出版社，2014。 高千惠 著，《叛逆的捉影：當 代藝術家的新迷思》。台北市：遠流 2006。 暮澤剛巳著，蔡青雯譯，《當代藝術關鍵詞 100》，臺北市：城邦文化出版社，2011。 羅伯特．艾得金著，黃麗絹譯，《藝術開講：當代意念、運動與詞彙導引》，臺北市：藝術家出 版社，1996。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 教師講授、案例分析、機構參訪、課堂討論、口頭及書面報告…。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 課程內容除原有兩大創作實踐單元，亦規劃配合現地創作、概念延展與共創等子題，單元長度與 內容將依照學生進度與作品完成度進行調整，如遇國定假日與校際活動週將進行彈性調動。 週次 課程內容 備註 1 課程簡介與說明 2 藝術專題與創作理念研討-媒材 資料搜集與分析 3 藝術專題與創作理念研討-敘事 概念分享與討論 4 創作概念、實踐與研討-環境反思 實例討論 5 創作概念、實踐與研討-文化語境 實例討論 6 創作實踐與概念討論-系譜與脈絡 實例討論 7 期中研討（一）專題報告、發表與討論 發表、討論與分析 8 期中研討（二）專題報告、發表與討論 發表、討論與分析 9 工作室、藝文機構參訪 依實際情形調整。 10 藝術專題發想與創作理念討論 II 概念討論與修正 11 實踐製作與討論 II 實例討論 12 實踐製作與討論 II 實例討論 13 實踐製作與討論、展出形式、空間規劃與調整。 實例討論 14 藝術專題講座與討論 依實際邀請情形調整。 15 期末成果（一）：期末綜合發表與討論 成果發表、討論與分析 16 期末成果（二）：期末綜合發表與討論 成果發表、討論與分析 *課程安排依實際授課情形作調整，配合校內外展覽賞析、參觀藝術家工作室、邀請專業創作者 進行講座與座談…等，戶外活動將依天候情況進行調動 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 期中成果 30%；期末成果 30%；作業進度、出席、課堂討論與學習態度 40% *請假須提前依校方規則進行線上申請，請自行參閱<國立清華大學學生請假辦法>。 *課堂缺課、遲到、作業遲交、缺交，將嚴重影響學期成績。 *缺課超過三次以上者(包含事假等，且不接受當日課前臨時請假)，出缺席成績將以 0 分計。 *手機使用原則，課堂中請務必關閉手機鈴聲，如非必要勿使用。 ● 敘明學生使用 AI 的規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 經仔細考量後，本課程授課教師認為不宜於此門課程當中使用生成式人工智慧於課堂學習當中。 因本課程的內容於生成式 AI 中尚有諸多錯誤，且容易影響學生對基礎核心知識之判讀。 根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使用， 以下為相關的監管機制： ◼ 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報告或個 人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予 計分。 ◼ 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 ● docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number JAD 227100 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 35 中文名稱 Course Title 素描：圖像與媒材二 英文名稱 Course English Title Drawing: Image and Media II 任課教師 Instructor 吳宇棠 Wu, Yu-Tang 上課時間 Time T7T8 上課教室 Room 南大 8301 課程簡述： 本課程為進階素描創作。課程內容包含：1.以媒材選擇題材的進階操作；2.非紙質基底材的選擇 與操作；3.畫面結構參照與暗示；4.異質媒材同時使用的操作判斷；5.綜合的自由習作。 課程關鍵字：素描，混合媒材，肌理，筆觸， 畫面空間，現代藝術 課程大綱 課程說明： 本課程為進階素描創作。課程內容包含：1.以媒材選擇題材的進階操作；2.非紙質基底材的選擇 與操作；3.畫面結構參照與暗示；4.異質媒材同時使用的操作判斷；5.綜合的自由習作。 教學進度： 第一週 基本概念與上課規定說明 第二~四週 眾聲喧嘩：素描語言與空間重構 第五~七週 基底探討：肌理的本源； 第八週 期中作業評分 第八~十週 結構參照：從過去看向未來 第十一~十三週 媒材調性：異質空間 第十四~十五週自由習作 第十六週 期末評分與檢討 成績考核： 期中與期末作品評分各佔 30%；課堂參與、作業進度與學習態度合佔 40% 修讀本門課程之學生應準時到課；缺課或遲到將被扣分。缺課（不論任何假別）達五次，學期成 績將不及格。 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的圖像、作業、報告或個 人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 參考書籍： 王公澤。《現代素描教與學：48 則啟發式素描訓練》。臺北市：雄獅，2003。 布施英利。《不要畫筆的繪畫教室》。臺北市：如果，2008。 貝蒂．愛德華。《像藝術家一樣思考》。杜蘊慧、張索娃譯。臺北市：木馬文化，2021。 (Edwards, Betty.
