docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Intermediate English II 中級英文二 Spring 2026 Course Number 11420LANG102102 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二 110 Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday ■ Thursday □ Friday ■ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. □ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 可選課學生 身分別 □ 前標生 ■ 中級生 □ 初級生 Language Level □ A2+－B1（初級） ■ B1-B2（中級） □ B2（中高級） 加簽說明 ■ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 楊幸瑜 Jane Yang janeyang1129@gmail.com None By appointment Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one‐year course is designed to improve and enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. Students will have opportunities to learn the key components of English (pronunciation, vocabulary, and grammar) and practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form (listening, reading, speaking, and even writing), and develop their confidence and fluency while they are practicing and performing various language tasks in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their essential knowledge of English language and engage themselves in everyday and even authentic communication. Requirements—Students are required to prepare the designated learning activities BEFOREHAND, REGULARLY attend the class, ACTIVELY participate in classroom activities, and complete each assignment ON TIME. Aside from class participation and practices based on the textbook, students are encouraged to work on a self‐access learning project based on designated videos, reading texts, and online English-learning materials. 2 Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunity to 1. develop accuracy and fluency in using key grammar structures such as question forms, Present Simple vs. Present Continuous, and Present Perfect vs. Past Simple. 2. strengthen listening and reading comprehension skills by identifying main ideas, specific information, and speakers’ attitudes in various contexts. 3. expand topic-based vocabulary and use of modifiers to describe people, routines, feelings, and life experiences more vividly. 4. build speaking fluency and interactional strategies through pair discussions, interviews, and opinion-sharing activities that simulate real- life communication. 5. enhance writing skills by composing short texts such as opinion paragraphs, routine descriptions, and personal reflections. 6. improve communicative competence by practicing follow-up questions, active listening, turn-taking, and emotional expression. 7. enhance learner autonomy and reflection through personalized speaking and writing tasks linked to students’ real lives. CEFR Can-do Statements (B1 & B1+) Reception Listening OVERALL LISTENING COMPREHENSION B1 Can understand the main points of clear standard speech on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, articulated. [overall listening comprehension] EOP B1 Can understand straightforward factual information about common everyday or job-related topics, identifying both general messages and specific details, provided speech is clearly articulated in a generally familiar accent. [overall listening comprehension] EAP/ EOP LISTENING AS A MEMBER OF A LIVE AUDIENCE B1 Can follow in outline straightforward short talks on familiar topics provided these are delivered in clearly articulated standard dialect. [listening as a member of a live audience] EAP/ EOP LISTENING TO ANNOUNCEMENTS & INSTRUCTIONS B1 Can understand simple technical information, such as operating instructions for every equipment. [listening to announcements & instructions] EAP/ EOP B1 Can follow detailed directions. [listening to announcements & instructions] LISTENING TO RADIO, AUDIO & RECORDINGS B1 Can understand the main points of radio news bulletins and simpler recorded material about familiar subjects delivered 3 relatively slowly and clearly. [listening to radio, audio & recordings] Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B1 Can read straightforward factual texts on subjects related to his/her field and interest with a satisfactory level of comprehension. [overall reading comprehension] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can scan longer texts in order to locate desired information, and gather information from different parts of a text, or from different texts in order to fulfil a specific task. [reading for orientation] EAP/ EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B1 Can recognize significant points in straightforward newspaper articles on familiar subjects. [reading for information & argument] B1+ Can identify the main conclusions in clearly signaled argumentative texts. [reading for information & argument] EAP B1+ Can recognize the line of argument in the treatment of the issue presented, though not necessarily in detail. [reading for information & argument] EAP READING INSTRUCTIONS B1 Can understand clearly written, straightforward instructions for a piece of equipment. [reading instructions] EOP Interaction Spoken Speaking CONVERSATION B1 Can enter unprepared into conversations on familiar topics. [conversation] B1 Can follow clearly articulated speech directed at him/her in everyday conversation, though will sometimes have to ask for repetition of particular words and phrases. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B1 Can generally follow the main points in an informal discussion with friends provided speech is clearly articulated in standard dialect. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 Can give or seek personal views and opinions in discussing topics of interest. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1 Can make his/her opinions and reactions understood as regards solutions to problems or practical questions of where to go, what to do, how to organize an event (e.g., an outing). [informal discussion (with friends)] B1 Can express belief, opinion, agreement, and disagreement politely. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP 4 B1+ Can follow much of what is said around him/her on general topics provided interlocutors avoid every idiomatic usage and articulate clearly. [informal discussion (with friends)] B1+ Can express his/her thoughts about abstract or cultural topics such as music, films. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can explain why something is a problem. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can give brief comments on the views of others. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can compare and contrast alternatives, discussing what to do, where to go, who or which to choose, etc. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP FORMAL DISCUSSION (MEETINGS) B1 Can take part in routine formal discussion of familiar subjects which is conducted in clearly articulated speech in the standard dialect and which involves the exchange of factual information, receiving instructions or the discussion of solutions to practical problems. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can follow much of what is said that is related to his/her field, provided interlocutors avoid very idiomatic usage and articulated clearly. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP/ EOP GOAL-ORIENTED COOPERATION (E.G., REPAIRING A CAR, DISCUSSING A DOCUMENT, ORGANIZING AN EVENT) B1 Can make his/her opinions and reactions understood as regards possible solutions or the question of what to do next, giving brief reasons and explanations. [goal- oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can follow what is said, though he/she may occasionally has to ask for repetition or clarification if the other people’s talk is rapid or extended. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] B1+ Can explain why something is a problem, discuss what to do next, compare and contrast alternatives. [goal- oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can give brief comments on the views of others. [goal- oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] INFORMATION EXCHANGE B1 Can find out and pass on straightforward factual information. [information exchange] B1+ Can exchange, check out and confirm accumulated factual information on familiar routine and non-routine matters within his/her field with some confidence. [information exchange] EAP/ EOP 5 B1+ Can describe how to do something, giving detailed instructions. B1+ Can synthesize and report information and arguments from a number of sources. [information exchange] EAP/ EOP Interaction Written Writing OVERALL WRITTEN INTERACTION B1+ Can convey information and ideas on abstract as well as concrete topics, check information and ask about or explain problems with reasonable precision. [overall written interaction] EAP/ EOP CORRESPONDENCE B1+ Can write personal letters giving news and expressing thoughts about abstract or cultural topics such as music, films. [correspondence] NOTES, MESSAGES& FORMS B1+ Can take messages communicating inquiries, explaining problems. [notes, messages & forms] Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B1 Can reasonably fluently sustain a straightforward description of one of a variety of subjects within his/her field of interest, presenting it as a linear sequence of points. [overall spoken production] EAP/ EOP SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: DESCRIBING EXPERIENCE B1 Can narrate a story. [sustained monologue: describing experience] EAP SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: PUTTING A CASE (E.G., IN A DEBATE) B1 Can briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions, plans and actions. [sustained monologue: putting a case (e.g., in a debate)] B1+ Can develop an argument well enough to be followed without difficulty most of the time. [sustained monologue: putting a case (e.g., in a debate)] EAP/ EOP PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENTS B1 Can deliver short, rehearsed announcements on a topic pertinent to everyday occurrences in his/her field which, despite possibly very foreign stress and intonation, are nevertheless clearly intelligible. [public announcements] ADDRESSING AUDIENCES B1 Can give a prepared straightforward presentation on a familiar topic within his/her everyday life, briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions, plans and actions. [addressing audiences] Production Written OVERALL WRITTEN PRODUCTION B1 Can write straightforward connected texts on a range of familiar subjects within his field of interest, by linking a series of shorter discrete elements into a linear sequence. [overall written production] 6 CREATIVE WRITING B1 Can write straightforward, detailed descriptions on a range of familiar subjects within his/her field of interest. [creative writing] EAP/ EOP B1 Can write a description of an event, a recent trip – real or imagined. [creative writing] B1 Can narrate a story. [creative writing] REPORTS & ESSAYS B1+ Can write short, simple essays on topics of interest. [reports & essays] EAP B1+ Can summarize, report and give his/her opinion about accumulated factual information on familiar routine and non-routine matters within his/her field with some confidence. [reports & essays] EAP Reception Communication Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B1 Can identify unfamiliar words from the context on topics related to his/her field and interests. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP/ EOP B1 Can extrapolate the meaning of occasional unknown words from the context and deduce sentence meaning provided the topic discussed is familiar. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] Interaction Communication Strategies TAKING THE FLOOR (TURNTAKING) B1 Can initiate, maintain and close simple face-to-face conversation on topics that are familiar or of personal interest. [taking the floor (turntaking)] B1+ Can intervene in a discussion on a familiar topic, using a suitable phrase to get the floor. [taking the floor (turntaking)] COOPERATING B1+ Can summarize the point reached in a discussion and so help focus the talk. [cooperating] EAP/ EOP ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B1+ Can ask someone to clarify or elaborate what he/she has just said. [asking for clarification] PLANNING B1 Can work out how to communicate the main point(s) he/she wants to get across, exploiting any resources available and limiting the message to what he/she can recall or find the means to express. [planning] B1+ Can rehearse and try out new combinations and expressions, inviting feedback. [planning] Worki ng with Text Comm unicati ve Langua ge Compe tenceNOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B1+ Can take notes during a lecture, which are precise enough for his/her own use at a later date, provided the topic is EAP 7 within his/her field of interest and the talk is clear and well-structured. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) PROCESSING TEXT B1 Can paraphrase short written passages in a simple fashion, using the original text wording and ordering. [processing text] EAP B1+ Can collate short pieces of information from several sources and summarize them for somebody else. [processing text] Communicative Language Competence Range GENERAL LINGUISTIC RANGE B1 Has enough language to get by, with sufficient vocabulary to express him/herself with some hesitation and circumlocutions on topics such as family, hobbies and interests, work, travel, and current events, but lexical limitations cause repetition and even difficulty with formulation at times. [processing text] VOCABULARY RANGE B1 Has a sufficient vocabulary to express him/herself with some circumlocutions on most topics pertinent to his/her everyday life such as family, hobbies and interests, work, travel, and current events. [vocabulary range] Pragmatic FLEXIBILITY B1 Can exploit a wide range of simple language flexibly to express much of what he/she wants. [flexibility] B1+ Can adapt his/her expressions to deal with less routine, even difficult situations. [flexibility] TAKING THE FLOOR (TURNTAKING) B1+ Can intervene in a discussion on a familiar topic, using a suitable phrase to get the floor. [taking the floor (turntaking)] COHERENCE B1 Can link a series of shorter, discrete simple elements into a connected, linear sequence of points. [coherence] PROPOSITIONAL PRECISION B1 Can express the main point he/she wants to make comprehensibly. [propositional precision] SPOKEN FLUENCY B1 Can keep going comprehensibly, even though pausing for grammatical and lexical planning and repair is very evident, especially in longer stretches of free production. [spoken fluency] B1+ Can express him/herself with relative ease. Despite some problems with formulation resulting in pauses and “culde- sacs”, he/she is able to keep going effectively without help. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Intermediate English II 中級英文二 Spring 2026 Course Number 11420LANG102105 Credits 2 Classroom Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday ▓ Friday □ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. ▓ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 可選課學生 身分別 □ 前標生 ▓ 中級生 □ 初級生 Language Level □ A2－A2+（初級）  B1-B1+（中級） □ B2（中高級） Prerequisites 加簽說明 不開放人工加簽，所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 蔡佩蓉 Katherine Tsai k_tsai@gapp.nthu.edu.tw N/A N/A Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one‐year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, and reading activities plus grammar review and vocabulary development. A four-skill coursebook plus a self‐access learning project will be integrated to design learning tasks and provide opportunities for students to practice language learning strategies, get exposed to English in any form, and develop their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After having taken this course, students are expected to consolidate their knowledge of English language and engage themselves more confidently and fluently in authentic communication in everyday settings and even in academic settings. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. review and practice grammar points and sentence structures to describe and discuss a variety of topics and issues related to their life. 2. build up theme-based vocabulary and even academic words for and through reading and listening to conversations, interviews, talks, and lectures. 3. practice academic skills such as outlining, summarizing, note-taking, and critical thinking while listening, reading, speaking, and writing. 2 4. present and explain information, perspectives, or problem-solving in speaking and writing tasks or activities. CEFR Can-do Statements (B1 & B1+) Reception Listening OVERALL LISTENING COMPREHENSION B1 Can understand straightforward factual information about common everyday or job-related topics, identifying both general messages and specific details, provided speech is clearly articulated in a generally familiar accent. [overall listening comprehension] EAP/ EOP LISTENING AS A MEMBER OF A LIVE AUDIENCE B1 Can follow in outline straightforward short talks on familiar topics provided these are delivered in clearly articulated standard dialect. [listening as a member of a live audience] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can follow a lecture or a talk within his/her own field, provided the subject matter is familiar and the presentation straightforward and clearly structured. [listening as a member of a live audience] EAP/ EOP Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B1 Can read straightforward factual texts on subjects related to his/her field and interest with a satisfactory level of comprehension. [overall reading comprehension] EAP/ EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT B1+ Can identify the main conclusions in clearly signaled argumentative texts. [reading for information & argument] EAP B1+ Can recognize the line of argument in the treatment of the issue presented, though not necessarily in detail. [reading for information & argument] EAP Interaction Spoken Speaking INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B1 Can give or seek personal views and opinions in discussing topics of interest. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1 Can express belief, opinion, agreement, and disagreement politely. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can express his/her thoughts about abstract or cultural topics such as music, films. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can explain why something is a problem. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP/ EOP FORMAL DISCUSSION (MEETINGS) B1+ Can follow much of what is said that is related to his/her field, provided interlocutors avoid very idiomatic usage and articulated clearly. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP/ EOP GOAL-ORIENTED COOPERATION (E.G., REPAIRING A CAR, DISCUSSING A DOCUMENT, ORGANIZING AN EVENT) B1 Can make his/her opinions and reactions understood as regards possible solutions or the question of what to do next, giving brief EAP/ EOP 3 reasons and explanations. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] B1+ Can explain why something is a problem, discuss what to do next, compare and contrast alternatives. [goal-oriented cooperation (e.g., repairing a car, discussing a document, organizing an event)] EAP/ EOP INFORMATION EXCHANGE B1+ Can exchange, check out and confirm accumulated factual information on familiar routine and non-routine matters within his/her field with some confidence. [information exchange] EAP/ EOP B1+ Can synthesize and report information and arguments from a number of sources. [information exchange] EAP/ EOP Interaction WrittenWriting OVERALL WRITTEN INTERACTION B1+ Can convey information and ideas on abstract as well as concrete topics, check information and ask about or explain problems with reasonable precision. [overall written interaction] EAP/ EOP Production Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN PRODUCTION B1 Can reasonably fluently sustain a straightforward description of one of a variety of subjects within his/her field of interest, presenting it as a linear sequence of points. [overall spoken production] EAP/ EOP SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: DESCRIBING EXPERIENCE B1 Can give straightforward descriptions on a variety of familiar subjects within his field of interest. [sustained monologue: describing experience] EAP/ EOP B1 Can narrate a story. [sustained monologue: describing experience] EAP SUSTAINED MONOLOGUE: PUTTING A CASE (E.G., IN A DEBATE) B1+ Can develop an argument well enough to be followed without difficulty most of the time. [sustained monologue: putting a case (e.g., in a debate)] EAP/ EOP Reception Communi cation Strategies IDENTIFYING CUES & INFERRING (SPOKEN & WRITTEN) B1 Can identify unfamiliar words from the context on topics related to his/her field and interests. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP/ EOP Interaction Communi cation Strategies COOPERATING B1+ Can summarize the point reached in a discussion and so help focus the talk. [cooperating] EAP/ EOP Working with Text NOTE-TAKING (LECTURES, SEMINARS, ETC.) B1+ Can take notes during a lecture, which are precise enough for his/her own use at a later date, provided the topic is within his/her EAP 4 field of interest and the talk is clear and well-structured. [note- taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) PROCESSING TEXT B1 Can paraphrase short written passages in a simple fashion, using the original text wording and ordering. [processing text] EAP 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 30% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 10% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Jerry Lambert. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Elementary 初級 Spring 2025 Course Number 11420LANG102201 Credits 2 Classroom Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday Friday 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. □ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 可選課學生 身分別 □ 前標生 □ 中級生 初級生 Language Level A2+－B1（初級） □ B1-B2（初級） □ B2（中高級） Prerequisites 具備英語句型結構基本概念、詞彙量約 2000 字。 加簽說明 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 □ Reminder: Please take the required English courses in accordance with the scheduled curriculum offered by our school. Your personal scheduling or preference of taking courses during your college stay will NOT be a valid excuse for the teacher to take your request for extra course registration into account. 停修條件 The student’s application for course withdrawal will NOT be approved if 1. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 6 classes. 3. The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 4. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過六次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原因 避免學生規避「低修」學分數而選課，或以其他理由選課但不上課等情事 提醒：請於選課前參考課程大綱，了解評分方式、各週進度。並於第一堂課進一步了 解作業、報告、考試的規劃與所需處理時間。評估自已的學習量能，避免修課失衡。 2 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email 林鈺凢 yufanlin@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, reading and writing. The course will be conducted mainly based on the designated textbook; diverse activities will also be integrated into class in order to build students’ vocabulary bank, strengthen the knowledge of grammar patterns and English learning strategies. Students are given the chances to use English in a friendly learning context for developing their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After taking this course, students are expected to be equipped with the knowledge of English language and engage themselves more actively and confidently in authentic conversations in school and even everyday settings. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will be given the opportunity to 1. Identify and apply the vocabulary words in certain contexts through reading essays, listening to short dialogues and discussions in class. 2. Review and practice the grammar patterns, sentence structures, and language skills to have conversations in a variety of topics with peers and instructors. 3. Use problem-solving skills and independent thinking skills to answer and ask questions raised by the instructors and peers in class. 4. Build up a learning networking with peers with different expertise in order to get them exposed to different possibilities of English applications. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. [Listening] Can catch the main point in short, clear, simple messages and announcements. [listening to announcements & instructions] 2. [Reading] Can understand short, simple texts on familiar matters of a concrete type which consist of high-frequency everyday or job-related language. [overall reading comprehension] 3. [Spoken interaction] Can communicate in simple and routine tasks requiring a simple and direct exchange of information on familiar and routine matters to do with work and free time. [overall spoken interaction] 4. [Spoken interaction] Can discuss what to do, where to go and make arrangements to meet. [informal discussion(with friends)] 5. [Spoken production] Can give a short, rehearsed, basic presentation on a familiar subject. [addressing audiences] 3 6. [Sociolinguistic appropriateness] Can socialize simply but effectively using the simplest common expressions and following basic routine. 7. [Grammar accuracy] Uses some simple structures correctly, but still systematically makes basic mistakes—for example, tends to mix up tenses and forgets to mark agreement; nevertheless, it is usually clear what he/she is trying to say. 8. [Coherence] Can use the most frequently occurring connectors to link simple sentences in order to tell a story or describe something as a simple list of points. 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) Teaching materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Jerry Lambert. (2021). American English File 2, 3rd Edition. New York: Oxford University Press. ISBN: 978-0-19- 490639-5 CEFR Scale A2 A2+ □ B1 □ B1-B2 □ B2 □ B2+ □ C1 Learning/Resource Platform Techers may upload the teaching materials such as audio files, lecture slides, assignments, quizzes, and supplementary materials to NTHU designated learning platforms. Teaching Activities: Lectures 口頭講授 Pair/Group discussion 配對／分組討論 Assignments 作業 Student presentations 學生報告 Quizzes 小考 4 Requirements & Rules: 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. ü The instructor takes attendance every week at 08:10 throughout the semester. If you are all present whenever the instructor takes the roll, you will get 60 (i.e. the primitive score) in this category (i.e. attendance & participation). The other 40 points will be given based on how passionate, active and interactive you are in class and the contributions you make to the class. 每次上課 08:10 點名，皆無缺席即可於此類別得到 60 分，此類別另外的 40 分為課堂活動參與， 將觀察學生是否積極於課堂中與同學互動並主動參與討論並完成交派任務。 ü If you are absent from a class meeting, 10 points from “participation” will be deducted from this primitive score. The student never attends class nor submits assignments. 2. The student is absent or asks for leave with NO valid excuses for more than 6 classes. 3. The student never explains to or discusses with the teacher his/her difficulty in taking care of this subject. 4. The student neither offers valid excuses on his application for course withdrawal nor notifies the teacher beforehand. 學生如遇有以下情形，其停修申請將不予「同意」 1. 學生未曾到課或繳交任何作業。 2. 學生無故缺席或未有證明之請假超過六次 3. 學生從未向老師解釋、或與之討論，修讀本課程時的困難 4. 學生未在停修申請上敘明或以其他通訊方式告知老師停修本課程之原因 避免學生規避「低修」學分數而選課，或以其他理由選課但不上課等情事 提醒：請於選課前參考課程大綱，了解評分方式、各週進度。並於第一堂課進一步了 解作業、報告、考試的規劃與所需處理時間。評估自已的學習量能，避免修課失衡。 2 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email 林鈺凢 yufanlin@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Course Aims / Description Primary aim This one-year course is designed to enhance students’ overall English competence through listening, speaking, reading and writing. The course will be conducted mainly based on the designated textbook; diverse activities will also be integrated into class in order to build students’ vocabulary bank, strengthen the knowledge of grammar patterns and English learning strategies. Students are given the chances to use English in a friendly learning context for developing their confidence and fluency in the classroom and outside the classroom. After taking this course, students are expected to be equipped with the knowledge of English language and engage themselves more actively and confidently in authentic conversations in school and even everyday settings. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will be given the opportunity to 1. Identify and apply the vocabulary words in certain contexts through reading essays, listening to short dialogues and discussions in class. 2. Review and practice the grammar patterns, sentence structures, and language skills to have conversations in a variety of topics with peers and instructors. 3. Use problem-solving skills and independent thinking skills to answer and ask questions raised by the instructors and peers in class. 4. Build up a learning networking with peers with different expertise in order to get them exposed to different possibilities of English applications. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. [Listening] Can catch the main point in short, clear, simple messages and announcements. [listening to announcements & instructions] 2. [Reading] Can understand short, simple texts on familiar matters of a concrete type which consist of high-frequency everyday or job-related language. [overall reading comprehension] 3. [Spoken interaction] Can communicate in simple and routine tasks requiring a simple and direct exchange of information on familiar and routine matters to do with work and free time. [overall spoken interaction] 4. [Spoken interaction] Can discuss what to do, where to go and make arrangements to meet. [informal discussion(with friends)] 5. [Spoken production] Can give a short, rehearsed, basic presentation on a familiar subject. [addressing audiences] 3 6. [Sociolinguistic appropriateness] Can socialize simply but effectively using the simplest common expressions and following basic routine. 7. [Grammar accuracy] Uses some simple structures correctly, but still systematically makes basic mistakes—for example, tends to mix up tenses and forgets to mark agreement; nevertheless, it is usually clear what he/she is trying to say. 8. [Coherence] Can use the most frequently occurring connectors to link simple sentences in order to tell a story or describe something as a simple list of points. 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) Teaching materials and References Textbook(s) Christina Latham-Koenig, Clive Oxenden, and Jerry Lambert. Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour Nga Khing LIM yclin2005@gmail.com emails preferred class hours Course Aims / Description1 Primary aim This introductory course aims to enhance students’ general English fluency in listening, reading, speaking and writing. This subject will cover a series of skills: a. review the fundamental notions of English grammar; b. to understand situational English about different topics; c. to use appropriate lexeme and essential collocations in context to express idea and communicate with each other naturally. Learners will be guided by the instructor to build up English fluency in the uses of words and expressions as well as the application of grammar. Audio and visual learning materials that relate to the theme of each unit will also be provided to diversify learning resources. Through the course, learners will be able to see improvements in the four skills - listening, reading, speaking and writing. Subsidiary aim In this course students will have opportunities to 1. comprehend exact meanings of vocabulary in written and spoken contexts as well as enlarge its storage by working on skills of prefixes, suffixes roots and word families. 2. Develop proficiency in academic English by exploring synonyms, antonyms, theme-based words and phrases and collocation in assigned readings. 3. Facilitate students with grammatical notions by highlighting its applications in spoken and written texts. 4. Assign speaking and listening tasks to students to practice conversation or dialogue, listening dictation, pair discussion and everyday talk. 5. Enhance students’ reading efficiency and speed by featuring the identification of main ideas, topic sentences and supporting details. Corresponding CEFR Can-do 1. A2 Can give a simple description or presentation of people, living or working conditions, daily routines, likes/dislikes, etc. as a short series of simple phrases and sentences linked into a list. [overall spoken production] 6. A2+ Can initiate, maintain and close simple, face-to-face conversation. [taking the floor (turntaking) 7. A2 Can produce brief everyday expressions in order to satisfy simple needs of a concrete type: personal details, daily routines, wants and needs, requests for information. The course will be conducted mainly based on the designated textbook; diverse activities will also be integrated into class to build students’ vocabulary bank, strengthen the knowledge of grammar patterns and English learning strategies. Students are given the opportunity to use English in a friendly learning context for developing their confidence and fluency in and outside the classroom. Besides, group discussions and presentations are held to help students gain practical knowledge of daily English, such as organizing travel plan, giving a small talk about specific topic, and express opinions clearly while having group discussions. After taking this course, students are expected to be equipped with the knowledge of English language and engage themselves more actively and confidently in authentic conversations and activities at school and even in everyday settings. Subsidiary aim In this class, students will have opportunities to 1. Identify and apply the vocabulary words in certain contexts through reading essays, listening to short dialogues and discussions in class. 2. Review and practice the grammar patterns, sentence structures, and language skills to have conversations in a variety of topics with peers and instructors. 3. Use problem-solving skills and independent thinking skills to answer and ask questions raised by the instructors and peers in class. 4. Build up a learning networking with peers with different expertise in order to get them exposed to different possibilities of English applications. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements 1. docs.text: 1 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) National Tsing Hua University Spring 2026 Upper-Intermediate English III_Reading Tentative Syllabus_M1M2 COURSE INFORMATION Course Number 11420LANG103001 Credits 2 Classroom General II (綜二館) 104 Class hours ■ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday ■ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. □ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 學生身分別 ■ 頂標生 □ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Extra Selection: 開放加簽之條件 加簽說明 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 ■ 人數上限後，開放人工加簽，學生必須符合以下條件，於第一週上課時，備妥 加簽申請表，請老師同意並簽署加簽，申請送達英語教育中心辦公室，再由老師 線上簽核完成。 ■ 條件 1：第一週必須到課。 □ 條件 2：須有其他時段【選讀英語文】衝堂無法選課之證明（如選課紀錄或本 學期所有科目課程表） □ 條件 3：自所屬選課階段（大二生：第 1-2 次選課；大三、大四學生：第 3 次 選課）起，亂數選課皆未選上（選上但退選者，不得以人工加簽再次選課） ■ 條件 4：應屆畢業生 □ 條件 5：__________ 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個人考量，未對 應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定加簽某特定課程，英語教育 中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 INSTRUCTOR Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) mthwang14@hotmail.com (full-time teachers only) (full-time teachers only) COURSE GOALS & DESCRIPTION 中高級英文三閱讀為一門兩學分的學期課程，幫助中高級程度之大一新生鞏固並精進英文閱讀能力。 透過廣泛閱讀，學習在短時間內快速正確精準把握文章大意與重點，拓展不同領域的字彙及閱讀技巧。 透過精讀，學習深度了解文章具體及抽象意涵，討論分析文本內涵與外延，評估作者立意觀點與語氣， 批判思辨議題，與實際世界互動。 This high-intermediate level English course is designed to help students develop extensive and intensive reading skills to grasp the point and support in the text, to explore vocabulary and reading skills by studying discipline-specific rhetoric of language patterns, and further to analyze and discuss issues that can be inferred or implied by what is presented in the text. Students will have training on academic reading skills and strategies and critical thinking skills, working to apply the skills and language being learned in task-based 2 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) collaborative activities that extend each reading chapter. By the end of this course, students will learn to develop the ability to understand and deliver academic arguments and to gain proficiency in using the language in academic contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) ✓ Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 30% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 30% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 20% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 10% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK Textbook Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking Level 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 Online Learning SPARK PLATFORM at learn.eltngl.com Teacher-led or Self-Study CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2 □ B1 □ A2 □ A1 3 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) GRADING 1. Attendance and participation – 15% 2. Quizzes – 30% 3. Midterm reading project & 5-minute talk – 25% 4. Uniform Final Exam – 30% UNIFORM FINAL EXAM This uniform final exam will take place, in the classrooms where the class usually meet and in regular class meeting hours, in Week 16. (統一期末考訂於第十六週，原班級教室與上課時間考試。) Note: Pathways Units 1, 4, 6 to be taught during class sessions, Unit 8 designated for student self- study, and all these four units covered in final exam. (註: 課堂教授 Pathways 第 1,4,6 單元，學生自學第 8 單元，期末考範圍 1,4,6,8 全部四單元。) CLASSROOM LANGUAGE ■ English 80 % ■ Mandarin 20% CLASS ACTIVITIES Group or individual presentations ◆ Research, prepare, and deliver presentations on assigned topics, developing communication skills, confidence, and the ability to organize and share ideas effectively. Jigsaw reading ◆ Divide an article or text into sections. Students read their section, summarize it, and share it with peers to complete the full picture. Critical analysis discussions ◆ Choose articles or essays and have students discuss the author’s purpose, tone, and main arguments. Discussion Circles ◆ Provide prompts related to course content or current events. Students take turns sharing opinions and supporting their ideas with examples. Vocabulary building activities ◆ Expand and apply vocabulary through tasks such as word maps, matching synonyms, and writing stories, enhancing understanding and usage in context. Interpretation projects ◆ Analyze and interpret information from texts, charts, graphs and illustrations. Present findings clearly and connect them to real-world applications. 4 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) CLASS RULES 1. Students are required to attend each class session and conscientiously participate in classroom learning activities in order to be regarded as full attendance and granted a score of 90 in the grading category of Attendance & Participation. (上課全勤，且認真參與課堂學習， 出勤參與成績得 90 分。） 2. Occasional absences up to three times will lead to a zero in the score for Attendance & Participation category, and five absences will result in a failure in this course. （三次無故缺席，無法獲得任何出勤參與成績; 五次無故缺席，學期總成績不及格。） 3. Authorized absence under exceptional circumstances can be granted, if evidence for justifiable cause can be produced. （有正當理由並可提出證明的特殊狀況，方可准假。） REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (課程使用 AI 的原則) □ 完全開放使用且無須註明 □ 有條件開放，依課程規定使用生成式 AI。 ■ 禁止使用，作業或報告必須由學生本人產出。 (AI-assisted assignments are NOT allowed; only content generated by the student can be accepted.) □ 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 生成式 人工智慧 倫理聲明 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，相關監管機制如下: ⚫ 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報 告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重 新評分或不予計分。 ⚫ 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 依據上述指引，本課程對於 AI 使用策略之考量與決議: 利用人工智慧生成書寫文字已是一般人輕易可得的事，不須依賴他人代工，幾個按 鍵就可產出有內容的文字，切要主旨前後一致，敘事說理文意貫串，字詞句法精準修 飾。利用機器瞬間數百萬次改寫改說，重新置換字詞字句，可輕易躲過剽竊偵測軟體， 達到 100% Unique 獨特原創性，輕鬆取得及格以上滿意的分數。我們若想逆向溯源找 出機器撰寫改說的證據，或是查驗文字內容是否由人類或機器創作，其難度相對高，畢 竟人類語文表達，就本質來說，雖有語法約定俗成的限制，但也容許相當大的自由程 度，同樣意思可以不同字詞句法表達，容許使用不同旨趣細微差別的文字，這也是人工 智慧文字內容生成系統建構所利用的語言特性。 然而，若是不需付出任何努力學習，就可取得一篇精緻完美的報告或論述文章，這 對於學校作為建構知識學習場域實質構成欺瞞，對於社會公益公平負面影響尤其鉅大。 畢竟，學習者工作本質就是學習，抄襲造假不但無助於學習，適足以鼓勵欺瞞造假負面 價值，更是扼殺學習工作建構知識技能本質的意義。因此，學術工作由他人或機器代工 都是違背學術倫理的行為。學習者選擇誠實努力工作或是欺瞞他人找代工，這是倫理善 惡的分野，直接相關學習探索進程。本課程任課教師經審慎考量，本課程授課教師認為 本課程不宜使用生成式人工智慧作為課堂活動內容或學習輔助工具。 學 生 使 用 AI 條件 ▓ 禁止使用，作業或報告必須由學生本人產出。(AI-assisted assignments are NOT allowed: only content generated by the student personally can be accepted.) 5 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) COURSE SCHEDULE Week Date Main Unit 4 Rethinking Transport Explore the Theme: Going Electric Reading: Green Air Travel Academic Track: Global Studies/Business Studies + Quiz #2 ✓ Recognizing and evaluating different viewpoints (EAP) ✓ Writing Sentences with Initial Phrases (EAP) ✓ Organizing a Comparative Essay (EAP) ✓ Understanding Multiword Phrases (EAP) ✓ Predict, Infer Meaning, Evaluate, Reflect (EAP) 11. 5/4 12. 5/11 Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) Prepared by Jennifer Liu 2 ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well-supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) ✓ Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) Course Goals: ⚫ This course aims to enhance students’ academic reading ability with useful reading strategies. The designated textbook provides academic readings materials to consolidate comprehension across different fields. Students are guided from a great variety of reading passages so as to be familiar with contextualized vocabulary and various aspects toward issues. After input from all types of reading materials, students are encouraged to express opinions on related issues with the practice on presentation skills. Course Descriptions: ⚫ Lecture, as well as group discussion, presentation, and language activities will help students get prepared for daily and academic reading tasks. Note-taking skills, vocabulary, and reading skills are designed to improve students’ reading ability, while discussion, debate, and presentation would train student’s academic communication. Class materials are uploaded on eeclass. (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw) UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 以 下 為 建 議 比 例 ， 老 師 可 依 各 班 上 課 內 容 調 整 。 1. ISBN: 9780357980101 CEFR Scale ■ B2+ □ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 GRADING 黑 色 字 體 為 統 一 固 定 比 例 ； 藍色字 體 請 (5 項 )至 少 選 3-4 項 1. Attendance and participation – 15% (Attendance 5% + Participation 10%) 2. Presentations – 10% 3. Assignments – 25% 4. Quizzes – 20% 5. Uniform Final Exam – 30% The uniform final exam, accounting for 30% of the semester grade, takes place in the usual classrooms and class meeting times in week 16. Four units of the textbook will be covered in the uniform exam. ⚫ Pathways (Book 4): Units 1, 4, 6, 8 CLASSROOM LANGUAGE 建 議 老 師 以 英 語 授 課 之 比 例 至 少 70%。 ■ English __70__% ■ Mandarin __30__% SUGGESTED CLASS ACTIVITIES ⚫ English Online Learning Site 英 語 自 學 平 台 (VoiceTube) ⚫ Group/ individual presentations on selected articles ⚫ Listening comprehension activities ⚫ Jigsaw reading ⚫ In-class discussion ⚫ Vocabulary building activities ⚫ Thought-provoking questions & discussion ⚫ Interpretation project/ text comprehension REGULATIONS FOR USING AI 學生使用 AI 的條件 AI-assisted reports and assignments are ☑ allowed in limited instances: AI can be used to prepare reports and assignments by brainstorming, but students must show how it helped them reach the result. Reminder: When students use AI—no matter how much—must be responsible to ensure the correctness of the information. CLASS RULES 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. (1) If you are absent, please report to the Academic Information System WITHIN ONE WEEK. Sign-ups must be completed by Week 3; the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this requirement, begin preparing at least two weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, memorize your speech, and rehearse thoroughly. I. Two Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) Confirm your presentation article. b) Meet with your partner and divide the work evenly. c) Read the article carefully at least once. d) Post your questions on the article title and your answers on eeclass. II. One Week Before the Presentation Day a) Post your subheadings of the article on eeclass. 1. Number all paragraphs first. 2. Group paragraphs logically and give each group a subheading. 3. Use short phrases, not full sentences. b) Post your vocabulary list on eeclass. • This list is different from “word sharing.” It should contain around 15 or more words, depending on the article’s length and difficulty. (If the article is longer and harder, you will need to include more vocab words.) c) Vocabulary List Guidelines i. Include each word, its part of speech (i.e. noun, verb, or adjective, etc.), the English definition (as used in the article), and an example sentence from the dictionary. ii. Number the words and list them in order of appearance. iii. If you cannot find an example in dictionaries, use the sentence from your article (do not invent your own). iv. Recommended dictionaries: 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English http://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/epidemic 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. TheFreeDictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/innumerable ◼ Note: Use Longman first, as definitions in class are usually drawn from it. If not suitable, consult Cambridge, then The Free Dictionary. d) Do not email me your vocabulary list. Proofreading is your responsibility. However, if you have difficulty finding a definition, you may ask Jennifer. e) Compose your speech as early as possible. f) Memorize and rehearse thoroughly before presentation day. 7 III. On the Presentation Day a) Materials • Distribute copies of your vocabulary list to classmates. • Submit one copy of your vocabulary list and your written report to the teacher before presenting. b) Content of the Presentation Your presentation should include: 1. Summary (3 minutes) • Tip: List key words first, then organize them into main ideas using your own logic and words. • Do not copy sentences directly from the article. 2. Vocabulary Sharing (2 minutes) • Choose 2-3 words or phrases that impressed you most. • Explain why they were memorable. • You may also share a sentence that you find interesting in the article instead of words or phrases 3. Personal Responses (2 minutes each speaker) • Each presenter must share their own thoughts and reflections after reading. c) Time Limit • Total time: 10 minutes • Article summary: 3 mins. • Vocabulary/ sentence sharing: 2 mins. • Personal responses: 2 mins. per speaker ◼ You must stop immediately when time is up, even if your presentation is unfinished. d) Q&A • After your talk, classmates and the instructor will ask questions about the article or your presentation. • Both presenters must take turns answering. • Students who ask questions will earn extra class participation point for that day. e) Written Report 1. Type a written report including: article summary, vocabulary sharing, and your responses. 2. Indicate how you and your partner divided the work. 3. Submit a copy to the teacher before presenting, and also upload the report to eeclass no later than the presentation day. 4. AI Usage Policy: You must not use AI to generate your speech. However, you are encouraged to use AI to proofread or revise your speech. If you do so, you must submit: • Your original version, • AI’s revised version, and • A sort list of lessons you learned from the AI’s feedback. 8 Appendix II Rubric for Pair Article Presentation Category Description Point Value Volume, Articulation, & Pronunciation • speaks loudly and clearly • articulates his/her words • uses correct pronunciation 20 Preparation • posts questions about the article title and their answers two weeks prior the presentation day • posts the finalized version of article subheadings and word list on eeclass one week before the presentation day • distributes the copies the vocabulary list on time • hands in the written report on time • posts the finalized written report on eeclass by the presentation day • answers questions from the teacher as well as the fellow students well 20 Delivery • no long pauses • well-organized • adopts a proper speed, intonation, and suitable pauses • has enough eye contact • doesn’t read notes • has good time control 20 Content Summary: • includes the key points • does not copy sentences from the article • organized Word sharing: • explains the reasons for choosing the words • explains the meanings of the words used in the article • suggests how the words/phrases can be used Response: • meaningful reflection 20 Vocabulary List & Written Report Vocabulary list: • includes all important new words • chooses correct meanings used in the article • few errors • a complete list • numbers and lists the words according to their order of appearance in the article Written report: • typed • few grammatical errors • organized • includes work allocations 20 Total 100

Students are required to prepare the designated passages BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in class discussions and complete exercise sections ON TIME. Listening input: A variety of authentic English-speaking contexts, including university lectures, interviews, podcasts, and classroom discussions not only activate students’ background knowledge of the topic, prime them for the authentic and inspirational content they will meet in the thought-provoking TED Talks, but also guide them systematically through strategies and activities to meet future academic, personal or professional goals. Specific and key academic skills are focused in each theme-based unit, where students effectively learn to predict, identify main ideas/details/inferences, take notes and manage lengthy input. Pronunciation is also highlighted as an aid to improving both listening comprehension & speaking fluency. Speaking output: Presentation skills inspired by the TED speakers give students the techniques & authentic language they need to successfully deliver their own presentations, help them gain the opportunity to personalize the language they learn, and build their confidence in expressing ideas and opinions. Visual/digital literacy will be promoted through lots of infographics and speaking activities designed to involve students working with a partner or in a group. With connected ideas and integrated language skills, students will give individual, pair and group projects/presentation regularly throughout the semester. The ultimate goals of the course are to encourage students to take charge of their learning and to facilitate their essential 21st century skills—collaboration, communication and critical thinking. Students are required to prepare the relevant parts BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in classroom activities and complete exercises ON TIME. Listening Input: Students will listen to spoken English in a variety of authentic scenarios such as university lectures, interviews, news reports, thought-provoking TED Talks and classroom discussions to allow them to develop their understanding of the topics in order to effectively prepare for the skills required in their future academic, personal and career objectives. Specific skills will be developed in each theme-based unit where students can learn to effectively predict, identify main ideas, details and inferences, take notes and follow detailed, lengthy discussion. There will be a focus on pronunciation as a means of promoting listening comprehension and speaking fluency. Students will also be encouraged to develop good critical- thinking skills to challenge ideas. Speaking output: Students will learn to deliver their own effective presentations including watching TEDTalks made by inspirational speakers which will allow students to develop authentic language appropriate for their presentation. This will allow students to further develop their ability to speak in front of an audience not only through effective verbal communication but also with the use of appropriate body language which will build their confidence in communicating their ideas. Visual and digital literacy will be Upper-intermediate English III Listening & Speaking 3 prepared by encouraged through the use of infographics and the use of PowerPoint slides to assist in supporting better presentations. This can be achieved successfully through student collaboration by working in pairs or threes in which group projects and presentations can be held regularly throughout the semester. The ultimate goal of the course is to encourage students to take control of their own learning and to Upper-intermediate English III Listening & Speaking 3 prepared by develop the essential skills of collaboration, communication and critical thinking which are so valuable in the 21 st century. docs.text: 1 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) National Tsing Hua University Spring 2026 Upper-Intermediate English III_Reading Tentative Syllabus_M3M4 COURSE INFORMATION Course Number 11420LANG103011 Credits 2 Classroom General II (綜二館) 104 Class hours ■ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday □ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. ■ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 學生身分別 ■ 頂標生 □ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Extra Selection: 開放加簽之條件 加簽說明 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 ■ 人數上限後，開放人工加簽，學生必須符合以下條件，於第一週上課時，備妥 加簽申請表，請老師同意並簽署加簽，申請送達英語教育中心辦公室，再由老師 線上簽核完成。 ■ 條件 1：第一週必須到課。 □ 條件 2：須有其他時段【選讀英語文】衝堂無法選課之證明（如選課紀錄或本 學期所有科目課程表） □ 條件 3：自所屬選課階段（大二生：第 1-2 次選課；大三、大四學生：第 3 次 選課）起，亂數選課皆未選上（選上但退選者，不得以人工加簽再次選課） ■ 條件 4：應屆畢業生 □ 條件 5：__________ 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個人考量，未對 應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定加簽某特定課程，英語教育 中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 INSTRUCTOR Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) mthwang14@hotmail.com (full-time teachers only) (full-time teachers only) COURSE GOALS & DESCRIPTION 中高級英文三閱讀為一門兩學分的學期課程，幫助中高級程度之大一新生鞏固並精進英文閱讀能力。 透過廣泛閱讀，學習在短時間內快速正確精準把握文章大意與重點，拓展不同領域的字彙及閱讀技巧。 透過精讀，學習深度了解文章具體及抽象意涵，討論分析文本內涵與外延，評估作者立意觀點與語氣， 批判思辨議題，與實際世界互動。 This high-intermediate level English course is designed to help students develop extensive and intensive reading skills to grasp the point and support in the text, to explore vocabulary and reading skills by studying discipline-specific rhetoric of language patterns, and further to analyze and discuss issues that can be inferred or implied by what is presented in the text. Students will have training on academic reading skills and strategies and critical thinking skills, working to apply the skills and language being learned in task-based 2 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) collaborative activities that extend each reading chapter. By the end of this course, students will learn to develop the ability to understand and deliver academic arguments and to gain proficiency in using the language in academic contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) ✓ Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 30% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 30% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 20% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 10% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK Textbook Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking Level 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 Online Learning SPARK PLATFORM at learn.eltngl.com Teacher-led or Self-Study CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2 □ B1 □ A2 □ A1 3 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) GRADING 1. Attendance and participation – 15% 2. Quizzes – 30% 3. Midterm reading project & 5-minute talk – 25% 4. Uniform Final Exam – 30% UNIFORM FINAL EXAM This uniform final exam will take place, in the classrooms where the class usually meet and in regular class meeting hours, in Week 16. (統一期末考訂於第十六週，原班級教室與上課時間考試。) Note: Pathways Units 1, 4, 6 to be taught during class sessions, Unit 8 designated for student self- study, and all these four units covered in final exam. (註: 課堂教授 Pathways 第 1,4,6 單元，學生自學第 8 單元，期末考範圍 1,4,6,8 全部四單元。) CLASSROOM LANGUAGE ■ English 80 % ■ Mandarin 20% CLASS ACTIVITIES Group or individual presentations ◆ Research, prepare, and deliver presentations on assigned topics, developing communication skills, confidence, and the ability to organize and share ideas effectively. Jigsaw reading ◆ Divide an article or text into sections. Students read their section, summarize it, and share it with peers to complete the full picture. Critical analysis discussions ◆ Choose articles or essays and have students discuss the author’s purpose, tone, and main arguments. Discussion Circles ◆ Provide prompts related to course content or current events. Students take turns sharing opinions and supporting their ideas with examples. Vocabulary building activities ◆ Expand and apply vocabulary through tasks such as word maps, matching synonyms, and writing stories, enhancing understanding and usage in context. Interpretation projects ◆ Analyze and interpret information from texts, charts, graphs and illustrations. Present findings clearly and connect them to real-world applications. 4 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) CLASS RULES 1. Students are required to attend each class session and conscientiously participate in classroom learning activities in order to be regarded as full attendance and granted a score of 90 in the grading category of Attendance & Participation. (上課全勤，且認真參與課堂學習， 出勤參與成績得 90 分。） 2. Occasional absences up to three times will lead to a zero in the score for Attendance & Participation category, and five absences will result in a failure in this course. （三次無故缺席，無法獲得任何出勤參與成績; 五次無故缺席，學期總成績不及格。） 3. Authorized absence under exceptional circumstances can be granted, if evidence for justifiable cause can be produced. （有正當理由並可提出證明的特殊狀況，方可准假。） REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (課程使用 AI 的原則) □ 完全開放使用且無須註明 □ 有條件開放，依課程規定使用生成式 AI。 ■ 禁止使用，作業或報告必須由學生本人產出。 (AI-assisted assignments are NOT allowed; only content generated by the student can be accepted.) □ 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 生成式 人工智慧 倫理聲明 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，相關監管機制如下: ⚫ 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報 告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重 新評分或不予計分。 ⚫ 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 依據上述指引，本課程對於 AI 使用策略之考量與決議: 利用人工智慧生成書寫文字已是一般人輕易可得的事，不須依賴他人代工，幾個按 鍵就可產出有內容的文字，切要主旨前後一致，敘事說理文意貫串，字詞句法精準修 飾。利用機器瞬間數百萬次改寫改說，重新置換字詞字句，可輕易躲過剽竊偵測軟體， 達到 100% Unique 獨特原創性，輕鬆取得及格以上滿意的分數。我們若想逆向溯源找 出機器撰寫改說的證據，或是查驗文字內容是否由人類或機器創作，其難度相對高，畢 竟人類語文表達，就本質來說，雖有語法約定俗成的限制，但也容許相當大的自由程 度，同樣意思可以不同字詞句法表達，容許使用不同旨趣細微差別的文字，這也是人工 智慧文字內容生成系統建構所利用的語言特性。 然而，若是不需付出任何努力學習，就可取得一篇精緻完美的報告或論述文章，這 對於學校作為建構知識學習場域實質構成欺瞞，對於社會公益公平負面影響尤其鉅大。 畢竟，學習者工作本質就是學習，抄襲造假不但無助於學習，適足以鼓勵欺瞞造假負面 價值，更是扼殺學習工作建構知識技能本質的意義。因此，學術工作由他人或機器代工 都是違背學術倫理的行為。學習者選擇誠實努力工作或是欺瞞他人找代工，這是倫理善 惡的分野，直接相關學習探索進程。本課程任課教師經審慎考量，本課程授課教師認為 本課程不宜使用生成式人工智慧作為課堂活動內容或學習輔助工具。 學 生 使 用 AI 條件 Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) Prepared by Jennifer Liu 2 ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well-supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) ✓ Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) Course Goals: ⚫ This course aims to enhance students’ academic reading ability with useful reading strategies. The designated textbook provides academic readings materials to consolidate comprehension across different fields. Students are guided from a great variety of reading passages so as to be familiar with contextualized vocabulary and various aspects toward issues. After input from all types of reading materials, students are encouraged to express opinions on related issues with the practice on presentation skills. Course Descriptions: ⚫ Lecture, as well as group discussion, presentation, and language activities will help students get prepared for daily and academic reading tasks. Students are required to prepare the designated passages BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in class discussions and complete exercise sections ON TIME. Listening input: A variety of authentic English-speaking contexts, including university lectures, interviews, podcasts, and classroom discussions not only activate students’ background knowledge of the topic, prime them for the authentic and inspirational content they will meet in the thought-provoking TED Talks, but also guide them systematically through strategies and activities to meet future academic, personal or professional goals. Specific and key academic skills are focused in each theme-based unit, where students effectively learn to predict, identify main ideas/details/inferences, take notes and manage lengthy input. Pronunciation is also highlighted as an aid to improving both listening comprehension & speaking fluency. Speaking output: Presentation skills inspired by the TED speakers give students the techniques & authentic language they need to successfully deliver their own presentations, help them gain the opportunity to personalize the language they learn, and build their confidence in expressing ideas and opinions. Visual/digital literacy will be promoted through lots of infographics and speaking activities designed to involve students working with a partner or in a group. With connected ideas and integrated language skills, students will give individual, pair and group projects/presentation regularly throughout the semester. The ultimate goals of the course are to encourage students to take charge of their learning and to facilitate their essential 21st century skills—collaboration, communication and critical thinking. Students are required to prepare the relevant parts BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in classroom activities and complete exercises ON TIME. Listening Input: Students will listen to spoken English in a variety of authentic scenarios such as university lectures, interviews, news reports, thought-provoking TED Talks and classroom discussions to allow them to develop their understanding of the topics in order to effectively prepare for the skills required in their future academic, personal and career objectives. Specific skills will be developed in each theme-based unit where students can learn to effectively predict, identify main ideas, details and inferences, take notes and follow detailed, lengthy discussion. There will be a focus on pronunciation as a means of promoting listening comprehension and speaking fluency. Students will also be encouraged to develop good critical- thinking skills to challenge ideas. Speaking output: Students will learn to deliver their own effective presentations including watching TEDTalks made by inspirational speakers which will allow students to develop authentic language appropriate for their presentation. This will allow students to further develop their ability to speak in front of an audience not only through effective verbal communication but also with the use of appropriate body language which will build their confidence in communicating their ideas. Visual and digital literacy will be encouraged through the use of infographics and the use of PowerPoint slides to assist in supporting better presentations. This can be achieved successfully through student collaboration by working in pairs or threes in which group projects and presentations can be held regularly throughout the semester. Attendance will be tracked from the first week, so please make sure you attend the first class on time. Attendance Policy ➢ Starting Point: 9 (起始點: 9 分) ➢ Lateness: -2 (遲到: 2 分) ➢ Absence: -5 (缺席: 5 分) ➢ Irrelevant Work in Class: -2 (做課堂不相關的事: 2 分) The starting attendance score is 9 points. Each late arrival deducts 2 points. Each absence deducts 5 points. Engaging in irrelevant activities in class deducts 2 points. (This includes using a phone for non-class-related activities or working on assignments for other courses.) The score has no lower limit but a maximum of 20 points. In other words, a negative attendance score will lower your semester grade, while a high attendance score can earn you up to 5 extra points towards your semester grade. 出席成績從 9 分開始計算，並依以下規則增減：每次遲到扣 2 分，缺席扣 5 分。若在課堂上從事無關活動 （如使用手機處理與課程無關的事務或做其他課程作業），則扣 2 分。分數累積上限為 20 分，無下限。換 言之，若出席成績為負分，將併入學期成績計算；若累積達 20 分，則學期成績額外加 5 分。 All these seemingly complicated and trivial calculations for attendance and class participation are designed to encourage you to speak more English and participate more actively in class. The more you engage in each class, the more harvest you’ll reap from this course. 4 PAIR ARTICLE PRESENTATION Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class. Sign-ups must be completed by the third week, and the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this course requirement, students must: • Begin preparation at least two weeks in advance • Meet all deadlines • Memorize their speeches • Rehearse thoroughly (For further details, see Appendices I & II) IN-CLASS TASKS/WORKSHEETS Each class includes pair or group tasks and discussions, and all students are required to participate actively. Four or five will be randomly selected for grading. • If you are absent, the worksheet score will be 0. • Late submissions will not be accepted. Pop quizzes may also be given before student presentations; these will count for 1/4 of the total 20% quiz grade. It will cover four units of the textbook: Units 1, 4, 6, and 8. Units 1, 4, and 8 will be taught in class, while Unit 6 must be studied independently by students. COURSE SCHEDULE Week Date Main Topic Reading Strategies Critical Thinking 1. 2/25 Course Introduction & Orientation Introduction to the BEST Test of English Proficiency* 2. 3/4 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Reading Test* ✓ Identifying main ideas and key details (EAP) 5 3. 3/11 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Writing Test*  Recognizing claims and counterclaims (EAP) 4. 3/18 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace ✓ Understanding cohesion (EAP) 5. 3/25 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace  Summarizing a text (EAP) 6. 4/1 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Recognizing and evaluating different viewpoints (EAP) 7. 4/8 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Using a concept map (EAP) 8. 4/15 Quiz#1 9. 4/22 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Understanding complex sentences (EAP)  Inferring meaning (EAP) 10. 4/29 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport  Comparing and contrasting two perspectives (EAP) 11. 5/6 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Reading extended texts (EAP) 12. 5/13 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Asking questions as you read (EAP) 13. 5/20 Quiz#2 14. 5/27 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Understanding supporting examples (EAP)  Interpreting visual data (EAP) 15. 6/3 Unit 8 Living Longer  Synthesizing (EAP) 16. 6/10 Uniform Final Exam (原班級教室與上課時間 考試) Note: Unit 6, “Why Language Matters,” is designated as a self-learning unit for students. 6 Appendix I Pair Article Presentation Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class without using PowerPoint slides. Sign-ups must be completed by Week 3; the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this requirement, begin preparing at least two weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, memorize your speech, and rehearse thoroughly. I. Two Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) Confirm your presentation article. b) Meet with your partner and divide the work evenly. c) Read the article carefully at least once. d) Post your questions on the article title and your answers on eeclass. II. One Week Before the Presentation Day a) Post your subheadings of the article on eeclass. 1. Number all paragraphs first. 2. Group paragraphs logically and give each group a subheading. 3. Use short phrases, not full sentences. b) Post your vocabulary list on eeclass. • This list is different from “word sharing.” It should contain around 15 or more words, depending on the article’s length and difficulty. (If the article is longer and harder, you will need to include more vocab words.) c) Vocabulary List Guidelines i. Include each word, its part of speech (i.e. noun, verb, or adjective, etc.), the English definition (as used in the article), and an example sentence from the dictionary. ii. Number the words and list them in order of appearance. iii. If you cannot find an example in dictionaries, use the sentence from your article (do not invent your own). iv. Recommended dictionaries: 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English http://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/epidemic 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. TheFreeDictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/innumerable ◼ Note: Use Longman first, as definitions in class are usually drawn from it. If not suitable, consult Cambridge, then The Free Dictionary. d) Do not email me your vocabulary list. Proofreading is your responsibility. However, if you have difficulty finding a definition, you may ask Jennifer. e) Compose your speech as early as possible. f) Memorize and rehearse thoroughly before presentation day. 7 III. On the Presentation Day a) Materials • Distribute copies of your vocabulary list to classmates. • Submit one copy of your vocabulary list and your written report to the teacher before presenting. b) Content of the Presentation Your presentation should include: 1. Summary (3 minutes) • Tip: List key words first, then organize them into main ideas using your own logic and words. • Do not copy sentences directly from the article. 2. Vocabulary Sharing (2 minutes) • Choose 2-3 words or phrases that impressed you most. • Explain why they were memorable. • You may also share a sentence that you find interesting in the article instead of words or phrases 3. Personal Responses (2 minutes each speaker) • Each presenter must share their own thoughts and reflections after reading. c) Time Limit • Total time: 10 minutes • Article summary: 3 mins. • Vocabulary/ sentence sharing: 2 mins. • Personal responses: 2 mins. per speaker ◼ You must stop immediately when time is up, even if your presentation is unfinished. d) Q&A • After your talk, classmates and the instructor will ask questions about the article or your presentation. • Both presenters must take turns answering. • Students who ask questions will earn extra class participation point for that day. e) Written Report 1. Type a written report including: article summary, vocabulary sharing, and your responses. 2. Indicate how you and your partner divided the work. 3. Submit a copy to the teacher before presenting, and also upload the report to eeclass no later than the presentation day. 4. AI Usage Policy: You must not use AI to generate your speech. However, you are encouraged to use AI to proofread or revise your speech. If you do so, you must submit: • Your original version, • AI’s revised version, and • A sort list of lessons you learned from the AI’s feedback. 8 Appendix II Rubric for Pair Article Presentation Category Description Point Value Volume, Articulation, & Pronunciation • speaks loudly and clearly • articulates his/her words • uses correct pronunciation 20 Preparation • posts questions about the article title and their answers two weeks prior the presentation day • posts the finalized version of article subheadings and word list on eeclass one week before the presentation day • distributes the copies the vocabulary list on time • hands in the written report on time • posts the finalized written report on eeclass by the presentation day • answers questions from the teacher as well as the fellow students well 20 Delivery • no long pauses • well-organized • adopts a proper speed, intonation, and suitable pauses • has enough eye contact • doesn’t read notes • has good time control 20 Content Summary: • includes the key points • does not copy sentences from the article • organized Word sharing: • explains the reasons for choosing the words • explains the meanings of the words used in the article • suggests how the words/phrases can be used Response: • meaningful reflection 20 Vocabulary List & Written Report Vocabulary list: • includes all important new words • chooses correct meanings used in the article • few errors • a complete list • numbers and lists the words according to their order of appearance in the article Written report: • typed • few grammatical errors • organized • includes work allocations 20 Total 100
