docs.text: 1 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) National Tsing Hua University Spring 2026 Upper-Intermediate English III_Reading Tentative Syllabus_W3W4 COURSE INFORMATION Course Number 11420LANG103023 Credits 2 Classroom General II (綜二館) 103 Class hours ■ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday □ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. ■ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 學生身分別 ■ 頂標生 □ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Extra Selection: 開放加簽之條件 加簽說明 □ 不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 ■ 人數上限後，開放人工加簽，學生必須符合以下條件，於第一週上課時，備妥 加簽申請表，請老師同意並簽署加簽，申請送達英語教育中心辦公室，再由老師 線上簽核完成。 ■ 條件 1：第一週必須到課。 □ 條件 2：須有其他時段【選讀英語文】衝堂無法選課之證明（如選課紀錄或本 學期所有科目課程表） □ 條件 3：自所屬選課階段（大二生：第 1-2 次選課；大三、大四學生：第 3 次 選課）起，亂數選課皆未選上（選上但退選者，不得以人工加簽再次選課） ■ 條件 4：應屆畢業生 □ 條件 5：__________ 提醒：學生修讀英文領域課程，請依本校規劃選課之修業年級選課。如因個人考量，未對 應年級而逕自改於其他修業年級選課之英文領域課程，或指定加簽某特定課程，英語教育 中心與任課教師將礙難配合或處理。 INSTRUCTOR Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) mthwang14@hotmail.com (full-time teachers only) (full-time teachers only) COURSE GOALS & DESCRIPTION 中高級英文三閱讀為一門兩學分的學期課程，幫助中高級程度之大一新生鞏固並精進英文閱讀能力。 透過廣泛閱讀，學習在短時間內快速正確精準把握文章大意與重點，拓展不同領域的字彙及閱讀技巧。 透過精讀，學習深度了解文章具體及抽象意涵，討論分析文本內涵與外延，評估作者立意觀點與語氣， 批判思辨議題，與實際世界互動。 This high-intermediate level English course is designed to help students develop extensive and intensive reading skills to grasp the point and support in the text, to explore vocabulary and reading skills by studying discipline-specific rhetoric of language patterns, and further to analyze and discuss issues that can be inferred or implied by what is presented in the text. Students will have training on academic reading skills and strategies and critical thinking skills, working to apply the skills and language being learned in task-based 2 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) collaborative activities that extend each reading chapter. By the end of this course, students will learn to develop the ability to understand and deliver academic arguments and to gain proficiency in using the language in academic contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) ✓ Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 30% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 30% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 20% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 10% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK Textbook Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking Level 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 Online Learning SPARK PLATFORM at learn.eltngl.com Teacher-led or Self-Study CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2 □ B1 □ A2 □ A1 3 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) GRADING 1. Attendance and participation – 15% 2. Quizzes – 30% 3. Midterm reading project & 5-minute talk – 25% 4. Uniform Final Exam – 30% UNIFORM FINAL EXAM This uniform final exam will take place, in the classrooms where the class usually meet and in regular class meeting hours, in Week 16. (統一期末考訂於第十六週，原班級教室與上課時間考試。) Note: Pathways Units 1, 4, 6 to be taught during class sessions, Unit 8 designated for student self- study, and all these four units covered in final exam. (註: 課堂教授 Pathways 第 1,4,6 單元，學生自學第 8 單元，期末考範圍 1,4,6,8 全部四單元。) CLASSROOM LANGUAGE ■ English 80 % ■ Mandarin 20% CLASS ACTIVITIES Group or individual presentations ◆ Research, prepare, and deliver presentations on assigned topics, developing communication skills, confidence, and the ability to organize and share ideas effectively. Jigsaw reading ◆ Divide an article or text into sections. Students read their section, summarize it, and share it with peers to complete the full picture. Critical analysis discussions ◆ Choose articles or essays and have students discuss the author’s purpose, tone, and main arguments. Discussion Circles ◆ Provide prompts related to course content or current events. Students take turns sharing opinions and supporting their ideas with examples. Vocabulary building activities ◆ Expand and apply vocabulary through tasks such as word maps, matching synonyms, and writing stories, enhancing understanding and usage in context. Interpretation projects ◆ Analyze and interpret information from texts, charts, graphs and illustrations. Present findings clearly and connect them to real-world applications. 4 Prepared by Man-Ting Huang (黃滿庭) CLASS RULES 1. Students are required to attend each class session and conscientiously participate in classroom learning activities in order to be regarded as full attendance and granted a score of 90 in the grading category of Attendance & Participation. (上課全勤，且認真參與課堂學習， 出勤參與成績得 90 分。） 2. Occasional absences up to three times will lead to a zero in the score for Attendance & Participation category, and five absences will result in a failure in this course. （三次無故缺席，無法獲得任何出勤參與成績; 五次無故缺席，學期總成績不及格。） 3. Authorized absence under exceptional circumstances can be granted, if evidence for justifiable cause can be produced. （有正當理由並可提出證明的特殊狀況，方可准假。） REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (課程使用 AI 的原則) □ 完全開放使用且無須註明 □ 有條件開放，依課程規定使用生成式 AI。 ■ 禁止使用，作業或報告必須由學生本人產出。 (AI-assisted assignments are NOT allowed; only content generated by the student can be accepted.) □ 本課程無涉及 AI 使用 生成式 人工智慧 倫理聲明 根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取禁止使 用，相關監管機制如下: ⚫ 修讀本門課程之學生應注意本門課不得繳交使用生成式人工智慧所產出的作業、報 告或個人心得。若經查核發現，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重 新評分或不予計分。 ⚫ 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 依據上述指引，本課程對於 AI 使用策略之考量與決議: 利用人工智慧生成書寫文字已是一般人輕易可得的事，不須依賴他人代工，幾個按 鍵就可產出有內容的文字，切要主旨前後一致，敘事說理文意貫串，字詞句法精準修 飾。利用機器瞬間數百萬次改寫改說，重新置換字詞字句，可輕易躲過剽竊偵測軟體， 達到 100% Unique 獨特原創性，輕鬆取得及格以上滿意的分數。我們若想逆向溯源找 出機器撰寫改說的證據，或是查驗文字內容是否由人類或機器創作，其難度相對高，畢 竟人類語文表達，就本質來說，雖有語法約定俗成的限制，但也容許相當大的自由程 度，同樣意思可以不同字詞句法表達，容許使用不同旨趣細微差別的文字，這也是人工 智慧文字內容生成系統建構所利用的語言特性。 然而，若是不需付出任何努力學習，就可取得一篇精緻完美的報告或論述文章，這 對於學校作為建構知識學習場域實質構成欺瞞，對於社會公益公平負面影響尤其鉅大。 畢竟，學習者工作本質就是學習，抄襲造假不但無助於學習，適足以鼓勵欺瞞造假負面 價值，更是扼殺學習工作建構知識技能本質的意義。因此，學術工作由他人或機器代工 都是違背學術倫理的行為。學習者選擇誠實努力工作或是欺瞞他人找代工，這是倫理善 惡的分野，直接相關學習探索進程。本課程任課教師經審慎考量，本課程授課教師認為 本課程不宜使用生成式人工智慧作為課堂活動內容或學習輔助工具。 學 生 使 用 AI 條件 docs.text: Tentative Syllabus for “Upper-Intermediate English: Listening and Speaking” in Fall, 2024 Classroom: 綜二 103 Class Hours: Wednesday 8:00 ~ 9:50 (W12) and 10:10 ~ 12:00 (W34) Credits: 2 Instructor: 馬紹芸 (Shao-Yun Ma) E-mail: elisama1112@gmail.com 課程概述與目標 This course aims at enhancing students' listening comprehension and speaking ability by exposing them to various intriguing materials suitable to their levels. With broad range of listening materials and academic vocabulary assembled from the Academic Word List (Coxhead, 2000) and CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages), students are expected to learn and acquire high-intermediate to advanced level of listening and speaking skills. The activities in the textbook include lecture-based listening exercises to facilitate students' listening comprehension skills as well as to inspire students’ language use and relate to themes through a variety of TED talks. Classroom activities are designed with the intention of meeting their needs and arousing interests to improve their English vocabulary and listening as well as speaking skills for future uses. University Student Core Competency Indicators 25% 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 25% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 20% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 15% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 15% 5. Example 2: Students are permitted to use generative AI tools, and they should explain the usage of AI tools and relevant parameter settings in their course output. Class Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. 2. Absence from a class is NO excuse for not knowing the assignment and what has been discussed in that class. It is YOUR responsibility to ask your fellow classmates what has been covered and what will be doing in the class. 3. Plagiarism and cheating on the exam is absolutely not permitted. If someone is found plagiarizing or cheating on an exam, it means he/she will get a zero point for that exam. 4. There will be NO make-up exams/presentations unless valid and official reasons for absence are presented beforehand. 5. Mandarin 30% Upper-­‐intermediate English III Listening & Speaking 2 prepared by Iris Chang Course Goals / Description 中 高 級 英 文 三 聽 講 為 一 門 2 學 分 學 期 課 程，為 訓 練 中 高 級 程 度 之 大 一 學 生 習 得 進 階 主 題 式 英 語 溝 通 與 表 達 ， 強 化 學 生 思 考 、 組 織 及 表 達 的 整 合 技 能 ； 並 培 養 學 生 發 現 問 題 、 以 英 語 提 問 並 表 達 意 見 的 能 力，經 由 實 境 口 說 與 演 講 訓 練，增 進 學 生 英 語 聽 力 及 訓 練 演 說 技 巧 。 This semester-based English III course is specifically designed to enhance Freshman students’ listening & speaking competency at the intermediate to high-intermediate level. Students are required to prepare the designated passages BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in class discussions and complete exercise sections ON TIME. Listening input: A variety of authentic English contexts, including talks, discussions, and conversations not only help expand students’ existing knowledge about interesting and contemporary topics, but also guide them systematically through strategies and activities to meet future academic, personal or professional goals. Specific learning points are focused in each theme-based chapter, where students effectively learn to manage lengthy listening input by predicting, identifying main ideas/details, and taking notes. Pronunciation is also highlighted to improve students’ listening comprehension and speaking fluency. Speaking output: Presentation skills inspired by the Ted talks give students the techniques and authentic language they need to deliver their own presentations. Accuracy-based and fluency-based activities for specific communicative functions will help students gain the opportunity to personalize the language they learn, and to build their confidence in expressing their ideas and opinions. Communicative speaking activities including games, role-plays, and conversation practice are designed to reinforce the chapter content and to allow students to practice integrated language skills. Individual and group projects/presentations will also be given throughout the semester. The ultimate goal of this course is the encourage students to take charge of their own learning and to facilitate the essential l 21st century skills – collaboration, communication and critical thinking. Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) Prepared by Jennifer Liu 2 ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well-supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) ✓ Develop foundational academic writing skills, such as crafting clear, concise paragraphs and organizing ideals logically for academic assignments. (EAP) Course Goals: ⚫ This course aims to enhance students’ academic reading ability with useful reading strategies. The designated textbook provides academic readings materials to consolidate comprehension across different fields. Students are guided from a great variety of reading passages so as to be familiar with contextualized vocabulary and various aspects toward issues. After input from all types of reading materials, students are encouraged to express opinions on related issues with the practice on presentation skills. Course Descriptions: ⚫ Lecture, as well as group discussion, presentation, and language activities will help students get prepared for daily and academic reading tasks. Note-taking skills, vocabulary, and reading skills are designed to improve students’ reading ability, while discussion, debate, and presentation would train student’s academic communication. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善 用 英 語 學 習 資 源 ， 培 養 獨 立 學 習 英 語 的 習 慣 能 力 Classroom Languages ■ English 80 %  Mandarin 20 % Upper-intermediate English III Listening & Speaking 2 prepared by Yvonne Huang Course Aims / Description 中高級英文三聽講為一門 2 學分學期課程，為訓練中高級程度之大一學生習得進階主題式英語溝通與表達， 強化學生思考、組織及表達的整合技能；並培養學生發現問題、以英語提問並表達意見的能力，經由實境口說 與演講訓練，增進學生英語聽力及訓練演說技巧。 This semester-based course is specifically designed to enhance freshman students’ listening & speaking competency at the upper-intermediate level. Students are required to prepare the designated passages BEFORE class, ACTIVELY participate in class discussions and complete exercise sections ON TIME. Listening input: A variety of authentic English-speaking contexts, including university lectures, interviews, podcasts, and classroom discussions not only activate students’ background knowledge of the topic, prime them for the authentic and inspirational content they will meet in the thought-provoking TED Talks, but also guide them systematically through strategies and activities to meet future academic, personal or professional goals. Specific and key academic skills are focused in each theme-based unit, where students effectively learn to predict, identify main ideas/details/inferences, take notes and manage lengthy input. Pronunciation is also highlighted as an aid to improving both listening comprehension & speaking fluency. Speaking output: Presentation skills inspired by the TED speakers give students the techniques & authentic language they need to successfully deliver their own presentations, help them gain the opportunity to personalize the language they learn, and build their confidence in expressing ideas and opinions. Visual/digital literacy will be promoted through lots of infographics and speaking activities designed to involve students working with a partner or in a group. With connected ideas and integrated language skills, students will give individual, pair and group projects/presentation regularly throughout the semester. The ultimate goals of the course are to encourage students to take charge of their learning and to facilitate their essential 21st century skills—collaboration, communication and critical thinking. docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University Spring 2026 Upper-Intermediate English III_Reading Class F3F4 COURSE INFORMATION Course Number LANG 103038 Credits 2 Classroom 綜二 203 Class hours □ Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday ■ Friday □ 8:00A.M. – 9:50A.M. ■ 10:10A.M. – 12:00P.M. 學生身分別 ■ 頂標生 □ 前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Extra Enrollments: Not Available 本課程不提供加簽 INSTRUCTOR Name Email Office Office Hour 劉文貞 (Jennifer W. Liu) wenchenl2013@gmail.com 綜二 210 Friday 1:30 pm-3:30 pm (By Appointment) COURSE GOALS & DESCRIPTION This two-credit semester course, High-Intermediate English Reading III, is designed to help first-year college students at a high-intermediate level strengthen and enhance their English reading skills. Through extensive reading, students will develop the ability to quickly and accurately grasp the main ideas and key points of texts, while expanding their vocabulary and reading techniques across various fields. Intensive reading activities will further enable students to understand both concrete and abstract meanings in texts, discuss and analyze the author’s intent, engage in critical thinking, and connect topics to real-world contexts. Class activities include lectures, group discussions, pair practice, and presentations. Upon completing the course, students will be able to: ✓ Read and comprehend texts at a high-intermediate level, using strategies for both extensive and intensive reading. (EAP) ✓ Identify and understand the main ideas and specific details of various texts efficiently and accurately. (EAP) ✓ Expand and retain knowledge of content-specific vocabulary, collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and phrasal verbs for academic and professional contexts. (EAP) ✓ Develop critical thinking skills by evaluating an author’s purpose, tone, and bias, and forming well- supported opinions about the text. (EAP) ✓ Utilize effective study skills, such as note-taking and summarizing, to support academic success. (EAP) ✓ Interpret and integrate information from charts, illustrations, and photographs, alongside textual content. (EAP) ✓ Engage with texts beyond surface-level understanding by forming independent ideas and opinions about key topics. (EAP) 2 UNIVERSITY STUDENT CORE COMPETENCY INDICATORS 課程核心能力 1. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英語溝通與表達能力 25% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深度分析與組織思考能力 25% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英語學習策略與技巧 25% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣能力 15% UNIFORM TEXTBOOK Vargo, M., Blass, L. & Sherman K. (2025). Pathways: Reading, Writing, and Critical Thinking 4 (3rd Edition). National Geographic Learning. ISBN: 9780357980101 CEFR Scale ■ C1 □ B2 □ B1 □ A2+ □ A2 E-LEARN PLATFORM https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw RECOMMENDED ONLINE DICTIONARIES 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English Online https://www.ldoceonline.com/ 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. The Free Dictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/ REGULATIONS FOR USING AI (AI 使用原則) Students are not allowed to use AI to generate any assignments, including in-class worksheets. However, they are allowed to use AI to revise their assignments or answers. When doing so, students need to provide their original version, the revised version by the AI, and a list of lessons or insights they have gained from the AI’s revised version. GRADING 1. Attendance and Participation – 15% 2. Pair Article Presentation – 15 % 3. Quizzes – 20 % 4. In-Class Tasks/ Worksheets – 15 % 5. Assignments – 5% 6. Uniform Final Exam – 30% 3 Class Participation/ Attendance Students are expected to attend each class punctually and actively participate in pair, group, and class discussions. If you cannot attend, you must (1) email the teacher and (2) apply for leave trhough the school’s online system. Some details here: • Student Leave Policies: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-264831,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Student Leave Guidelines: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1480-269011,r7918.php?Lang=zh-tw • Related Document Downloads: https://sa.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/412-1480-21552.php?Lang=zh-tw Important rules for this course: 1. For sick or personal leave, you must provide valid docuents. ▪ For sick leave, a medical receipt or certificate is required. 2. For quizzes, presentations, and the final exam, you must show official documents to arrange a make-up. ▪ Travelling or taking driver’s license test is not an acceptable reason. 3. If your leave request is not approved, it will count as an absence. Attendance, punctuality, and class participation will be recorded for evaluation. Attendance will be tracked from the first week, so please make sure you attend the first class on time. Attendance Policy ➢ Starting Point: 9 (起始點: 9 分) ➢ Lateness: -2 (遲到: 2 分) ➢ Absence: -5 (缺席: 5 分) ➢ Irrelevant Work in Class: -2 (做課堂不相關的事: 2 分) The starting attendance score is 9 points. Each late arrival deducts 2 points. Each absence deducts 5 points. Engaging in irrelevant activities in class deducts 2 points. (This includes using a phone for non-class-related activities or working on assignments for other courses.) The score has no lower limit but a maximum of 20 points. In other words, a negative attendance score will lower your semester grade, while a high attendance score can earn you up to 5 extra points towards your semester grade. 出席成績從 9 分開始計算，並依以下規則增減：每次遲到扣 2 分，缺席扣 5 分。若在課堂上從事無關活動 （如使用手機處理與課程無關的事務或做其他課程作業），則扣 2 分。分數累積上限為 20 分，無下限。換 言之，若出席成績為負分，將併入學期成績計算；若累積達 20 分，則學期成績額外加 5 分。 All these seemingly complicated and trivial calculations for attendance and class participation are designed to encourage you to speak more English and participate more actively in class. The more you engage in each class, the more harvest you’ll reap from this course. 4 PAIR ARTICLE PRESENTATION Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class. Sign-ups must be completed by the third week, and the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this course requirement, students must: • Begin preparation at least two weeks in advance • Meet all deadlines • Memorize their speeches • Rehearse thoroughly (For further details, see Appendices I & II) IN-CLASS TASKS/WORKSHEETS Each class includes pair or group tasks and discussions, and all students are required to participate actively. At the end of each session, the instructor will collect the worksheets. Four or five will be randomly selectly for grading. • If you are absent, the worksheet score will be 0. • Late submissions will not be accepted. ASSIGNMENTS All assignments must be typed and turned in on time. Late assignments will not be graded. QUIZZES Two quizzes, as scheduled in the course outline, will test students on both vocabulary and the content of the textbook articles as well as articles presented by classmates. Pop quizzes may also be given before student presentations; these will count for 1/4 of the total 20% quiz grade. UNIFORM FINAL EXAM The uniform final exam (30% of the semester grade) will take place in the regular classroom at the usual class meeting time in Week 16. It will cover four units of the textbook: Units 1, 4, 6, and 8. Units 1, 4, and 8 will be taught in class, while Unit 6 must be studied independedntly by students. COURSE SCHEDULE Week Date Main Topic Reading Strategies Critical Thinking 1. 2/27 No Class (Peace Memorial Day) Watch a lesson video on • Course Introduction & Orientation • Introduction to the BEST Test of English Proficiency* 2. 3/6 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace ✓ Identifying main ideas and key details (EAP) 5 Introduction to the BEST Reading Test* 3. 3/13 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace Introduction to the BEST Writing Test*  Recognizing claims and counterclaims (EAP) 4. 3/20 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace ✓ Understanding cohesion (EAP) 5. 3/27 Unit 1 The Changing Workplace  Summarizing a text (EAP) 6. 4/3 No Class (Children’s Day) Watch a video lesson on Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Recognizing and evaluating different viewpoints (EAP) 7. 4/10 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Using a concept map (EAP) 8. 4/17 Quiz#1 9. 4/24 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport ✓ Understanding complex sentences (EAP)  Inferring meaning (EAP) 10. 5/1 Unit 4 Rethinking Transport  Comparing and contrasting two perspectives (EAP) 11. 5/8 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Reading extended texts (EAP) 12. 5/15 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Asking questions as you read (EAP) 13. 5/22 Quiz#2 14. 5/29 Unit 8 Living Longer ✓ Understanding supporting examples (EAP)  Interpreting visual data (EAP) 15. 6/5 Unit 8 Living Longer  Synthesizing (EAP) 16. 6/12 Uniform Final Exam (原班級教室與上課時間 考試) Note: Unit 6, “Why Language Matters,” is designated as a self-learning unit for students. 6 Appendix I Pair Article Presentation Students will choose an article from the course packet and deliver a 10-minute pair presentation in class without using PowerPoint slides. Sign-ups must be completed by Week 3; the presentation schedule will be announced afterward. To fulfill this requirement, begin preparing at least two weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, memorize your speech, and rehearse thoroughly. I. Two Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) Confirm your presentation article. b) Meet with your partner and divide the work evenly. c) Read the article carefully at least once. d) Post your questions on the article title and your answers on eeclass. II. One Week Before the Presentation Day a) Post your subheadings of the article on eeclass. 1. Number all paragraphs first. 2. Group paragraphs logically and give each group a subheading. 3. Use short phrases, not full sentences. b) Post your vocabulary list on eeclass. • This list is different from “word sharing.” It should contain around 15 or more words, depending on the article’s length and difficulty. (If the article is longer and harder, you will need to include more vocab words.) c) Vocabulary List Guidelines i. Include each word, its part of speech (i.e. noun, verb, or adjective, etc.), the English definition (as used in the article), and an example sentence from the dictionary. ii. Number the words and list them in order of appearance. iii. If you cannot find an example in dictionaries, use the sentence from your article (do not invent your own). iv. Recommended dictionaries: 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English http://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/epidemic 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. TheFreeDictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/innumerable ◼ Note: Use Longman first, as definitions in class are usually drawn from it. If not suitable, consult Cambridge, then The Free Dictionary. d) Do not email me your vocabulary list. Proofreading is your responsibility. However, if you have difficulty finding a definition, you may ask Jennifer. e) Compose your speech as early as possible. f) Memorize and rehearse thoroughly before presentation day. 7 III. On the Presentation Day a) Materials • Distribute copies of your vocabulary list to classmates. • Submit one copy of your vocabulary list and your written report to the teacher before presenting. b) Content of the Presentation Your presentation should include: 1. Summary (3 minutes) • Tip: List key words first, then organize them into main ideas using your own logic and words. • Do not copy sentences directly from the article. 2. Vocabulary Sharing (2 minutes) • Choose 2-3 words or phrases that impressed you most. • Explain why they were memorable. • You may also share a sentence that you find interesting in the article instead of words or phrases 3. Personal Responses (2 minutes each speaker) • Each presenter must share their own thoughts and reflections after reading. c) Time Limit • Total time: 10 minutes • Article summary: 3 mins. • Vocabulary/ sentence sharing: 2 mins. • Personal responses: 2 mins. per speaker ◼ You must stop immediately when time is up, even if your presentation is unfinished. d) Q&A • After your talk, classmates and the instructor will ask questions about the article or your presentation. • Both presenters must take turns answering. • Students who ask questions will earn extra class participation point for that day. e) Written Report 1. Type a written report including: article summary, vocabulary sharing, and your responses. 2. Indicate how you and your partner divided the work. 3. Submit a copy to the teacher before presenting, and also upload the report to eeclass no later than the presentation day. 4. AI Usage Policy: You must not use AI to generate your speech. However, you are encouraged to use AI to proofread or revise your speech. If you do so, you must submit: • Your original version, • AI’s revised version, and • A sort list of lessons you learned from the AI’s feedback. 8 Appendix II Rubric for Pair Article Presentation Category Description Point Value Volume, Articulation, & Pronunciation • speaks loudly and clearly • articulates his/her words • uses correct pronunciation 20 Preparation • posts questions about the article title and their answers two weeks prior the presentation day • posts the finalized version of article subheadings and word list on eeclass one week before the presentation day • distributes the copies the vocabulary list on time • hands in the written report on time • posts the finalized written report on eeclass by the presentation day • answers questions from the teacher as well as the fellow students well 20 Delivery • no long pauses • well-organized • adopts a proper speed, intonation, and suitable pauses • has enough eye contact • doesn’t read notes • has good time control 20 Content Summary: • includes the key points • does not copy sentences from the article • organized Word sharing: • explains the reasons for choosing the words • explains the meanings of the words used in the article • suggests how the words/phrases can be used Response: • meaningful reflection 20 Vocabulary List & Written Report Vocabulary list: • includes all important new words • chooses correct meanings used in the article • few errors • a complete list • numbers and lists the words according to their order of appearance in the article Written report: • typed • few grammatical errors • organized • includes work allocations 20 Total 100

All quiz papers should be kept till the end of the semester for later reference. 4. Midterm project –15% It includes an assignment of Unit 6 and a quiz on the unit. Four units( Units 1, 4, 6, & 8) of the textbook will be covered in the uniform exam. Because of the strict attendance and participation policy, some seats may become available during the first three weeks. Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This course equips students with the ability to read English news articles and express opinions on news and current issues, preparing them for future academic studies. It seeks to stimulate interest, expand vocabulary in journalistic English, and build background knowledge of diverse topis—politics, society, finance, technology, medicine, environment, humanities, arts, leisure, and sports—through extensive exposure to authentic news articles. 2. Subsidiary aim By completing the course, students will be able to: ⚫ understand the structure and characteristics of news writing ⚫ extend and consolidate vocabulary and reading skills across fields ⚫ appreciate satire, humor, and metaphor in news reports ⚫ gain familiarity with historical and cultural contexts of current affairs ii ⚫ develop critical thinking, participate in discussions, and express opinions ⚫ build habits of reading, listening to, and watching news reports University Student Core Competency Indicators 英文核心能力指標 No. Core Competency Indicators % 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 20 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 25 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 25 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10 Corresponding CEFR Can-do Statements 1. Attendance will be tracked from the first week, so please make sure you attend the first class on time. Attendance Policy ➢ Starting Point: 9 (起始點: 9 分) ➢ Lateness: -2 (遲到: 2 分) ➢ Absence: -5 (缺席: 5 分) ➢ Irrelevant Work in Class: -2 (做課堂不相關的事: 2 分) The starting attendance score is 9 points. Each late arrival deducts 2 points. Each absence deducts 5 points. Engaging in irrelevant activities in class deducts 2 points. (This includes using a phone for non-class-related activities or working on assignments for other courses.) The score has no lower limit but a maximum of 20 points. In other words, a negative attendance score will lower your semester grade, while a high attendance score can earn you up to 5 extra points towards your semester grade. 出席成績從 9 分開始計算，並依以下規則增減：每次遲到扣 2 分，缺席扣 5 分。若在課堂上從事無關活動 （如使用手機處理與課程無關的事務或做其他課程作業），則扣 2 分。分數累積上限為 20 分，無下限。換言 之，若出席成績為負分，將併入學期成績計算；若累積達 20 分，則學期成績額外加 5 分。 All these seemingly complicated and trivial calculations for attendance and class participation are designed to encourage you to speak more English and participate more actively in class. The more you engage in each class, the more harvest you’ll reap from this course. Quizzes Two scheduled quizzes (see course outline) will test students on: • Vocabulary • Content of the news articles discussed in class and presented by peers • News reading strategies and writing conventions In addition, pop quizzes may be given before student news presentations. Pop quizzes will account for one-third of the quiz grade (10% of the final grade). v News Presentation Students must select a news section (e.g. international news, national news, or opinion, etc.) and give EITHER a group OR an individual presentation. The chosen article must be printed and distributed to all classmates at least one week prior to the presentation day. To succeed, students should begin preparing at least 3 weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, memorize their speeches, and rehearse thoroughly so that they can deliver their presentation confidently without reading from a script. (See Appendices I and II for details.) In-Class Tasks and Worksheets Every class will include individual, pair or group tasks and discussions. Each student is expected to participate actively and contribute meaningfully. At the end of the class, worksheets will be collected. 3 or 4 will be randomly selected for grading. • If you are absent, the worksheet score will be 0. • Late submissions will not be accepted Take-Home Assignments All take-home assignments must be typed and turned in on time. These assignments are designed to build on class progress, so late work cannot be graded. MOOC Videos Students are required to watch the assigned MOOC videos (https://mooc.nthu.edu.tw/course/info/391) and complete the related discussions, exercises, or tests. Since there is not enough class time to introduce all of the essential material, these videos provide explanations of news English conventions and news reading strategies. They are an important supplement to the course and ensure that students come to class prepared to apply these concepts in discussions and assignments. Copy Fee A copy fee of NT$100-120 will be collected once during the semester to cover the course packet, test sheets and handouts. Instructor’s Guidelines for Success • Attend all classes regularly and on time. • Contribute actively to pair, group, and class discussions. • PREVIEW EACH NEWS ARTICLE (including the PRESENTATION ARTICLE) BEFORE CLASS. Use the news reading strategies we practice in class, and come with subheadings and annotations prepared. • Ask questions whenever you don’t understand—your curiosity helps everyone learn. • Browse through news headlines and news stories every day. • Listen to or watch English news broadcasts regularly to stay familiar with current affairs. • Review and build your vocabulary every day—it’s the key to understanding more. • If you ever feel you are falling behind, please reach out to your classmates or your teacher. vi Course Outline Week Date Content News Writing Features and News Reading Presentation Students will choose a news section (e.g., international news, national news, or opinion, etc.) and give either a group or an individual presentation in class. The sign-up will be completed in Week 3, and the presentation list will be announced then. To succeed, students should begin preparation about 3 weeks in advance, meet all deadlines, and rehearse carefully. Because the evaluation process begins 3 weeks before the presentation, please read the following guidelines closely. I. Three Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) Begin browsing news headlines to find a topic that interests you. (Make sure it belongs to the news section you have signed up for the presentation.) b) Email Jennifer the link (URL) to the article instead of attaching a file. In your email, include your presentation date, the news section you’ve signed up for, and the correct word count of the article. c) How to choose an article Please choose your news article from the following sources: i. Newspapers: ◼ English newspapers in Taiwan: Taipei Times, Taiwan News ◼ U.S. newspapers: The New York Times, Washington Post, Los Angeles Times, etc. ◼ UK newspapers: The Times, The Guardian, etc. ii. News agencies: AP, Reuters, CNA (https://focustaiwan.tw/) , etc. If you wish to use another source, please discuss it with me in advance. d) The article must be published after the first day of this semester, __Sep. 1 __. e) Make sure the article belongs to the news section you signed up for. f) The article length should be between 470 and 1200 words. This ensure it is substantial enough for analysis but still manageable within the presentation time. g) Please email me your article early to allow time for approval and preparation. (Do not wait until the last minute.) h) Once your article has been finalized, please keep it. This will give you enough time to focus on preparation and practice. II. Two Weeks Before the Presentation Day a) You should have finalized your article choice with Jennifer by now. b) Post your article link on eeclass. c) Post your questions on the headline as well as their answers on eeclass. d) For Group Presentations Only:  Show Jennifer a printed outline of your presentation.  Make an appointment with Jennifer to present in her office. III. One Week Before the Presentation Day a) Distribute copies of your presentation article to your classmates in class. (**Week 16 presenters must distribute the article copies on Dec. 2nd (for M56 Class) and Dec. 5th (For R56 Class) 1. When preparing the original copy, include the date, and the name of the newspaper, the xii news agency, and the journalist(s). The font size should be at least 12 pt, and leave enough margin space for classmates to take notes. 2. DO NOT CHANGE THE ARTICLE’S LAYOUT, INCLUDING NUMBERING THE PARAGRAPHS OR HIGHLIGHING THE VOCAB WORDS. 3. Before making copies, please email Jennifer the original file for approval. b) Post your subheadings of the article on eeclass. 1. Number the paragraphs first. 2. Group the paragraphs and give each group a subheading. 3. Subheadings should be phrases not full sentences. c) Post your vocab list of the article on eeclass. 1. The vocabulary list is different from ‘word sharing.’ It should contain around 15 or more words, depending on the length and difficulty level of the article. 2. How to make the vocabulary list i. Create a list of words you don't know from this article. Each entry must include the word, its part of speech, (e.g. noun, verb, or adjective, etc.), the English definition used this article, and an example sentence. ii. Number the words in the order they appear in the article. iii. If you cannot find an example sentence from dictionaries, you may use the sentence from the article. Do not create your own sentence. iv. Use the following dictionaries to look up definitions and examples: 1. Longman Dictionary of Contemporary English http://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/epidemic 2. Cambridge Dictionary https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ 3. TheFreeDictionary http://www.thefreedictionary.com/innumerable Note: Please consult Longman or Cambridge first. The definitions I provide in class are mostly from these two dictionaries because they are easier to understand and remember. If you cannot find a suitable definition there, then use TheFreeDictionary. d) Do not email me your vocab list. You are responsible for proofreading it. However, if you have trouble finding a suitable definition for a word, you are welcome to ask Jennifer. e) Compose your speech as early as possible. f) Memorize and rehearse your speech well before your presentation day. g) For Group Presentations Only: 1. Have your ppt slides 100% ready for the 2nd meeting. 2. Bring your own laptop, presentation article and vocablary list. 3. Come to Jennifer’s office on time and present your entire presentation. 4. Revise your presentation based on Jennifer’s feedback. xiii IV. On the Presentation Day a) Distribute copies of the vocabulary list to your classmates, and submit one copy of the vocabulary list to the teacher during the class recess. b) [For Individual Presentations Only] Turn in your written report to the teacher before you step up to the podium to present. c) Content of the Presentation & Time Limit  Individual News Presentation (7 mins.) (With NO ppt slides) 1) News summary (3 mins.) : Summarize the news story. Tip: List some key words first. Then, organize the key words/main ideas in your own logic and in your own words. 2) Vocabulary word sharing (2 mins.) : Choose one or two new words you learned from the article and explain why the words made a strong impression on you. If time allows, you may also share a sentence from the article that you find interesting. 3) Your response to the news story (2 mins.) : Share your personal thoughts or reactions after reading the article. Q&A: After your presentation, your classmates and the teacher will ask you questions about the article or your presentation. (Students who ask questions can earn extra class participation points that day.)  Group News Presentation (25 mins.) (WITH ppt slides) 1) Warm-Up Activity (5 mins.) 2) Vocabulary (3 mins.) 3) Comprehension of the News Article (10 mins.) • Comprehension Questions • Subheadings 4) Extension Discussion (6 mins.) 5) Conclusion (1 min.) Please complete your speech within the time limit. When the time is up, you must stop immediately, even if you have not finished. d) Written Report (For Individual Presentations Only) 1. Type a written report of your presentation and give it to the teacher before you present on the presentation day. 2. The report should include: summary, word sharing and personal response/ thoughts after reading the article. 3. Post your written report on eeclass no later than the presentation day. 4. AI Usage Policy: You must not use AI to generate your speech. However, you are encouraged to use AI to proofread or revise your speech. If you do so, you must submit: • Your original version, • AI’s revised version, and • A sort list of lessons you learned from the AI’s feedback. e) PPT Slides (For Group Presentations Only) 1. Post your ppt slides on eeclass instead of submitting a written report. 2. Your last slide must include the detailed work allocation of all group members, both for preparation and for the in-class presentation. xiv Appendix II Rubric for Individual News Article docs.text: 1 National Tsing Hua University 中高級選讀英文［學術閱讀與討論］M56 Spring 2026 Course Number LANG 2000 _42_ Credits 2 Classroom 請查閱校務資訊系統的課 程資訊後填入 Class hours  Monday □ Tuesday □ Wednesday □ Thursday □ Friday  1:20P.M. – 3:10P.M. □ 3:30P.M. – 5:20P.M. □ 10:10 A.M. – 12:00 P.M. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes)  EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level □ B1（中級） □ B1-B2  B2（中高級）  B2+ □ C1 Core Ability  comprehension/reception  communication/interaction □ production 可選課學生 身分別  頂標生  前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Prerequisites 修畢中高英文一、二或中高英文三閱讀、聽講 加簽說明  不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 林嘉瑜 joylin.nthu@gmail.com 綜二 209 TBD Course Aims / Description1 Primary aim This course primarily aims to introduce students to a diverse range of academic topics, providing them with a foundation for further discussion and exploration. Additionally, the course offers supplementary practice in academic vocabulary and critical reading strategies. Through a variety of textual and visual materials, students will be guided to consider different perspectives on various issues. After receiving input, students will be encouraged to express their opinions, demonstrate their understanding, and engage in formal discussions related to the topics covered. Supplementary course materials can be found on the eeclass course website. (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/). Participation in class discussions and activities is required and will contribute to the final grade. Homework may be given weekly and will be due in the following week. Students are expected to come to class prepared to discuss designated chapters and assignments. Quizzes will be designed to test students’ learning on reading and vocabulary skills. The final report will be designed to incorporate various reading topics and discussion skills covered in this semester. 1 請參閱 Bloom’s Taxonomy of Measurable Verbs。 2 Subsidiary aim In this class, students are encouraged to develop the following abilities for academic purposes. (1) To identify main ideas and supporting details in academic readings. (2) To explain the main points of readings in academic discussions. (3) To interpret the meaning from complex sentence structures in academic readings. (4) To exchange and collect the main points from various academic texts. (5) To construct ongoing discussions on academic topics. (6) To evaluate writer’s perspectives in readings and argue for their own points of view. CEFR Can-do Statements (B2, B2+ and C1) Reception Listening OVERALL LISTENING COMPREHENSION B2 Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP B2 Can follow extended speech and complex lines of argument provided the topic is reasonably familiar, and the direction of the talk is sign-posted by explicit markers. [overall listening comprehension] B2+ Can understand standard spoken language, live or broadcast, on both familiar and unfamiliar topics normally encountered in personal, social, academic or vocational life. Only extreme background noise, inadequate discourse structure and/or idiomatic usage influence the ability to understand. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP C1 Can understand enough to follow extended speech on abstract and complex topics beyond his/her own field, though he/she may need to confirm occasional details, especially if the accent is unfamiliar. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] C1 Can understand in detail lengthy, complex texts, whether or not they relate to his/her own area of specialty, provided he/she can reread difficult sections. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR ORIENTATION B2 Can scan quickly through long and complex texts, locating relevant details. [reading for orientation] EAP B2 Can quickly identify the content and relevance off news items, articles and reports on a wide range of professional topics, deciding whether closer study is worthwhile. [reading for orientation] EAP EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT 3 B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] B2+ Can obtain information, ideas and opinions from highly specialized sources within his/her field. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP B2+ Can understand specialized articles outside his/her field, provided he/she can use a dictionary occasionally to confirm his/her interpretation of terminology. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP C1 Can understand in detail a wide range of lengthy, complex texts likely to be encountered in social, professional or academic life, identifying finer points of detail including attitudes and implied as well as stated opinions. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP Interaction Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN INTERACTION B2 Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] B2 Can highlight the personal significance of events and experiences, account for and sustain views clearly by providing relevant explanations and arguments. [overall spoken interaction] B2+ Can use the language fluently, accurately and effectively on a wide range of general, academic, vocational or leisure topics, marking clearly the relationships between ideas. [overall spoken interaction] EAP EOP B2+ Can communicate spontaneously with good grammatical control without much sign of having to restrict what he/she wants to say, adopting a level of formality appropriate to the circumstances. [overall spoken interaction] C1 Can express him/herself fluently and spontaneously, almost effortlessly. [overall spoken interaction] C1 Has a good command of a broad lexical repertoire allowing gaps to be readily overcome with circumlocutions. [overall spoken interaction] C1 There is little obvious searching for expressions or avoidance strategies; only a conceptually difficult subject can hinder a natural, smooth flow of language. [overall spoken interaction] UNDERSTANDING NATIVE SPEAKER INTERLOCUTOR B2 Can understand in detail what is said to him/her in the standard spoken language even in a noisy environment. [understanding native speaker interlocutor] C1 Can understand in detail speech on abstract and complex topics of a specialist nature beyond his/her own field, though he/she may need to confirm occasional details, especially if the accent is unfamiliar. [understanding native speaker interlocutor] EAP EOP CONVERSATION 4 B2 Can engage in extended conversation on most general topics in a clearly participatory fashion, even in a noisy environment. [conversation] B2 Can sustain relationships with native speakers without unintentionally amusing or irritating them or requiring them to behave other than they would with a native speaker. [conversation] B2 Can convey degrees of emotion and highlight the personal significance of events and experiences. [conversation] C1 Can use language flexibly and effectively for social purposes, including emotional, allusive and joking and joking usage. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can take an active part in informal discussion in familiar contexts, commenting, putting point of view clearly, evaluating alternative proposals and making and responding to hypotheses. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can with some effort catch much of what is said around him/her in discussion, but may find it difficult to participate effectively in discussion with several native speakers who do not modify their language in any way. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP B2+ Can keep up with an animated discussion between native speakers. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2+ Can express his/her ideas and opinions with precision, present and respond to complex lines of argument convincingly. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP C1 Can easily follow and contribute to complex interactions between third parties in group discussion even on abstract, complex unfamiliar topics. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP FORMAL DISCUSSION (MEETINGS) B2 Can participate actively in routine and non-routine formal discussion. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP B2 Can follow the discussion on matters related to his/her field, understand in detail the points given prominence by the speaker. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP B2 Can contribute, account for and sustain his/her opinion, evaluate alternative proposals and make and respond to hypotheses. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP B2+ Can keep up with an animated discussion, identifying accurately arguments supporting and opposing points of view. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP B2+ Can express his/her ideas and opinions with precision, present and respond to complex lines of argument convincingly. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP C1 Can easily keep up with the debate, even on abstract, complex unfamiliar topics. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP 5 C1 Can argue a formal position convincingly, responding to questions and comments and answering complex lines of counter argument fluently, spontaneously and appropriately. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP Interaction Written Writing OVERALL WRITTEN INTERACTION B2 Can express news and views effectively in writing, and relate to those of others. [overall written interaction] C1 Can express him/herself with clarity and precision, relating to the addressee flexibly and effectively. [overall written interaction] CORRESPONDENCE B2 Can write letters conveying degrees of emotion and highlighting the personal significance of events and experiences and commenting on the correspondent’s news and views. [correspondence] C1 Can express him/herself with clarity and precision in personal correspondence, using language flexibly and effectively, including emotional, allusive and joking usage. [correspondence] Interaction Communi cation Strategies TAKING THE FLOOR (TURNTAKING) B2 Can intervene appropriately in discussion, exploiting appropriate language to do so. [taking the floor (turntaking)] EAP EOP B2 Can initiate, maintain, and end discourse appropriately with effective turntaking. [taking the floor (turntaking)] B2 Can initiate discourse, take his/her turn when appropriate and end conversation when he/she needs to, though he/she may not always do this elegantly. [taking the floor (turntaking)] B2 Can use stock phrases (e.g., “That’s a difficult question to answer”) to gain time and keep the turn whilst formulating what to say. [taking the floor (turntaking)] C1 Can select a suitable phrase from a readily available range of discourse functions to preface his/her remarks appropriately in order to get the floor, or to gain time and keep the floor whilst thinking. [taking the floor (turntaking)] EAP EOP COOPERATING B2 Can help the discussion along on familiar ground, confirming comprehension, inviting others in, etc. [cooperating] B2+ Can give feedback on and follow up statements and inferences and so help the development of the discussion. [cooperating] EAP EOP C1 Can relate his/her own contributions skillfully to those of other speakers. [cooperating] ASKING FOR CLARIFICATION B2 Can ask follow-up questions to check that he/she has understood what a speaker intended to say, and get clarification of ambiguous points. [asking for clarification] PLANNING B2 Can plan what is to be said and the means to say it, considering the effect on the recipient(s). [planning] 6 COMPENSATING B2 Can use circumlocution and paraphrase to cover gaps in vocabulary and structure. [compensating] EAP MONITORING & REPAIR B2 Can correct slips and errors if he/she becomes conscious of them or if they have led to misunderstandings. [monitoring & repair] B2 Can make a note of “favorite mistakes” and consciously monitor speech for it/them. [monitoring & repair] EAP C1 Can backtrack when he/she encounters a difficulty and reformulate what he/she wants to say without fully interrupting the flow of speech. [monitoring & repair] EAP EOP Sociolinguistic SOCIOLINGUISTIC APPROPRIATENESS B2 Can with some effort keep up with and contribute to group discussions even when speech is fast and colloquial. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] B2+ Can express him/herself confidently, clearly and politely in a formal or informal register, appropriate to the situation and the person(s) concerned. Please leave messages on eeclass, using the “personal messages” function. eeclass email 2 prepared by Vicky Hsu Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This course is designed for students who hope to read English short stories for pleasure and for improvement of reading comprehension and skills. Through reading a variety of contemporary and classical short stories and discussing the plot and the theme behind the stories, students are expected to engage in a close reading of the language used in the stories and make connections between the stories and any or all of the following: the personal world, aspects of human nature, society and the wider world. Students will get prepared for reading fiction beyond the classroom after taking up this course. 2. Subsidiary aim The activities related to reading a short story will be divided into seven phases: (1) reflecting on the topic before reading and relating prior knowledge and personal experience to the topic (2) understanding important literary elements and structures of a story and identifying examples in the short stories (EAP) (3) developing the habit of reading fiction (4) enhancing reading comprehension skills and reading strategies (5) interacting with classmates in the discussion of the situations, confrontations, and challenges faced by the main characters (6) exploring and sharing context clues, perspectives, and cultural information (7) investigating authentic language use and rhetorical devices such as form, tone, word use, and imagery (EAP) 3. Corresponding CEFR Can-do statements Can-do statement #1 B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low-frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] Can-do statement #2 B2 Can take an active part in informal discussion in familiar contexts, commenting, putting point of view clearly, evaluating alternative proposals and making and responding to hypotheses. [informal discussion (with friends)] Can-do statement #3 B2 Can give a clear, prepared presentation, giving reasons in support of or against a particular point of view and giving the EAP 3 prepared by Vicky Hsu advantages and disadvantages of various options. [addressing audiences] Can-do statement #4 B2 Can use a variety of strategies to achieve comprehension, including listening for main points, checking comprehension by using contextual clues. [identifying cues & inferring (spoken & written)] EAP Can-do statement #5 B2+ Can give feedback on and follow up statements and inferences and so help the development of the discussion. [cooperating] EAP Can-do statement #6 B2 Can understand a clearly structured lecture on a familiar subject, and can take notes on points which strike him/her as important, even though he/she tends to concentrate on the words themselves and therefore to miss some information. [note-taking (lectures, seminars, etc.) EAP Can-do statement #7 B2 Can with some effort keep up with and contribute to group discussions even when speech is fast and colloquial. [sociolinguistic appropriateness] 英文核心能力指標 University Student Core Competency Indicators No. Core Competency Indicators 1. 英語溝通與表達能力 (ability to communicate and express oneself in English) 30% 2. 深度分析與組織思考的能力 (ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English) 30% 3. 英語學習策略與技巧 (knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques) 20% 4. 對英語與多元文化的國際視野 (global views of English and multicultural diversity) 10% 5. 善用英語學習資源，培養獨立學習英語的習慣與能力 (ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self-learning habit) 10% Teaching Materials and References Textbook(s) Course pack (a selection of classical and famous short stories) for in-class discussion and for the independent & extensive reading project CEFR Scale □ B1 □ B1-B2  B2 □ B2+ □ C1 Platforms for course materials and learning resources 1. 清華大學 eeclass 數位學習系統 https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/ 2. Schedule your reading: The teacher will not remind you when to start reading or how many stories or pages await you. You need to make sure that you have plenty of time for this project. 4. Annotate: Reading is not only understanding literary meanings of words and sentences but also having an intellectual conversation with the text and even the character(s) or the author. You may ask questions, comment on meaning, and relate the text to your personal events or reflections while you are reading. You may refer to the following methods for annotating a text.  Post-it notes: If you are a person who does not like to write in a book, you may want to invest in a supply of post it notes.  Colors: If you feel really creative, or are just super organized, you can even color code your annotations by using different color post-its, highlighters, or pens  Brackets: If several lines seem important, just draw a line down the margin and underline/highlight only the key phrases.  Asterisks: Place and asterisk next to an important passage; use two if it is really important  Marginal notes: Use the space in the margins to make comments, define words, ask questions, etc.  Text marking: Caution! Do not underline or highlight too much! You want to concentrate on the important elements, not entire pages (use brackets for that).  Shapes: Use circles, boxes, triangles, squiggly lines, stars, etc. Source: https://en.wikiversity.org/wiki/A_Reader%27s_Guide_to_Annotation 11 prepared by Vicky Hsu Part 2 Creating a reading log (70%) Your reading log must show that you have read and understood the short stories you choose and that you are capable of applying the reading strategies and identifying literary devices that we have practiced throughout the semester. You can’t be wrong with your responses, as these reflect your personal reactions or connections to the text. Take some risks and be honest. Use the sample prompts to help you get started with expressing your likes/dislikes, confusion, and observations. Be careful: It’s NOT literary analysis or criticism. 250-300 E. In the letter, you may tell the character how you feel about the problem(s) and struggle(s) he or she went through, how much you understand the ways he or she deals with the conflict, and why he or she makes a critical decision or judgment. You may also express what inspires you, or how his/her words in the story inspire or enlighten you. Be careful about the format and the wording. F. Memorable Quotes Copy at least at one sentence from each story you have read and explain why these lines caught your attention and/or how the quotes move or inspire you. Your explanation can be in English or Chinese. Be careful that you are not expected to explain the story around the quote. 。 Memorable quotes 12 prepared by Vicky Hsu Extended Reading Checklist Directions Check () the short stories you have read for completing your extended reading project. The ability to communicate and express oneself in English 英 語 溝 通 與 表 達 能 力 10% 2. The ability to think critically and organize ideas logically in English 深 度 分 析 與 組 織 思 考 能 力 20% 3. The knowledge of English learning strategies and techniques 英 語 學 習 策 略 與 技 巧 30% 4. Global views of English and multicultural diversity 對 英 語 與 多 元 文 化 的 國 際 視 野 10% 5. The ability to use existing English learning resources and development of independent self- learning habits 善 用 英 語 學 習 資 源 ， 培 養 獨 立 學 習 英 語 的 習 慣 能 力 2 prepared by Yvonne Huang Course Aims / Description 1. Primary aim This course is designed to introduce students to the interpretation world and its real practice. Consecutive interpretation will be covered starting from a very general aspect gradually into the professional domain. Students will not only gain the knowledge on the interpretation as a whole, but also learn and develop the most basic technique to interpret accurately and fluently from English into Chinese and vice versa chunks of articles or speeches (usually 2-3 minutes long). 2. Subsidiary aims 1. to enhance confidence in oral communication and in getting message across 2. to develop interests in building the bridge between two cultures 3. to enhance English listening and speaking ability 4. to improve the skills of summarizing and grasping main ideas/key messages 5. to explore both general and professional areas of studies Course Methodology The main focus of the course will be on the practice of basic techniques and interpretation itself. In the first half of the semester and before the actual interpretation practices begin, students will receive training and learn some basic skills including: 1. shadowing 2. short-term memory recall 3. summarizing & paraphrasing 4. BIG numbers 5. sight interpretation 6. word choice 7. note-taking In the second half of the semester, workshops and mock conferences will be held, where students will have numerous interpretation practices on interested topics and speeches. Course Materials Handouts will be distributed in class with e-files @ eeclass site. * Our Class Material Site eeclass * Yvonne’s MOOC site 中英口譯揭密 * Learning/Resource Platform  Chinese & English news channels  YouTube  TED Talks  Interpretation related news & sharing  Online English dictionaries (Oxford, Longman, Macmillan etc.) Declaration for Student Use of AI Fully open for use without attribution. Students are free to use AI tools without the need to provide 3 prepared by Yvonne Huang attribution in their course work. Grading Policy Attendance & Performance 15% Assignments 35% Mock Conferences 25% Final Exam 25% Classroom Languages  English 70 %  Mandarin 30 % Teaching Activities  Lectures  Lab training  Assignments (shadowing & self/peer evaluation)  Listening comprehension activities  In-class (pair / group) discussion  Vocabulary building activities  Thought-provoking questions & discussion  English Online Learning Site Class Rules 1. Class attendance, lesson preparation and active class participation are required. Attendance will be taken every week throughout the semester. If students are absent due to uncontrollable circumstances (e.g., illness, emergency, important occasions, etc.), a valid proof must be provided within two weeks. All leave requests should be submitted through the school’s online system. Five absences with approved requests or three absences without requests will result in a failing grade. 2. Absence from a class is NO excuse for not knowing the assignment and what has been discussed in that class. It is YOUR responsibility to ask your fellow classmates what has been covered and what will be doing in the class. 3. Plagiarism and cheating on the exam is absolutely not permitted. Students found plagiarizing or cheating on an exam will receive a zero point for that exam. 4. There will be NO make-up exams/presentations unless valid and official reasons for absence are presented beforehand. 5. The handouts given in the class should be kept at least till the end of the semester for later reference or final exam. 6. Cellular phone should be turned off during the two-hour class period. 4 prepared by Yvonne Huang Detailed Syllabus WK. Course Type □ EGP (English for general purposes)  EAP (English for academic purposes) □ EOP (English for occupational purposes) Language Level □ B1（中級） □ B1-B2  B2（中高級）  B2+ □ C1 Core Ability  comprehension/reception  communication/interaction □ production 可選課學生 身分別  頂標生  前標生 □ 中級生 □ 初級生 Prerequisites 修畢中高英文一、二或中高英文三閱讀、聽講 加簽說明  不開放人工加簽。所有學生須由選課系統亂數選課。 Instructor & Contact Information: Name Email Office & Tel Office Hour 林嘉瑜 joylin.nthu@gmail.com 綜二 209 TBD Course Aims / Description1 Primary aim This course primarily aims to introduce students to a diverse range of academic topics, providing them with a foundation for further discussion and exploration. Additionally, the course offers supplementary practice in academic vocabulary and critical reading strategies. Through a variety of textual and visual materials, students will be guided to consider different perspectives on various issues. After receiving input, students will be encouraged to express their opinions, demonstrate their understanding, and engage in formal discussions related to the topics covered. Supplementary course materials can be found on the eeclass course website. (https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/). Participation in class discussions and activities is required and will contribute to the final grade. Homework may be given weekly and will be due in the following week. Students are expected to come to class prepared to discuss designated chapters and assignments. Quizzes will be designed to test students’ learning on reading and vocabulary skills. The final report will be designed to incorporate various reading topics and discussion skills covered in this semester. 1 請參閱 Bloom’s Taxonomy of Measurable Verbs。 2 Subsidiary aim In this class, students are encouraged to develop the following abilities for academic purposes. (1) To identify main ideas and supporting details in academic readings. (2) To explain the main points of readings in academic discussions. (3) To interpret the meaning from complex sentence structures in academic readings. (4) To exchange and collect the main points from various academic texts. (5) To construct ongoing discussions on academic topics. (6) To evaluate writer’s perspectives in readings and argue for their own points of view. CEFR Can-do Statements (B2, B2+ and C1) Reception Listening OVERALL LISTENING COMPREHENSION B2 Can understand the main ideas of propositionally and linguistically complex speech of both concrete and abstract topics in a standard dialect, including technical discussions in his/her field of specialization. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP B2 Can follow extended speech and complex lines of argument provided the topic is reasonably familiar, and the direction of the talk is sign-posted by explicit markers. [overall listening comprehension] B2+ Can understand standard spoken language, live or broadcast, on both familiar and unfamiliar topics normally encountered in personal, social, academic or vocational life. Only extreme background noise, inadequate discourse structure and/or idiomatic usage influence the ability to understand. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP C1 Can understand enough to follow extended speech on abstract and complex topics beyond his/her own field, though he/she may need to confirm occasional details, especially if the accent is unfamiliar. [overall listening comprehension] EAP EOP Reception Reading OVERALL READING COMPREHENSION B2 Can read with a large degree of independence, adapting style and speed of reading to different texts and purposes, and using appropriate reference sources selectively. Has a broad active reading vocabulary, but may experience some difficulty with low- frequency vocabulary. [overall reading comprehension] C1 Can understand in detail lengthy, complex texts, whether or not they relate to his/her own area of specialty, provided he/she can reread difficult sections. [overall reading comprehension] READING FOR ORIENTATION B2 Can scan quickly through long and complex texts, locating relevant details. [reading for orientation] EAP B2 Can quickly identify the content and relevance off news items, articles and reports on a wide range of professional topics, deciding whether closer study is worthwhile. [reading for orientation] EAP EOP READING FOR INFORMATION & ARGUMENT 3 B2 Can understand articles and reports concerned with contemporary problems in which the writer adopts particular stances or viewpoints. [reading for information & argument] B2+ Can obtain information, ideas and opinions from highly specialized sources within his/her field. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP B2+ Can understand specialized articles outside his/her field, provided he/she can use a dictionary occasionally to confirm his/her interpretation of terminology. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP C1 Can understand in detail a wide range of lengthy, complex texts likely to be encountered in social, professional or academic life, identifying finer points of detail including attitudes and implied as well as stated opinions. [reading for information & argument] EAP EOP Interaction Spoken Speaking OVERALL SPOKEN INTERACTION B2 Can interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction, and sustained relationships with native speakers quite possible without imposing strain on either party. [overall spoken interaction] B2 Can highlight the personal significance of events and experiences, account for and sustain views clearly by providing relevant explanations and arguments. [overall spoken interaction] B2+ Can use the language fluently, accurately and effectively on a wide range of general, academic, vocational or leisure topics, marking clearly the relationships between ideas. [overall spoken interaction] EAP EOP B2+ Can communicate spontaneously with good grammatical control without much sign of having to restrict what he/she wants to say, adopting a level of formality appropriate to the circumstances. [overall spoken interaction] C1 Can express him/herself fluently and spontaneously, almost effortlessly. [overall spoken interaction] C1 Has a good command of a broad lexical repertoire allowing gaps to be readily overcome with circumlocutions. [overall spoken interaction] C1 There is little obvious searching for expressions or avoidance strategies; only a conceptually difficult subject can hinder a natural, smooth flow of language. [overall spoken interaction] UNDERSTANDING NATIVE SPEAKER INTERLOCUTOR B2 Can understand in detail what is said to him/her in the standard spoken language even in a noisy environment. [understanding native speaker interlocutor] C1 Can understand in detail speech on abstract and complex topics of a specialist nature beyond his/her own field, though he/she may need to confirm occasional details, especially if the accent is unfamiliar. [understanding native speaker interlocutor] EAP EOP CONVERSATION 4 B2 Can engage in extended conversation on most general topics in a clearly participatory fashion, even in a noisy environment. [conversation] B2 Can sustain relationships with native speakers without unintentionally amusing or irritating them or requiring them to behave other than they would with a native speaker. [conversation] B2 Can convey degrees of emotion and highlight the personal significance of events and experiences. [conversation] C1 Can use language flexibly and effectively for social purposes, including emotional, allusive and joking and joking usage. [conversation] INFORMAL DISCUSSION (WITH FRIENDS) B2 Can take an active part in informal discussion in familiar contexts, commenting, putting point of view clearly, evaluating alternative proposals and making and responding to hypotheses. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can with some effort catch much of what is said around him/her in discussion, but may find it difficult to participate effectively in discussion with several native speakers who do not modify their language in any way. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2 Can account for and sustain his/her opinions in discussion by providing relevant explanation, arguments and comments. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP B2+ Can keep up with an animated discussion between native speakers. [informal discussion (with friends)] B2+ Can express his/her ideas and opinions with precision, present and respond to complex lines of argument convincingly. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP C1 Can easily follow and contribute to complex interactions between third parties in group discussion even on abstract, complex unfamiliar topics. [informal discussion (with friends)] EAP EOP FORMAL DISCUSSION (MEETINGS) B2 Can participate actively in routine and non-routine formal discussion. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP B2 Can follow the discussion on matters related to his/her field, understand in detail the points given prominence by the speaker. [formal discussion (meetings)] EAP EOP B2 Can contribute, account for and sustain his/her opinion, evaluate alternative proposals and make and respond to hypotheses.
