docs.name: 基礎越南語二
docs.text: 國立清華大學114-02 基礎越南語（二） 授課老師：段雅芳 聯絡Email: ph.doan19@gmail.com 教學目標： 1. 本課程的目標是教授學生越南語。其中包括閱基礎發音、聽說讀寫四個技能， 文化的部分也將隨課程進行介紹予學生。 2. 課程內容包括練習拼音、簡單語法、句型應用、應用文知識、越南文化特色 及差異。學生於修習課程結束後，可以獲得基礎的越南語發音和生活簡單的 會話技能。 3. 最少掌握300個詞彙以及15個常用語法。 教學綱要： 第二外語－越南語（二）內容包括： 1. 發音：單元音+尾音、雙元音＋尾音的發音。 2. 語言單元：數字、與數字有關的會話主題，包括購物、詢問價格、時間說法、 與時間有關的語言內容（如：學習、工作的時間、時間表、一天的行程、日 記等），另一個主題是家裡成員，學員能介紹家裡每個成員的基本資料。 3. 多元的練習作業：聽說讀寫四個技能。 教科書： 段雅芳《速學越南語－零基礎自學、教學都適用！》，新北市：漢宇國際文化， 民108.10。 參考書： 1. 陳凰鳳編著，《越南語發音入門》，新北市：統一出版社。 2. 阮蓮香《大家的越南語初級１》，台北：瑞蘭國際出版社，2016年11月。 3. 莫子祺《實用越南語口語教程》，北京：北京大學出版社，2014 年 5 月。 4. Nguyễn Văn Huệ chủ biên Giáo trình tiếng Việt cho người nước ngoài Tập 1, Nhà xuất bản Đại học Quốc Gia Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, năm 2006. 5. Nguyễn Văn Huệ chủ biên Giáo trình tiếng Việt cho người nước ngoài Tập 2, Nhà xuất bản Đại học Quốc Gia Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, năm 2004. 教學進度表： 週次 主題 內容 第一週 第四課：我學越南文 四年了。 複習數字+跟數字有關的會話（詢問 多少） 表達學習和工作的時間 如何看懂越南地址 第二週 第四課：我學越南文 四年了。 數字有關的主題 表達距離（多少公里／小時） 閱讀練習 第三週 第四課：我學越南文 四年了。 練習寫作：學習和工作的狀況及未來 計畫 發音：雙母音 繳交第一次發音的作業 第四、五週 第五課：現在是幾 點？ 表達時間的方式、詢問幾點 表達上下班、上下課的時間表 口語練習：一天的行程 第六、七週 第五課：現在是幾 點？ 對時間做評論：早、晚 副詞：hơi, quá, lắm 進行邀約，討論時間 閱讀練習 繳交第二次發音的作業 第八週 期中考 口試＋測驗 第九、十週 第六課：今天是星期 幾？ 年月日的說法 詢問何時、多久 口語練習：討論旅行的時間 第十一、十二週 第六課：今天是星期 幾？ 表達近的未來 閱讀：日記寫作練習 發音：雙元音＋尾音 繳交第三次發音的作業 第十三週 文化分享週 認識越南各節日 第十四、十五週 第七課：你的家庭有 幾個人？ 認識家人稱謂的人稱代名詞 介紹家人 表達不確定的事件：「好像」說法 第十六週 期末考 筆試 成績評定： 平日出席率、提問與表現：10% 每堂課點名，除重大事故外，缺席四次者點名 成績不得分。 作業：30%（發音和寫作） 期中考試：30% 期末考試：30%

docs.name: 基礎泰語一
docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程教學大綱 課程簡介 Course Description 介紹泰國數字單位及筆劃練習，介紹數字單位運用，介紹泰文聲韻母及韻母。 能夠使用基礎會話與泰國人溝通。 自住旅遊專用語，問候語篇，你電話號碼幾號？，買東西篇，能給我一個折扣嗎？， 量詞，顏色，在路邊攤點菜及泰語文法。 課程目標與學習成效 Course Objectives & Learning Outcomes 1.能了解曼谷話，曼谷話是泰語的標準語。 วัตถุประสงค์ 2.在短期內能聽、說、讀、寫常用泰語、自我介紹、打招呼、問路、買東西。 3.在此學期，若按照教師的學法，保證到泰國觀光必能以泰語跟泰國人溝通，買東西不 受騙，不迷路。 4. 認識泰國的觀光勝地,泰國人的思想、文化、泰國人的基本禮貌（合掌,說話,送禮、 禁忌）。 5.將來能進修，而到泰國發展，例如：推廣中華文化、作生意、傳道、作研究、工作、 當中文教師、編中文課本等的重要基楚技能。 6.目前在泰國華語人才的需求量甚大，泰國正掀起了華文熱，很歡迎華文母語者到泰 國任教教中文，若懂泰文是將來的優勢。 7.為了提高學泰文的效率，教師建議錄音回家復習，有行線的筆記本。 8.泰國人個性溫和好客，從來不排華，沒有種族歧視，是個值得居住的地方，若懂泰 文就沒有溝通障礙。 9.學泰文不是件很難的事，只要有信心與恆心，不早放棄，保證會成功。 每週課程進度與作業要求 Course Schedule & Requirements 【請詳述：課程內容與指定閱讀／教學活動與課前、課後作業/學生學習投入時間（含 課堂教學時數）】 教材:新版大家來學泰語 400 元，泰文第㇐步 320 元與基礎泰文字(二)150 元(教科 書可以使用整個學年) docs.text: 1 國立清華大學課程教學大綱(基礎泰語二) 課程簡介 Course Description 介紹泰文清音詞與青尾音與濁音詞與濁尾音，簡化，變化，簡略，泰文前引字， 復合子音，共同當韻尾 ，二十個麥姆安。 自住旅遊專用語，問路，認識泰國的日月年，時間，祝福語，辦簽證，訂機票泰語文 法。 課程目標與學習成效 Course Objectives & Learning Outcomes 1.能更了解深入進階泰國話，並提升泰語的溝通能力。 2.認識泰國的觀光勝地,泰國人的思想、文化、泰國人的基本禮貌（合掌,說話,送禮、禁忌）。跨文化 與語言的角度廣大的視野。 3.為了提升泰文的拼音能力、使學習者能拼出泰文詞彙。 4.在此學期能聽與說進階的自住旅遊專用語，認識問路，日月年，時間，祝福，辦簽證，訂機票， 看得懂泰文字以及學泰語文法。 5.在此學期能讀與寫泰文中的字母、韻母的拼音法。 6.在此學期能了解中、高、低子音與長韻母和短韻母之拼音法。 7.在文法方面，認識泰語未來式、完成式，並能夠應用疑問句、肯定句，以及否定句在溝通語交談 上。 8.將來能進修，而到泰國發展，例如：推廣中華文化、作生意、傳道、作研究、工作、當中文教師、 編中文課本等的重要基礎技能。 9.目前在泰國華語人才的需求量甚大，泰國正掀起了華文熱，很歡迎華文母語者到泰國任教教中文， 若懂泰文是將來的優勢。 每週課程進度與作業要求 Course Schedule & Requirements 【請詳述：課程內容與指定閱讀／教學活動與課前、課後作業/學生學習投入時間（含 課堂教學時數）】 教材:大家來學泰語與基礎泰文字 2 (第㇐週要準備剛好的錢購買基礎泰文字○2 150 元) 2 週次 課程內容 1 第七節泰文清音詞與青尾音 P.58-61 第七課問路生詞與會話 2 第七節泰文清音詞與青尾音 P.62-65 第七課問路句行練習 3 第七節泰文清音詞與青尾音 P.67-69 第八課日月年生詞 4 第八節泰文濁音詞與濁尾音 P.70-73 第八課日月年會話 5 第八節泰文濁音詞與濁尾音 P.74-77 第八課日月年句行練習 6 第八節泰文濁音詞與濁尾音 P.78-82 第九課時間生詞 7 第九節泰文簡化，變化，簡略 P.83-91 第九課時間與會話 8 第九節泰文簡化，變化，簡略 P.92-101 第九課時間句行練習 9 期中考 10 第十節泰文前引字 P.102 第十課祝福生詞語會話 11 第十節泰文前引字 P.103 第十課祝福句行練習 12 第十節泰文前引字 P.104 第十一課辦簽證生詞與會話一 13 第十節復合子音 P.105-106 第十一課辦簽證生詞與會話二 14 第十節復合子音 P.107-108 十一課辦簽證句行練習 15 第十節共同當韻尾 P.109-110 第十二課訂機票生詞與會話 16 第十節二十個麥姆安 P.111-112 第十二課訂機票句行練習 17 會話練習 18 期末考 3 評量工具與策略、評分標準 Evaluation Criteria 【明列評量項目與給分標準】 1. 每週作業 20 分（準時交作業） 2. 課堂表現 20 分（準時上課無故缺席、遲到、學習態度、聽從教授、為教師或同學服務、幫助同學） 3. 每週小考 20 分（考試只是一種鼓勵同學進步，別擔憂） 4. 其中考試 20 分 5. 期末考 20 分 總共 100 分 指定／參考書目 Textbook &References 【為維護智慧財產權，請務必使用正版書籍】 1. 如何增進泰文字彙能力》文翔圖書公司。 2. 鄧欣然《泰語入門 อักษรภาษาไทยเบืÊองต้น》三思堂文化事業有限公司，台北縣新店市，台灣。(02)89902588。 3. 李錫強《標準泰國語 ภาษาไทยมาตรฐาน》冠唐國際圖書股份有限公司 1998.(02)2298-1127。 4. 傅增有《泰語三百句 ภาษาไทย》三思堂文化事業有限公司。 5. ผศ.ดร.เรืองอุไร อินทรประเสริฐ ,มโนรมย์ พิพิธกุล 《แบบหัดอ่านภาษาไทย๑ - docs.name: 基礎印尼語二
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11420LE 140200 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 35 中文名稱 Course Title 基礎印尼語二 英文名稱 Course English Title Bahasa Indonesia Basic II 任課教師 Instructor 尤溫柔 (Juli Joe) 教師連絡方式： 手機：0932-299191 EMAIL：jou.joe@gmail.com Line：julijoe0117 課程 Line 群組： 上課時間 Time 週四 15:30 – 18:20 上課教室 Room 綜二 103 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 1.透過本課程希望學生: a. 可以學到在日常生活中所使用的口語詞彙，並能了解印尼語更進階的文法。 b. 更了解印尼的在地文化。 c. 有能力用印尼語打電話到印尼店詢問商品。 2.內容涵蓋： 日常生活，旅遊用詞，詢問商品 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) bahasa Indonesia, 印尼語, 口說, 文化, 異國, culture, oral, dialog, 印尼店 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) 本課程適合有一點基礎的印尼語學者。通過朗讀課文（以會話形式）、 扮演角色、對話練習、簡單的口頭報告（對話內容）等教學手段培養 學習著聽，說，讀，寫的言語技能和運用印尼語實際打電話到印尼店 詢問商品的能力。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 以交際為主要原則、精講多練、師生互動、講練結合的活動練習、任 務型教學。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) 印尼語，一學就上手！（第二冊）QR Code 版 ● 參考書籍 (References) 我的第一本印尼語文法 ：用最科學的方法，聰明記住印尼語文 法！ ● 教學進度 (Syllabus) 會依照教學/考試需要而做 調整 週 進度 1 2026/2/26 -複習句型，數字，時間 -聽力練習 2 2026/3/5 天氣：希望不要下雨（P. 11） 3 2026/3/12 傳統市場：你要買哪一種水果？（P. 29） 4 2026/3/19 -回教過年的文化（影片欣賞） -手作編製 Ketupat 5 2026/3/26 -購物：還有其他顏色嗎？（P. 49） -地點：火車站位在哪裡？（P. 69） 6 2026/4/2 校際活動週（停課一日） 7 2026/4/9 -交通：需要換車嗎？（P. 89） -期中考前複習 8 2026/4/16 期中考(筆試) 9 2026/4/23 -問路：巴士總站往哪兒走？（P. 109） -打電話到印尼店劇本練習 10 2026/4/30 -通訊：最好選擇這張卡。（P. 129） -打電話到印尼店劇本練習 11 2026/5/7 -旅遊：我要租車。（P. 149） -打電話到印尼店劇本練習 12 2026/5/14 -餐廳：有什麼推薦的？（P. 169） -打電話到印尼店劇本練習 13 2026/5/21 -報案：我的錢包不見了。（P. 191） -打電話到印尼店劇本練習&實際 call out 14 2026/5/28 打電話到印尼店實際 call out 15 2026/6/4 複習 16 2026/6/11 期末考 (口試, 筆試) ● 成績考核 (Evaluation) 出席+課堂參與 20% 功課 20% 期中考 (筆試) 30% 期末考 (口試, 筆試) 30% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用 AI 進行協作或互學，以提 升本門課產出品質。根據本校公布之「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養 培養指引」，本門課程採取有條件開放，說明如下  學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說 明如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方 式。若經查核使用卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有 權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或不予計分。  本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片 或口頭標注。  修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。

docs.name: 中級越南語一
docs.text: 國立清華大學114-02 越南語中級（一） 授課老師：段雅芳 聯絡方式：ph.doan19@gmail.com 教學目標： 1. 本課程目標為提升學生的越南語的聽說讀寫四個能力。課程以不同的主題內 容，輔以基礎文法，結合介紹越南文化。 2. 透過本課程，學生將能習得進階閱讀技巧、進階語詞與句型寫作能力及進階 應用文寫作技巧，同時讓學生具備基礎越南話口語和聽力技巧。 3. 不斷練習聽講讓學生流利使用越南語日常基本對話，能跟越南人做基本的溝 通。 4. 授課內容為家庭、購物、飲食。 5. 語言目標：增加 200 個詞彙、15 個語法重點。 教學綱要： 中級越南語（一）內容包括： 1. 發音：越南語的音節結構，韻尾發音的原則。 2. 語言單元：家庭介紹、購物及在餐廳用餐。在家庭介紹主題，學員學會說明 家裡成員的狀況並且提出自己的想法、能夠給予評論。在購物主題，學員使 用數字練習越南錢幣的用法，利用網路的資訊建立買賣情境讓學員練習詢問 價格、殺價技巧，進一步表達對物品的評價，另外老師也介紹一些越南有名 的購物地點。在餐廳點餐的主題，學員能夠看懂簡單的菜單，對菜餚的品質 及價格提出評價，學習語言過程也帶入越南飲食文化的知識。 3. 多元的練習作業：翻譯、寫作練習、口說任務和聽力練習等。 教科書： 段雅芳《速學越南語－零基礎自學、教學都適用！》，新北市：漢宇國際文化， 民108.10。 參考書： 1. 陳凰鳳編著，《越南語發音入門》，新北市：統一出版社。 2. 阮蓮香《大家的越南語初級１》，台北：瑞蘭國際出版社，2016年11月。 3. 莫子祺《實用越南語口語教程》，北京：北京大學出版社，2014 年 5 月。 4. Nguyễn Văn Huệ chủ biên Giáo trình tiếng Việt cho người nước ngoài Tập 1, Nhà xuất bản Đại học Quốc Gia Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, năm 2006. 5. Nguyễn Văn Huệ chủ biên Giáo trình tiếng Việt cho người nước ngoài Tập 2, Nhà xuất bản Đại học Quốc Gia Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, năm 2004. 教學進度表： 週次 主題 內容 第一、二週 第七課：你的家庭有 幾個人？ 認識越南家族中的人稱代名詞 使用猜測的言語表達不確定的事 認識越南教育體制 第三、四週 第七課：你的家庭有 幾個人？ 副詞「剛剛」表達剛發生的事 詢問「了嗎？」 表達家人的關係 口說、閱讀練習：我的家庭 第五週 第七課：你的家庭有 幾個人？ 寫作：我的家庭 發音：韻尾 m、n、ng 第一次發音作業 第六、七週 第八課：我想買一件 奧黛。 比較的說法（差等比較） 討論價格貴便宜 詢問價格以及殺價的方式 增加購物的詞彙 第八週 期中考 口試＋測驗 第九、十週 第八課：我想買一件 奧黛。 購物時常用的言語：請求、試著、委 婉拒絕 表達對物品的評價（對水果、衣服的 評價） 第十一週 第八課：我想買一件 奧黛。 閱讀寫作練習 發音：韻尾 nh、ch 第二次發音作業 第十二、十三週 第九課：請給我看菜 單 認識越南菜餚 描述菜餚的味道 對菜餚的味道和價格說出評價 第十四、十五週 第九課：請給我看菜 單。 看懂越南的菜單 餐廳點餐常用會話 討論各國美食的差異 繳交寫作作業 第十六週 期末考 筆試 成績評定： 平日出席率、提問與表現：15% 每堂課點名，除重大事故外，缺席四次者點名 成績不得分。 作業：30%（發音和寫作的作業） 期中考試：25% 期末考試：30%

docs.text: 教學目標： 1.能更了解深入進階泰國話，並提升泰語的溝通能力。 2.認識泰國的觀光勝地,泰國人的思想、文化、泰國人的基本禮貌（合掌,說話,送禮、禁忌）。跨文 化與語言的角度廣大的視野 3.為了提升泰文的拼音能力、與閱讀能力，使學習者能拼出泰文詞彙。 4.在此學期能聽與說進階的飛機上用語、問方向與位置、訂房間、餐廳可以學到如何點餐、認識 泰國的菜單、旅遊同學可以學到觀光景點、購買東西與殺價、泰國同學交流上課用語等。 5.在此學期能讀與寫泰文中的字母、韻母的拼音法。 6.在此學期能了解中、高、低子音與長韻母和短韻母之拼音法。 在文法方面，認識泰語未來式、完成式，並能夠應用疑問句、肯定句，以及否定句在溝通語交談 上。 ***第一週請務必出席,缺席者等於放棄本課程*** (準備購物 12 堂泰語實用會話原價 500 元 打 8 折 400 元)(教科書可以使用整個學年) 1 旅遊同學可以學到觀光景點(第一段) ，例如: 玉佛寺，臥佛寺，鄭王廟，等等。 2 旅遊同學可以學到觀光景點(第二段)，例如: 玉佛寺，臥佛寺，鄭王廟，等等。 3 郵局同學可以學到寄包裹回台灣 (第一段) 。 4 郵局學可以學到寄包裹回台灣(第二段) 。 5 銀行同學可以學到泰國的銀行用語，可以辦業務，例如開戶，存款，辦金融卡，兌換貨幣。 6 銀行同學可以學到泰國的銀行用語，可以辦業務，例如開戶，存款，辦金融卡，兌換貨幣。 7 醫院同學可以學到如何去醫院看病(第一段)，例如: 掛號，跟醫生交談 8 醫院同學可以學到如何去醫院看病(第二段)，例如: 掛號，跟醫生交談 9 期中考 10 理髮廳同學可以學到剪髮(第一段)，例如:去泰國剪頭髮，燙頭髮怎麼說 11 理髮廳同學可以學到剪髮(第二段)，例如: 去泰國剪頭髮，燙頭髮怎麼說 12 理髮廳同學可以學到剪髮，去泰國剪頭髮，燙頭髮怎麼說 13 氣象報告同學可以學到天氣用語(第一段) ，可以學到跟天氣有關 14 氣象報告同學可以學到天氣用語(第二段) ，可以學到跟天氣有關 15 學校裡同學可以學到在學校相關的用語(第一段) ，例如:認識中文的筆順 16 學校裡同學可以學到在學校相關的用語(第二段) ，例如:認識泰文的學校用語 17 學校裡同學可以學到在學校相關的用語(第三段) ，例如:認識泰文的科目 18 期末考 評量工具與策略、評分標準成效 Evaluation Criteria 1. 每週作業 20 分（準時交作業） 2. 課堂表現 20 分（準時上課無故缺席、遲到、學習態度、聽從教授、為教師或同學服 務、幫助同學） 3. 每週小考 20 分（考試只是一種鼓勵同學進步，別擔憂） 4. 其中考試 20 分 5. 期末考 20 分 總共 100 分

docs.name: 音韻學二
docs.text: ● 課程說明(Course Description) This course design is divided in two. The first half introduces students with phonological topics on feature geometry, underspecification, stress, tone and intonation, prosodic morphology, and productivity, diachrony and synchrony, abstractness. The second half focuses on Optimality Theory and some of its subsequent developments. The aim is tripartite. It shows various speech patterns of the world’s languages. It presents how phonological theories explain the speech patterns. And it equips students with basic abilities to analyze linguistic data and to develop an argument through review exercises. ● 指定用書(Text Books) Hayes, Bruce P. (2008) Introductory Phonology. Malden, Blackwell Publishing. Kenstowicz, Michael J. (1994) Phonology in Generative Grammar. Blackwell Pubishing. Gussenhoven, Carlos and Haike Jacobs (2005) Understanding Phonology. Oxford University Press. Goldsmith, John (2011) The Handbook of Phonological Theory, 2nd Edition, Wiley- Blackwell. ● 參考書籍(References) David, Odden (2005) Introducing Phonology. docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number LING500500 學分 Credit 3 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 歷史語言學 英文名稱 Course English Title Historical Linguistics 任課教師 Instructor 廖秀娟 (LIAO, HSIU-CHUAN) 開課週數 16 週 授課語言 英文授課 上課時間 Time Wednesday (三) 9:00AM- 12:00noon (W234) 上課教室 Room 人社 C519 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters This course aims to provide students with basic skills in comparative-historical linguistics through a problem-solving approach. Students will be introduced to the standard Comparative Method and the internal reconstruction method. More specifically, students will learn how to use the Comparative Method to reconstruct the sound system, semantic, lexical, morphological, and syntactic properties of a language family/group, and to infer the linguistic prehistory of a language family/group (or a language). In addition to reconstruction, this course also introduces different theoretical perspectives on language change (especially on sound change). 請輸入課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」至少 5 個, 每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文, 以半形逗點分隔 (必填) Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Sound change, reconstruction, subgrouping, the Comparative Method, Regularity/Neogrammarian Hypothesis 課程大綱 Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) Historical linguistics (歷史語言學) (also known as comparative linguistics (比較語言學), comparative-historical linguistics (比較-歷史語言學), or diachronic linguistics (歷時語言學)) is the field of linguistics that deals with various aspects of language change, including mechanisms, results, and theories of language change (語言變化的機制、結果與解釋語言變化的理論). Making use of both inductive (歸納法) and deductive (演繹法) approaches to the investigation of language data, comparative-historical linguistics aims to address at least the following key issues: (a) genetic relationship (語言親屬關係): to figure out whether or not two or more languages are genetically related (i.e. whether two or more languages have developed from the same historical source, or whether they belong to the same language family (語系)). (b) subgrouping (語言分群): to figure out which language is more closely related to which language among genetically related languages. (c) homeland (原鄉): to figure out the possible center of dispersal (擴散 中心) of a language family (e.g. Taiwan is considered to be the most plausible homeland of the Austronesian family (南島語系)). This course aims to provide students with basic skills in comparative- historical linguistics through a problem-solving approach. Students will be introduced to the standard Comparative Method and the internal reconstruction method. More specifically, students will learn how to use the Comparative Method to reconstruct the sound system, semantic, lexical, morphological, and syntactic properties of a language family/group, and to infer the linguistic prehistory of a language family/group (or a language). In addition to reconstruction, this course also introduces different theoretical perspectives on language change (especially on sound change). Through a series of lectures, in-class practice exercises, and homework assignments, students are expected to develop the following linguistic skills: (i) identifying cognates (同源詞) in genetically related languages; (ii) reconstructing linguistic properties (e.g. sounds and sound systems, word structures, sentence structures, etc.) of earlier stages of a language (by the internal reconstruction method) and of a language family (by the Comparative Method); (iii) making use of reconstructed cultural vocabulary (文化詞彙) to infer the prehistory of a language group or a language family (e.g. to figure out the homeland of a language group or a language family, the dispersal routes of a language group, earlier cultural traits of a language group, etc.). In addition to the above-mentioned linguistic skills, students are expected to develop reasonably good abilities in logical reasoning and critical thinking, scientific thinking and reflection, and also skills in verbal communication and academic writing. Topics to be addressed include, but are NOT limited to, the following: (i) genetic relationship and distant genetic relationship (語言親屬關係與遠距語言 親屬關係); (ii) sound change and theories of sound change (音變與音變理論); (iii) Neogrammarian and the Comparative Method (新語法學派與(歷史語言學) 比較方法): phonological reconstruction (語音重建/構擬) and subgrouping (語言 分群); (iv) language contact and borrowing; (v) semantic universals, semantic change and lexical change (語義普遍性、語義變化與詞彙變化); (vi) semantic reconstruction and lexical reconstruction (語義重建/構擬與詞彙重建/構擬); (vii) linguistic prehistory (語言史前史)/ cultural reconstruction (文化重建/文化構擬): proto-culture (原始文化) and homeland (原鄉); (viii) internal reconstruction (內 部重建/構擬); (ix) morphological change and morphological reconstruction (形 態變化與形態重建/構擬); ***This course will be lectured in English. ***Chinese translation for technical terms will be provided. Students can ask questions in either English or Mandarin Chinese. ***It is very likely that we will finish every class meeting late (possibly 30 minutes ~ one hour later than the scheduled time frame). ***POLICY ON AUDITING No auditing option is available for this course. ● 指定用書(Text Books) Anderson, Stephen R. 2015. We will begin each class meeting with my lecture and/or student presentations, and then work on historical linguistics problems from Blust’s (2018) 101 problems and solutions in historical linguistics: A workbook in class. docs.text: Experimental Phonetics Instructor: Feng-fan Hsieh Spring 2026 1. Course Description This course serves as an advanced introduction to the methods and quantitative analysis used in experimental phonetics. It bridges the gap between phonetic theory and data science. Students will learn how to: Acquire and Measure: Record high-quality audio and measure acoustic properties (duration, intensity, pitch, formants) using Praat. Process: Use R to organize, clean, and visualize phonetic data. Analyze: Apply statistical models—specifically regression modeling—to test linguistic hypotheses. The course moves from the physics of sound (Acoustics) to the statistics of speech (Regression), culminating in a final research project. 2. Textbooks [KJ] Johnson, Keith (2011). Acoustic and Auditory Phonetics (3rd ed.). Wiley-Blackwell. [RMLD] Sonderegger, Morgan (2023). Regression Modeling for Linguistic Data. MIT Press. [Software] Praat (Boersma & Weenink) & R/RStudio. 3. Requirements & Grading Participation (10%): In-class discussion and lab exercises. Lab Assignments (40%): bi-weekly assignments involving acoustic measurement and R coding. Midterm Project (20%): A small-scale replication study (Data collection + Visualization). Final Project (30%): An original experiment (Hypothesis + Analysis + Write-up). 4. Weekly Schedule Phase I: Signal Processing & R Foundations Week 1: Introduction & Tools of the Trade Topic: What is experimental phonetics? Setting up the "Lab" on your laptop. Reading: [RMLD] Ch. 1 (Introduction to R). Lab: Installing Praat, R, RStudio. Basic R syntax. Recording best practices. Week 2: Basic Acoustics & Digital Signal Processing Topic: Simple harmonic motion, Sound waves, Analog-to-Digital conversion (Sampling rate, Quantization). Reading: [KJ] Ch. 1 (Basic Acoustics) & Ch. 2 (Digital Signal Processing). Lab: Digitizing sound; Oscillograms and Spectra in Praat. Week 3: Source-Filter Theory & Vowels (I) Topic: Tube models, Standing waves, Resonance, Formants. Reading: [KJ] Ch. 6 (Tube Models) & Ch. 7 (Vowels). Lab: Measuring F1/F2 in Praat. Stats: [RMLD] Ch. 2 (Data Visualization with ggplot2). Plotting the Vowel Space. Week 4: Vowels (II) & Data Wrangling Topic: Vowel normalization, Intrinsic pitch/intensity, Advanced spectral analysis (LPC vs. FFT). Reading: [KJ] Ch. 8 (Vowels/Auditory). Stats: [RMLD] Ch. 3 (Basics of Regression). The concept of "Model". Lab: Automating measurements with simple Praat scripts. Phase II: Consonants & Linear Regression Week 5: Stop Consonants & VOT Topic: Aerodynamics of stops, Voice Onset Time (VOT), Burst spectra. Reading: [KJ] Ch. 9 (Fricatives - aerodynamics part) & Ch. 10 (Stops). Lab: Measuring VOT and closure duration. Stats: [RMLD] Ch. 4 (Simple Linear Regression). Case study: Predicting VOT from Place of Articulation. Week 6: Fricatives & Spectral Moments Topic: Turbulence, Frication noise, Center of Gravity (COG), Skewness, Kurtosis. Reading: [KJ] Ch. 9 (Fricatives). Lab: Measuring Spectral Moments in Praat. Stats: [RMLD] Ch. 5.1-5.3 (Multiple Linear Regression). Case study: COG ~ Place + Vowel Context. Week 7: Pitch, Intonation & Tone Topic: F0 tracking algorithms (Autocorrelation), Tone acoustics. Reading: [KJ] Selected readings on Tone acoustics. Lab: Pitch tracking correction; Time-normalizing pitch contours. Stats: [RMLD] Ch. 5.4-5.6 (Interactions). Why "Main Effects" are rarely enough in Phonetics. Week 8: Midterm Project Presentations Activity: Students present a visualization and preliminary analysis of a small dataset. No new reading. Phase III: Advanced Modeling (The "Regression" Focus) Week 9: Categorical Data Analysis (I) Topic: Perception experiments (Identification tasks). Probability vs. Odds. Reading: [RMLD] Ch. 6 (Logistic Regression basics). Lab: Designing a simple perception task in Praat/PsychoPy. Week 10: Categorical Data Analysis (II) Topic: Analyzing binary outcomes (e.g., Sound change: Deleted vs. Retained). Reading: [RMLD] Ch. 7 (Logistic Regression application). Lab: Fitting logistic models to perception data. Week 11: The "Independence" Violation Topic: Why simple regression fails for linguistic data (Speaker/Word variation). Random Intercepts. Reading: [RMLD] Ch. 8 (Mixed-Effects Models: Concepts). Lab: Visualizing by-speaker and by-item variation. Week 12: Linear Mixed-Effects Models (LME) Topic: Random Slopes, Maximal structure (Keep it Maximal). Reading: [RMLD] Ch. 9 (LME in practice with lme4). Lab: Re-analyzing the Midterm data using LME. Week 13: Model Comparison & Reporting Topic: ANOVA for models, AIC/BIC, p-values (Likelihood Ratio Tests). How to write up results for journals (JASA/JPhon style). Reading: [RMLD] Ch. 10 (Model selection/checking). Lab: Drafting the "Results" section. Phase IV: Special Topics & Final Project Week 14: Advanced Topic Option A: Introduction to Generalized Additive Mixed Models (GAMMs) for time-series data (e.g., Pitch contours, Ultrasound tongue curves). Option B: Bayesian basics (brms). Week 15: Project Workshop / Peer Review Students bring their final project data and R code for troubleshooting and peer feedback. Week 16: Final Project Presentations

At its core, finiteness refers to verb forms that are marked for features such as tense or person agreement. However, the way finiteness is encoded varies significantly across languages. This course explores fundamental issues surrounding finiteness, with special reference to the following questions: (i) what is the definition of finiteness; (ii) what are the grammatical properties of finiteness; and (iii) how is finiteness represented in languages without agreement markers? 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Finiteness, Agreement, Tense, Chinese Syntax, Clause Structure 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) Finiteness is one of the most extensively discussed yet least clearly defined concepts in grammatical theory. Students will be introduced to crosslinguistic patterns related to the expression and interpretation of different types of arguments via discussion of several foundational publications in this field as well as some ongoing debates. In addition to the crosslinguistic component, we will also dedicate some time to explore this issue within the Austronesian languages. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 句法學 Syntax, 語意學 Semantics, 構詞學 Morphology, 論元結構 Argument Structure, 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) This course explores argument structure: the patterns in language connected to how nominal arguments are related with their predicates and how these relations are manipulated (e.g., increased, decreased, etc). Students will be introduced to common patterns and linguistic diversity in morphosyntactic realization and associated semantic inferences. Specific issues that the course will cover include valency changing operations (e.g., passives, applicatives, and causatives), thematic roles and interpretation (e.g., affectedness, agentivity, etc.), and event structure. The first part of the course will focus on introducing foundational and recent research in this area, discussing relevant theoretical debates about key issues. The second part of the course will focus on specific phenomena in Austronesian languages, discussing how these phenomena can inform the aforementioned theoretical debates. ● 指定用書(Text Books) There is no textbook for this class. Instead, readings for the class will consist of journal papers and excerpts from published books and dissertations. A representative list is given in the References section. Bingley: Emerald Publishing. ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) This course will have a seminar format where each class session will have one or two assigned readings. For each week, students are expected to do the reading in advance and post a discussion question or comment on the course website related to the reading. In addition, one student will be assigned to present the key points (e.g., main theoretical claims, key data, broader theoretical context, etc.) of one of the readings for that week to the class. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) • Week 1: Orientation and Introduction • Weeks 2-3: Foundations • Week 4: External arguments • Week 5-8: Valency changing operations • Week 9-10: Semantic issues: Volitionality, Affectedness, etc. • Week 11-14: Austronesian case studies • Week 15: (Buffer week) • Week 16: Term paper presentations ● 成績考核(Evaluation) • In-class paper presentation = 15% • Discussion comment/question posts = 25% • Class participation = 10% • Term paper presentation = 15% • Term paper writeup = 35% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output Usage of generative AI for this class is conditionally open: it is allowed in this course but should be discussed with and approved by the instructor and be indicated in the submission. For example, you may use generative AI to help you think of ideas or to fix your grammar or writing style. You may also use Generative AI to help summarize a text, but this should be done as a way to enhance or supplement your reading of the text, and not as a replacement for reading a text. As this is a graduate level course, there will be a higher standard for academic honesty compared to undergraduate courses. Students are expected to properly cite any resources they use in their term papers (or presentations if applicable). This includes clearly stating how you used Generative AI in your work, as well as having a references section and in-text citations. The exact format is not important (though I will give you pointers), as long as it is consistent and provides enough information to easily identify or find the resource used. Students may refer to the readings or the references section of this syllabus for examples. ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) We will use Google Classroom for all class materials and communication, including discussion posts. Prerequisites: Phonology (I) and (II) Course descrip4on: This course can be regarded as a "biased" introducOon to the PhoneOcs-Phonology Interface, aiming at exploring to what extent phoneOc substance and/or funcOonal factors may influence onto phonology. So the major goal of this course is to familiarize students with funcOonal approaches to phonological theorizing, in parOcular, those under the rubric of “PhoneOcally Based Phonology.” Our discussion will include — but not limited to — the following issues: i) the role of naturalness in phonology, (or, where do markedness laws come from?), ii) language-specific phoneOc details and models of phoneOc realizaOon, and if Ome permi[ng, (iii) pros and cons of funcOonalism in phonology. In addiOon, this course also features a series of "demonstraOons" showing how phoneOc and phonological phenomena in SiniOc languages can be analyzed under the framework of phoneOcally based phonology. docs.text: 1 Bilingual Sentence Processing (雙語語句訊息處理) Instructor: Yi-ching Josephine Su Office: HSS B511 Phone: ex. 34512 Course Overview Owing to globalization and the ease of access to information facilitated by the Internet, individuals' exposure to multiple languages is becoming increasingly possible. It is believed that bilingual or multilingual speakers outnumber monolingual speakers in the world’s population. As a result, there have been a growing amount of research in the past two decades investigating how semantic and syntactic representations are built incrementally in online sentence processing by people who know two languages. Topics like whether bilingual speakers process their second language in a manner similar to monolingual speakers of the target language and whether and how executive functions like working memory span and attention allocation may influence the time course of sentence processing for bilingual speakers as compared with monolingual speakers have raised several interesting hypotheses and also debates. The goal of this course is to introduce the state-of-the-art in the research of bilingual sentence processing through reading articles addressing relevant issues and learn how to use the free software LINGER to conduct a sentence processing experiment as the final project. Requirements 1. Class presentation (30%) 2. Final project (60%): Choose a topic and design a self-paced reading experiment. Find 10-15 participants to do the experiment. docs.text: 114學年第二學期(三) 生命科學導論 (Introduction to Life Science) 課程大綱 課程名稱: 11420-LS110301生命科學導論 (Introduction to Life Science) 任課老師: Kuo, Li-Yaung (郭立園)、Kao, Mou-Chieh (高茂傑)、Lin, Yi-Fan (林亦凡) Time: W7W8W9 (15:30-18:20); Room: LSII-107R 一、課程說明 (Course Description) 本課程主要 提供 本校非主修生科系(但已修過大學有機化學以上學分優先)的學生，對於 生命科學之認識。主要以選用的Starr夫婦所著的生物學為教科書，全方位介紹當代生物學 討論與關注的課題 [詳見下列 授課內容、課程表]。 本課程 將分三方面來介紹 “生命科學”: 1. 從 傳統生物學研究的內容[如: 早期的生物與相關之演化課題] 到近代生物學所關注的議題 [如:生物圈的現代、未來與生態、環境相關] 2. 從物理、化學角度開始介紹生物分子、細胞、遺傳、免疫、癌病生成與相關近代生物科 技應用，幫助未曾在大學修習過生物課程的學生了解生命科學的基礎理論。 3. 從生物個體的角度介紹生理學。從生物個體之組織、器官、系統的協調了解生物有機體 如何的運作以維續生命。 *這些介紹 將使學生方便整合所學，而立即應用到與本身相關的特定議題研究。並可作為 未來研讀高階課程的準備。論文研究與生命科學有關之學生，可以優先選修本課程。 二、指定用書 (Text Books) “Biology Today and Tomorrow with Physiology, 6th Edition by C. docs.text: 114 學年度 基礎生物學實驗 任課老師: 李以如 ijlee@life.nthu.edu.tw LSI R203 ext 42748 陳韋靜 wcchen@life.nthu.edu.tw LSI R105W ext 42686 任課助教: 黃詩婷 sthuang@life.nthu.edu.tw LSII R328C ext 35859 黃育萱 yhhuang@life.nthu.edu.tw LSII R328C ext 35859 上課地點: 普通生物學實驗室 LSII R103 上課時間: 每週二, 1:20 pm ~ 5:00 pm Syllabus Week Date Teacher Topic Content 1 2/24 李以如 陳韋靜 實驗安全與設備介紹 顯微鏡介紹 (a) 課程說明 (b) 維護實驗環境整潔 (c) 實驗室安全規則講解與儀器設備介紹 (d) 顯微鏡原理與操作 2 3/3 李以如 微生物觀察與培養(一) 細菌的觀察、分離與培養 3 3/10 李以如 微生物觀察與培養(二) 細菌的染色、鑑定與計數 4 3/17 李以如 顯微操作技術(一) 魚類解剖觀察、耳石取樣及標本包埋 5 3/24 李以如 顯微操作技術(二) 樣品研磨、顯微鏡觀察及照相 6 3/31 陳韋靜 酵母菌實驗(一) 觀察酵母菌生殖型態 7 4/7 陳韋靜 酵母菌實驗(二) 觀察酵母菌芽痕 8 4/14 李以如 生態學實驗(一) 校園水質採樣 9 4/21 李以如 生態學實驗(二) 藻類計數 10 4/28 陳韋靜 動物發生與發育(一) 斑馬魚軟骨染色 11 5/5 陳韋靜 動物發生與發育(二) 觀察動物發育胚胎 12 5/12 陳韋靜 種子生理與酵素(一) 種子休眠與萌芽 13 5/19 陳韋靜 種子生理與酵素(二) 澱粉水解酶之表現 14 5/26 李以如 陳韋靜 期末考 實驗環境整理 (a) 筆試 (b) 清點使用器具與整理實驗環境 評分方式： 項目 比例 評分標準 平時表現 22% (a) 出席狀況 (b) 實驗儀容：實驗衣及服裝穿著(ex 包鞋) (c) 實驗過程表現與實驗態度 (d) 實驗器材完善度：打破或毀損將酌量扣分 實驗報告 48% 12 份預報 + 6 份報告 期末考 30% 筆試 實驗記錄與報告（Laboratory report and note) 學習和養成書寫實驗報告是這門生物實驗課重要的一環，實驗報告可依個人實驗需要稍加增減 和修改。每一新單元開始前請同學繳交上一單元實驗成果報告給助教審查，希望這門實驗課能提供良好 的機會，可以啟發同學們在實驗研究上的興趣並重視研究精神。本學期需繳 6 份完整報告，實驗成果記 錄報告注重原創性和應用性，資料分析和實驗報告撰寫，均為必須。實驗報告撰寫規格如下 : I. 實驗名稱（heading) : 包括組別和姓名。 II. 目的（goal) : 簡短清晰的寫 1-5 個句子。描述實驗目的，探討有趣和重要的生物問題。 III. 方法（method) : 讓同學有多方了解實驗儀器的機會，培養實際操作之能力，並鼓勵創造新方法。 IV. 結果和討論（results and discussion) : (a). 有系統的呈現實驗當中所觀察到的現象和記錄下來的 data。 (b). 實驗後所做的計算和圖表。圖表要排序並標示計量單位，如此 ，在寫結果和討論時，才容 易引用 (The information found in Figure 1….) 。 (c). 對 data 的分析和比較及從中所做的推論 (interpretation and unknown identification) 。 (d). 整個實驗的結論。 如果結果未達成目標或不如預期，也請說明可能的原因，及重做時可改進之處。 問題回答（Answers and Questions) : 講義上的問題和老師與助教詢問的問題回答。 實驗規則補充： 1. 上課務必注意時間，請勿喧鬧。 2. 實驗課服裝： 實驗衣、長褲、包腳的鞋子，長髮者必須將頭髮紮起。 3. 預報一單元每人一份，於每次上課時將紙本帶給助教檢查， 參考實驗講義內容整理，亦可另外附加自己查到的參考資料，務必註明參考書目。 4. 結報一單元一組一份： a. 繳交日期：該單元結束後、下一次上課日課程開始前統一繳交給助教。 遲交一天扣報告成績 5 分，遲交時間未滿一天者，以一天計。 b. 繳交形式：eeclass 電子繳交，同一組結報一起繳交。 c. 結報內容：封面— 實驗單元、班別、組別、成員名單與學號、註明分工 實驗目的 實驗方法與流程 實驗結果與分析 結果討論 參考資料及問題回答 （其他可參考科學論文寫作相關書籍）

docs.text: 遺傳學(Genetics) 一、課程說明(Course Description) Genetics is a 16-week course designed for biology majors and is part of the core that all biology majors must complete. The objective of the course is to introduce the principles of Mendelian, molecular, quantitative and population genetics. In addition to the body of facts associated with genetics, you will be introduced to the methods that various scientists have used to solve different problems in genetics and the methodology that was used to test competing theories. Teaching materials will be provided to students before lectures for their preparation. Discussion and asking questions are highly encouraged. It is a very good idea to read assigned chapters before the lecture instead of afterward. Ask questions if concepts are initially unclear. Students who study the material before class and come to class with prepared questions, in general, will do much better than those who do not. It is also a good habit to take notes during lecture. Group study is encouraged - having to explain something to someone really focuses your attention on what you do or don't understand! However, while you are encouraged to talk to each other about solving problems, you must be able to work on your own when writing out the answers. After final exam, one more class will be provided to clarify students’ concepts and answer their questions. 二、指定用書(Text Books) Genetics: Analysis and Principles (volume 1 and 2), 7th edition by Snustad and Simmons (Wiley) 三、參考書籍(References) No. 四、教學方式(Teaching Method) Lectures in class, and may have homework or in-class test depending on lecturers. 五、教學進度(Syllabus) Week Date Weekday Topic Lecturer 1 23-Feb Monday Chapter 1, 2 李政昇 25-Feb Wednesday Chapter 3 李政昇 2 2-Mar Monday Chapter 4 李政昇 4-Mar Wednesday Chapter 4, 5 李政昇 3 9-Mar Monday Chapter 5, 6 李政昇 11-Mar Wednesday Chapter 6 李政昇 4 16-Mar Monday Chapter 7 李政昇 18-Mar Wednesday Chapter 8 李政昇 5 23-Mar Monday Chapter 8, 9 李政昇 25-Mar Wednesday Chapter 19 張筱涵 6 30-Mar Monday Chapter 19, 20 張筱涵 1-Apr Wednesday Chapter 20 張筱涵 7 6-Apr Monday 民族掃墓節補假 8-Apr Wednesday Chapter 24 張筱涵 8 13-Apr Monday 期中考 李/張 15-Apr Wednesday Chapter 24 張筱涵 9 20-Apr Monday Chapter 10, 11 廖品超 22-Apr Wednesday Chapter 11 廖品超 10 27-Apr Monday Chapter 12 廖品超 29-Apr Wednesday Chapter 12, 17 廖品超 11 4-May Monday Chapter 17, 18 廖品超 6-May Wednesday Chapter 18 廖品超 12 11-May Monday 期中考 廖品超 13-May Wednesday Chapter 13 廖品超 13 18-May Monday Chapter 13, 14 廖品超 20-May Wednesday Chapter 15 廖品超 14 25-May Monday Chapter 16, 21 廖品超 27-May Wednesday Chapter 21 廖品超 15 1-Jun Monday Chapter 22, 23 廖品超 3-Jun Wednesday Chapter 23 廖品超 16 8-Jun Monday 期末考 廖品超 六、成績考核(Evaluation) 前半部(李老師、張老師) 50%：midterm (35%) in-class quiz x 3 (5% each) homework x 3 and class participation (as bonus in certain situations) 後半部(廖老師) (50%) : Midterm (25%), Final (25%) 七、採用下列何項 AI 使用規則 (Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 八、可連結之網頁位址 https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/

docs.name: 神經退化分子遺傳機制
docs.text: 113 學年第 2 學期 神經退化分子遺傳機制 (Molecular Genetics of Neurodegeneration) 課程大綱 課程名稱:11320LS 344300 Molecular Genetics of Neurodegeneration 任課老師: Chang, Hui Yun (張慧雲) Time: T7T8 (15:30-17:20) Room: 生二 213 一、課程說明 (Course Description) 本課程旨在提供學生打下堅實的分子遺傳學和神經科學基礎，並深入探討當今備受關注的神經 退化疾病。課程內容涵蓋神經科學領域的前沿議題，以及神經退化疾病的預防與治療策略。透 過本課程，學生將能深入了解神經系統的運作機制，掌握神經退化 疾病的分子機制，並為未來的研究做好準備。（詳見課程大綱） 本課程 將分三方面來介紹 「分子遺傳學與神經退化簡述」: 1. 從傳統神經科學研究的內容 [如: 早期的神經細胞與相關之大腦意識課題] 到 近代神經科 學所關注的議題 [如:學習記憶，過去、現在和未來與阿茲海默症相關課題] 2. 從物理神經學、神経化學的方向開始介紹生物分子、細胞、遺傳、免疫、幫助未 曾在大學修習專題或研究生了解神經科學的基礎理論，神經退化等各種疾病的特徵退 化疾病生成與相關近代病理醫療科技應用。 3. 從動物個體的角度介紹生理神經科學。從生物個體之大腦神經系統、周圍神經連 結器官、管官系統的協調了解生物神經系統體如何的運作，幫助了解神經退化的過程 如何影響神經系統以維續生命的基礎科學。 *這些介紹 將使學生整合所學，而立即 應用到與本身相關的特定議題研究。並可作為未來研讀高階課程的準備。論文研究與 生命科學有 關之學生，可以優先選修本課程。" Course Description: This course aims to provide students with a solid foundation in molecular genetics and neuroscience, with a particular focus on contemporary neurodegenerative diseases. The curriculum covers cutting- edge topics in neuroscience, as well as preventive and therapeutic strategies for neurodegenerative disorders. Through this course, students will gain a deep understanding of the nervous system's mechanisms, grasp the molecular underpinnings of neurodegenerative diseases, and prepare for future research endeavors. (For detailed course outline, please refer to the syllabus.)" "Molecular Genetics and Neurodegeneration: From Bench to Bedside" This course provides a comprehensive overview of molecular genetics and neurodegeneration, bridging fundamental science with clinical applications. Through three key components: 1. Historical and Conceptual Perspectives: We will explore the historical evolution of neuroscience and examine contemporary research on learning, memory, and neurodegenerative diseases. 2. Molecular and Cellular Foundations: This section will delve into the core principles of molecular and cellular biology, genetics, and immunology, providing students with the foundational knowledge to understand the cellular and molecular underpinnings of neurodegenerative disorders. 3. Physiological Systems and Disease: We will examine the intricate workings of the nervous system and explore how these systems are disrupted in neurodegenerative diseases, with a focus on translating research findings into potential therapeutic interventions. 二、Text Books 1. Basic Neurochemistry: Principles of Molecular, Cellular, and Medical Neurobiology, edited by Scott Brady and Monica Carson. 2. Physics of the Mind: A Quantum View of the Brain, Werner Loewenstein 3. Neurodegenerative Diseases: Unifying Principles" by Jagan A. Pillai 四、 教學方式(Teaching Method) 本課程將結合傳統的投影片講解與創新的多媒體教學（如 PowerPoint、線上學習平 台），提供學生多元化的學習體驗。 五、 教學進度(Syllabus) 詳情請參考下頁。 六、 成績考核(Evaluation) 為符合現代化教學趨勢，本課程將採用多元化的評量方式，包括： • 單元測驗：評量學生對基礎知識的掌握(3-31)。 • 應用型作業：評量學生將理論應用於實務的能力 (5-12)。 • 期末報告：評量學生獨立研究與表達能力 (6-9)。 113 學年第 2 學期 神經退化分子遺傳機制 (Molecular Genetics of Neurodegeneration) 課程表 Instructor: Chang, Hui-Yun (張慧雲) Email: huiyun@life.nthu.edu.tw Time: T7T8 (15:30-17:20) Room: Life Science Build II- 213 Textbook: Principles of Neural Science; Eric R. According to International Society for Neuroethology: "Neuro-" refers to neurons, and "ethology" is the study of animal behavior, so "neuroethology" is a branch of science that seeks to understand the neural basis of "natural" animal behavior. • Find your topic o “rats, mice, zebrafish, drosophila” (commonly used model animals) NOT allowed as topics o “learned behaviors through associative conditioning, decision making related studies, drug addiction, etc” (laboratory trained behavior) NOT allowed as topics o Make sure your topic has a “Neuro-” and “ethology” component • Grading policy For the presenter o Original research paper (NOT review paper) published within three years (after 01/2023) and meet the “topic” requirement above (4%) o One-page (ONE page only) write-up (10%) about the research paper, covering - Research background and major question (first paragraph) - Methodology and results (second paragraph) - Your evaluation about the paper (final paragraph) ** point deduction for more than ONE page** o Oral presentation (10%) 12-minute talk with no more than 10 ppt slides excluding the title page ** point deduction for more than 10 ppt slides** ** at the end of the semester, everyone needs to compile the above three parts “in order” into ONE pdf file, as the final report of this assignment** (due 10 am of 6/15, submitted to eeclass. Late submissions will count for 0 point) For all others o In class note-taking (10%). For each of the presentation, - What is the research topic and question? - How did they address the question? - What is their major finding?

docs.text: Page 1 of 2 國立清華大學 114 學年第 2 學期生科系書報討論 課號: 390202 任課教師: 李以如 上課時間: R2 (週四 9:00-9:50 AM) 上課教室: 生二 217 課程簡述: 本課程將讓生命科學領域的學生學習如何從期刊論文獲取最新研 究知識，將學習到的技能包括：如何搜尋、閱讀、引用期刊論文，並且將期刊 論文的內容在課堂上報告分享。 一、課程說明 在本課程中，每位同學將會有一次上台報告一篇自選期刊論文 的機會，報告時間為25-30分鐘，內容須包含Introduction, Results, Conclusion and Discussion，以及回答同學提問。 報告論文主題不限，但請選擇發表在聲譽良好期刊、有 4-7 張 圖的研究論文，請勿選擇 Review Article 作為報告論文。 從學期初到報告的兩週前都可以將自選之期刊論文寄給授課教 師評估該篇論文是否適合課堂報告。 二、指定用書 生命科學領域相關期刊 三、參考書籍 生命科學領域相關期刊 四、教學方式 同學上台報告的前一週，可以和老師約時間討論論文與報告內 容；報告當中，老師會參與討論與提問；同學報告完後，老師 會簡短講評。 五、教學進度 請見下頁。 六、成績考核 出席: 20%，無法出席請依學校規定請假，遲到一次扣 3 分， 無故不到者一次扣 10 分。無論何種原因請假，均請於缺席日 的兩週內補交關於當週 paper 的報告一份，格式會公布於 eeclass。 報告: 55%，由教師就報告者對文獻內容的掌握(30%)、投影片 準備(10%)、時間掌控(5%)、及回答問題的表現(10%)進行評 分。 參與討論: 25% (1) 課堂討論: 15%，每一堂課在同學報告中提出有意義的問 題或參與討論可得 3 分。 (2) 提出建議: 10%，以手寫紙本方式提出你對同學報告的建 議繳交給老師，老師會針對你的建議評分，並將全班意見統整 後分享給報告同學。 Page 2 of 2 七、老師聯絡方 式 電子郵件: ijlee@life.nthu.edu.tw 校內分機: 42748 辦公室: 生科一館 203 室 Week Date 上課內容 報告同學姓名 Week 1 2/26 排定報告日期，如何準備報告 part I NA Week 2 3/5 如何準備報告 part II NA Week 3 3/12 如何準備報告 part III NA Week 4 3/19 No Class NA Week 5 3/26 同學報告 1 Week 6 4/2 No Class Week 7 4/9 同學報告 2 NA Week 8 4/16 同學報告 3 NA Week 9 4/23 同學報告 4 Week 10 4/30 同學報告 5 Week 11 5/7 同學報告 6 Week 12 5/14 同學報告 7 Week 13 5/21 同學報告 8 Week 14 5/28 同學報告 9 Week 15 6/4 同學報告 10 Week 16 6/11 No Class

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11420LS 390204 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 12 中文名稱 Course Title 書報討論 英文名稱 Course English Title Seminar 任課教師 Instructor 李政昇 上課時間 Time R2 上課教室 Room 生二 206 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 本課程旨在培養學生研讀高影響力科學期刊的習慣與學術素養。透過深入拆解論文邏輯與數據 詮釋，學生將掌握生命科學前沿趨勢，並接受完整的學術溝通訓練，包括：製作專業投影片、 進行簡潔扼要的口頭報告，以及磨練答辯與提問技巧。期能藉此引導學生發掘研究興趣，為未 來的學術或職涯發展奠定紮實基礎。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Seminar、Journal Article、Literature Reading、Oral Presentation、Discussion 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) The goal of this course is to develop students' academic literacy and their ability to engage with high- impact scientific literature. By breaking down the logic of scientific papers and interpreting complex data, students will stay abreast of cutting-edge trends in life sciences. Students will also undergo rigorous training in academic communication—specifically in designing professional slides, delivering concise presentations, and navigating Q&A sessions. This course serves as a stepping stone for students to discover their research passions and establish a solid groundwork for their future careers. ● 指定用書(Text Books): N/A ● 參考書籍(References): 兩年內發表的生物科學期刊（推薦 Cell, Nature, Science, Nature Communications, PNAS, Nucleic Acids Research, EMBO, Science Advances, Cell Reports 等）的文章，建議（但不局限於）DNA repair、chromatin dynamics 的相關主題。 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 每周由一位學生進行口頭報告，針對不同的文獻做報告與討論。 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 前兩週為課程規範介紹與報告順序安排、教師講解報告要點並示範。同學需於開學後兩週內選 定要報告的論文，並徵得老師同意。之後每週一位同學報告。 報告前一周須寄給全班 PDF 檔案，報告前兩天（週二）須將投影片寄給老師。報告時間 30-35 分鐘，提問與討論 10 分鐘，老師講解 5 分鐘。每次課堂結束後，每人須繳交互評分數及建議。 若期末有多餘時間將進行三分鐘演講活動。 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 報告整體表現（80%）：老師評分 60%、準時寄送 PDF 檔案及投影片 5%、同學互評 15%。 聽眾於課堂發問、參與討論（20%）。 Bonus：三分鐘演講（若有時間進行的話，5%）。 出席為必要條件，無故缺席一次扣 10 分。請假須依正常程序辦理，若超過兩次，須完成額外指 定作業，否則超過兩次後每次扣 5 分。遲到每 5 分鐘扣 1 分。 當週報告同學因私人因素無法報告者，扣總成績 20 分。 ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用 AI 進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出品 質。根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告，說明如下: • 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成 式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而，在本課程的「個人反思 報告」、「小組採訪作業」中，學生不得使用生成式 AI 工具撰寫作業。若經查核使用 卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或 不予計分。 • 本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。 • 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/

docs.text: 毒素學研究與應用特論(一) Special topics in toxinology research and applications I 一、課程說明 Course description Nature has evolved toxins as bioweapons for predation and defense. Broadly considered as a subfield of pharmacology and toxicology, toxinology is the science of studying venoms and toxins produced by diverse organisms. This course (special topics) is dedicated to the teaching of pharmacology and toxinology aspects of natural toxins and related compounds, where at the end of the course, students should be able to: 1. Explain the origins and functions of natural toxins. 2. Describe research methods used in the field. 3. Discuss the potential applications of toxins in biodiscovery and biotechnology. 二、指定用書 Text books Mackessy, S.P. (Ed.). (2021). Handbook of Venoms and Toxins of Reptiles (2nd ed.). CRC Press. https://doi.org/10.1201/9780429054204 三、參考書籍 References 1. Tan C. H. (2022). Snake Venomics: Fundamentals, Recent Updates, and a Look to the Next Decade. Toxins, 14(4), 247. https://doi.org/10.3390/toxins14040247 2. Križaj I. Toxinology and Pharmacology of Snake Venoms. Toxins (Basel). 2023 Mar 10;15(3):212. doi: 10.3390/toxins15030212 四、教學方式 Teaching method Lectures, group meeting, discussion. The course is mostly available in English (>70%). 五、教學進度 Syllabus The following topics will be covered: - Venom evolution and origin - Venom proteins and their compositions - Bioactivity and structure-function relationship of venom proteins - Immunological properties of venom proteins - Research methods in venom study - Biomedical application of venoms and toxins 六、成績考核 Evaluation 成績評量： Assignment：50% Report or reflective journal: 20% End-semester assessment：30% 七、AI 使用規則 AI use and regulation Open with conditions: Students should make footnotes or relevant annotations regarding the use of generative AI in their assignments or reports. In the case of non-compliance, the teacher or the university reserves the rights to re-evaluate the assignment or report. 有條件開放：學生須於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」 或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成式 AI 進行議題發 想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。若經查核使用卻無在 作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作 業或報告重新評分或不予計分。 八、可連結之網頁 位址(相關網頁) https://vetoxprotein.wixsite.com/pmolab

docs.text: MEDICAL DEVICES AND INTERFACES LSBT 5750 | SPRING, 2026 SYLLABUS LAST UPDATED ON 2/23/2026 PAGE 1 OF 4 Course Info LSBT 5750 | MEDICAL DEVICES & INTERFACES Life Science Building II, R213 Tue, 9am – 12pm Instructor CHIH-CHENG (IRIC) HUANG chihchenghuang@mx.nthu.edu.tw (03)571-5131 ext. 42685 Life Science Building II, R212 Office hours: Thu, 11am – 12pm (or by appointment) TA ROWAN DELGADO MARQUEZ rowand@gapp.nthu.edu.tw Office: TBA Office hours: by appointment Grading 20% | Homework 30% | Midterm 50% | Final Project Course Description At the crossroads between biology, electronics, information, engineering, and medicine, development of medical devices necessitates cross-disciplinary collaboration of talents from diverse fields. This course aims to provide individuals with a basic understanding of biosensors and bioelectronics. Through the final project on an R&D plan of cutting-edge medical devices, students will brainstorm and translate textbook knowledge into innovative product ideas. The first half of this class will be focused on cellular/molecular biology and the associated signal that can be transduced by sensing elements. Topics will include electrochemical processes that lead to membrane potentials and ionic currents, electrical models for the conductance of nerve cells, extracellular and intracellular stimulation, etc. The second half of the course will introduce working principles of various biosensors, such as electrochemical, magnetic, and optical sensors, as well as their technological advancement, on-field applications, and prospective developments in medical diagnostics. Course Goals & Objectives - To cultivate T-shaped and M-shaped professionals. - Understand basic operation principles of various biosensors. - Be able to use a programming app (e.g., MATLAB, Python, etc.) - Be able to deliver a striking presentation through effective teamwork. - Be able to write a technically sound research proposal. Pre-requisites - N/A. References - Florinel-Gabriel Bănică, Chemical Sensors and Biosensors: Fundamentals and Applications, Wiley, 2012. - David Issadore and Robert M. Westervelt, Point-of-Care Diagnostics on a Chip | Springer, 2013. - Avraham Rasooly and Keith E. Herold, Mobile Health Technologies: Methods and Protocols, Humana Press, 2015. Examination - The midterm will be held on the 13th week of the Spring Semester. Homework Policy - No late homework will be accepted. - Generative AI (Gen-AI) can be used for homework, but direct “copying-and- pasting” is not allowed. Academic Integrity A zero-tolerance policy towards academic dishonesty will be enforced. Academic misconduct includes, but is not limited to, cheating, plagiarism, and collusion. A failing grade (F) will be given, and cases will be forwarded to the Academic Integrity Office. An individual is encouraged to read the official campus policy. Please speak with the instructor if you have any concerns. MEDICAL DEVICES AND INTERFACES LSBT 5750 | SPRING, 2026 SYLLABUS LAST UPDATED ON 2/23/2026 PAGE 4 OF 4 FAQ I cannot attend your scheduled office hours. Are you available at other times? Feel free to email me/TA and schedule a meeting on an as-needed basis. What is the late homework policy? All assignments are due on the specified dates at the start of class. No late homework will be accepted. Can I work with someone else on homework? Absolutely. I do not mind, and in fact encourage, working together on the homework. That said, everyone needs to turn in their own, original homework. (No, you cannot write one copy and photocopy it…) The homework is set up to allow you to apply the techniques that we learn in class and prepare you for the exam. What should I do if I find an error on my midterm? If an error was made grading your exam, please bring the graded exam to me within five days of it being returned and email me a re-grading request explaining the issue. Be cautioned though, I reserve the right to re-grade the entire exam. What should I do if I have an Authorization for Accommodation (AFA) letter? Please schedule a meeting with the instructor if you require special accommodation due to a disability. What score do I need to get to pass? There is no pre-determined percentage to pass the class; the “pass” percentage will be determined after the final score has been graded. The entire class will be graded on a curve.

docs.text: 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) This course explores the immune system's dual role in maintaining health and contributing to diseases like cancer, autoimmunity, and chronic inflammation. Students will delve into the mechanisms of modern immunotherapies, including immune tolerance, immune cell signaling, and key therapeutic strategies such as immune checkpoint inhibitors and CAR T-cell therapies. Emphasis will be placed on critical analysis through group discussions and presentations, with a forward-looking focus on preclinical advancements. ● 指定用書(Text Books) - none ● 參考書籍(References) - “Cellular and Molecular Immunology 10th edition” by Abbas, Lichtman and Pillai - Published journal papers ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) This course adopts a combination of lectures, interactive discussions, and group presentations to foster active learning. External seminars by guest speakers will provide additional perspectives on cutting-edge immunotherapies. The course is offered in English. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Week data (tentative) 1. Course introduction and overview 2. Lecture “Normal Immune response” 3. Lecture Immune activation and immunosuppressants 4. Lecture “Mechanisms of Immune tolerance 5. Lecture “Immune checkpoints and therapy” 6. Lecture “Cancer immunology and immune therapy” 7. Lecture TBA 8. Exam and Groupwork introduction Groupwork presentation 9. Special Lecture by external speaker 10~14. Groupwork 15. Lecture TBA 16. Final Discussion - Schedule for groupwork discussion is flexible, and determined depending on number of students enrolled - Special seminars by external speakers are being scheduled ● 成績考核(Evaluation) (tentative) Attendance 20% Exam 50% Presentation/discussion 30% Active participation in discussions, clarity and depth in presentations, and performance on exams will form the basis of evaluation. ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output. docs.text: 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) The immune system, orchestrated by leukocytes, plays a vital role in maintaining homeostasis in the body. Various nuclear factors are essential for immune organogenesis, leukocyte lineage development, differentiation, effector functions and immune tolerance. In addition, understanding epigenomic regulation has become an urgent area of study. This course offers an introduction to the discovery, functions, and latest research on these nuclear factors, enhancing students understanding of immune cell biology. ● 指定用書(Text Books) none ● 參考書籍(References) related papers ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) Lecture, presentation and discussion ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Week 1. docs.text: Seminar course 課程大綱 (Detailed Course Syllabus) 課程說明 (Course Description) The immune system, not only protects our body from infections but also plays a crucial role in physiological and pathological processes such as cancer, inflammation, autoimmune diseases, metabolism and aging. In this course, we aim to update our knowledge of immunology and develop a deeper understanding of the complexity of the immune system. Each student will select a research article on immunology, and present in the class. Attendance is recorded by submitting a questionnaire sheet for each class. Additionally, each student is required to submit three reports on papers introduced by others. The mentor will help presenters prepare their presentations upon request, assist in understanding the presentation, and facilitate discussions. This course will be conducted in English. 指定用書 (Text Books) None 參考書籍 (References) Recently published research articles that match the aim of the class. 教學方式 (Teaching Method) PowerPoint presentations and discussions led by students and the mentor. 教學進度 (Syllabus) Weeks 1-3: Introductory course: general background in immunology, tips for preparing presentation. Weeks 4-16: Active seminar presented by students, supervised by the mentor. 成績考核 (Evaluation) Attendance 40% Presentation 20% Discussion & reports 40% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output. docs.text: 生醫學院轉學生探索學習課程 CLSM Transfer Student Exploratory Studies Spring 2026 Instructor: 焦傳金 Contact info: 生科二館 646, 03-574-2464, ccchiao@life.nthu.edu.tw Classroom: 教育館 101 教室 Class time: F5F6 (13:20-15:10) 課程目的 本課程以轉校/轉系學生為主要對象，旨在協助他們順利銜接並適應新的學習與 生活環境。課程透過引導學生熟悉校園資源、學院修課規劃與跨領域探索機會， 促進其積極參與學業與校園活動，進而建立對學校的歸屬感。同時，本課程亦 著重於批判思考與自我探索的培養，幫助學生在轉換過程中重新定位自我學習 方向與未來發展目標，找到人生的目的、意義與方向。 課程目標 (Student in transition ) A 協助學業成功：透過本課程，學生將能 1. 應用適當的策略來調整他們的課程學習方式 2. 運用有效的方式來進行時間管理 3. 熟悉與他們學習有關的彈性學制 B 認識清華並與清華建立連結：透過本課程，學生將能 1. 使用適當的校園資源，並參與有助於他們在課堂內外學習的機會 2. 與同學、老師和行政同仁建立正向的關係 3. 瞭解清華大學的歷史與傳統 C 促進個人發展、幸福和社會責任：透過本課程，學生將能 1. 建立自己的價值觀和身份認同，並瞭解這些價值觀和身份認同如何形塑 他們的觀點，以及發展與自己相同或不同立場的人的關係 2. 發展促進健康的策略，並理解身心健康如何影響他們的學業和個人成功 3. 進行自我的生涯規劃，並對未來的職場方向有所瞭解 課程閱讀材料 1. 保持原來的樣子就很好了(稻垣榮洋 2024/10/09) 課程要求及評分 課堂參與及討論 15% 拜訪教授與撰寫心得 10% 參加校園活動紀錄 10% 探索校園神秘地點 10% 撰寫履歷 10% 期中狀況分享 15% 期末專題 30% 課程安排 週次 課程主題 課程 目標 內容 Week 1 2/27 和平紀錄日 補假一天 校園探索 B 參加校園活動 Week 2 3/6 認識彼此 / 學習規劃 BC 相見歡、認識學校/學院、彈性學 制、大專生專題介紹 EYP 工具（九宮格、wayfinding） 說明”拜訪教授與撰寫心得”之作業 內容 示範 Show and Tell Week 3 3/13 自我探索 / 設計人生 C 瞭解自我, 設計人生 (生涯卡, 奧德塞 1.0, 3.0) 完成參加校園活動紀錄 Week 4 3/20 學習策略 學術倫理/AI 素 養 A 做筆記、寫作業、準備考試 誠信原則、學務章則、著作權、AI 素養與倫理 Week 5 3/27 工讀、實習與出 國交換 AB 校內外工讀、實驗室專題生、企業 實習、出國交換 Week 6 4/3 兒童節補假 學習規劃 B 完成拜訪教授與撰寫心得 Week 7 4/10 大一年 年會 探索校園 B 清華校園走讀（通識中心張繼瑩老 師與助教帶領） Week 8 4/17 時間管理與睡眠 管理 AC 規律作息、習慣養成、睡眠品質、 睡眠時間與長度 Week 9 4/24 期中狀況分享 ABC 學習成效檢核、分享校園資源使用 期中狀況分享（個人報告） Week 10 5/1 勞動節補假 探索校園 B 認識清華的歷史與傳統 完成探索校園神秘地點 Week 11 5/8 身心健康與壓力 調適 C 50 分鐘 Mindfulness 課程 規律運動、心理諮商、壓力釋放 繳交期末專題構想書 Week 12 5/15 表達與溝通 AC 簡報製作、短講技巧 與授課老師討論期末專題方向與實 施方式 Week 13 5/22 目標設定 C 職涯訪談、學長姊分享（畢業 3 年 內，每人 20 分鐘） Week 14 5/24 履歷撰寫 C CV、自我介紹 完成撰寫履歷 Week 15 6/5 人際互動與多元 文化 C 同學/室友關係、親密關係、師生關 係 多元共融、性別平等、與外籍生對 話或一起探索校園（小組活動）、 討論各國文化議題、討論微歧視 Week 16 6/12 期末成果分享 ABC 給下一屆新生的信與影片、解決校 園真實問題的專題研究 繳交期末成果並進行專題研究成果 分享 課堂參與及討論 15% 每週 2 人進行以物件為導向的 Show and Tell（說故事與公眾短講） 參與課堂分組討論 拜訪教授與撰寫心得 10% 邀請一位生醫學院教授在校內 Café 聊天，瞭解他的學習歷程，他對生醫學院學 生未來發展的想法，並撰寫最少 500 字心得（提供$$$） 參加校園活動紀錄 10% 參加校內各式活動 2 次，並提供證明（照片或收據） 探索校園神秘地點 10% 詢問同學（街訪同學) 2 個清華神秘地點，親自前往且說明神秘之處，拍照上傳 撰寫履歷 10% 寫一份暑期實習申請的個人履歷 期中狀況分享（個人報告）15% 分享開學後到現在所面臨的挑戰與嘗試解決的成效 （每人 5 分鐘） 期末專題 30% 1. 寫一封給下一屆同學的信，並拍攝一個 3 分鐘影片，讓下一屆同學瞭解這 門課對其影響（個人成果） 2. 針對清大生醫學院學生或清大全校學生所面臨的問題，進行研究並試圖找 出解決方案（團體報告） 加分項目 5% 探索校園附近美食或新竹市景點探索（拍照打卡）

docs.nameEn: English for Academic Communication in Life Sciences and Medicine
docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年度第 2 學期課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11420LSC 104400 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 中文名稱 Course Title 生命科學與醫學學術英文溝通 英文名稱 Course English Title English for Academic Communication in Life Sciences and Medicine 任課教師 Instructor 陳子福 廖品超 周雅菁 李以如 (依上課順序列名) 上課時間 Time W7 上課教室 Room 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 本課程專為國立清華大學生命科學院與醫學院的學生設計，旨在培養學生於學術情境中有效運用英文的 能力。課程內容涵蓋閱讀、寫作、口語表達與簡報技巧，並以生命科學與醫學相關主題為核心。課程由 四位教師共同授課，各自以其專業領域與教學風格，提供多元化的學習體驗。透過閱讀與分析科學文 章、摘要與寫作練習，以及學術簡報與討論演練，學生將逐步提升理解與應用英文的能力。本課程著重 實用性，協助學生在研究討論、團隊合作及學術會議中，能夠清楚且有效地表達專業觀點。 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) This course is designed for undergraduate students in the Colleges of Life Sciences and Medicine at NTHU, with the goal of enhancing their ability to use English effectively in academic contexts. The course covers reading, writing, oral communication, and presentation skills, focusing on topics related to life sciences and medicine. It is jointly taught by four instructors, each bringing their expertise and teaching style to provide students with diverse training experiences. docs.nameEn: Special Topics on Molecular Motors and Axonal Transport
docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年第下學期課程大綱 科號 Course No. LSMC510700 組別 group 學分 credit 2 人數限制 Size limit 0 修課年級 For grade ■ 大學部 年級以上 (undergraduate) ■ 碩士班一年級以上(含博士班) graduate ■ 碩士班二年級以上(含博士班) 上課時間 Time F7F8 教室 Room 505A LSBI 科目中文名稱 Course title in Chinese 分子馬達與軸突運輸特論 科目英文名稱 Course title in English Special topics on Molecular Motors and Axonal Transport I 任課教師 Teacher 王歐力 擋修科目 Prerequisite 擋修分數 credit ※下列各欄由任課教師提供※ 一、課程說明 Course Description The motivation for this class originates from recent findings that relate molecular motors to neurodegeneration. Though I generally believe that complex diseases (such as cancer or neurodegeneration) rely on complex network of entangled factors, the idea that malfunction in neuronal transport leads to accumulation of axonal “disease proteins” (tau in Alzheimer’s disease, neurofilaments in ALS or α-synuclein in Parkinson’s disease), and thus to neuropathological phenotypes, seems not only scientifically sound but is indeed reflected in a large set of publications (which we will discuss in part in this class). The bidirectional transport of cargoes along microtubules guarantees neuronal function as polarization, elongation, neuronal plasticity and, based on recent studies, even brain wiring and higher brain functions. Compared to its thin diameter, the axon is an extremely crowded cellular extension housing a diverse set of cytoskeletal elements as microtubules, neurofilaments and actin filaments as well as many types of different organelles as synaptic vesicles, mitochondria and RNA granules. Even more challenging for the axonal transport system is that the cytoskeleton is largely cross- linked with microtubule- and neurofilament-binding proteins, whereas microtubules are not smooth themselves but decorated with MAPs, providing acute obstacles for motors. Many of neuropathological disease phenotypes related to axonal transport and cytoskeleton resemble those in adult-onset neurodegenerative diseases (AONDs), a group of neurological disorders that are based on an age-dependent diminishment in neuronal function associated with a decline in synaptic activity, axonal connectivity, degeneration of axons and synapses (“dying back” pattern) and, at a later stage, neuronal cell death. To develop novel therapeutic strategies, we need to understand how to delay or even cure neurodegeneration which becomes increasingly important as human lifespan increases and therefore incidences of AONDs, specifically in Taiwan with its very low birth rates and the expected severe increase in the aged population. 二、指定用書 Text Books Chapters in current cell biology textbooks (“Alberts”, Lodish”, “Pollard” etc.) related to the cytoskeleton and molecular motors. 三、參考書籍 References See HTTP below 四、教學方式 Teaching Method Lecture (PI) and student’s journal presentations. 五、教學進度 Syllabus 2 hourly seminar whole semester, no exam 六、成績考核 Evaluation Attendance: 20%. Performance: 35%. Presentation: 45% 七、位址 http:// http://life.nthu.edu.tw/~laboiw/Handouts/index.html

There is a particular focus on the genetic basis of phenotypic structures, how they change during evolution, and how novel structures arise. The fundamentals of evo-devo will be introduced. We will also discuss articles from the original scientific literature at class. 二、指定用書 1. Arthur W 1997. The Origin of Animal Body Plans . Cambridge (UK): Cambridge University Press. 2. Implications of the Cancer Stem-Cell Hypothesis for Cancer Prevention and Therapy 成績評量： 計分項目 準則 配分比％ Presentation 同儕評分 60％ Attendance 缺席一次扣 3 分 30％ Questions 提問一次加 1 分 10% 生成式人工智慧倫理聲明 本課程秉持透明與負責任的原則，鼓勵學生在學習過程中充分利用人工智慧（AI） 進行協作或互相學習，以提升課程成果的品質。我們遵循本校公布的「大學教育 場域AI協作、共學與素養培養指引」，並在以下條件下實施： 使用條件： 學生在課堂作業或報告中使用生成式AI，須在「標題頁註腳」或「引 用文獻後」簡要說明其使用方式，包括但不限於議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考 等。 透明度要求： 學生需清楚地指出生成式AI的應用範疇，確保他們理解及認識到 AI工具僅作為輔助工具，而非取代個別學生的原創性和責任。 檢核措施： 若教師、學校或相關單位發現學生在作業或報告中使用生成式AI卻 未標明其使用方式，有權重新檢核並重新評分，或者可能不予計分。 課程素養培養： 這項政策旨在培養學生正確、合理且道德的AI使用態度，使其 能夠善用科技工具，同時保持學術誠實與創造性。 透過以上措施，我們期望學生在使用生成式AI的同時，能夠保持學術誠實，並遵 循相關的倫理原則。本課程致力於培養學生在數位時代中具有深厚專業知識和道 德素養的技能，以應對未來的挑戰。 請假規定 國立清華大學學生請假辦法 第四條 學生於期中、期末考試不得請假。但因公、急病、分娩、近親喪亡、臨時發生不 可抗力或不可歸責於當事人之因素，應檢附相關證明文件經任課教師同意。惟任 課教師另有規定者，從其規定。 第五條 准假權責： 一、事假、病假、喪假、娩假：二日以內由任課教師核准；三日以上由任課教師 核准、系/班（所）主任（所長）備查。 二、心理假、生理假：逕送任課教師備查。 三、原住民族歲時祭儀假：由原住民族學生資源中心查核學生身分及行政院原住 民族委員會公告之所屬族群歲時祭儀日期通過後，逕送任課教師備查。 四、公假：學生社團或校隊由學務單位承辦人、學務單位主管、學生事務長核准； 系（所）活動、兵役或無法歸類之活動由系（所）單位承辦人、系/班（所）主 任（所長）、學院院長核准；行政單位因公派遣學生出任公務由行政單位承辦人、 行政單位二級主管、行政單位一級主管核准，並提供任課教師備查。

docs.name: 分子與細胞生物學新進展
docs.nameEn: Frontiers in Molecular and Cellular Biology
docs.text: 國立清華大學 114 學年度第 2 學期課程大綱 科號 Course Number LSMC546000 學分 Credit 1 人數限制 Class Size 0 中文名稱 Course Title 分子與細胞生物學新進展 英文名稱 Course English Title Frontiers in Molecular and Cellular Biology 任課教師 Instructor 蕭尊先 上課時間 Time Fa 上課教室 Room 生二 LSII 213 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 This course covers the principles of molecular and cellular biology, emphasizing their integration in understanding life processes. Topics include gene regulation, cell signaling, tissue development, molecular evolution, and biodiversity, as well as the molecular and cellular bases of immunity, tumorigenesis, infectious diseases, and host–microbe interactions. By connecting these disciplines, students will gain insights into how molecular mechanisms drive organismal function, adaptation, and disease, preparing them to address modern biological and biomedical questions from a systems-level perspective. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) 分子生物學、細胞生物學、演化生物學, 發育生物學, 分子與細胞免疫, 感染症疾病 Molecular biology, Cellular biology, Evolutionary biology, Developmental biology, Molecular and cellular immunology, Infectious diseases 課程大綱 (必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明 (Course Description) The course aims to connect faculty members, postdoctoral researchers, graduate and undergraduate students from the Institute of Molecular and Cellular Biology. It features three-minute English oral presentations by students and postdoctoral fellows, and experts from the bioindustry and/or the English education field will be invited to deliver guest lectures. All participants are encouraged to share their research experiences and presentation feedback across laboratories, thereby fostering collaboration and improving presentation skills. The invited speakers are expected to share bioindustrial insights and/or tips for an English presentation with all participants. ● 指定用書 (Text Books) N/A ● 參考書籍 (References) Individual research reports ● 教學方式 (Teaching Method) 1. Students are required to participate in a 3-minute English oral competition to present their research on related topics. Faculty members and guest lecturers will provide their suggestions to help students improve their presentation skills. 2. Guest lectures 3. Field work ● 教學進度 (Syllabus) Day 1 (14th Jan)  3-minute English oral competition (9:00~10:00)  Feedback form judges and Guest lecture: Tips for English presentation (10:10~12:00)  Networking across the laboratories of IMCB (12:10~14:10)  Guest lecture in bioindustry and discussion (14:20~17:20) Day 2 (15th Jan)  Field work: Introduction to fern ecology in Taiwan (9:00~17:20) ● 成績考核(Evaluation) Report, Attendance. The final evaluation will be announced in class. Faculty members serve as judges to grade in the oral competition. ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 可參考下列網頁範例 See the following web page for examples. https://curricul.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/404-1208-248357.php?Lang=zh-tw ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) 11420LSMC546000 分子與細胞生物學新進展 修課規定 本課程為 114 下學期的選修課程，但會在寒假時(2026/1/14-15)進行兩天密集式 授課，欲修課的學生須先進行課程再於開學時進行課程加選。 評分方式：通過 (pass) 或 不通過 (fail) 欲通過本課程的學生須達成以下條件： 1. 全程出席分生所 Retreat 活動，需要簽到 (1/14-15，兩天) 2. 繳交兩份報告： A. 繳交一頁 三分鐘英語學術簡報(3MT)競賽 PPT 投影片 (內容須按照課 程中講師之建議製作，如有參加三分鐘英語學術簡報競賽，則只需繳交 按建議修改後的版本即可)，並且請在備忘稿處附上講稿 (建議長度： 為了使 3MT 簡報清晰且節奏良好，字數以 350–450 字為佳)。 B. 一份英文心得報告，主題可針對第一天活動的生技產業或是第二天的田 野調查，內容須涵蓋：What I know, What I want to know, What I learned 三個面向，一頁 A4，至少 300 字，不得用 AI 直接生成。 3. 繳交一份學習單 (中英文皆可)：於 Day 1 networking 時間，詢問至少三位 來自不同實驗室的同學，並記錄以下資訊：姓名、實驗室、研究主題、特 別擅長的實驗技術。 備註： 1. 修課同學不一定要參加三分鐘英語學術簡報競賽。 2. 第二天的步道健行，如有身體不適，得以在組員陪同下提前返回老街休息 站。 3. 學習單內容請自行記錄，並於當天活動結束前繳交給助教或授課教師。 4. 兩份報告請在規定時間內繳交上傳至 eeclass 網站。 5. 如未完成以上課程通過條件，教師可以不同意加選。 11420LSMC546000 Course Guidelines for “Frontiers in Molecular and Cellular Biology” This course is offered in the 114 Spring semester. However, a two-day intensive course will be held during the winter break (January 14–15, 2026). Students who want to take this course must first complete the intensive program and then add the course during the enrollment period at the beginning of the semester. Grading: Pass / Fail To pass the course, students must fulfill the following requirements: 1. Full participation in the IMCB Retreat - Students must attend the retreat for the entire duration on January 14–15 and complete the required sign-in. 2. Submission of two assignments: A. One-page Three-Minute English Academic Presentation (3MT) Competition PPT slide The slide must follow the guidelines provided by the instructor during the course. Students who participate in the 3MT only need to submit the revised version that incorporates the instructor’s suggestions. Please also include the speech script in the notes section (Recommended length: 350–450 words for a clear, well-paced 3MT presentation). B. One English reflection report Topics may focus on (1) the bioindustry lecture on Day 1 or (2) the introduction of fern ecology on Day 2. The report must include three components: What I know, What I want to know, and What I learned. One A4 page, at least 300 words. AI-generated content is not allowed. 3. Submission of one learning worksheet (in Chinese or English) - During the Day 1 networking session, students must talk to at least three students from different laboratories and record the following information: Name, Laboratory, Research topic, and Experimental expertise. Notes 1. Students taking the course are not required to participate in the 3MT competition. 2. For the hiking activity on Day 2, students who feel unwell may return early to the 11420LSMC546000 rest area with the accompaniment of their group members. 3. Please submit the learning worksheet to the TA or instructor before the end of the day’s activities. 4. The two required assignments must be uploaded to the eeclass system before the deadline (will be announced in the class). 5. Students who fail to meet the above requirements may not be approved for course enrollment.

docs.nameEn: Special Topics in Homologous Recombination of Chromosomes II
docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number 11420LSMC546200 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 0 中文名稱 Course Title 染色體同源重組特論二 英文名稱 Course English Title Special Topics in Homologous Recombination of Chromosomes II 任課教師 Instructor 李政昇 上課時間 Time F7F8 上課教室 Room 生一 421A 課程簡述(必填) (最多 500 個中文字) 本欄位資料會上傳教育部課程網 Brief Course Description (required) (50-200 words if possible, up to 1000 letters) 這門課將介紹染色體同源重組的主要觀念以及研究方法。主要會以酵母菌做為闡述的對象，了 解染色體的斷裂是如何被修復，內容涵蓋酵母菌遺傳學與分子生物學為主。 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」(必填) 至少 5 個,每個關鍵字至多 20 個中文,以半形逗點分隔 Please fill in at least 5 course keywords (up to 40 letters for each keyword) and use commas to separate them.(required) Homologous Recombination, DNA repair, chromosome dynamics, DNA double strand break 課程大綱(必填)Detailed Course Syllabus ● 課程說明(Course Description) This class will introduce the major concepts and methods in homologous recombination of chromosomes. The students will learn how DNA double strand breaks are repaired by homologous recombination mainly in budding yeast. Both conceptual background in yeast genetics and detailed molecular approaches to analyze chromosomes will be covered. ● 指定用書(Text Books): DNA Recombination Editor(s): Tsubouchi, Hideo ISBN: 978-1-61779-129-1 Humana Press ● 參考書籍(References): Selected papers from high profile journals ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) All students are required to read all assigned chapters and papers and then participate in classroom discussion. ● 教學進度(Syllabus) 02/27 Week 1: 和平紀念⽇補假 03/06 Week 2: Analysis of Meiotic Recombination Intermediates by Two-Dimensional Gel Electrophoresis 03/13 Week 3: Mapping of Crossover Sites Using DNA Microarrays 03/20 Week 4: Using the Semi-synthetic Epitope System to Identify Direct Substrates of the Meiosis-Specific Kinase, Mek1 03/27 Week 5: Genetic and Molecular Analysis of Mitotic Recombination in Saccharomyces cerevisiae 04/03 Week 6: 兒童節補假 04/10 Week 7: Genetic and Molecular Analysis of Mitotic Recombination in Saccharomyces cerevisiae 04/17 Week 8: Genetic and Molecular Analysis of Mitotic Recombination in Saccharomyces cerevisiae 04/24 Week 9: In Vivo Site-Specific Mutagenesis and Gene Collage Using the Delitto Perfetto System in Yeast 05/01 Week 10: Detection of RNA-Templated Double-Strand Break Repair in Yeast 05/08 Week 11: Tracking of Single and Multiple Genomic Loci in Living Yeast Cells 05/15 Week 12: Cell Biology of Homologous Recombination in Yeast 05/22 Week 13: Cell Biology of Homologous Recombination in Yeast 05/29 Week 14: Live Cell Imaging of Meiotic Chromosome Dynamics in Yeast 06/05 Week 15: Live Cell Imaging of Meiotic Chromosome Dynamics in Yeast 06/12 Week 16: The week of final exam ● 成績考核(Evaluation) Class discussion: 40% Assigned presentation: 40% Attendance: 20% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output 基於透明與負責任的原則，本課程鼓勵學生利用 AI 進行協作或互學，以提升本門課產出品 質。根據本校公布之佈的「大學教育場域 AI 協作、共學與素養培養指引」，本門課程採取 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於作業或報告，說明如下: • 學生可於課堂作業或報告中的「標題頁註腳」或「引用文獻後」簡要說明如何使用生成 式 AI 進行議題發想、文句潤飾或結構參考等使用方式。然而，在本課程的「個人反思 報告」、「小組採訪作業」中，學生不得使用生成式 AI 工具撰寫作業。若經查核使用 卻無在作業或報告中標明，教師、學校或相關單位有權重新針對作業或報告重新評分或 不予計分。 • 本門課授課教材或學習資料若有引用自生成式 AI，教師也將在投影片或口頭標注。 • 修讀本課程之學生於選課時視為同意以上倫理聲明。 ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) https://eeclass.nthu.edu.tw/

docs.text: 國立清華大學課程大綱 科號 Course Number LSMC574600 學分 Credit 2 人數限制 Class Size 24 中文名稱 Course Title 消化系統的奧秘:從基礎到臨床治療 英文名稱 Course English Title Gastrointestinal System: From Basic to Therapeutics 任課教師 Instructor 黃千瑜(HUANG, CHIEN-YU) 劉懿璇(LIU, YI-SHIUAN) 上課時間 Time W3W4 上課教室 Room 生二 107 課程簡述 This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the gastrointestinal (GI) system, which plays a vital role in digestion, absorption of nutrients, and overall health. Students will explore the physiological processes that govern GI function and learn about pharmacological interventions for various GI diseases. By the end of the course, students should have a solid understanding of the physiology of the GI system and its pharmacological aspects. 課程內容「中文暨英文關鍵字」 消化生理學、消化系統藥理、腸胃藥物、止吐藥、臨床藥物治療 Gastrointestinal physiology, Gastrointestinal Pharmacology, Gastrointestinal Medications, Antiemetic, Drug Therapy 課程大綱 ● 課程說明(Course Description) 課程設計包含基礎生理學、藥理學與臨床藥物治療，以及相關論文導讀。利用論文導讀以及一 堂口頭報告，可提升學生高密度自主性學習，培養學生主動、積極、獨立思考的學習精神，增 進學生溝通及獨立思考的能力。 本課程目標為建立學生消化系統相關的基礎生理藥理概念、學術論文與臨床治療的整合能力。 ● 指定用書(Text Books) Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed., 2020 Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology 8th 2022 Basic and Clinical Pharmacology, Katzung et al., 16th edition ● 參考書籍(References) 課堂指定論文 ● 教學方式(Teaching Method) 課堂教學 ● 教學進度(Syllabus) Week 授課內容 授課教師 1 藥理概論 I 黃千瑜 2 消化道概論 劉懿璇 3 食物在消化道中的推進與混合 劉懿璇 4 藥理概論 II 黃千瑜 5 消化道的分泌功能 劉懿璇 6 消化性潰瘍藥物 黃千瑜 7 論文導讀 I 黃千瑜/劉懿璇 8 消化與吸收 劉懿璇 9 促腸胃蠕動劑 黃千瑜 10 論文導讀 II 黃千瑜/劉懿璇 11 肝臟生理 劉懿璇 12 腹瀉/便秘藥物 黃千瑜 13 論文導讀 III 黃千瑜/劉懿璇 14 止吐藥物 黃千瑜 15 代謝與能量 劉懿璇 16 期末口頭報告 黃千瑜/劉懿璇 ● 成績考核(Evaluation) 出席 10%，課堂參與 10%，論文導讀參與 40%，期末報告 40% ● 採用下列何項 AI 使用規則(Indicate which of the following options you use to manage student use of the AI) 有條件開放，請註明如何使用生成式 AI 於課程產出 Conditionally open; please specify how generative AI will be used in course output ● 可連結之網頁位址 相關網頁(Personal Website) eeclass
